Mercury help

This guide holds Mercury’s own help, gathered from support.mercury.com in November 2026. Mercury is a financial technology company that offers business and personal banking through partner banks. The guide covers opening an account, sending and receiving money, cards, statements and documents, and Mercury’s other business tools. Each heading names the category, Business or Personal, then the subject.

Left out on purpose: legal pages such as terms, privacy policies and disclosures, pages for law enforcement and developers, and Android-only articles, as this collection covers Windows, the web, iPhone and iPad, and Alexa.

The help text belongs to its publisher and is gathered here unchanged for accessible reading. This guide’s own arrangement and wording are available under CC BY-SA 4.0.

Business: 1099 Filing

1099 Filing FAQs

What 1099 Forms does Mercury support?

Mercury currently supports 1099-NEC and 1099-MISC filings. Mercury also generates 1099-INTs for businesses who have earned interest.

How is Mercury’s 1099 Filing product different from the 1099-INT Mercury generates?

Mercury issues a 1099-INT if you’ve earned $10 or more in interest on your Mercury accounts. This form reports your interest income to the IRS and is provided automatically each year. You’ll use it when filing your taxes. In contrast, Mercury’s 1099 Filing product helps you create and file 1099-NEC and 1099-MISC forms for your business. These forms report payments you’ve made to others, such as contractors, freelancers, rents, or royalties.

What is a 1099-NEC or 1099-MISC Form?

  • 1099-NEC refers to an IRS tax form used to report payments of $2,000 or more made to nonemployees for services. This typically applies to freelancers, independent contractors, sole proprietors, and other service providers. If your business pays someone who is not on payroll, you may be required to file a 1099-NEC.
  • 1099-MISC refers to an IRS tax form used to report a variety of payments that don’t fall under wages, salaries, or nonemployee compensation. Businesses must issue a 1099-MISC when they make certain types of payments, such as rent, royalties, or prizes, above IRS reporting thresholds.

Does Mercury handle state filings?

Yes. We help you file 1099-NEC and 1099-MISC forms with the IRS and all 50 states. We also support 1099 corrections.

What information do customers need to file a 1099?

A W-9 and the reportable total you paid the recipient during the tax year.

How does Mercury determine who appears on the “Add a 1099 Recipient” page?

Mercury includes all Recipients and ACH/Wire Pull counterparties in this step.

How does Mercury calculate 1099 reportable payments?

Mercury includes the following based on IRS guidance for 1099 reportable transactions. If you need to exclude certain transactions from this list, you can do so by Adding a 1099 Recipient, selecting them, and clicking “Edit Filing”.

  • Payments made to a Recipient (ACH, Check, Wire, Intl. Wire)
  • ACH Pulls
  • Wire Pulls

Mercury does not include the following as they are not reportable on a 1099-NEC or 1099-MISC. If you believe a transaction is missing, you can manually add a transaction in the “Edit Filing” page.

  • Card payments
  • Reimbursements
  • Transfers to a linked account

Can I add a team member to file 1099s?

Yes, when managing roles and permissions, assign the Accountant role or a Custom User role with the Accounting permission to let a team member manage and file 1099s for the company. Custom Users with the Accounting permission will only see transactions from the bank accounts they have access to, so be sure to grant access to any accounts with 1099 reportable transactions.

What if a customer made a payment outside of Mercury?

You can manually add external payments by adding a 1099 Recipient and clicking “Edit Filing” in the bottom menu. From there, you can open each recipient’s filing profile and add new external transactions.

What if a customer paid a recipient outside of Mercury?

  • You can add a new Recipient from the Recipients page, or by clicking “Create Recipient” from the “Add Recipient” menu
  • Navigate to Payments > Taxes > Get Started and select them as a 1099 recipient
  • Once you have selected your 1099 recipients and completed the initial workflow, you will see an Edit filing button.
  • From there, you can open each recipient’s filing profile and add new external transactions.

Can a user file 1099s now and the rest later?

Absolutely. File in multiple batches; each submission is processed and billed separately.

Can a user file for a counterparty?

Yes, all counterparties (entities paid via ACH Pull) will appear in the “Add a 1099 Recipient” step when Getting Started with 1099 Filing. Simply select the counterparty you would like to file for and proceed to the next step.

What’s the difference between a 1099 Recipient, a Recipient, and a Counterparty?

Recipients are anyone a customer has paid through Mercury, while Counterparties are those paid via ACH Pull. For tax purposes, these are grouped into 1099 Recipients, which are filing profiles used specifically for 1099 forms. Each 1099 Recipient must have a unique Name/TIN combination, and if duplicates exist, customers can combine filing profiles to ensure their filings remain accurate.

Does Mercury support 1099 Withholdings?

No, Mercury does not support any Federal or State backup withholding reporting. If you have backup withholdings you must file these outside of Mercury.

Why does my State Filing status stay on “Submitted” instead of changing to “Accepted”?

Only states that participate in the IRS CF/SF (Combined Federal/State Filing) program send us an electronic Accepted status. If your recipient’s state does not participate in CF/SF, Submitted is the final status we can show in Mercury. For more details about the filing, please contact your state tax agency directly.

Does Mercury resolve IRS notices?

Mercury does not resolve IRS notices; you’re responsible for the accuracy of the information provided.

How does pricing work?

  • Customers can download W9 and Payment information for free from the Recipients page. Advanced 1099 capabilities such as Filing 1099s with the IRS and States are available for free as part of our paid Mercury Plus and Mercury Pro plans (learn more about pricing here) or for a flat fee of $5 per 1099 Form for non-subscribers. We do not charge any additional fees for filing a 1099 Correction.
  • Non-subscribers will see a checkout page in order to complete filing. Fees are debited from their Mercury account after submission

For specific guidance on your tax filing obligations, please consult with a qualified tax professional. Mercury does not provide tax advice. Tax regulations can be complex and vary based on individual circumstances, so it’s important to seek personalized advice from an expert who can assess your unique situation.

File 1099-NEC and 1099-MISC forms in Mercury

Mercury 1099 Filing lets you prepare, e-file, and distribute IRS Form 1099 NEC and 1099 MISC – all from your Mercury dashboard. It pulls all eligible payments you’ve already made through Mercury, collects missing W-9s from recipients, helps you file with the IRS and states, and securely delivers recipient copies.

This streamlined workflow helps you file with the IRS and states, saves time by eliminating spreadsheets and manual uploads, and keeps everything in one place by letting you track eligibility, filings, and tax documents all from one place.

Who is required to file a 1099-NEC and/or 1099-MISC?

1099 reporting is required by law: Every business “engaged in a trade or business” with U.S. persons* is legally required to file a 1099-NEC or 1099-MISC if it makes certain types of payments — typically $2,000 or more for services and/or $10 or more in royalties in a tax year — to non-employees or specific entities. The most common forms are 1099-NEC, used for payments to independent contractors, and 1099-MISC, used for other reportable payments such as rent or royalties. The IRS can charge penalties up to $660 for each form a business fails to correctly file on time. Additionally, interest will accrue on your outstanding penalty balance until you pay off the amount.

*For federal tax purposes, you are considered a U.S. person if you are:

  • An individual who is a U.S. citizen or U.S. resident alien;
  • A partnership, corporation, company, or association created or organized in the United States or under the laws of the United States; An estate (other than a foreign estate); or A domestic trust

The following table provides the 2026 IRS filing deadlines for the 1099-NEC and 1099-MISC. While the IRS e-file deadline for the 1099-MISC is March 31, it must still be delivered to recipients by February 1. For that reason, we still surface Feb 1 as the filing deadline for both the NEC and MISC within the product experience.

Form type

Purpose

Recipient copy due

IRS e-file due

1099-NEC

Non-employee compensation (contractors, freelancers, lawyers)

Feb 1

Feb 1

1099-MISC

Rent, royalties, prizes, settlements, and other income

Feb 1

Navigating the Taxes page

  • Navigate to the Taxes page, which is located on the left-hand menu under the Payments section
  • Here, you will find two tabs, the 1099 Filing tab and the Tax Documents tab.
    • The 1099 Filing tab is where you manage the 1099 filing process. Click Get Started to add 1099-eligible recipients, send W-9 requests, review payment data, and e-file forms with the IRS and state agencies.
    • The Tax Documents tab is your document hub. It includes all W-9 and W-8BEN forms submitted by recipients, any 1099-NEC and 1099-MISC forms you’ve filed through Mercury, and any 1099-INT forms Mercury has issued for your account.

Getting started with 1099 Filing

  • Navigate to Payments > Taxes
  • Make sure to specify the Tax Year dropdown as the year you want to file for
  • Click Get Started from the 1099 Filing page
  • Add 1099 Recipients who meet the payment, location, and tax entity criteria provided by the IRS. Mercury will show a list of all your Recipients and Counterparties to choose from. When possible, we’ll suggest recipients who appear to meet the IRS criteria for 1099 Filing.
  • Select a 1099 Form type for each recipient. If someone received both NEC and MISC payments, you can choose more than one option. Not sure which form to choose? Click here to learn more.
  • Request W9s or upload one manually for recipients who are missing a W9
  • Once you complete these steps, you will land on the Filing Summary page
Handling duplicates
  • On the Add 1099 Recipients step, if you notice duplicate profiles for the same entity, select them and click the profile icon in the bottom menu to combine them into one 1099 filing. This only affects 1099 Filing — the profiles remain separate elsewhere in Mercury. To permanently merge recipients, go to the Recipients page.
  • To unlink recipients in a combined filing, select the profile, click the profile icon in the bottom menu, then click the unlink icon next to the recipient you want to separate.
Granting permissions for 1099 Filing
  • Admins automatically get access to 1099 Filing.
  • When managing roles and permissions, assign the Accountant custom role or a Custom User role with the Accounting permission to let a team member manage and file 1099s for the company.
  • Custom Users with the Accounting permission will only see transactions from the bank accounts they have access to, so be sure to grant access to any accounts with 1099 reportable transactions.

Completing your filing summary tasklist

Your Filing Summary dashboard shows all 1099 recipients and a checklist of tasks needed to complete filing. Missing or invalid information will appear as a status in the table and as a task at the top of the page. Hover over any error to see what it means and how to resolve it. Nothing left to do? Kick back and relax until Filing season (Jan 1 - Feb 1).

Tip: How to edit filing details for a 1099 Recipient

  • Hover over a 1099 Recipient
  • Click “Edit Filing” on the right side of the row
  • Make any changes necessary for that year’s 1099 filing

Note: Mercury overrides filing details based on the latest uploaded W9 or manually edited data from the Edit Filing page.

Filing 1099s

Once January 1st comes around, you will be able to File for each of your 1099 Recipients.

  • Navigate to Payments > Taxes
  • If you haven’t enabled 1099 Filing yet, click Start Filing from the primary banner
  • If you already have recipients ready to file, click Start Filing from the tasks section

Once you file your 1099s, you can navigate back to the Taxes page and view the Federal and State Filing statuses as well as the Recipient Delivery status.

Pricing: Customers can download W9 and transaction data for free from the Recipients page. Advanced 1099 capabilities such as Filing unlimited 1099s with the IRS and States are available as part of our paid Mercury Plus and Mercury Pro plans (learn more about pricing here) or for a flat fee of $5 per 1099 Form for non-subscribers. We do not charge any additional fees for filing 1099 Corrections.

Delivering 1099s to recipients

Once you file your 1099s, Mercury will generate and deliver 1099 forms to each recipient. This typically takes up to 1 business day.

If you file before 1/29

  • For recipients without an email address on file, Mercury will print and mail their 1099s
  • For recipients with an email address on file, Mercury will email them that their 1099 is ready to download and ask for e-consent to view it online. If they decline consent or do not respond by 1/30, Mercury will print and mail their 1099 so it arrives before the February 1 deadline

If you file on 1/29 or later

  • For recipients without an email address on file, Mercury will print and mail their 1099s
  • For recipients with an email address on file, Mercury will print and mail their 1099s and also email them that their 1099 is ready to download and ask for e-consent to view it online
Submitting a 1099 correction

You can void or file a 1099 Correction at no additional cost. To do this, follow these steps:

  • Navigate to Payments > Taxes
  • Void a Filing
    • Navigate to the Recipient you want to void and click Void Filing
    • Make the necessary changes by selecting which form to void and click Void
    • Your forms are now voided. If you wish to file for this recipient in the future, you can do so by filing a Correction
  • Correct a Filing
    • Navigate to the Recipient you want to correct and click Correct Filing
    • Make the necessary changes and click Submit Correction
    • Once you file your Correction, you can navigate back to the Taxes page and view the Federal and State Filing statuses as well as the Recipient Delivery status for the correction

Note: You will only see the option to Correct Filing after the original 1099 has been submitted and marked as “Accepted” by the IRS. This can take up to 4 business days.

FAQs

Refer to 1099 Filing FAQs found here.

For specific guidance on your tax filing obligations, please consult with a qualified tax professional. Mercury does not provide tax advice. Tax regulations can be complex and vary based on individual circumstances, so it’s important to seek personalized advice from an expert who can assess your unique situation.

How should I handle duplicate 1099s?

Each unique TIN (taxpayer identification number) should correspond to a single 1099-NEC and/or 1099-MISC.

If you notice there are duplicate profiles for the same entity that share matching information, such as names, bank account details (routing and account numbers), emails, or addresses, you can select and then combine these profiles by clicking on the icon (👥) in the action menu.

Which 1099 should I select?

1099-NEC (Most common)

Non-employee compensation: Used for paying freelancers, contractors and others for services.

1099-MISC (Less common)

Rent: Report business rent paid to a non-corporate entity, such as an individual.

Royalties: Payments $10 or more for the use of intellectual property.

Other Income: Prizes, legal settlements, income from hobbies, bonus payments and more.

Not common

Fishing Boat Proceeds: Share of income paid to crew members from a commercial fishing boat.

Medical and Health Care Payments: Payments of $2,000 or more to doctors, hospitals, or medical providers.

Substitute Payments in Lieu of Dividends or Interest: Payments made when a broker covers dividends or interest owed to an investor.

Crop Insurance Proceeds: Insurance payouts of $2,000 or more to farmers for crop losses.

Gross Proceeds Paid to an Attorney: Total payments to an attorney, even if not for legal services.

Fish Purchased for Resale: Payments to anyone who catches and sells fish to resell in business.

Section 409A Deferrals: Deferred income reported under IRS Section 409A rules.

Non-qualified Deferred Compensation: Payments from a non-qualified deferred compensation plan.

Who should receive a 1099?

1099 Eligible

Recipients you paid at least $2,000 for services or $10 in royalties during the tax year who are based in the U.S. and are not your W2 employee.

Exceptions

  • C Corps or S Corps
    • Unless they are law firms & legal providers
  • Payments made via credit cards or third-party payment processors (ex. PayPal, Stripe)
  • Payments made for expense reimbursements

Business: Accounting

Applying transaction categories

Categories are optional labels that can be used to group transactions to provide you better insights, set up accounting workflows, and more. Mercury suggests a list of categories for every business, which you can edit, add to, or use as is. You can choose where and how you surface them to employees to streamline accounting.

Key workflows for categories

  • We suggest a list of categories for every business. You can edit that list by creating new categories for company-specific programs (like “Travel for conference” or “Health and wellness stipend” or “Hosting Fees”) or delete ones that aren’t relevant to your company.
  • Edit the transaction types eligible for categories so you and your team can select them when submitting reimbursements, categorizing card transactions, or categorizing other money in or money out
  • Automate with accounting. Streamline your end of month close by mapping categories to your GL codes.

Creating categories

  • Click on your company name in the left-hand corner of your dashboard and click Settings
  • Select Categories from the left hand side bar
  • Click on Create Category
    • If you’ve created tags, you’ll be able to copy these over as new categories
  • Enter the name of the category and choose where employees will see them: for reimbursements, card spend, or other transactions (eg. ACH payments, Wires etc)
  • Hit Save in order to save your new category and you’re all set

Managing categories

Editing

Edited category names will update across all previously categorized transactions. To edit category names:

  • Navigate to Categories
  • Click on the pencil icon for the existing category you’d like to edit
  • Make the necessary edits and select Save
Deleting

Deleted categories won’t be available for future transactions, but will remain assigned to historical transactions. To delete a category:

  • Navigate to Categories
  • Click on the trash icon for the category you’d like to delete
  • Select Yes, Delete and you’re all set

Applying categories

When submitting reimbursements
  • Navigate to Reimbursements
  • Click on “Submit Expense”
  • Select the category from the Expense Category dropdown
  • Fill out the rest of the details
  • Click Review
  • Select Submit
On the transactions page for all transactions
  • Navigate to Transactions
  • Click the transaction to categorize
  • Select the category from the Category dropdown
  • Fill out the other details as needed
  • Exit the transaction and you’re all set
On the accounting page
  • Navigate to Accounting
  • Go to the Category column and select the category from the dropdown
  • Fill out the other details as needed and you’re all set

Creating accounting rules for categories

Categories can be mapped to GL codes for accounting purposes.

GL codes are standardized codes used in accounting systems to classify and record every financial transaction. They correspond directly to your company’s Chart of Accounts and are essential for generating accurate financial statements like the balance sheet or income statement. For accounting and tax filings purposes, every single transaction must have a GL code.

If one of your categories is always mapped to a specific GL code, you can create a rule to do that automatically to every future transaction. With categorization rules in place, GL codes will be automatically applied to each transaction once a category is set, which you can review on the Accounting page before syncing transactions to your accounting tool.

  • Navigate to Accounting
  • Click on the gear near the upper right corner to open your accounting settings
  • Click Create a Rule to get started

FAQs

How does this work with transaction tags?

Tags were launched as a beta feature in October of 2024, and categories were built to address some of the feedback we gathered from tags users. If you currently use tags, we’ll give you the option to copy those over as new categories. For historical transactions, we’ve preserved existing tags. Tags will still be searchable, so you’ll still be able to filter transactions by tags and reference tags in transaction exports as needed.

Are categories available on the mobile app?

Yes. While you can’t create or manage categories via mobile app, you can apply any that were previously created in the web app to your transactions and reimbursements.

Categorizing your transactions with GL codes

The Accounting page allows Admin and Bookkeeper users to to review, categorize, and sync expense records directly to Xero, QuickBooks Online, or NetSuite. If you aren’t connected to one of these accounting softwares, you may also export transactions (including categories) in CSV form to be uploaded to accounting software of your choice.

Speed up categorization

Automated categorization

Customers with enriched categorization enabled will see accounting GL code columns pre-filled with a category suggested by Mercury — it will be indicated with a sparkle icon. This suggested GL code is a prediction based on your previous categorization behavior and will improve over time, as you interact with the feature.

You can always override the suggested GL code by clicking on the dropdown and selecting a new input. To accept the suggestion, simply select transaction(s) to “Mark as Ready” and then sync to your accounting tool.

Categorization rules

You can also manually create categorization rules that consistently apply a specified GL code based on the information Mercury has about the transaction. You will be prompted to set up these rules when you first integrate your accounting software with Mercury. You can also update or edit these rules at any time by navigating to the Accounting page and selecting the gear icon in the top right to access your categorization rules.

Categorization rules can be created for the following attributes, listing in order of priority:

  • Category - automate based on the custom categories you apply to transactions yourself
  • Counterparty (merchant, customers or recipients) - automate based on who you are paying, or awaiting payment from
  • Team member - automate transactions from a specific employee
  • Card - automate based on the specific debit or credit card used for the transaction
  • Merchant type - the vendor type that detect automatically

Note: Categorization rules based on merchants will only be applied to card transactions

Categorization rules are applied hierarchically based on how precise the attribute is, with custom “Category” rules taking precedence over “Merchant” rules, which take precedence over team member, etc. - going top to bottom in hierarchy from the list above.

All categorization rules apply to future transactions versus historic ones.

Exclude from review

There might be some transactions that you prefer to categorize outside of Mercury and not see on the Accounting page. To help reduce clutter, we have the “Exclude from Review” action, which you can use in the below ways:

  • On the Accounting page, select either an individual or multiple transactions and apply the “exclude from review” action.
  • Under categorization rules, choose “exclude from review” as the output of a rule instead of a GL code. When a transaction with the specified parameters comes in, it will be excluded from the default Accounting page view.

Transactions that are excluded from review will be visible in your accounting software, but not in the “needs review” and “sync” flow on Mercury.

To see all excluded transactions, navigate to Add Filter > Status > Excluded from review. To bring a transaction(s) back to your “Needs review” filter, select the applicable transaction(s) from this view, and click on “Include in review” under the actions menu.

Adding or editing categories as a non-admin or bookkeeper

If you are an Employee or Custom user in Mercury, you may not have access to the Accounting page. However, you will be able to edit the categories for transactions you’ve made directly in the Transactions page.

To do so, select a transaction to view the category (if any) automatically assigned. If the transaction requires categorization you can edit or add one via the Transactions Details panel that appears on the right side of the page when selecting transactions.

FAQ

What does it cost to sync transaction details on the Accounting page to my accounting software?

QuickBooks and Xero enriched automations, as well as the ability to import bank feed connections across QuickBooks, Xero, and NetSuite, are free. If you want to use our enriched NetSuite accounting integrations and automations to sync your card transactions to NetSuite, you’ll want to upgrade to a paid plan. Other IO card features are still free to use.

Learn more about pricing here.

What type of transactions can be mapped, categorized, and synced from the Accounting page?

The accounting page surfaces all incoming and outgoing transactions, with the exception of Treasury transactions and internal transfers.

If I create a categorization rule, will it impact past transactions?

Not necessarily. Categorization rules will generally only impact transactions that come through after the rule has been created. However, manually updating the Mercury Category on a past transaction will trigger the mapping engine to run and update the GL code if applicable.

How can I tell if a categorization rule has been applied to a transaction?

When a categorization rule has been applied you will see a sparkles icon next to the GL code.

How does automated categorization interact with categorization rules?

Both tools work hand in hand to automate and speed up your categorization. When a transaction comes in, if its attributes are eligible for a categorization rule, then the GL code output will come from that categorization rule. If not, then we will proceed with our model predictions and suggest a category based on similar transactions. If you do not have any categorization rules set up, then we will run all your transactions through our predictive model.

What happens when I nudge a cardholder?

When you nudge a cardholder via the action column, the cardholder will receive an email reminding them to update the transaction with any required information that is missing, specifically a receipt and/or Mercury Category.

How to categorize transactions in your Mercury business account

When you review your transaction activity in Mercury, you have the option to categorize them. Categorization helps you organize your financial data so it’s easier to interpret trends, prepare reports, and collaborate with your accounting tools or bookkeeping partners.

On Mercury, categorizing a transaction means labeling it with one or both of the following:

  • A category: labels used within Mercury, such as “Software,” “Travel,” or “Revenue”
  • A GL code: labels that come directly from your accounting system, such as “6100 · Office Expenses” or “4000 · Services Revenue”

This article explains what each option means, how they differ, and when to use them.

Categories

GL codes

Summary

Optional labels that can be used to group transactions to provide you better insights.

Required standardized codes used in accounting systems to classify and record every financial transaction.

Why use them

To get high level company insights.

For financial reporting and tax-readiness.

Who uses them

Founders, admins - and anyone looking to understand the general trends in the company’s money movement.

You can also ask employees to categorize their own transactions.

Finance team, accountants - and anyone looking to create accurate financial statements and get you tax ready.

Where to configure

Mercury gives you a set of suggested categories to start. You can edit them as needed:

Edit in Settings > Categories

Create and edit entirely in your accounting software. Mercury pulls these in automatically.

About categories

Categories are optional labels that can be used to group transactions to provide you better insights. When you apply categories to transactions, you can easily filter them to see how much your company spent on Travel or on Software, for example.

Mercury suggests a list of categories for every business, which you can edit, add to, or use as is. You can also determine where and how you surface them to employees.

Creating categories
On the Transactions page:
  • Navigate to Transactions
  • Open the drop down on any transaction
  • Click Add category
  • Enter the name of the category and choose where employees will see them: for reimbursements, card spend, or other transactions (eg. ACH payments, Wires etc)
  • Hit Save
In Settings:

  • Select Categories from the left hand side bar
  • Click on Create Category
  • Enter the name of the category and choose where employees will see them: for reimbursements, card spend, or other transactions (eg. ACH payments, Wires etc)
  • Hit Save
Editing categories
  • Navigate to Categories
  • Click on the pencil icon for the existing category you’d like to edit
  • Make the necessary edits and select Save

Edited category names will update across all previously categorized transactions

Deleting categories
  • Navigate to Categories
  • Click on the trash icon for the category you’d like to delete
  • Select Yes, Delete and you’re all set

Deleted categories won’t be available for future transactions, but will remain assigned to historical transactions.

Applying categories to transactions
Automated categorization

We use AI to automatically suggest categories for your transactions - they will be indicated with a sparkle icon. You can always override the suggested category by clicking on the dropdown and selecting a new input. Our system will learn from your interactions and improve the quality of our recommendations.

We will automate categorization for as many transactions as we can, based on historical precedent.

Categorization rules

You can create rules that consistently apply a specified category based on the information Mercury has about the transaction.

Rules can be edited at any time by navigating to the Accounting page and selecting the gear icon in the top right to access your categorization rules.

Categorization rules can be created for the following attributes:

  • Counterparty (merchant, customers or recipients) — who you are paying, or awaiting payment from
  • Team member — transactions from a specific employee
  • Card — the specific debit or credit card used for the transaction
  • Merchant type — the vendor type that we detect automatically for card transactions
  • Amount — less than, more than, or equal to a value
  • Description — a specific keyword or phrase in the description
  • Budgets — spend associated with a specific budget
  • Departments — a specific functional department set up in Mercury or via your HRIS. These are your team departments, not the departments or locations from your accounting software.

You can set multi-condition rules by clicking on the plus icon when creating a rule. All categorization rules apply to future transactions versus historic ones.

Note: by default, all transactions categorized via a mapping rule will be automatically marked as ready. To turn this setting off for individual rules:

  • Go to the Accounting settings page
  • Click into the rule you would like to edit
  • Toggle the auto-mark ready setting off for that rule

  • Click the transaction to categorize
  • Select the category from the Category dropdown
  • Fill out the other details as needed
  • Exit the transaction
When submitting reimbursements

  • Click on Submit Expense
  • Select the category from the Expense Category dropdown
  • Fill out the rest of the details
  • Click Review
  • Select Submit
On the accounting page
  • Navigate to Accounting
  • Go to the Category column and select the category from the dropdown

About GL codes

GL codes are standardized codes used in accounting systems to classify and record every financial transaction. They correspond directly to your company’s Chart of Accounts and are essential for generating accurate financial statements like the balance sheet or income statement. For accounting and tax filings purposes, every single transaction must have a GL code.

When you integrate Mercury to QuickBooks, Xero, or NetSuite, we automatically pull in your GL codes.

Applying GL codes to transactions

The GL code column is automatically surfaced on your Accounting and Transactions page when you integrate Mercury to QuickBooks, Xero, or Netsuite.

GL codes can then be applied to transactions in different ways:

1 - Automated categorization

Customers with enriched categorization enabled will see accounting GL code columns pre-filled with a GL code suggested by Mercury - it will be indicated with a sparkle icon. This suggested GL code is a prediction based on your previous categorization behavior and will improve over time, as you interact with the feature.

You can always override the suggested GL code by clicking on the dropdown and selecting a new input. To accept the suggestion, simply select transaction(s) to “Mark as Ready” and then sync to your accounting tool.

You can also turn this feature off by navigating to Accounting > Settings and toggling Auto-categorization off. When AI categorization is off, only your manually created categorization rules will apply.

2 - Categorization rules

You can also create categorization rules that consistently apply a specified GL code based on the information Mercury has about the transaction. You will be prompted to set up these rules when you first integrate your accounting software with Mercury.

Rules can be edited at any time by navigating to the Accounting page and selecting the gear icon in the top right to access your categorization rules. Categorization rules can be created for the following attributes:

  • Counterparty (merchant, customers or recipients) — who you are paying, or awaiting payment from
  • Team member — transactions from a specific employee
  • Card — the specific debit or credit card used for the transaction
  • Merchant type — the vendor type that we detect automatically for card transactions
  • Amount — less than, more than, or equal to a value
  • Description — a specific keyword or phrase in the description
  • Budgets — spend associated with a specific budget
  • Departments — a specific functional department set up in Mercury or via your HRIS. These are your team departments, not the departments or locations from your accounting software.

You can set multi-condition rules by clicking on the plus icon when creating a rule.

Note: Categorization rules based on merchants will only be applied to card transactions

All categorization rules apply to future transactions versus historic ones.

3 - Manual categorization

Admin and Accountant users can manually apply GL codes to transactions on the Accounting page. Choose a category from the dropdown for a single transaction, or select multiple transactions (up to 100 per page) to apply categories in bulk using the action bar at the bottom of the screen. If you’ve connected NetSuite or QuickBooks Online, you can set departments or locations in bulk the same way

Applying multiple GL codes to transactions

If needed, you can apply multiple GL codes to a transaction. This can be done when you are creating a bill or sending money.

Excluding transactions from review

There might be some transactions that you prefer to categorize outside of Mercury and not see on the Accounting page. To help reduce clutter, we have the “Exclude from Review” action, which you can use in the below ways:

  • On the Accounting page, select either an individual or multiple transactions and apply the “exclude from review” action
  • Under categorization rules, choose “exclude from review” as the output of a rule instead of a GL code. When a transaction with the specified parameters comes in, it will be excluded from the default Accounting page view

Transactions that are excluded from review will be visible in your accounting software, but not in the “needs review” and “sync” flow on Mercury.

To see all excluded transactions, navigate to Add Filter > Status > Excluded from review. To bring a transaction(s) back to your “Needs review” filter, select the applicable transaction(s) from this view, and click on “Include in review” under the actions menu.

Syncing transactions to the accounting software

Admin and Accountant users will be able to sync the expense records directly to Xero, QuickBooks Online, or NetSuite from the Accounting page. If you aren’t connected to one of these accounting softwares, you may also export transactions (including categories) in CSV form to be uploaded to accounting software of your choice. You can learn more about syncing transactions here.

By default, Mercury syncs your Ready transactions to your connected accounting software daily. You can switch to weekly syncs, or turn off auto-sync for manual control, all from your Accounting Settings page.

A few things to know:

  • Any transaction in a Ready state at the time of the scheduled sync will be included.
  • When a transaction fails to sync due to a technical issue, such as a disruption in our integration, Mercury will automatically retry syncing these transactions at the next scheduled sync.
  • When a transaction fails to sync because of something in your accounting setup that needs your attention, like a missing or incorrect GL code, these transactions will be flagged for you to review and correct before they can sync successfully.
  • You can view the last sync timestamp and sync history from the Synced tab on the Accounting page.

Using categories in conjunction with GL codes

Categories can be mapped to GL codes for accounting purposes. If one of your categories is always mapped to a specific GL code, you can create a rule to do that automatically to every future transaction. With categorization rules in place, GL codes will be automatically applied to each transaction once a category is set, which you can review on the Accounting page before syncing transactions to your accounting tool.

  • Click on the gear near the upper right corner to open your accounting settings

Integrating with NetSuite

Our NetSuite integration allows you to sync transaction details and automatically create accounting records in NetSuite by assigning NetSuite GL (General Ledger) codes to transactions directly from your Mercury dashboard.

This integration only allows transaction information to be synced from Mercury to NetSuite. Any changes in NetSuite won’t sync back to Mercury.

Connecting to NetSuite

  • Go to Settings > Integrations
  • Locate the NetSuite integration. Click Connect
  • Follow the prompts to connect Mercury to your NetSuite account and map your Mercury accounts to NetSuite general ledger accounts
    • Once connected, NetSuite will show as Active on your Integrations page, where you can manage and check the status of the integration at any time
Syncing initial Mercury bank feed to NetSuite

Once the NetSuite connection is complete your Mercury bank data will import to NetSuite automatically based on the date range you selected. Transactions will be pushed from Mercury to NetSuite and synced to your Match Bank Data page within NetSuite once a day.

Please note - you may not see transactions right away as the initial sync may take several minutes depending on the volume of transactions being synced. If you don’t see your transactions come through by the end of the day, please reach out to us.

Assigning NetSuite GL codes to Mercury payments

Mercury Pro customers who use NetSuite can categorize their transactions and payments before they are reconciled in NetSuite. Once you connect to NetSuite, Mercury will automatically pull in your NetSuite GL codes so you can add them to transactions.

Whenever possible, Mercury will use AI and your categorization history to pre-fill GL codes for your transactions - these suggestions will be indicated with a sparkle icon. You can always override them by clicking on the dropdown and selecting a new input. The suggestions will improve over time, the more you interact with the feature. You can turn this feature off by navigating to Accounting > Settings and toggling Auto-categorization off.

You also manually apply GL codes to transactions in a few different places:

  • On your Accounting page, select individual or multiple transactions and pick a GL code from the dropdown
  • On your Transactions page, click open a Transaction to view the details and select from the GL code dropdown
  • If you’re creating a new payment manually or by uploading an invoice, select from the GL code dropdown as you’re setting up the payment details
  • If you want to add a category to an upcoming payment that was already scheduled, you can view the payment details on your Payments page and select from the GL code dropdown there

See our guide on categorizing your transactions from the Accounting page for more information.

Syncing transactions to NetSuite

Manual sync
  • On the Accounting page, review your transactions and ensure all required fields (e.g. GL code, counterparty, and department, if your NetSuite account requires one) are filled in
  • Select individual or multiple transactions and click Mark as Ready
  • Click the Sync button to push ready transactions to NetSuite

This syncs any additional transaction attributes (GL codes, classes, departments, counterparty, attachments, and/or notes) you’ve added in Mercury to your accounting software, matching them to the original transaction record there.

Once the sync is complete, you’ll see a confirmation message, or any relevant errors.

Auto-sync

By default, Mercury will automatically sync your Ready transactions to NetSuite on a daily schedule. If you prefer to sync transactions manually, you can turn auto-sync off on the Accounting Settings page:,

  • Navigate to Accounting > Settings
  • Toggle auto-sync off

Any transaction in a Ready state at the scheduled run time will be included. If a sync fails, the affected transactions will remain in a failed state — auto-sync won’t retry automatically. You can re-sync them manually from the Accounting page, and view sync history and the last successful sync timestamp in the Synced tab.

Frequently asked questions

What does it cost to use Mercury’s NetSuite integration?

The ability to import bank feed connections is free. You can upgrade to a paid plan to use our enriched NetSuite accounting integration to categorize transactions and create accounting records in NetSuite directly from your Mercury dashboard.

Learn more about pricing here.

Will I have to go through all the setup steps again if the connection breaks?

No. Most of these steps are only required for the initial setup. If the connection breaks, you can try to reconnect from your Integrations settings, but make sure not to delete your connection.

Can I choose which Mercury accounts I want to sync with NetSuite bank feed?

No, currently all available Mercury accounts will sync.

What types of transactions can I assign GL codes to from my Transactions page?

You can add GL codes to incoming and outgoing wires, ACH transfers, checks, and card transactions. The only transaction types currently excluded are transfers and IO payments.

Why can’t I categorize transfers and IO payments?

They don’t create a record in NetSuite. They show up in your NetSuite bank feed, where you can match them.

If I create a recurring payment, will the same GL code be assigned automatically to all future payments?

Yes, the GL code you assign to the first payment will be automatically assigned to all future payments in the series.

If I make changes in NetSuite to a transaction, will those be reflected in my Mercury account?

No, the connection is a one-way sync. Transaction information is passed from Mercury to NetSuite, and any changes in NetSuite won’t pass back to Mercury.

What happens if NetSuite requires a department?

If your NetSuite account requires a department on every transaction, Mercury won’t sync a transaction without one. You’ll see a sync error so you can add the department and sync again.

Integrating with QuickBooks Online

Our QuickBooks Online integration allows you to sync transaction details and automatically create accounting records in QuickBooks by assigning GL (General Ledger) codes to transactions directly from your Mercury dashboard.

Connecting to QuickBooks

  • Click your company name in the top left-hand corner of the dashboard
  • Go to Settings > Integrations
  • Hover over QuickBooks and click Connect
  • Follow the instructions to connect Mercury to your QuickBooks bank feed
  • Optional: Set up Enrichment to enable the auto-categorization of your transactions and the syncing additional transaction fields - such as GL codes, classes, locations, receipts, and vendor information.
  • Follow the prompts to connect to QuickBooks and map your Mercury accounts to QuickBooks general ledger accounts to ensure proper syncing
  • Click Complete

Note: Enriching your QuickBooks integration is only available for QuickBooks SimpleStart and higher plans. The QuickBooks Solopreneur plan is not supported at this time.

After connecting
  • Once connected, QuickBooks will show as “Active” on your Integrations page, where you can manage and check the status of the connection at any time
  • If you don’t see the option to add GL codes or an account is missing:
    • Ensure your QuickBooks bank feed is connected
    • Set up Enrichment to:
      • Let Mercury automatically categorize your transactions
      • Sync accounting records with QuickBooks
      • Enrich your QuickBooks sync with GL codes, classes, locations, attachments, notes, and more
Disconnecting from QuickBooks

To disconnect your QuickBooks integration, you’ll need to remove the connection in both Mercury and QuickBooks.

  • Go to Settings > Integrations in Mercury on web
  • Click Disconnect next to QuickBooks
  • Open QuickBooks and confirm the bank feed is also disconnected via Bank Transactions > Link Account > Manage Connections

Applying QuickBooks GL codes

Once you connect to QuickBooks and set up enrichment, Mercury will automatically pull in your QuickBooks GL codes so your transactions can be categorized and synced to the associated accounting records in QuickBooks.

Whenever possible, Mercury will use AI and your categorization history to pre-fill GL codes for your transactions - these suggestions will be indicated with a sparkle icon. You can always overwrite them by clicking on the dropdown and selecting a new input. The suggested GL codes will improve over time, the more you interact with the feature. You can turn this feature off by navigating to Accounting > Settings and toggling Auto-categorization off.

You can also manually apply GL codes to transactions in a few different places:

  • On your Accounting page, select individual or multiple transactions and pick a GL code from the dropdown
  • On your Transactions page, click open a Transaction to view the details and select from the GL code dropdown
  • If you’re creating a new payment manually or by uploading an invoice, you’ll have the option to select GL codes
  • If you want to add a category to an upcoming payment that was already scheduled, you can view the payment details on your Payments page and select from the GL code dropdown there

Syncing transactions to QuickBooks

Manual sync
  • On the Accounting page, review your transactions and ensure all required fields (e.g. GL code, counterparty) are filled in
  • Select individual or multiple transactions and click Mark as Ready
  • Click the Sync button to push ready transactions to QuickBooks

This syncs any additional transaction attributes (GL codes, classes, locations, counterparty, attachments, and/or notes) you’ve added in Mercury to your accounting software, matching them to the original transaction record there.

Once the sync is complete, you’ll see a confirmation message, or any relevant errors.

Auto-sync

By default, Mercury will automatically sync your Ready transactions to QuickBooks on a daily schedule. If you prefer to sync transactions manually, you can turn auto-sync off on the Accounting Settings page.

Any transaction in a Ready state at the scheduled run time will be included. If a sync fails, the affected transactions will remain in a failed state — auto-sync won’t retry automatically. You can re-sync them manually from the Accounting page, and view sync history and the last successful sync timestamp in the Synced tab of the Accounting page.

Once the sync is complete, you will see a confirmation message, or relevant errors that might come up.

FAQs

Is the integration with QuickBooks free to use?

Yes. Our QuickBooks integration is free to use. Learn more about pricing.

Some features, such a multi-GL code categorization, require Mercury Plus or Mercury Pro.

Why did my bank feed connection stop working, and how do I fix it?

You’ll need to reset the connection on both sides — in Mercury and in QuickBooks. Here’s how:

  • Disconnect the bank feed in Mercury via Integrations
  • In QuickBooks, go to Bank Transactions→ click the Link Account dropdown → select Manage Connections
  • Find all Mercury connections and un-toggle each account listed under them
    • This step is key to ensuring a healthy reconnection
  • Re-establish the bank feed connection from Mercury using the steps listed here
What types of transactions can have GL codes applied to them?

You can categorize incoming and outgoing wires, ACH transfers, and checks. The only transaction types currently excluded are internal transfers and IO payments.

Why can’t I categorize transfers and IO payments?

Transfers and IO payments are categorized automatically by our system and/or QuickBooks.

Can I turn off enriched categorization for my QuickBooks integration?

No — you can’t turn off enriched categorization after your integration is set up.

If you’d prefer not to use it, you have two options:

  • Ignore enriched categorization:
  • You can leave categorization fields in Mercury untouched and manage everything directly in QuickBooks. Your transactions will still sync via the bank feed. Additional data (like categories or notes) is only sent if you take action in Mercury, though some transactions (like internal transfers) may still be automatically categorized and synced.
  • Reconnect with bank feed only:
  • You can disconnect and reconnect your QuickBooks integration, and during setup choose to connect only the bank feed (skipping enriched categorization).

Enriched categorization is optional, but allows you to add categories, notes, and attachments in Mercury and sync that information to QuickBooks alongside your transactions.

Do you support Treasury transactions in the bank feed?

Yes. For QuickBooks, navigate to Transactions > Bank transactions, then click “Link account” button (not the arrow next to it) and go through the steps to authenticate. Locate your Treasury account from the list, map it to a QuickBooks GL, and click Connect.

Some important things to note:

  • After clicking “Link account,” you may be able to select a saved Mercury connection or create a new one: we suggest creating a new one. You can locate “Mercury” under “Recommended” at the bottom of the page, or search for “Mercury” in the search bar.
  • If you had a Mercury Treasury account linked to QuickBooks before April 2025, we recommend the below steps to reduce transaction duplication:
    • Map your account to the same GL code you used for Treasury before
    • In the “Link account” flow, select a start date (at the bottom of the page) that is after the last Treasury transactions register date in QuickBooks
If I create a recurring payment, will the same GL code be assigned automatically to all future payments?

Yes, the GL code you assign to the first payment will be automatically assigned to all future payments in the series.

If I make changes in QuickBooks to a transaction, will those changes be reflected in my Mercury account?

No, the connection is a one-way sync. Transaction information is passed from Mercury to QuickBooks, and any changes in QuickBooks won’t pass back to Mercury.

What QuickBooks plans does this integration work with?

Categorizing and syncing payments is only available for the QuickBooks Online Essentials tier or higher. We also don’t currently support QuickBooks Desktop. Learn more about QuickBooks plan options.

Can I turn off AI categorization for my QuickBooks integration?

Yes. You can enable or disable Mercury’s AI categorization from Accounting > Settings. When turned off, only your manually created categorization rules will apply.

Frequently asked questions

Is the integration with Xero free to use?

What types of transactions can have GL codes applied to them?

Mercury users can categorize incoming and outgoing wires, ACH transfers, and checks. The only transaction types currently excluded are transfers and IO payments.

Why can’t I categorize transfers or IO payments?

Transfers and IO payments are categorized automatically by our system and/or Xero.

If I create a recurring payment in Mercury, will the GL code apply to all future transactions?

Yes, the GL code you assign to the first payment will be automatically assigned to all future payments in the series.

If I make changes in Xero to a transaction, will those be reflected in my Mercury account?

I lost connection to my Xero account. What should I do?

As part of a recent upgrade to the Mercury–Xero integration, accounts that did not complete the migration were disconnected on February 18. You’ll need to reconnect from your Integrations page.

What to expect after reconnecting:

  • Transaction categorization: Previously categorized transactions in Mercury will remain in Mercury only and will not sync to Xero. After you reconnect, only transactions categorized going forward will sync to Xero. If previously categorized transactions appear in your “Needs review” view, you can use the “Exclude from review” action to hide them.
  • Mercury Credit Card users:
    • Reconcile all outstanding items under “Credit” in Xero and archive that bank account, as your credit transactions will no longer feed there after the migration.
    • Your credit transactions will now feed into the “Mercury Credit” account in Xero (usually at the bottom of your account list and described as #MERC). This is the recommended approach by Xero.

Managing accounting integrations

Mercury lets you integrate with popular accounting softwares so your transactions sync seamlessly. This article explains which integrations are available, how syncing works, and how to review and manage transactions from the Accounting page.

Available accounting integrations

You can connect Mercury to the following accounting platforms:

  • QuickBooks Online
  • Xero
  • NetSuite

Each integration has its own setup steps and limitations. For details, visit the dedicated support article for the software you’re using.

If you don’t have an accounting integration connected, you can still export transactions (including categories) as a CSV file and upload them to your accounting software manually. Click the download icon on your Accounting page to get started.

Syncing basic transaction data

When you connect Mercury to QuickBooks Online, Xero, or NetSuite, Mercury sends a bank feed with baseline transaction details including:

  • Amount
  • Description
  • Transaction date

The bank feed syncs automatically multiple times a day.

Enriching transaction data

You can optionally add additional details to transactions in Mercury before syncing them to the accounting software, including:

  • GL codes
  • Classes (if applicable)
  • Departments or locations, (if applicable)
  • Counterparty (like vendor or customer, if applicable)
  • Receipts and attachments
  • Notes

Note: You can add these details from either the Transactions or Accounting page, but they won’t sync to your accounting software unless you sync them from the Accounting page.

Syncing enriched transaction data from the Accounting page

The Accounting page lets Admin and Accountant users review, categorize, and sync transactions to your connected accounting software.

Get started by clicking on Accounting from the left-hand side of your dashboard.

Review and prepare transactions

Transactions are grouped based on what needs to be done before syncing:

  • Review tab:
    • Ready to approve: review transactions that are already coded, then mark them as ready to sync.
    • Needs categorization review: check Mercury’s suggested coding and make any necessary changes.
    • Missing accounting details: see which transactions are missing accounting coding.
    • Missing receipt or note: see which transactions are missing required spend documentation.
  • Ready to sync tab: transactions that have been marked as ready will sync on the cadence you set.
  • Synced tab: transactions that have been successfully synced to your accounting software.

Tip: To turn off grouped views, click the list icon next to the integration status.

Note: When you sync enriched transaction data, Mercury does not create a duplicate transaction. The existing bank feed entry in your accounting software is updated with the new details; your accounting software will prompt you to match the updated transactions, as needed.

Resolve sync errors

If a transaction fails to sync, it will appear in the Sync errors tab. You can click into a transaction to view the specific error message.

Once the issue is resolved, you can mark the transaction as ready and sync again.

FAQs

How do I switch to a different accounting platform?

To switch accounting platforms, disconnect your current integration in Mercury and then connect the new one. GL code assignments don’t carry over when you switch. If you want a record of how your transactions were categorized, export a CSV of your transactions before you disconnect.

Mercury is a fintech company, not an FDIC-insured bank. Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Members FDIC.

Using classes, departments, and locations in Mercury

Classes, departments, and locations let you track your spending and revenue according to the parts of your business they belong to, such as a project, team, or office. They come from your accounting software, you apply them to transactions in Mercury, and they sync back to the accounting software.

Which fields you’ll see

The fields available in Mercury depend on your accounting software:

  • Classes: QuickBooks Online and NetSuite
  • Departments: NetSuite
  • Locations*: QuickBooks Online

*In QuickBooks, the Location label can be used to mean Business, Department, Division, Location, Property, Store or Territory. In Mercury’s Accounting page and relevant assets, we represent these in the “QuickBooks Location” field, regardless of which Location label is selected in QuickBooks.

Who can use them

Classes, departments, and locations are available to organizations with an enriched QuickBooks Online or NetSuite integration. Only users with Accounting permissions can see them.

Note: Xero tracking categories aren’t supported yet. QuickBooks Simple Start doesn’t support classes, and QuickBooks location tracking is only available on certain plans.

Getting fields from your accounting software

Once your enriched integration is set up, Mercury imports your classes, departments, and locations automatically, and refreshes them on the same schedule as your GL codes.

To add or rename one, make the change in your accounting software. It will show up in Mercury after the next refresh. If you don’t see a field in Mercury, check that it’s turned on in your accounting software.

Categorizing transactions

On the Accounting page, each field has its own column. You can:

  • Choose a value in the column for any transaction
  • Open a transaction and set it in the details panel
  • Select multiple transactions to set the same value for all of them at once

If you don’t use a field, you can hide its column from the Accounting page controls.

You can also add a class when you send money, pay a bill, or submit a reimbursement. Departments and locations can only be added from the Accounting page for now.

Syncing to your accounting software

When you sync a transaction, Mercury sends its class, department, or location along with the GL code, and fills in the matching field on the record in your accounting software. Once a transaction is synced, these fields can’t be edited in Mercury.

If your NetSuite account requires a department on every transaction, Mercury won’t sync a transaction without one. You’ll see a sync error so you can add the department and sync again.

Supported transaction types

You can tag all incoming and outgoing transactions except internal transfers and IO payoffs.

FAQs

Can I create classes, departments, or locations in Mercury?

No. You create and manage them in your accounting software, and Mercury pulls in the latest list.

How are these different from HR departments?

Departments under Settings > Departments organize your team in Mercury, for things like approvals and spend tracking. They’re separate from the departments in your accounting software, and the two aren’t linked.

Can I tag a line item with a class, or only the whole transaction?

You can assign classes to a transaction on the Accounting page, and to individual line items when you send money or pay a bill. In both cases, the class shows up on the line item when it syncs to your accounting software.

Can categorization rules set a department or location?

Yes, categorization rules can assign a department to future transactions. Learn more about setting up categorization rules.

Locations can be assigned on the Accounting page, either to individual transactions or in bulk.

Business: Capital

Create a SAFE and manage investor funds in Mercury

You can create, sign, and distribute a SAFE investment document right from your Mercury account. We help connect and track each investment back to each SAFE, and provide a dashboard for you to stay up-to-date on the progress in real time.

What is a SAFE?

A SAFE (Simple Agreement for Future Equity) is an agreement between an investor and a company that provides rights to the investor for future equity in the company similar to a warrant, except without determining a specific price per share at the time of initial investment. It was created in 2013 by Carolynn Levy as an alternative to traditional convertible notes.

You can read more about SAFEs, the different types and much more here.

Who are SAFEs for?

SAFEs are ideal for startups and early-stage companies looking for early fundraising from investors, allowing them to invest money in a company in exchange for equity in the company at a later date.

Right now, only companies formed and incorporated in the U.S and structured as C-corps can create SAFEs via Mercury. This mostly comes down to C-corps having the tax treatment and equity structures appropriate for SAFEs. Since SAFEs are designed to convert into equity during a future financing round, they align well with the growth trajectory and financing needs of C-corps.

Why SAFEs through Mercury?

  • Mercury’s SAFEs are loaded with features like e-signature and direct investment tracking within the SAFE dashboard.
  • The SAFE agreement is generated within the Mercury platform, making collaboration and signing with investors easy.
  • SAFEs are sent via payment links. We’ll generate a “routing” account with separate details to protect your actual account information. Once funds are received, we’ll automatically transfer them to your designated account.
    • SAFEs can be paid via ACH, domestic or international wire using the payment details sent to the recipient
  • Mercury takes care of tracking payments associated with specific SAFEs, ensuring efficient and transparent management of funding rounds.
  • You can access a comprehensive SAFE dashboard, allowing you to review and manage all past and present SAFEs to see who’s signed, who’s sent payment, and what’s been deposited into your Mercury account.

Getting started

Once you and an investor reach an agreement on terms, you can generate a SAFE agreement within the Mercury platform. The SAFEs tab won’t appear on your account unless your organization is a US C-Corp.

As long as you’re an admin on the account, you can get started by following these steps:

  • Click on Accounts found on the left-hand side of your dashboard and select Financing
  • Open the SAFEs tab to Start Now
  • Fill out the terms based on discussions with your investor
  • Confirm your company details (you can edit these if needed within your Settings)
  • Input your investor’s details (type of investor, name, address, etc.)
  • Review the details of your SAFE agreement, input emails of anyone you’d like cc’d, and click Send We’ll email your investor details of the SAFE, payment details and a link to sign
  • You’ll be notified via email once the SAFE has been signed and funds have been deposited. You can always check on the status of your SAFE through the Finance page

You can check on the status of SAFE agreements from this dashboard and take actions like manually marking the SAFE as paid or canceling it if needed.

How much does it cost?

SAFEs by Mercury are free to all Mercury customers.

Glossary of Terms

  • Valuation Cap - This value effectively “caps” the valuation at which the SAFE converts to equity.
  • Pre-Money or Post-Money Valuation - The value of a pre-money SAFE is dependent on the valuation at the next priced round, whereas a post-money SAFE effectively locks in the percentage the investor will own when the SAFE is converted to shares. Pre-money SAFEs are typically considered more founder-friendly, but many investors require post-money SAFEs.
  • Discounts - SAFEs convert to shares during the next priced round, when a valuation is set. If a discount was included in the SAFE terms, the shares are converted at 100% — discount % of the valuation.
  • Pro-Rata Rights - Included as a side letter, this establishes a right for the investors to invest in the next fundraising round.
  • Most Favored Nation - This provision guarantees that the terms of the SAFE are equal or better than the terms other investors are receiving. This clause is typically seen as investor-friendly.

We know you’re busy building something great; we’ve provided this SAFE feature to simplify the process of raising funds. The documents provided are based on industry standards. Before using these forms, review the terms to ensure they fit your needs and consult a lawyer if needed.

Mercury Technologies Inc. (“Mercury” and/or “Platform”) operates solely as a platform allowing issuers seeking financing through private placements using a SAFE to easily create a template legal document. The Platform is not a registered broker-dealer or investment advisor, and does not offer investment advice or participate itself in the sale of securities. SAFEs by Mercury is not a securities product or investment advice and is not offered by Mercury Investment Services LLC or Mercury Advisory LLC.

Mercury Working Capital FAQs

Mercury Working Capital* is a short-term business loan that provides upfront funding to help cover expenses and support growth. Learn how it works, who’s eligible, and what to expect when applying, receiving funds, and making repayments.

Is Mercury Working Capital a line of credit?

No. Mercury Working Capital* is a term loan, not a revolving line of credit. You receive a lump sum upfront and repay it in fixed weekly payments over a set term, typically 4 to 11 months. Repaying doesn’t free up credit to borrow again. If you want more funding later, we’ll consider a new offer once you’ve repaid at least 50% of your loan and your account is in good standing.

When should my company opt for a working capital loan?

A working capital loan is a great option for businesses that need short-term financing to bridge the gap between outgoing expenses and incoming revenue. These loans are especially useful when gearing up for a busy season (like the holidays) or during a slow period. The funds can help cover expenses such as payroll, rent, inventory, advertising, and other short-term liabilities that might be hard to cover when cash flow fluctuates.

What types of businesses can apply?

Mercury Working Capital* is available to businesses across a wide range of industries, including businesses that:

  • Sell physical products online (through their own store, drop-shipping, or an online marketplace)
  • Sell products through retail or wholesale channels
  • Sell software subscriptions or digital products (e.g., SaaS)
  • Provide services to other businesses (e.g., professional services)
  • Provide services to individual customers
  • Operate as a marketing or advertising agency

Do I qualify for Mercury Working Capital?

The best way to find out is to complete our quick eligibility questionnaire, accessible by clicking Accounts > Financing on the left-hand side of your Mercury dashboard.

To be eligible, your company must:

  • Be a corporation or LLC incorporated in the United States. At this time, we are unable to offer working capital loans to businesses operating in California.
  • Meet the time in business, revenue, and cash balance requirements below.

Ecommerce businesses

All other businesses

Time in business

Revenue (past 12 months)

Minimum cash balance

$10K

How much can I borrow?

You can typically borrow up to 20% of your annual revenue, with a maximum of $5,000,000. The exact amount you’re offered is determined during underwriting.

How do repayments work?

Your term sheet will contain your complete repayment plan, which breaks down your exact weekly payment amount and term length. Terms range from 4 to 11 months, and most fall within 4 to 6 months. You’ll work with our underwriting team to find a term length that suits your business’s needs.

Your first repayment will process 7 days after the funds are deposited into your account and then continue every 7 days until the loan is completely paid off.

What are the fees?

There’s a simple, flat fee that’s determined upfront as part of the underwriting process and is a percentage of your total advance amount. That fee is spread out evenly across all your weekly payments so you don’t have to pay it all at once. There are no hidden costs or compounding interest.

Why is the annual percentage rate (APR) on my offer higher than the flat fee?

The flat fee is a percentage of your advance, while the APR shows that same cost annualized, which is how loans are commonly compared. Because Mercury Working Capital* terms are shorter than a year and you repay weekly, the APR comes out higher than the fee percentage.

Your fee itself doesn’t change. If you’d like to see how your APR is calculated, your capital specialist can walk you through it.

How is Mercury Working Capital different from other funding options?

Mercury Working Capital* prioritizes helping you clearly understand the cost of your capital, and gives you a personal, ongoing relationship with capital specialists who can consult on maximizing your use of capital, credit, and banking,* so you can grow and operate at your best.

  • Our fee structure is straightforward and competitive, with a single, fixed fee spread evenly across each of your weekly repayments.
  • We offer fixed weekly payments, providing predictability and ease of forecasting compared to the daily remittances associated with revenue-based payback products.
  • Our repayment terms don’t penalize you for success. Your payments stay the same when your business is doing well, and your fee is reduced if you repay early.
  • We do not require a personal guarantee to secure your loan.

How do I apply for Mercury Working Capital?

  • Complete the eligibility questionnaire. It asks how your business operates, with options for online sellers, retail/wholesale, software, B2B services, services to individual customers, and marketing or advertising agencies.
  • Connect your accounts. If you’re eligible to apply, you’ll be asked to connect your company’s banking and accounting platforms so our underwriters can review your application. Supported accounting platforms include NetSuite, QuickBooks, Xero, and Mercury Books. If you don’t see your accounting platform or can’t connect it, you’ll be asked to upload your financials manually instead.
  • Connect a storefront or continue without one. If you run an ecommerce business, we strongly recommend connecting your storefronts (e.g., Shopify, Amazon) in the Storefronts section. If you are not an ecommerce business and do not have a storefront, select Skip this step. This marks the section complete so you can submit your application.

My company doesn’t use an ecommerce platform or payment processor. Can I still apply?

Yes. Connecting an ecommerce platform or payment processor is not required. In the Storefronts section of the application, select Skip this step and confirm. Our underwriters will review your application using your banking and accounting data.

The eligibility requirements above still apply to all businesses. If you reload the page before submitting and the Submit button is blocked again, select Skip this step once more.

What documents should I have ready when applying?

We’ll ask for some basic information about your business, but most of the detailed financial information is pulled automatically when you connect your platforms. Make sure to have login information handy for:

  • Your bank(s)
  • Your accounting software (e.g., QuickBooks, Xero, NetSuite)
  • Your commerce platform(s), if you have them (e.g., Shopify, Amazon, Woo)

If you don’t see your platform listed, you can upload the requested information manually.

Do I need a bank account through Mercury in order to receive Mercury Working Capital?

Yes. The funds from your Mercury Working Capital* loan will be deposited into your Mercury account*.

If you’re not a Mercury customer already, you’ll be prompted to set up Mercury login credentials to check your eligibility. If you’re approved, you’ll then need to set up an account with Mercury* before funds are deposited. You don’t need to wait until then to simplify your business finances. Feel free to apply for an account with Mercury at any time here.

If I apply but then decide I don’t want to move forward, am I under any obligation?

No. If you’re approved, you’ll have time to review your term sheet and agreement and ask any questions so you can feel confident moving forward. If you decide not to move forward after reviewing the agreement, we completely understand.

How long does it take to apply and get funds?

The application takes about 10 minutes, and you’ll typically hear back from our underwriting team in about 2-3 business days. From there, the terms and agreement review process is unique to each applicant, but a simple process can be as fast as a few days.

Once your agreement is signed, you’ll have access to your loan dashboard in your Mercury account within 1-2 business days. You can draw your loan funds immediately. Funds often arrive instantly once drawn, but may take up to 48 hours.

Will applying impact my credit score?

No. Applying for Mercury Working Capital* does not affect your personal or business credit score.

If I get an offer now, does it improve my chances of getting another offer later?

Each application is reviewed independently and is not affected by previous applications or loans.

Can I get another advance after my first loan?

Yes. If your account is in good standing, we’ll consider a new offer once you’ve repaid at least 50% of your original loan.

If I already have an IO credit card, can I also apply for a working capital loan?

Yes. Having an IO credit card** does not prevent you from using another Mercury credit product. Mercury Working Capital* and IO work well together to help extend your runway.

Who can view the Working Capital page?

Users on your account with permissions set to “view all accounts” can navigate to and see the Working Capital page.

More questions? Fill out this form and our team will be in touch shortly.
