Track investor payments with Round Tracker

Round Tracker helps you close your fundraising round with a clear view of every investor payment. Create a round, add your investors, and Mercury emails each of them wire instructions for the account you choose. As wires arrive, you can see who has funded, who’s still outstanding, and how close you are to your target, without updating a spreadsheet.

Round Tracker works for both priced and SAFE rounds, and you can keep managing agreements and signatures in the tools you already use. It doesn’t add a new way to move money: investors send standard wires to your Mercury account, and Round Tracker shows you where each one stands.

Who can use Round Tracker

Round Tracker is available to eligible US C-corporations and LLCs. To create a round, you need to meet these requirements:

  • Your company is a US-based C-corp
  • Your company is a US-based LLC
  • You’re an admin on the account. Only admins can see Round Tracker

If you don’t see Round Tracker in your dashboard, check your organization type and your role first.

How Round Tracker works

Round Tracker follows your round from setup to close:

  • Create a round. Set a target amount, a closing date, and the Mercury account where investors will send funds. See Getting started below.
  • Add your investors. List each investor’s email and the amount they’re investing.
  • Share wire instructions. Mercury emails each investor the account and routing numbers for your destination account.
  • Track incoming wires. Payments that cover an investor’s full amount are matched to that investor automatically. You can mark any other payment as received yourself.
  • Close the round. The round is marked Closed in Round Tracker automatically when you reach your target, or you can close it manually at any time.

Getting started

Please note the Round Tracker tab won’t appear on your account unless your organization is a US C-Corp. Once you’ve confirmed you’re eligible, here’s how to set up a round in Mercury:

  • Click Accounts on the left side of your dashboard, then select Financing
  • Open the Round Tracker tab
  • Click Set up a round
  • Enter your round details: a name, your target amount, a closing date, and the account where you want wires to land
  • Then add the investors you’d like to invite, including each investor’s email and amount. You can also upload a CSV or PDF in just a few clicks with Command
  • Mercury automatically emails each investor wire instructions
  • Track investor payments from your round. The round closes automatically once you hit your target

Note: Round Tracker matches a wire to an investor automatically only when it covers their full amount. For any other payment, you can mark the investor as received yourself.

Need to prepare and sign SAFE agreements? Round Tracker helps you track the money, while Mercury SAFEs helps you manage the paperwork. Use Mercury SAFEs to prepare, send, and collect signatures on SAFE agreements. The two products are separate and don’t share investor information, so if you use both, you’ll add investors in each one. Learn more in Create a SAFE and manage investor funds in Mercury

FAQs

What types of rounds can I track?

You can track both priced rounds and SAFE rounds, including rounds where agreements are prepared and signed in other tools.

Do I need to change how I manage agreements and signatures?

No. Keep using the tools you already use for agreements and signatures. Round Tracker only handles wire instructions, incoming payments, and funding progress.

Can I create or sign agreements in Round Tracker?

No. Agreement preparation and signing happen outside Round Tracker. If you’re raising with SAFEs and want to prepare and sign them in Mercury, see Mercury SAFEs.

How do investors receive wire instructions?

Mercury emails each investor wire instructions that include the account and routing numbers for your destination account. There’s no public payment page to ensure sensitive account information remains private.

What happens if an investor sends a different amount than I entered?

Round Tracker only matches a wire to an investor automatically when it covers their full amount. For any other payment amount you will see that show up in your Round Tracker but you will then need to mark the investor as received yourself.

Is there a limit to how many wires I can receive?

No. There’s no limit to the number of incoming wires, but the round closes automatically once you reach your target.

Does Round Tracker move money for me?

No. Round Tracker doesn’t introduce any new money movement. It tracks wires that arrive in your destination account.

Do I need Mercury SAFEs to use Round Tracker?

No. Round Tracker works on its own, including for rounds where agreements are managed elsewhere.

Agent cards: Giving AI agents a card of their own

Agent cards are a new type of Mercury virtual card built specifically to be handed to AI agents - software programs businesses can use to handle routine work automatically, like buying things online, booking flights, or managing online ad spend. An agent card can be given to an agent so it can make purchases on your behalf, while you keep full control over how much it can spend and which card it can ever touch.

What is an AI agent?

An AI agent is a software program that can complete tasks on its own, without a person doing each step. Businesses use agents to handle repetitive work like buying office supplies, booking flights, or managing advertising.

Mercury doesn’t build AI agents. You build and run your own agent using whatever AI platform you choose (for example, Anthropic’s Claude, OpenAI, or others). Mercury provides the card, the security controls, and the oversight tools that keep your agent spending within the limits you set.

What is an agent card?

An agent card works like any other Mercury virtual card - it’s accepted anywhere Mastercard is accepted online - with two differences designed for autonomous use:

  • Your agent can retrieve the card’s credentials on its own. Unlike standard virtual or physical cards, an agent can pull an agent card’s number, expiration date, and security code (CVC) through Mercury’s API or CLI, so it can enter them at checkout without a person in the loop.
  • It comes with agent-specific guardrails. An agent can spend within the card limit you set, but it can never create new cards, raise its own limit, or reach any card you didn’t explicitly hand it.

Mercury Business customers can designate both debit and credit virtual cards as agent cards.

What you can use an agent card for

Agent cards are built for the online, and high-frequency, and time-intensive purchases that agents increasingly handle for businesses:

  • Vendor and procurement payments
  • Booking flights
  • Managing online advertising
  • API usage and developer tools
  • Software and SaaS subscriptions

How agent cards keep you in control

Several capabilities can be risky to give carte blanche to agents: card creation (imagine if an agent made a ton of cards and spent against them all at once), card updates (an agent could increase limits on cards it controls to spend more without your permission!), and access to card credentials.

Agent cards are designed so agents can only access card credentials - and only for the agent cards you give it, not your other virtual and physical cards. These protections are on from day one and can’t be turned off:

Agents via API/CLI:

Virtual Cards

Agent Virtual Cards

Create cards

✅

🔴

Update cards (Spend Limits, nickname)

✅

🔴

Retrieve PAN/Expiry/CVC

🔴

✅

Retrieve card info other than PAN/expiry/CVC

✅

✅

  • Only humans can create agent cards. An agent card can only be created by a person in the Mercury web or mobile app. Agents can’t create agent cards (only non-agent cards) themselves through the API or CLI.
  • Per-card spending limits. You set a daily, weekly, or monthly limit on agent cards, just as with normal virtual Mercury cards. The agent can never spend above these limits.
  • Agents can’t change their own limits. Spending limits are set and changed only by a human in-app - never by an agent through the API or CLI.
  • Agents can’t unfreeze their own card. Only a human can, in-app.
  • Card isolation. An agent can only retrieve credentials for the agent cards you explicitly hand to it via API/CLI, not your other normal virtual/physical cards.

Together, these cap your maximum exposure to the spending limits on only the agent cards a human created. A compromised or out-of-control agent can’t mint more cards or raise its own spend limit to get around it.

In the future, we’ll add even more granular capabilities to help you manage agent spend.

Your responsibility and liability

You’re in control of your agent cards, and you’re responsible for how your agent uses them - just as your company is responsible for purchases an employee makes on a corporate card.

You acknowledge and agree that you bear sole responsibility for all agent card transactions, which will be deemed authorized by you regardless of whether the agent acted within the scope of authority you or the company intended.

A few things worth knowing:

  • You keep your normal dispute rights. Agent card transactions can be disputed through Mercury’s standard process, the same as any other Mercury debit or credit card.
  • If your agent card credentials are stolen by a genuine outside party (not your own agent), that follows Mercury’s standard fraud-dispute process.

Your use of agent cards is governed by your Mercury IO Charge Card Agreement, Column Commercial Debit Card Agreement, and Terms of Use.

Setting up an agent card

Setup has two parts: a human creates the card in the app, then you instruct your agent to retrieve the credentials.

Step 1 - Create the agent card (web or mobile)

Only admins or team members with card-management permissions can create cards.

On web:
  • Go to your Cards page from your Mercury dashboard
  • On the top right, click Create Card
  • Select Debit or Credit and Virtual from the dropdown
  • Select the Agent checkbox
  • Give the card a nickname, like “Ad-buying agent card”
  • Set a daily, weekly, or monthly spending limit. You can change this later
  • Review the details and click Create Card
On mobile (make sure you’ve updated to the latest app version):
  • From Home, scroll down to Spending
  • Tap Spending
  • Tap the + on the top right of your screen. Select Debit and Virtual and tap the Agent checkbox

Agent cards appear labeled Agent in your card list and on the card detail page, so you can always tell them apart from your other cards.

Step 2 — Give your agent the card credentials via CLI

Your agent retrieves the card number, expiry, and CVC through Mercury’s Vault surface - available via API or CLI. Card credential access works only for agent cards, never for your regular virtual or physical cards.

CLI

You can find our CLI in this Github repo.

Claude Code

Once in Claude code, type mercury-cli. Claude code should pick up the package from Homebrew. You can also find our CLI here.

# List agent cards on an account (card IDs + masked PAN, no secrets)
mercury cards list --user-id

# Reveal one card's full number, CVV, and expiry
mercury cards reveal --card-id <card-uuid>
API

Request:

curl --request GET \
 --url <[vault-api.mercury.com](https://vault-api.mercury.com/api/v1/cards/{cardId}/reveal)> \
 --header 'accept: application/json' \
 --header 'Authorization: Bearer $MERCURY_TOKEN'

Response:

{
    "cardNumber": "5555666677778888",
    "expiration": {
        "month": 7,
        "year": 2031
    },
    "cvc": "234"
}

FAQs

Does Mercury build or control my AI agent?

No. You choose and run your own agent using whatever AI platform you prefer. Mercury provides the card and the controls around it; it doesn’t vet or manage your agent, much like it doesn’t manage the web browser you use.

Can my agent create its own cards or raise its own limit?

No. Both are human-only actions in the web or mobile app, and this can’t be changed. It’s what caps your exposure and makes agent cards safe to hand over to agents.

Can my agent see card details of other, non-Agent Mercury cards?

No. An agent can retrieve credentials only for the specific agent cards you assign to it. Every other virtual and physical card, and the rest of your account data, stays hidden from it.

Where are the card credentials stored on the way to the agent/when retrieved via API?

In a secure third-party vault. Mercury never stores raw card numbers or codes. Credentials are released only through authenticated requests, and you can restrict API requests to specific IP addresses.

How do I stop an agent immediately?

Freeze or cancel the card from the Cards page on web or mobile. It takes effect right away, and the agent can’t reverse it.

What happens to my card details once my agent has them?

When your agent pulls the card number, expiry, and CVC, those details move from Mercury into wherever your agent runs, including the AI platform you’re using to power it. From that point on, they live in your setup.

The simple way to think about it: Mercury keeps your credentials safe right up until your agent asks for them and we release them. After that, how they’re stored and used is in the hands of your agent and your AI provider. So when you’re choosing an AI platform and setting up your agent, it’s worth a look at how each one handles the details you give it.

What does Mercury collect and log about agent card activity?

The same kinds of information we handle for any Mercury card, transaction details such as amount, merchant, and date, and for agent cards - certain records of the API and CLI requests used to reveal credentials. We use this to run the service, monitor for fraud and misuse, and meet our legal and compliance obligations.

Business Debit Card FAQs

What’s the difference between a virtual card and a physical card?

Changing card limits

If you’re an admin or have card limit permissions, you can easily adjust the spending limit of any debit cards associated with your Mercury account. This allows you to keep a tighter control on spending and stick to daily or monthly budgets.

Here’s how:

  • Go to your Cards page
  • Click on the card with the limit you would like to edit to open the card details
  • Click More, then select Edit Limit
  • You can select a daily, weekly, monthly, yearly, on a permanent or temporary basis depending on the needs of your business. Daily limits give you more granular control, while monthly limits are a little more flexible

If you’re planning a purchase that requires a limit higher than the dashboard allows, please reach out to us with an invoice or contract representing the larger purchase. We’ll review your request to determine whether we can raise the card limit to that amount.

Cash withdrawal limits

You can use your Mercury debit card at ATMs to withdraw up to $1,000 cash per card per business day, with a maximum daily withdrawal limit per business being $3000.

For example, a business with 7 cardholders could in one business day withdraw up to $3k if 6 of the 7 card holders withdrew $500 each. The final card holder would technically still have a card limit of $1,000 cash withdrawal, but, because the overall company daily maximum would have already been reached no more cash could be withdrawn.

When do limits reset?

Limit windows begin at midnight UTC, unless otherwise noted:

  • Daily limits reset every day at midnight UTC, including weekends and holidays
    • Individual card ATM withdrawal limits follow the card’s spend limit and reset on the same schedule
    • The organization-wide ATM withdrawal limit resets at 10pm UTC only on business days (Monday-Friday excluding holidays)
      • Learn more about withdrawal limits in our Using your Mercury debit card at ATMs article.
  • Weekly limits reset every Sunday and last for seven days
  • Monthly limits reset on the first calendar day of each month and last through the end of the month

For example if you update your limit to monthly on September 15th, your new monthly spending limit would be in effect for the remainder of September and reset again on Oct 1st. Going forward, the limit will continue to reset on the 1st of each month. This is true for daily and weekly limits as well.

Adjusting your limits does not change how much you’ve previously spent in a period. For example: If you start the week with a limit of $100/day and spend $100 on Sunday, Monday, and Tuesday, you would have spent $300 for the week. On Wednesday, if you set a limit of $300/week, you won’t be able to spend until next week because you’ve already used up the limit for that period.

Setting a temporary daily, weekly, or monthly limit will always take into account the money you’ve spent within the set period. If on a Wednesday you set a temporary weekly limit for the next seven days, this temporary weekly limit will still reset on Sunday at 12am UTC.

If a charge exceeds your limit

Card limits are meant to help control spending and not prevent good-faith transactions from a merchant. In that spirit, there are a few legitimate reasons a merchant may be able to process a charge on your Mercury card above the limit you’ve set.

  • Recurring Charge or Subscription: Recurring charges are usually subscription-based. If the merchant was authorized to charge you with the initial debit, this authorization persists even if you alter your limits. In these cases, we recommend contacting the merchant to cancel the recurring payment - you can always re-authorize with them at a later date by re-signing up.
  • Force Posts: This occurs when a merchant uses a previous authorization code to push through a transaction. Governments and utilities use force posts most commonly, but they can also be used to refund money back to a canceled card.
  • Pre-authorizations: Similar to recurring charges (because technically the recurring charges are all pre-authorized). The debit card infrastructure allows a merchant to change the final charged amount by up to 20% before it’s automatically blocked. Think about paying at the pump or using a delivery service that charges an initial amount and then updates it to reflect tax or tips.

Regardless, if you believe a transaction is incorrect or fraudulent, we can help you resolve the situation.

Creating and managing category locked cards

Category locks allow you to restrict your card to certain types of purchases, such as “Software,” “Travel,” or “Restaurants.” When a category lock is in place, transactions outside of these categories will be automatically declined. Benefits of category locks include:

  • Enhanced Security: Prevent unauthorized purchases by restricting spending to specific categories.
  • Budgeting: Keep your spending within limits by only allowing transactions in essential categories.
  • Customized Control: Tailor your card’s usage to align with your personal or business needs.

How to lock your IO card to categories

Follow these steps to lock an existing card to specific spending categories:

  • Log into your Mercury account on the web.
  • Navigate to your Cards page.
  • Select the card you’d like to enable category locks on and click More.
  • Click on Category lock to begin adding your categories.
  • Under “Spend Categories”, select your categories and click Save Categories.

ℹ️You can also enable card locks when issuing a new debit or IO card. Under “Spend Control”, click Category Lock, select your categories, and finish setting up your card.

Managing Category Locks

You can view, edit or remove your category locks at any time from your Cards page. Either locate the card that needs editing or click Add filter to view all category-locked cards:

  • Click on the card that needs editing.
  • Locate the “Category Lock” section and click the pencil icon to edit your categories as needed.
  • You can add new categories or remove existing ones. To disable category locks entirely, simply deselect each category.
  • Click Save changes once you’ve made your necessary changes.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

  • Can I lock my card to multiple categories?
  • Yes, you can lock your card to one or multiple categories depending on your needs.
  • What happens if I try to make a purchase outside of my locked categories?
  • The transaction will be declined, ensuring your spending stays within your set boundaries. You will see the reason for the decline in the transaction.
  • Can I apply category locks to multiple cards?
  • Yes, each card can be locked to different categories independently.
  • Who can enable card locking?
  • Any admin or team member with card editing permissions.

Creating single use cards

Single-use cards are rolling out incrementally. Stay tuned for general availability.

Single-use cards are virtual debit and IO cards that automatically close after one purchase. They’re useful for one-time transactions and may help reduce the risk of unauthorized charges from unfamiliar merchants.

This article explains how to create a single-use card and what happens after you’ve used it.

Create a single-use card

You can create single-use cards from your Mercury dashboard on web.

  • Go to your Cards page
  • Click Create card
  • Select a Cardholder and enter a Card nickname
  • Under “Type,” select Debit or Credit, then Virtual
  • Under “Usage (optional),” check Single-use
  • Configure any additional settings, including spend controls, as needed
  • Set an optional expiration date
    • The card will stop working after its first approved purchase or when the expiration date passes, whichever comes first.
  • Click Create card

How single-use cards work

A single-use card automatically closes after its first approved purchase over $0. Once closed, its status changes to Used, and it can’t be reopened.

A few things to keep in mind:

  • Declined transactions and $0 authorization checks won’t count as a purchase, so your card will remain active
  • You can still receive refunds on a used card or dispute a transaction as you normally would
  • Since the card can only be used once, avoid using it for ongoing subscriptions or free trials
  • Charges submitted without an authorization request (known as “force posts”) can still be processed, even if your single-use card has already been used or is past its custom expiration date. If the card hasn’t been used yet, the transaction will mark it as used

If you need to make another transaction, you can create a new single-use or standard card.

Identity verification of card transactions (3D Secure)

3D Secure (3DS) is an additional security layer used during online credit and debit card transactions. It helps us prevent unauthorized card usage by asking cardholders to verify their identity through an extra authentication step.

Why am I seeing a 3D Secure challenge?

To protect you from fraud, we occasionally initiate challenges for extra verification on a transaction.

How does the 3D Secure challenge flow work?

  • Initiation: When you start an online transaction, we might ask for additional verification. You’ll see this request appear in a pop-up on the website where you’re making the purchase. Look for a message like the one below, which guides you through scanning a QR code, logging in and verifying your identity:
  • Notification: We’ll send you an email to the address on file and mobile notification. Each one will take you to your Mercury account to log in. You might have to update your mobile app to version 4.17 or later to receive 3DS notifications if you haven’t updated after March 24, 2025. Be on the lookout for an email with the subject line: “Verify Your Identity to Complete Your Purchase”
  • Challenge prompt: Once you’re logged into Mercury, we’ll ask if it’s you making the purchase, and you can confirm or deny. It’ll look like this:
  • Completion: Once you’ve let us know it’s you, we’ll complete the transaction.

What if I don’t receive a notification or the challenge times out?

  • Email notifications: You’ll always receive an email notification with a link to verify your transaction. The message will be sent to the email address associated with your Mercury account and will have the subject line “Verify Your Identity to Complete Your Purchase”.
  • Mobile notifications: Your Mercury mobile app might need to be updated to receive mobile 3DS notifications. If you haven’t updated your app after March 24, 2025, you might not receive a mobile notification. We also strongly recommend setting up biometric verification like FaceID to make it even easier (and more secure) to log in to the mobile app to complete verification.
  • Challenge timeout: For your security, challenges time out after 10 minutes. When you log in to the challenge, we’ll show you a countdown timer that displays how much time is left. If 10 minutes have passed since you attempted the transaction, try the transaction again with the merchant.

How do I know if my transaction was successful?

After successfully completing the 3D Secure challenge:

  • Confirmation screen: After you click or press “This was me” to verify your identity, we’ll show a confirmation screen letting you know the transaction will progress.
  • Merchant confirmation: You should also see the pop-up on your merchant website confirming that the transaction went through.
  • Mercury transactions: You should see the transaction reflected as pending on your Mercury Transactions page.

June 2026: IO card statement update

Starting June 15, 2026, Mercury is updating the IO card statement format to follow standard credit card accounting conventions. This article explains what’s changing, why, and what to expect on your next statement. For general information about IO card statements, see our main help article.

What’s changing

These updates bring IO card statements in line with standard credit card accounting conventions, making it clearer what was owed at the close of each billing period versus what’s scheduled to be paid.

Balances reflect the statement close date

Only activity through the close date appears on a given statement. If a payment or transaction occurs after the close date, it will show up on the following month’s statement instead.

Autopay appears as its own line item

Autopay no longer appears within the transaction list. It now shows separately on the statement cover page, with the scheduled payment amount and source account. Autopay doesn’t affect the balance for the closed period. Since autopay typically runs after your statement closes, it falls into the next billing period.

Charges and payments use opposite signs

Charges and balances display as positive values; payments and refunds display as negative. This follows standard credit card accounting conventions and is different from your Transactions page, which shows charges as debits from your spending power. Both reflect the same activity from different accounting perspectives.

Starting and ending balances are now connected

Your starting balance will always match the previous statement’s ending balance going forward.

FAQs

Do I need to do anything?

No action is required. The updated format will apply automatically to statements generated after June 15 2026.

Why does my starting balance not match my previous statement’s ending balance?

Your first statement for June 15 may show a starting balance that differs from your previous statement’s ending balance. This is a one-time difference as the new format takes effect. All statements going forward will carry balances forward consistently.

I made a payment but it’s not on my statement — where is it?

Payments appear on the statement for the period in which they post, not when they’re initiated. If a payment was initiated before your statement close date but posted after, it will appear on your next statement instead. To confirm the payment was processed, check your transaction history on your Credit page.

Does this change how autopay works?

The format change affects how autopay is displayed on your statement — not how it functions. Autopay will continue to run as scheduled.

Will statements issued before June 15, 2026 be reissued in the new format?

Regenerated statements will follow the new format.

Managing your Card-based Subscriptions

Mercury can help you automatically detect recurring subscription payments on your cards, making it easier to track and manage ongoing payments to your vendors.

To access a list of recurring transactions Mercury has identified as subscriptions, simply navigate to your cards page under Cards > Card Subscriptions.

On this page you be able to:

  • View active (and canceled) subscriptions, including the merchant, last payment, frequency, and the card the payment is associated with
  • Filter by card, merchant, and subscription status
  • Select the subscription to view the most recent history (as well as link to the Transactions page already filtered to the specific merchant) and make changes

Mercury will alert you when you cancel a card or remove a team member that is tied to a subscription; if a new subscription is detected; or if any duplicate subscriptions are detected.

Canceling a Subscription

By selecting a subscription, you will see two options to proceed with canceling a subscription.

Manage subscription on merchant website - this will link you directly to the merchant’s website where you can work with them to edit or cancel and ongoing subscription

Cancel Subscription - this will block further payments processed by this merchant on this particular card. If the card in question is locked to a merchant, Mercury will instead freeze the card so you can resume payments should you choose to.

The ‘Cancel Subscription’ does not notify the merchant and simply places a payment stop on your card. Because of this, depending on the terms of the subscription, you may still owe the merchant for failed payment attempts. Merchants also may be able to continue processing payments depending on their terms of use, and should this happen we recommend reaching out to the merchant to fully cancel. We will also work with you to dispute any incorrectly charged transactions that the merchant can’t help to remedy.

Canceled subscriptions will continue to display on this page (though marked as canceled) for your records.

Removing a Subscription

If Mercury has incorrectly identified a series of transactions as a subscription you can remove it by clicking into the subscription and selecting the ‘…’ in the bottom right of the Subscription details panel and choosing ‘This is not a subscription’.

Note: At this time this action cannot be undone.

Shipping & delivery timelines for Mercury cards

Once you order a physical Mercury card, it’s typically shipped by first-class mail and isn’t trackable. This article explains standard shipping timelines, what to expect during delivery, and how to order a replacement if your card doesn’t arrive.

Shipping timelines

Cards are shipped via USPS (for U.S. addresses) or Deutsche Post (for international addresses). Shipping times may vary and be extended depending on the destination, season (e.g. holidays), and local delivery conditions:

  • U.S. addresses: Typically arrive in 1-2 weeks
  • International addresses: Typically arrive in 2-3 weeks

Need to start spending sooner? You can use your card’s virtual details immediately from the Cards page while you wait for the physical card to arrive.

What to expect once a card is shipped

  • Cards arrive in a white envelope with the Mercury logo and name on the back
  • The return address is from New Jersey or Poland, depending on your location
  • The envelope is addressed to the cardholder

Note: If you’re sending your card to a registered agent’s address, delivery may be delayed. Registered agents need to sort and forward mail, which can add extra time.

How to order a replacement card

  • On web, click Cards in the left sidebar
  • Select the card that hasn’t arrived
  • Click More > Order replacement
  • Enter a reason (for our records) and confirm or update the mailing address

Note: Once you order a replacement, the original card will be canceled and cannot be reactivated. If it arrived later, destroy it and wait for the replacement.

Before requesting a replacement, make sure your address is correct and formatted properly:

  • Your address can include letters with accents (like é or ñ), hyphens (-), apostrophes (’), underscores (_), colons (:), and forward slashes (/).
  • Don’t use # or ;. For an apartment or suite, write “Apt 4” or “Suite 200” instead of “#4”
  • If possible, compare to any previously successful delivery addresses. You can see which address a card was sent to by checking your confirmation email titled: “Your physical debit card is on the way and your virtual card numbers are ready to use.”

FAQs

Can I change the address after my card has shipped?

No. Once a card is in transit, it can’t be rerouted. You’ll need to order a replacement card, where you can enter a new address. The original will be canceled automatically.

If you’ve already ordered two replacements and still haven’t received your card, please contact our support team for further help.

Can I expedite my card shipment?

You can expedite shipping for IO (credit) cards for an additional fee. Expedited shipping is not currently available for debit cards, which follow standard delivery timelines.

Expedited IO card delivery typically takes:

  • U.S. & Canada: 5-7 business days
  • International: 1-2 weeks

Shipping fees are shown during card issuance and vary based on the delivery destination.

Can I issue myself or a team member a metal card?

Metal cards are available as an upgrade for IO cards only. When issuing a physical card, you’ll see the option to upgrade to a metal card for a fee, which will be shown during card creation.

Can I track my card?

Most cards are shipped via standard mail and don’t include tracking. Tracking is only available if you selected priority shipping when issuing the card.

To check the status of your card, go to your Cards page and select the recently issued card—there you’ll see the latest available updates.

Understanding conversion fees for non-USD card transactions

Mercury charges a currency conversion fee of 3% on all Mercury business debit and IO transactions that are made in currencies other than USD. While IO cards cannot be used for ATM withdrawals, Mercury business debit cards can. Non-USD ATM withdrawals with debit cards are also subject to the same currency conversion fee. Note that this fee won’t be returned, even if your original transaction is refunded.

How to view your conversion fees

You can view currency conversion fees on your Transactions page. Each fee appears as a separate line item linked to the original non-USD transaction.

To see the full details:

  • Go to the Transactions page
  • Select the original purchase or fee entry titled “Intl. Transaction fee”
  • In the details panel, you’ll see:
    • The original transaction
    • The converted USD amount
    • The 3% conversion fee (shown as a linked transaction)

If you have multiple fee entries, selecting any one of them will show the associated purchase in the details panel.

Viewing totals

You can also view summaries of total fee spending:

  • On the Credit page
  • On your Credit statements
  • By filtering the Transactions page by Method and selecting Intl. Transaction Fee

Conversion fees, limits and IO Cashback

Currency conversion fees charged on purchases will not impact individual card limits. They do however apply against your overall borrowable credit for your business.

Non-USD transactions are eligible for IO Cashback rewards based on the converted USD amount at the time of purchase. However, any currency conversion fees applied to the transaction are excluded from cashback calculations.

Understanding pending card transactions

When you use your Mercury Debit or IO Credit card, you might notice that some charges show as pending before they’re finalized. This article explains what pending transactions mean, why the amount might be higher than expected, how long they typically take to settle, and how to check their status from your dashboard.

Why a transaction is pending

When you see a pending transaction, the merchant has started the payment process but hasn’t fully completed it. This is called a pre-authorization, which allows the merchant to request a hold on funds before they finalize or cancel the charge.

  • Pending transactions are not final
  • The merchant can settle or cancel the charge
  • You may see a temporary hold amount that differs from the final total

How long it takes to settle

Most pending transactions are resolved within 1–3 business days, but timing depends on the merchant. Here’s what to expect:

  • Some merchants settle the charge immediately while others wait until they reconcile their payments
  • We allow up to an industry-standard of 30 business days for the merchant to complete or cancel the transaction before it is cancelled

Why the pending amount may be higher

If you’re seeing a pending amount that’s greater than your purchase, it’s likely a pre-authorization. This happens when a merchant—like a gas station—places a temporary hold on your card for more than the final total.

These charges typically update to the correct amount once the merchant settles the transaction or drop off entirely after a few business days.

How to check the status of a card transaction

To check whether a card transaction is pending or posted:

  • Go to the Transactions page in your Mercury dashboard
  • Locate the transaction manually or use filters to narrow it down
  • Look for a “Pending” or “Failed” badge next to the transaction
  • Click into the transaction to view more details, including the reason if it failed

Looking for an authorization code?

In some cases, a merchant may ask you for an authorization code to help finalize a pending transaction. This code is a digital confirmation that’s generated when the transaction is approved. If a merchant requests this, reach out to our team with a link to the transaction, and we can provide you with it.

Using your Mercury debit card at ATMs

You can use your physical Mercury debit card to withdraw cash at compatible ATMs. This article explains ATM withdrawal limits, possible fees, and why you can’t deposit cash into your Mercury account.

ATM fees and compatibility

  • Some ATM operators may charge a separate convenience or operation fee that Mercury does not control
  • If you withdraw cash in a currency other than USD, Mercury charges a currency conversion fee — learn more here
  • Physical Mercury debit cards only work at ATMs that support chip entry, not magnetic stripe-only ATMs due to higher fraud risk
  • Virtual debit cards and Mercury IO cards are not supported at ATMs

Cash withdrawal limits

You can withdraw up to $1,000 per card per business day, with a maximum of $3,000 total per day across all cardholders.

Example: If 6 of your 7 cardholders each withdraw $500 in one day, the 7th cardholder won’t be able to withdraw any more funds that day, even though they haven’t hit their individual limit. The account-wide $3,000 daily cap applies.

How to check or change your limit:

  • Go to your Cards page
  • Click on the card you want to update
  • Select the More button and click Edit Limit
  • Review or adjust the cash withdrawal limit (up to $1,000)

Cash deposits with Mercury

Mercury doesn’t support cash deposits. While our partner banks have physical branch locations, they aren’t able to accept cash deposits for Mercury accounts. To fund your account, use a check, ACH transfer, or wire instead.

Troubleshooting withdrawal errors

IO or virtual card used: ATM withdrawals are only supported with a physical Mercury debit card. IO cards and virtual debit cards cannot be used at ATMs.

Transaction declined: Check your Transactions page for a failed transaction and review the decline reason listed. Common reasons include exceeding your individual $1,000 daily limit or the account-wide $3,000 daily cap across all cardholders.

ATM not on the Mastercard network: If no failed transaction appears, confirm the ATM displays the Mastercard logo. Mercury debit cards are only compatible with Mastercard-network ATMs.

Cash not dispensed but funds were deducted: Submit a dispute through the Mercury app or web dashboard and our team will investigate.

How Mercury reports IO card activity to business credit bureaus

Mercury reports IO credit card payment data to Experian, Equifax and Dun & Bradstreet - the three major credit bureaus - in order to help our customers build their business credit. These reports contain all historical IO statement payments and end of month balances.

Benefits of building good credit history

  • Access to Financing: A good credit score opens doors to better financing options, allowing you to secure loans, lines of credit, and business credit cards with favorable terms and lower interest rates.
  • Supplier Relationships: Suppliers often check your business credit score when deciding whether to extend credit terms. A positive score can help you negotiate better payment terms and build stronger relationships with suppliers.
  • Business Growth: A higher credit score can enhance your business’s credibility, making it easier to attract investors, partners, and customers. It can also lead to improved opportunities for expansion and growth.
  • Lower Costs: With a good credit score, you may qualify for lower insurance premiums and reduced lease costs, ultimately saving your business money.

Credit score and history questions

This should not impact individual credit scores of you or your team members, but only the overall business’s credit.

Should you have questions with regards to your credit score or history, we recommend contacting the credit bureaus.

The credit bureaus are able to parse the reports we send them and assign the correct credit information to the correct customer.

If you already have a DUNS number there is no need to report it to us. If you do not have a DUNS number and would like one, you can review our blog post to learn more about the steps to build business credit including registering with credit bureaus.

How your IO balance affects outgoing transactions from your Mercury business deposit account

If you have an outstanding balance on your IO Card account, Mercury may block an outgoing transaction from your Mercury business deposit account if sending it would leave you without enough funds in your deposit account to cover what you currently owe on IO. This is a normal part of how your IO card account and your Mercury business deposit account work together.

A simplified way to think about it:

A payment from your Mercury business deposit account may be blocked if: (deposit balance - payment amount) < outstanding IO balance

Example

  • You have $100 in your Mercury business deposit account.
  • You owe $80 on your IO balance.
  • You try to send a $30 outbound payment from your Mercury business deposit account.
  • After the payment, you’d have $70 in deposits, less than the $80 you owe on IO.
  • Because this would leave you short of what’s needed to cover your IO balance, the payment may be blocked.

What kinds of transactions this can apply to

This action can apply to most types of outbound money movement from your Mercury business deposit account, including:

  • ACH debits and pulls
  • Send-money payments
  • Checks
  • Wires
  • Debit card transactions
  • ATM withdrawals

Why Mercury blocks these payments

This process helps us make sure you keep enough deposits in Mercury to repay your outstanding IO balance before additional funds leave your Mercury business deposit account. It’s a preventative measure, not a penalty.

What you can do

If a payment is blocked for this reason, you generally have a few options:

  • Pay down your outstanding IO balance so your deposits are enough to cover it.
  • Reduce the amount of the outbound payment.
  • Add funds to your Mercury business deposit account.

Once there are enough funds in your Mercury business deposit account to cover your IO balance after the payment, you can re-try the transaction.

FAQs

Is this the same as an insufficient-funds decline?

No. You can have enough cash in your Mercury business deposit account to cover a payment on its own and still have that payment blocked, if paying it would leave you without enough deposits to also cover your outstanding IO balance. This process looks at your deposits and your IO balance together, not just your deposit balance alone.

Does this only apply to large payments?

No. It can apply to any outbound payment from your Mercury business deposit account, regardless of size, if sending it would create a shortfall between your remaining deposit balance and what you owe on IO.

Do I get any advance notice that my transaction may be blocked?

Yes. If you create an outgoing transaction in the Send Money flow that would cause your deposit account balance to drop below your IO balance, you will receive a notification in the user interface that the payment would cause your total available deposit balance to fall below the amount required to pay off your current IO card balance and advising that you leave at least the amount required to pay off your current IO balance in your account.

Do I get notified after my payment is blocked?

Yes. If your payment is blocked, you will receive an email notification that Mercury rejected your transaction because completing it would have caused your deposit account balance to drop below your IO balance.

What happens if my payment is blocked?

The payment will generally be returned or rejected. In some cases, it may be placed into a review queue as part of Mercury’s decision process. If you have questions about a specific blocked payment, reach out to our support team.

Making an IO payment

IO account holders are required to pay off their full statement balance on a regular schedule — daily or monthly, depending on your IO card type. To help manage this, Mercury requires you to set up automatic payments when you open your IO account. This article covers how autopay works and how to make a manual payment outside of your regular schedule. To learn more about qualifying for monthly repayments, see Qualifying for IO.

How IO autopay works

Autopay is set up by default when you open your IO account. You can configure:

  • The day your payment processes (for those with a monthly repayment schedule)
  • A primary account to pay from
  • A secondary account to use if your primary account doesn’t have enough available funds at the time of payment

You can edit your autopay settings at any time on your Credit page, as long as you don’t currently have a payment due.

Paying off your balance early

Making a manual payment lets you free up available credit outside of your normal autopay schedule. You can do this at any time.

Here’s how:

  • Select Cards from your left-hand sidebar on web and click Credit
  • Near the top, select the Pay button
  • Input your payment amount and the account you want to pay from, then select Review and Confirm Payment

A manual payment doesn’t stop your next autopay. Any purchases you make before your statement period ends are still part of that statement’s balance, and your next autopay collects it.

Navigating your IO card statement

Your IO statement is a monthly summary of activity on your IO card. It shows what you spent, what you paid, and your balance as of your statement end date. This article covers where to find you statement, what’s included in a statement and how autopay shows up.

Accessing your IO statements

Your IO card statements are available in the Documents & Data section of your Mercury account. Here’s how to access your statements:

  • Click your org name in the top left-hand corner of your dashboard on web
  • Click Documents & Data
  • Select your Credit account from the Accounts dropdown
  • Select the time period(s) and click Download

Statements are generated monthly. You can also download a CSV of your credit transactions from the same page.

What’s included in your IO statement

Each statement covers one billing period — from your statement start date to your statement end date. Only activity that occurred within that window appears on the statement. Transactions or payments that happen after the end date will appear on your next statement.

Your statement includes:

  • An overview of your IO credit account, including your credit limit, total spending, and cashback
  • All posted transactions during the billing period
  • Any payments you made during the billing period
  • Your statement balance as of the end date (what you owed at the close of the period)
How autopay shows on your statement

Autopay is shown as a scheduled payment on the statement cover page, separate from your statement balance. Autopay typically runs after your statement closes, so it falls into the next billing period rather than the current one.

If you make a manual payment before the statement end date, that payment will appear inside the statement itself.

How transactions are displayed on your statement

We recently updated how transactions on your IO card statement are shown to align with standard credit card accounting:

  • Charges and balances display as positive values — these represent amounts owed
  • Payments and refunds display as negative values — these represent reductions to your balance

This differs from your Transactions page, which shows charges as debits from your spending power. Both views are correct — they reflect the same activity from different accounting perspectives.

FAQ

Why are payments missing from my statement?

Payments appear on the statement for the period in which they post, not when they’re initiated. If a payment was initiated before your statement end date but posted after, it will appear on your next statement instead. To confirm the payment was processed, check your transaction history on your Credit page.

If I pay off my balance now, will a new purchase be included in my next autopay?

Yes. A manual payment reduces what you owe, but it doesn’t stop your next autopay or push later purchases to a future statement. Anything you buy before your statement period ends is part of that statement’s balance, and your next autopay collects it.

Example: You pay your balance down to $0, then make a $6,000 purchase before your statement period ends. That $6,000 is part of the same statement, so your next autopay collects $6,000.

Why does this month’s starting balance not match last month’s ending balance?

Starting May 15, 2026, we made some changes to the IO card statements. As a result, your first statement after May 15 may show a starting balance that differs from your previous statement’s ending balance. This is a one-time difference as the new format takes effect — it is not a bug or a missing payment. Going forward, your starting balance will always match the previous statement’s ending balance.

Are statements issued prior to May 2026 going to be reissued to follow the same format?

Yes, regenerated statements for download will follow the new format.

Qualifying for IO

Most U.S. based businesses qualify for an IO credit account on their first day with Mercury. Customers start with daily repayment schedules until they reach a total Mercury balance of $15k, at which point they can qualify for higher limits and choose between monthly or daily repayment schedules.

You can determine if your Mercury account qualifies for IO by going to your Credit Card page (Cards > Credit from your sidebar on web). If you qualify, you’ll be prompted to set up your IO account and card. If not, you’ll see instructions to apply.

Note, the IO card is a cash-underwritten charge card, meaning your IO balance cannot exceed the cash deposits you have held in Mercury.

Introductory access with daily payments

Most businesses qualify for an introductory IO account that requires same day repayment of balances and comes with a lower account credit limit. Eligibility for this introductory offer is determined by many different factors, such as the company’s size, spending patterns, and fundraising history.

If you have qualified, you should see the option to create an IO card when signing up for your Mercury account and will receive a physical IO card after your first deposit.

Qualifying for higher limits and monthly payments

To qualify for higher account limits and choose between monthly or daily payment schedules, your Mercury account needs to have at least $15k deposited across your Mercury checking, savings, and Treasury accounts. General history and usage of the Mercury platform will also be considered.

Learn more about IO limits here.

Deposits held in linked business accounts

We also review balances in linked business accounts and may grant additional credit based on external balances. Note that cash held in Mercury will allow for higher credit limits than cash held outside Mercury.

FAQs

How do I start using my IO card?

Eligible customers will see the option to create an IO cards from the Credit page (click Cards on the left-hand side of your dashboard. A Credit page will appear). The introductory IO card uses daily repayments and a cash-underwritten limit, typically up to $5,000, which adjusts based on the cash you hold in Mercury.

If you see a $0 available limit, that usually means you don’t yet have enough funds in your checking account. Because IO is cash-underwritten, your total IO balance can’t exceed the cash you have with Mercury. If a transaction would exceed that amount (even temporarily), it will be declined until you add funds or make a payment.

You can check whether you qualify and get started anytime by going to your dashboard and clicking Cards in the left-hand sidebar.

Can I switch from daily to monthly autopay later?

Yes. Once you reach a total Mercury balance of $15k, you can qualify for higher limits which you can request from your Credit page and you’ll be able to choose between monthly or daily repayment schedules.

What is dynamic autopay and when should I use it?

Dynamic autopay is an optional safety-net payment. You can set a threshold (for example, when 80% of my credit limit is used) so Mercury automatically makes a payment mid-cycle.

It helps keep available credit open without waiting for your normal daily or monthly autopay.

You can read more about setting up and editing autopay here.

Why might a transaction decline even if I have funds?

IO is a cash-underwritten charge card, which means your total IO balance can’t exceed the cash you hold in Mercury. If a purchase would put you over that amount—even temporarily—the transaction will be declined until you add funds or make a payment.

In some cases, pending transactions can also reduce your available credit. Pending charges still count toward your IO balance until they settle, which may temporarily limit how much you can spend.

If you’re seeing a $0 available limit, keep in mind that IO limits refresh once daily (around midnight). Your organization’s first deposit is the exception — we recalculate your limit shortly after it posts. For deposits after that, you may need to wait for the next daily refresh, or for pending transactions to settle, before your available credit updates.

How is cashback calculated and paid out?

You earn 1.5 % cashback on all settled purchases. Cashback is tallied monthly and deposited automatically. Returned or pending transactions don’t count until they settle.

You can view cashback on your Credit page.

I’m expecting a refund. Where do those funds go?

IO refunds are credited back to the IO card itself, creating a positive credit balance. They don’t automatically transfer to a checking or savings account. If you need the funds moved, contact Support to request a manual transfer.

Setting up and editing IO autopay

As an IO accountholder, you’re required to pay off your full balance each month. To do this, we require you to set up autopay when the account is first created.

Setting up autopay

When you first set up autopay, you’ll be asked to set one of your accounts as your primary payment account. You can also set an optional backup account, which will be used to replenish your primary account if you don’t have enough funds to cover your payment at the time of processing.

You’ll also need to decide how often you want the autopay to pay off your full balance. You can choose either daily or monthly. If monthly, you can choose a specific day you want the autopay to process.

Note: IO Autopay runs at midnight UTC on the scheduled autopay date. Some payments may appear “early” depending on your timezone.

Setting up dynamic autopay

You can also set up an additional “safety net” payment, which we call dynamic autopay. This setting is totally optional, but allows you to run an additional off-cycle automatic payment if you get close to hitting your credit limit.

You can choose the threshold at which the autopay processes (“when I only have 20% of my credit limit available”) and a maximum daily payment amount (“make a maximum payment of $12,000”). If you don’t choose a maximum daily payment, we’ll attempt to pay the full balance at the time the autopay is processed.

You can turn off dynamic autopay at any time if you’d rather make manual payments or just wait until your regular autopay processes.

Editing autopay settings

  • Go to your Credit Card page
  • Near the top of the page, hover your mouse over the grey box with your current autopay date, then select Edit Autopay
  • In the window that opens up, update any settings you’d like to change, then click Done

Note: If you change your autopay settings, your next scheduled payment will still process on its original date. Your updated settings will take effect at the end of your next statement period.

The IO Card is issued by Patriot Bank, N.A., Member FDIC, pursuant to a license from Mastercard International Incorporated.

Setting up limit-based autopay

In addition to your standard IO autopay settings, you can add an additional limit-based autopay rule to process payments and free up credit automatically when you get close to hitting your credit limit.

Limit-based autopay rules are triggered by settled IO card transactions and are not affected by pending charges.

Creating or editing a limit-based autopay rule

  • Go to your Credit Card account.
  • Near the top of the page, you’ll see your current autopay date. Hover over this, then select Edit autopay.
  • Under Autopay rules, you’ll see the option to enable or edit limit-based autopay.
  • In the setup or edit modal, you can choose the payment threshold, i.e. what percentage of your credit limit you have to hit to trigger an automatic payment.
  • You can optionally set a daily maximum payment. This is the maximum amount you want to be paid to your IO balance each day if the rule is triggered. If you leave this blank, we’ll automatically pay the total balance at the time the rule is triggered.
  • Once you hit Save, the rule will be active.

If the rule is triggered and an automatic payment is processed, you’ll receive an email notification letting you know whether the payment was successful or whether the payment failed due to an insufficient balance in your payment account.

Note: IO Autopay runs at midnight UTC on the scheduled autopay date. Some payments may appear “early” depending on your timezone.

You can turn off limit-based autopay at any time if you’d rather just wait for your standard autopay to process.

Understanding IO limit changes

When using your IO credit account, there are two types of limit you’ll want to be aware of:

  • Account limit - This is the amount you can borrow across your entire IO account, including all physical and virtual IO cards assigned to you and your team. This limit is set by our underwriting policies.
  • Card limit - This is the daily or monthly spending limit on an individual IO card. Maximum limits are determined by your account history with Mercury, but individual card limits (as long as they’re within the maximum) are set by the cardholder.

Of the two, your account limit is probably more important to keep a close eye on. You can also set up limit-based autopay rules to trigger automatic payments when you get close to hitting your account limit.

Why does my account limit change?

Your account limit may change from time to time based on a variety of factors. We’ll notify you when this happens. Below are some of the things that can play a role — though limits are evaluated holistically and may vary.

Deposits held in Mercury

Your account limit is based on a combination of the cash balance you hold in your checking, savings, or treasury accounts, alongside things like your Mercury history and activity. Because of this, the best way to have your credit limit reevaluated is by adding to and using your Mercury accounts regularly.

Deposits held in linked business accounts

We may consider balances in externally linked business accounts (connected via Plaid) when determining your IO credit limit. These balances can support your credit eligibility, but cash held in your Mercury account carries more weight.

Note: We do not currently underwrite credit limits based on balances in other Mercury accounts linked to your profile.

Choosing which linked accounts contribute to your credit limit

If you want to exclude your linked business accounts from impacting your overall credit limit, update your IO account settings on the credit page. At the moment, you can only include or exclude all linked business accounts as a whole.

Linked business account reconnection

If your linked business accounts lose their connection to Mercury, we’ll send you an email and give you 7 days to reconnect your account before changing your credit limit.

Financial statement underwriting

Eligible customers can work with our underwriting team to determine a custom limit based on your company’s full financial picture. Customers with limits based on financial statements will work with the underwriting team on a quarterly basis to reevaluate limits based on their latest company performance. To learn more about financial statement underwriting and see if you qualify, email help@mercury.com.

Requesting higher limits

Limits are reevaluated monthly, but may be evaluated more frequently if there’s a significant drop in your Mercury balance. This means that your limit will naturally increase as your business grows.

  • For account-level limits across your IO account, head to your Credit Card page and click Request a Limit Increase. Your request will be sent to our Credit team for review.
  • For card-level limits, head to your Cards page to locate the card that needs editing. More details can be found here.

FAQs

How are IO limits reviewed or increased?

IO limits are automatically reviewed by Mercury’s underwriting team, typically monthly. As your balances and account activity grow, your limit can increase without a manual request.

Customers with limits based on financial statements will work with the underwriting team on a quarterly basis to reevaluate limits based on their latest company performance.

If you need a faster review, an admin can select “Request a Limit Increase” from the top-right of the Credit page.

Can I choose which linked accounts affect my IO limit?

Yes. From your IO settings, you can include or exclude linked external business accounts from your credit-limit calculation. Cash held within Mercury generally supports higher limits than balances held elsewhere.

How can I restore my IO access if it was paused?

You can request reinstatement in your dashboard under Accounts → Credit Card → “Request Reinstatement”. If you don’t see this option or the option is greyed out, you will need to have an admin on the account do it or reach out to our support team for assistance.

My IO limit doesn’t match my deposits (if you’re on our introductory IO card))

With the introductory IO card, your spending limit equals your available cash balance, up to a maximum of $5,000.

Here’s how it works:

  • Each day, our system checks your Mercury deposits and sets your IO card limit to match them
  • Throughout the day, you can spend up to that amount on your IO card(s)
  • Around midnight we automatically deduct your total IO card spending for that day from your checking account
  • The remaining balance in your checking account becomes your new IO limit for the next 24-hour cycle
  • Pending transactions will also impact your available cash balance
  • The one exception is your organization’s first deposit (via ACH, wire, RTP, or check) — we recalculate your limit shortly after it posts, rather than waiting for the next daily update

  • Customizable reports and analytics on spending patterns
  • Business credit building with no personal guarantee
  • Fast and simple onboarding

Determining IO account limits

We use the same underwriting framework as our standard IO program, tailored for IO-only customers.

To evaluate your business, we look at:

  • Your application and financial statements
  • At least 90 days of balance and transaction data from your connected account(s)

Your credit limit adjusts based on your linked balances and other financial indicators. It may adjust over time based on your spending and financial performance.

Linking external accounts

You’ll need to connect at least one external bank account to:

  • Share transaction and balance data for underwriting
  • Set up autopay for IO repayment
  • Receive cashback
Linked business account reconnection

If your linked business accounts lose their connection to Mercury, we’ll send you an email and give you 7 days to reconnect your account before changing your credit limit.

How repayment works

  • IO balances are automatically repaid from your connected account monthly
    • You can view and edit your autopay schedule from your homepage
  • Repayments may take up to 3 business days to post
  • You must maintain one primary connected account at all times
  • To switch accounts, connect a new one first

After approval

Once your application is approved, you’ll get a confirmation email. You can also check your status anytime by logging in to your dashboard.

Once approved, you’ll be able to:

  • Activate and ship your IO card
  • Add team members and set spend limits
  • View transactions, manage cards, and update accounts from your dashboard

Managing team and permissions

From the Team page, you can add users to your IO-only account. This lets you issue them IO cards and control what they can do in the dashboard based on their role:

Admins have full access to the dashboard. They can issue and manage cards, view and categorize transactions, and manage team members and permissions.

Employees can be issued IO cards and view their own activity. They can’t access company financials, manage team members, or change account settings.

FAQs

What will my limit be?

Your IO credit limit is based on balances held in your linked accounts as well as information provided during the application progress. It may adjust over time based on your spending and financial performance.

We’ll provide updates to your limits via email or log into your dashboard anytime to review limit details.

Does IO build business credit?

Yes. Mercury reports IO payment activity to Experian, Equifax and Dun & Bradstreet. You can read more about credit reporting here.

How long does underwriting take after submitting financials?

You should hear back from our team within 2 business days. A member of our team will be in touch via email.

Are there any fees, spend requirements, or hidden conditions with the new product?

We don’t charge annual fees on IO cards, and because you’ll pay off your IO card automatically each month, you won’t incur any interest. However, we do charge an international transaction fee of up to 3% on non-USD IO card transactions. Note that this fee won’t be returned, even if your original transaction is refunded.

Can I remove my primary bank account connection?

No. You must keep one primary account connected at all times. To switch, connect a new one first.

Do I need a Mercury account to get cashback?

No. Cashback is sent to your connected external account. You can view a history of this cashback from your homepage as “Cashback deposit”.

Is this available to everyone?

For more details on opening an IO-only account, contact bd@mercury.com.

Can I connect my account manually?

No. Connecting an external account can only be done via Plaid. If your bank is not selectable from the dropdown, we’re currently unable to support a connection (including a manual connection via micro-deposit).

Creating and sending NDAs

Admins can create, send, sign, and track mutual non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) directly in Mercury on web. You can send an NDA to an existing payment recipient or someone you haven’t yet added as a recipient.

Mercury’s mutual NDA is based on Common Paper’s standard mutual NDA terms.

Create an NDA

You can start a new NDA from either the Recipients page or the Agreements tab in the Documents & Data section of your Mercury account.

From the Recipients page
  • Go to Payments and open the Recipients page
  • Find the NDAs column and click the + for the recipient you’d like to send an NDA to
  • Follow the prompts to create your NDA
From Documents & Data

Use this option if you want to create an NDA for someone who isn’t already a payment recipient.

  • Go to Documents & Data and click on the Agreements tab
  • Click +Create NDA
  • Follow the prompts to create your NDA

Complete your NDA

The NDA flow walks you through the information needed to create the agreement. You’ll also see a live PDF preview before sending it.

1. Configure the NDA

Enter the basic terms of the agreement:

  • Purpose: The reason for the NDA from the dropdown
  • Effective date: The date the agreement takes effect
  • Term length: How long the NDA remains in effect in years
  • Term of confidentiality: How long the confidentiality obligations remain in effect
  • Changes to standard terms (optional): Any adjustments you’d like to make to the Common Paper standard terms

Note: Mercury can’t advise you on which choice of law, jurisdiction, term length, or other legal terms to select, or whether the standard terms are appropriate for your situation. Consider consulting your legal counsel if you have questions about these choices.

2. Confirm your company information

Some company information will be filled in automatically. Review it and make any necessary changes:

  • Company legal name
  • Sender’s address
  • Governing law
  • Jurisdiction

Governing law determines which laws apply to the NDA, while jurisdiction determines where disputes related to the NDA may be brought.

3. Add the signatory

Enter the name and title of the person at your company who will sign the NDA.

4. Add the recipient

Select an existing recipient or create a new one and provide the following:

  • Full legal name
  • Street address
  • Company name
  • Title
5. Review and send

Review the information you’ve entered and the live PDF preview of the NDA.

Before sending, you can also:

  • Add someone as a CC if they need to receive the agreement
  • Sign the NDA before sending it to the recipient
  • When everything looks correct, click Send NDA

Sign an NDA

Each signer receives a secure link to review and electronically sign the NDA in their browser. Recipients don’t need a Mercury account to review or sign the agreement.

Once everyone has signed, the NDA is fully executed and the parties are notified.

Track and download NDAs

You can keep track of NDAs you’ve sent from Mercury:

  • On the Recipients page, check the NDAs column to see the status of an NDA associated with a recipient
  • In Documents & Data, open the Agreements tab to see all of your NDAs and open an NDA to view its details or download multiple NDAs at once

About the NDA terms

Mercury’s mutual NDA uses Common Paper’s standard mutual NDA terms. The standard agreement includes terms covering:

  • The purpose of the disclosure
  • What qualifies as confidential information
  • Treatment of confidential information provided “as-is”
  • Confirmation that the NDA doesn’t transfer intellectual property rights

Mercury doesn’t provide legal advice. You are responsible for determining whether the NDA and its terms are appropriate for your situation. Consider consulting your legal counsel if you have questions about the agreement or the terms you select.

Company address requirements

Having valid addresses on file is crucial for account verification, complying with regulatory requirements, and sending you things like physical cards. Below are the addresses we collect, reasons why, and requirements for each.

Company legal address

Your legal address is the address from your formation documents and the billing address for your cards that appears on your bank documents.

Company physical address

Your physical address is where you and your team work day-to-day. We may ask you to verify this if your legal address is a P.O. box, virtual address, mail center, or registered agent.

We collect this information to better understand our customers and meet legal and regulatory requirements. We’ll accept:

  • A verifiable residential address (if your company doesn’t have an office yet)

We don’t accept a P.O. box, virtual address, commercial mail receiving agency, mail center, or registered agent address.

We may also request documentation to verify your address. Documents must clearly show the company name, or the beneficial owner’s name, along with the full physical address (including unit numbers if applicable).

Accepted documents include (but aren’t limited to):

Company mailing address

Your mailing address must be a physical address, contain no special characters, and be deliverable according to the United States Postal Service. If you’re running into issues with the deliverability of your mailing address, here are steps to troubleshoot.

Company structures Mercury supports

Mercury supports most U.S.-registered business structures, including LLCs, corporations, partnerships, and non-profits. This article covers what each structure is generally used for, what Mercury needs from you at application, and which structures we can’t currently support.

What every structure needs, regardless of type

No matter how your business is set up, Mercury requires:

  • A state-filed formation document confirming your business is registered with a Secretary of State or similar authority (Articles of Organization, Articles of Incorporation, or a Certificate of Formation)
  • An IRS-issued EIN document. Read more about EINs here
  • Identification for anyone with 25% or more ownership, and for at least one person with operating control of the business

See Eligibility and requirements for opening a Mercury account for the full list.

Supported structures

LLC (Limited Liability Company)

An LLC is typically used by founders who want personal liability protection without the formality of a corporation — you file Articles of Organization with your state, and profits generally pass through to your personal tax return. It’s the most common structure among Mercury customers, from single-member freelance businesses to multi-member startups.

Mercury supports both single-member and multi-member LLCs. Since an LLC is a distinct legal entity, we’ll ask for your Articles of Organization (or state equivalent) and identification for any member who owns 25% or more of the company.

C Corporation

A C Corp is the standard structure for venture-backed and scaling companies — it issues stock, supports multiple classes of shares, and is taxed as its own entity separate from its owners. Most investors require this structure before writing a check.

Because a C Corp is registered by filing Articles of Incorporation, we’ll ask for that document along with identification for beneficial owners and your operating leadership.

S Corporation

An S Corp isn’t a separate legal entity — it’s a tax election made by an LLC or corporation to pass income, losses, and credits directly to shareholders and avoid corporate-level tax. Businesses often elect S Corp status once they’re profitable and want to reduce self-employment tax.

Since an S Corp is built on top of an underlying LLC or corporation, Mercury asks for that entity’s formation document, not a separate S Corp filing.

Partnerships and LLPs

General partnerships, limited partnerships, and limited liability partnerships (LLPs) are used when two or more people share ownership and want to define how profits, losses, and management responsibilities are split. Professional service firms — law firms, accounting firms, consultancies — often use LLPs specifically because they limit each partner’s liability for the others’ actions.

To open an account, your partnership needs to be registered with the state (for example, through a Certificate of Limited Partnership), and we’ll need ownership and ID information for each partner who meets the 25% threshold.

Note: partnerships and LLPs currently aren’t eligible for a Mercury Treasury account, though they can hold a standard Mercury Business account.

Non-profit corporations

Non-profit corporations are used by organizations pursuing a charitable, educational, religious, or other mission-driven purpose rather than distributing profit to owners. They’re formed the same way a for-profit corporation is — by filing Articles of Incorporation — which is why Mercury can support them even though ownership works differently.

Since non-profits don’t have traditional owners, we’ll ask for identification for board members or officers with significant operating control instead of beneficial owners.

Note: non-profits currently aren’t eligible for a Mercury Treasury account, though they can hold a standard Mercury Business account.

Structures we can’t currently support

  • Sole proprietorships — because they aren’t registered with a state, there’s no formation document to verify, which is required for every Mercury account
  • Trusts

Mercury also can’t open accounts for money services businesses (MSBs) or businesses operating in adult entertainment, cannabis, or internet gambling, regardless of company structure. See Eligibility and requirements for opening a Mercury account for the complete list.

Choosing a structure

If you haven’t yet formed your business, choosing the right structure depends on factors like liability protection, how you want to be taxed, and whether you plan to raise investment. This decision is best made with an attorney or accountant who can advise on your specific situation.
