Eligibility and requirements for opening a Mercury account

To open a Mercury account, your company must be formed and registered in the United States or a U.S. territory. This article covers who is eligible to apply, what information is required, which business types Mercury can and cannot support, and how beneficial ownership works.

Information required

To complete the application, you’ll need to provide the following:

  • Your business’s legal name
  • The industry your company serves and a description of what your business does
  • A physical address where you operate — this can be commercial or residential; in some cases, documentation may be required
  • Your company’s source of funds
  • Details about your current or planned U.S. operations
  • Business documents (see Gathering your documents for a full breakdown)
  • For each beneficial owner, you’ll also provide the physical address where that person currently lives. PO boxes, mail drops, and commercial mail-receiving or virtual address services can’t be used. We may ask for a document to verify the address. This is separate from your company’s address requirements.

Supported businesses

Mercury supports most U.S.-registered companies, including those founded by people living outside the U.S.

Mercury cannot open accounts for the following industries:

  • Money services businesses (MSBs) and crypto exchanges
  • Businesses operating in adult entertainment, cannabis, or internet gambling
  • Trusts

Mercury supports many crypto and Web3 businesses, including startups, DAOs, and funds. Eligible businesses can use their Mercury account to send funds to third-party crypto exchanges, but Mercury accounts can only hold fiat currency, not cryptocurrency.

Additional industry types may require more information, and eligibility is determined following a full review of your application.

International founders

Mercury supports U.S. companies with founders from around the world. You do not need to be a U.S. citizen or resident to apply.

To be eligible, your business must:

  • Be formed and registered in the United States or a U.S. territory
  • Have existing or planned operations in the U.S.
  • Have a U.S. or international address for its principal place of business — residential addresses are accepted, but registered agent addresses, P.O. boxes, and UPS Store addresses are not

Mercury cannot currently support accounts for businesses with founders living in certain countries and regions. See the full list here.

Beneficial owners

Beneficial ownership refers to individuals who directly or indirectly own 25% or more of a company. Mercury is required to collect information about all beneficial owners during the application — not just the primary applicant.

Who qualifies as a beneficial owner

Any person with 25% or more ownership must be listed, whether their ownership is direct or passes through a parent company or holding entity.

If your business is partially or fully owned by another legal entity — such as a holding company or LLC — you cannot list that entity as the beneficial owner. You must identify the individuals who own that entity, tracing ownership up the chain until you reach an individual.

Examples:

  • If four individuals each own 25% of your company, all four must be listed
  • If a holding company owns 50% of your company and two people each own 50% of that holding company, both individuals must be listed — each holds 25% passthrough ownership
  • Every company will have at least one beneficial owner. The total number will depend on your ownership structure

In addition to beneficial owners, you’ll identify one person who has significant responsibility for managing the company’s operations. This is typically the CEO, CFO, or COO, but can be anyone in a senior leadership role. This person will be granted admin access to the account once the application is approved.

Note: Anyone listed as a beneficial owner and/or team member on the account must be 18 years of age or older.

Documents required

You’ll need to submit supporting documentation for your business and each beneficial owner. For a breakdown of what’s accepted and how to prepare your documents, see Gathering your documents.

Getting an EIN

Your Employer Identification Number (EIN) is a number issued by the United States Internal Revenue Service (IRS) and used for filing your federal payroll taxes. You may also see it referred to as Federal Employer Identification Number (FEIN).

When you apply for a new Mercury account, you’ll need to provide one of the following documents to verify your EIN:

  • Form CP575
  • Form 147c
  • A completed SS-4 (filed and/or returned)

Still waiting on your EIN? You can apply for Mercury with your completed Form SS-4. Once approved, you can start using your account right away. Just provide your official EIN within 90 days.

Where to get an EIN

Reapplying if your Mercury application has been denied

Our team reviews each application in careful detail. While we cannot disclose specifics as to why a particular application was approved or rejected, decisions are based on whether the information provided adheres to our eligibility requirements.

If you have additional information that wasn’t previously available during your initial application, you are welcome to reapply. While we can’t guarantee an approval, we’ll take the new information into consideration and get back to you after we’ve reviewed your new application.

If you choose to reapply, please carefully review our eligibility requirements and ensure you have all the required documentation, as you may have missed something the first time. The requirements are listed below, and are described in greater detail here:

  • Your company’s formation documents (such as your Articles of Incorporation).
  • For US companies only: an IRS-issued EIN document (form CP575, form 147c, completed SS-4, or a screenshot of your EIN number confirmation from the IRS’s website may be acceptable on a temporary basis in place of an EIN).
  • An international passport or US government ID for each founder or majority owner of the company.

Once you’ve confirmed the above and you’re ready to reapply, simply log into your denied application, click your initials in the top right-hand corner of your dashboard and select Settings. Click on your organization’s name in the top-left and select Apply for a new account to get started.

Verifying your U.S. business operations

Some businesses without physical ties to the U.S. need to verify their U.S. operations. If your business doesn’t have a U.S. workplace, a beneficial owner living in the U.S., or a beneficial owner with a U.S.-issued ID, Mercury may request additional verification during your application or via email after your account is approved.

Proof of U.S. operations

Your business must have a legitimate connection to the U.S. Any of the following documents can serve as proof and must match deposit or payment activity in your Mercury account:

  • Record of a sale to a U.S.-based customer (a screenshot works)
  • Invoice or contract showing your relationship with a U.S.-based customer, partner, or supplier
  • Signed SAFE agreement
  • Signed investment agreement between both parties
  • Employment documentation for a U.S.-based employee, such as an employment agreement or W-2, showing the employee’s full legal name and residential address.
  • Payroll records showing payments to U.S.-based employees
  • Signed lease or rental agreement for a physical office or coworking space in the U.S. Registered agent, virtual, P.O. box, or mailbox addresses cannot be accepted.
  • Utility bill from the last 90 days
  • Your business’s most recent federal tax return with the IRS

Businesses that don’t operate in the U.S.

U.S. operations are required to maintain your Mercury account. If you don’t operate in the U.S., don’t plan to, or don’t have qualifying documentation, your account may be locked or eventually closed.

A note about emails from Mercury

As a general rule, look out for emails from Mercury with [Action Required] in the subject line. We typically use these emails when we need you to confirm information or take action related to your account.

Mercury is a fintech company, not an FDIC-insured bank. Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Members FDIC.

What happens after I submit my Mercury business account application?

You should receive a decision on your Mercury application quickly — usually within 0–2 business days.

Confirming your application was submitted

You’ll know your application was successfully submitted by checking the timeline on the right-hand side of your screen on web. A status of “In Review” means your application has been received and is being reviewed by our team. You can track your application status at any time by logging into Mercury on web or the mobile app.

What to expect during review

In some cases, Mercury may need additional documents or information before a decision can be made. If so, we’ll send a request to the email address(es) on file — be sure to check your inbox (including your spam folder) regularly.

If 7 business days have passed and you haven’t heard from us, double-check your inbox and spam folder to make sure we’re not waiting on additional information from you.

Expediting your review (optional)

You can expedite your application review by connecting an external bank account. This step is entirely optional. External account linking is only available through Plaid — if your bank isn’t listed, linking won’t be possible. Learn more about account linking here.

Things you can do while you wait

You don’t have to wait until your application is approved to get started. You can complete the following steps while your application is in review:

  • Set up a virtual debit card or request a physical one be shipped — it will be ready to use/shipped once your account is approved.
  • Invite team members and assign them roles — they’ll be notified and granted access once your account is approved.
  • Enable two-factor authentication (2FA) — this is required for all Mercury accounts. You can set it up through the Mercury app or an authenticator app of your choice.
  • Edit basic profile details by clicking your initials in the top-right corner of your dashboard.

Note: To make any changes to your application or submitted documents, contact our support team. If reaching out by email, please write in from the email address on file.

Deleting a pending application

You can delete applications that haven’t been submitted yet by logging into your Mercury account. Click your initials in the top-right corner of your dashboard on web, select Settings, and scroll down to Delete Application.

For applications that are pending review, please reach out to our team.

Business: Expense Management

Automatically forward receipt emails to Mercury

Mercury will automatically match receipts to the right transaction when you email or forward them to receipts@mercury.com. To make this process even easier, you can set up forwarding rules in your email account to automatically forward receipts from your card transactions to Mercury.

Setting up email forwarding in Gmail

  • Add receipts@mercury.com as a forwarding address in Gmail here
  • Find a receipt email associated with your IO card that you expect to see repeatedly (for example, the Square receipt for the coffee place around the corner that you go to every day)
  • Open the settings for that message and select Filter messages like these (see Gmail’s instructions)
  • Select the option to forward emails like these and select receipts@mercury.com from the dropdown (see Gmail’s instructions)
  • Select Create filter

Verifying autoforwarding with Gmail

  • After selecting Create filter you will receive both an email and a notification within your Mercury account
  • Follow the link in the email or head to mercury.com and login
  • Select your Tasks page and click the item regarding allowing auto-forward receipts
  • You will be taken to your Profile page in Settings - from here, select Allow

This will only be necessary the first time you setup an automatic forwarding rule with your Gmail email.

Automatically match receipts to transactions

To make receipt management faster and easier, we’ll automatically match receipts to the right transaction when you upload them on the Transactions page or forward them to receipts@mercury.com.

Setting receipt policies

To control when employees are required to upload receipts for transactions, configure your receipt policy from the Policies tab under Team Spend.

Learn more about managing card spend policies ↗.

Uploading receipts for auto-matching

You can upload receipts for automatic matching in a few ways:

  • From the Transactions page
  • From your email inbox
  • From the mobile app
  • From your phone via text

For reimbursements, follow the steps outlined here.

From the Transactions page

You can upload one or multiple receipts for auto-matching from the Transactions page by clicking Match Receipts. You can upload PDF, PNG, or JPEG files.

Uploading via email

After you make a transaction that requires a receipt, you’ll receive an email reminder to upload one. You can reply directly to that email with the receipt and it will be added to the transaction.

Set up email forwarding

Automatically or manually send receipt emails to Mercury so they can be matched to your transactions. You can forward receipt emails or send them as attachments to receipts@mercury.com from:

  • The email address associated with your Mercury account
  • Any email address added to your Mercury profile

Here’s how to add an email address for forwarding:

  • Head to Settings > My Profile
  • Scroll down to “Email receipt matching” and click Add
  • Enter your preferred email address and click Add Email
  • An email will be sent to that address prompting you to verify the email

Tip: Set up forwarding rules in your email account to automatically forward receipts from your card transactions to Mercury. Learn more here.

Connect your Gmail account

Connect Gmail to have receipt emails detected and matched to transactions automatically — no forwarding required. Learn more about Integrating with Gmail.

When forwarding a receipt, if the matching transaction already has a receipt, the new one will be added as an additional attachment. If multiple transactions match, the one without a receipt will be prioritized.

Through receipt texting

If your organization has SMS receipt collection enabled, you can receive text reminders for missing receipts and simply reply with a photo to automatically attach it to the correct transaction. You can also text receipt photos at any time. Learn more.

Matching receipts to all transactions

You can auto-match uploaded or emailed receipts to any transaction you have access to, not just your own. This is useful for managers, bookkeepers/accountants, and admins who collect receipts on behalf of their team. Here’s how:

  • On upload: Toggle Match receipts for all transactions from the “Match Receipts” upload modal on the Transactions page
  • Default setting: Go to Settings > My Profile to enable this as your default for both uploads and receipts emailed to receipts@mercury.com

Note: This setting only applies to transactions you can already view. It doesn’t grant new permissions or access.

Resolving matching errors

After we process and match receipts to their transactions, we’ll email you if any issues arise with a link to the Transactions page so you can reattempt your upload or upload receipts manually.

To reduce matching errors, follow these guidelines:

  • Send the receipt from a verified email. We only support automatic receipt matching when receipts are submitted from email addresses you’ve approved for forwarding. You can confirm, verify, and edit these email addresses from Settings > My Profile under “Emails for receipt or expense forwarding”.
  • Ensure the person submitting receipts is the person who made the transaction. In order to match the receipt, the user that made the purchase needs to be the one that submits the receipt.
  • Use a Mercury card. We cannot match receipts to transactions made with a non-Mercury card.
  • Ensure the receipt is for a transaction within the last year. For any purchases made more than 1 year ago, please manually upload the receipt.
  • Stick to one charge transaction per receipt. If you have multiple transactions on one receipt, it may cause a matching error. This also applies to:
    • Transactions charged at different dates (e.g. a single order that’s shipped and charged at different times)
    • Recurring payments or subscriptions
  • Invoices can be matched only if the charge has already been paid. Ensure the invoice shows the final settled amount, including any taxes, fees, or additional charges.
  • Avoid submitting split charges or charges across multiple cards. If you had a transaction that was charged across multiple dates or multiple cards, you may encounter a matching error.
  • Forward the original email directly to receipts@mercury.com to avoid attachment issues. Long email chains or multiple forwards can distort attachments, making them unreadable. Keep the email chain short and direct for the best results.
Receipt image guidelines:
  • Avoid tilted or angled photos. Ensure paper receipts lie flat on a table and photos are taken straight on to avoid any visual distortion that makes optical character recognition challenging.
  • Show all corners of receipts in photos. Avoid cropping the edges of the receipts and ensure photos show all four corners.
  • Ensure screenshots include dates and all relevant information.

Automatically match receipts with Gmail

When you connect your Gmail account to Mercury, incoming receipt emails are automatically detected and matched to the correct card transaction. No forwarding or manual uploads needed.

Connect your Gmail account

To set up automatic receipt matching, connect your Gmail account from your profile settings.

  • Go to Settings > My Profile
  • Scroll down to “Automatic matching via Gmail”
  • Click Connect to Gmail
  • You’ll be redirected to Google — sign in and select the account you want to connect
  • Review the permissions and allow Mercury access — this gives Mercury access to basic details like your name and email so it can detect receipts
  • Select what Mercury can access, then confirm
  • You’ll be returned to Mercury, where you’ll see that automatic matching via Gmail has been enabled

This is also where you can manage connected Gmail accounts — add additional accounts, edit existing ones, or resync any accounts that need attention. Mercury will flag accounts that are successfully connected or require resyncing.

How automatic receipt matching works

Once your Gmail account is connected, Mercury automatically detects receipt emails as they arrive and matches them to the correct card transaction.

To view a matched receipt:

  • Go to the Transactions page
  • Click into a transaction
  • The attached receipt will appear, labeled “auto-added from Gmail”

Find receipts manually

If you want to search for a receipt on a specific transaction, you can trigger a Gmail search directly from Mercury.

  • Click into a transaction on the Transactions page
  • Click Find attachments using Gmail
  • Mercury will open Gmail and run a search using pre-set filters to surface the relevant receipt email

FAQs

What can Mercury see in my Gmail inbox?

Mercury only scans your inbox for receipt-related emails. It does not read, store, or access other email content. The connection uses Google’s standard OAuth permissions, which you review and approve during setup.

If you have questions about how Mercury handles your data, refer to Mercury’s Privacy Policy (https://mercury.com/legal/privacy) for full details.

Does this work with email providers other than Gmail?

Automatic receipt matching currently works with Gmail only. Other email providers are not supported at this time.

What happens if a receipt doesn’t match to a transaction?

If Mercury can’t automatically match a receipt, it won’t be attached to a transaction. You can still find the receipt manually by clicking Find attachments using Gmail from within the transaction. Mercury will open Gmail with pre-set search filters to help you locate the relevant email.

How do I disconnect my Gmail account?

To disconnect a Gmail account:

  • Go to Settings > My Profile
  • Scroll down to “Automatic matching via Gmail”
  • Select the account you want to remove and follow the prompts to disconnect it

Once disconnected, Mercury will stop scanning that inbox for new receipts. Previously matched receipts will remain attached to their transactions.

How often does Mercury check my inbox?

  • When you first connect Gmail, Mercury scans the last 7 days of emails
  • After that, your inbox is checked once per hour for new receipt emails

Budgets: Setting up team spend

Budgets help you manage team spending by setting limits on how much team members can spend, where they can spend it, and for how long. You can create budgets for expenses like meals, travel, or office supplies, assign them to team members, and track spending from your Mercury dashboard.

How budgets work

Each budget has a per-person spending limit and rules for how it can be used. When creating a budget, you can configure:

  • Name and icon: Identify what the budget is for
  • Spending limit: Set how much each assigned team member can spend
  • Frequency: Choose whether the budget is one-time or recurring
  • Start and end dates: Set when the budget is available, starting today with no end date by default
  • Spending controls: Restrict spending to specific merchants or merchant types
  • Team members: Assign the budget to specific people, all team members, or newly invited team members

Budgets refill according to their frequency and become unavailable when their funds are exhausted or they expire. You can edit, reassign, or archive budgets as your team’s needs change.

Spending controls

Every budget includes a per-person spending limit. You can use the limit on its own or add restrictions:

  • Spend limit only: Transactions are declined if the budget doesn’t have enough funds available
  • Allow specific merchants: Only transactions from approved merchants are allowed
  • Allow specific merchant types: Only transactions from approved merchant types, such as restaurants or airlines, are allowed

Transactions that don’t meet a budget’s spending controls are declined, even if funds are available.

Budgets and cards

Budgets work with both Mercury debit and IO cards. Team members need at least one card to make purchases from their assigned budgets, but multiple budgets can share the same card.

When a card has multiple budgets, Mercury automatically assigns each transaction to the most relevant eligible budget based on the purchase details.

If a team member doesn’t have a card, you can issue one when creating a budget. If their existing card already has a spending limit, you can choose to keep that limit as a separate budget or replace it with the new budget.

Creating budgets

Admins and users with permission to manage spend can create and manage budgets from the Team Spend section of their Mercury dashboard.

Setting up budgets for the first time

If you haven’t created any budgets yet, select Team Spend from the left sidebar. You’ll be guided through setting up your team’s spending, including inviting team members, setting team policies, configuring cards, and setting up reimbursements.

Creating additional budgets

You can create more budgets at any time from the Budgets page under Team Spend.

  • Select Team Spend > Budgets from the left sidebar, then click Create budget
  • Choose one or more budget templates to customize, or start from scratch
  • Enter a budget name, icon, per-person spending limit, and optional description
  • Choose a spending control
  • Assign team members, set start and end dates, and optionally select a spending category
  • Review the budget preview on the right, then click Next
  • Choose which cards team members will use for their budgets:
    • For team members without cards, issue a new virtual or physical card
    • For team members with existing cards, assign the budget to an existing card or issue a new one
  • If an existing card has its own spending limit, choose how to handle it:
    • Convert existing limit into a budget: Keep the existing limit as a separate budget alongside the new budget
    • Replace existing limit with budgets: Remove the existing card limit and apply only the new budget rules
  • Review the budget details, assigned team members, and any new cards, then click Create budget

Assigning budgets to team members

You can assign an existing budget to a team member directly from the Team Spend home page.

  • Select Team Spend from the left sidebar
  • Click Assign spend in the upper-right corner
  • Choose an existing budget from the Select a budget dropdown
  • Click Next and follow the prompts to complete the assignment

You can also select Create a card or Create a budget from the Assign budgets window if you need to set up either one first.

Reviewing and managing budgets

You can review team spending from the Team Spend home page or see more detailed budget information from the Budgets page.

Reviewing team spending

The Team Spend home page provides an overview of your team’s spending, including:

  • Tasks requiring your attention
  • Total spending over the last 30 or 90 days, grouped by category
  • Summaries of budgets, spend policies, and reimbursements

You can also invite team members or assign existing budgets from this page.

Reviewing individual budgets

Select Team Spend > Budgets from the left sidebar to view your allocated budgets and spending activity.

The Budgets page includes two tabs:

  • Employee budgets: View existing budgets, spending limits, spend cycles, and assigned team members. Select a budget to review individual spending or add team members
  • Team members: View each team member’s assigned budgets and how much they’ve spent from each

You can also customize an individual team member’s spending limit, edit budgets, or archive budgets as needed.

Using budgets as a team member

Team members can spend from their assigned budgets using their Mercury cards or by submitting reimbursements.

They can also manage which budgets their expenses are assigned to:

  • Transactions: Review a transaction and reassign it to another budget from the Transactions page. If the reassignment would cause the new budget to exceed its limit, admin approval is required
  • Reimbursements: Select which budget a reimbursement should draw from when submitting a request

Managing budgets on mobile

You can view and use budgets in the Mercury mobile app for iOS and Android, but budgets can’t be created or edited from mobile. To create or edit budgets, use Mercury from a web browser.

Team members can use the mobile app to:

  • View assigned budgets, remaining balances, and recent activity
  • See which budget a transaction or reimbursement was assigned to
  • Add or update budgets on eligible transactions and reimbursements, though some changes may require admin approval
  • View budgets connected to their cards

Admins can also:

  • View budgets and spending across team members
  • Review team members’ cards and connected budgets
  • Assign budgets when issuing cards
  • Add or update budgets on eligible team member transactions

FAQs

Can I change a budget’s frequency after it’s created?

No. You can edit other budget settings, but not its frequency. To change how often a budget recurs, you’ll need to delete the existing budget and create a new one.

Can I customize an individual team member’s spending limit?

Yes. Open the budget and select a team member to review their spending and recent transactions. Click Customize to change their spending limit for the current cycle or all future cycles.

Can I apply multiple categories to a budget?

No. You can set one default category per budget, which is automatically applied to transactions for accounting purposes.

You can still change the category on individual transactions. If a budget covers different types of expenses, consider leaving its default category unset.

How does Mercury decide which budget a transaction belongs to?

If a card has one budget, transactions are automatically assigned to it.

If a card has multiple budgets, Mercury first checks which budgets are eligible based on their available funds and spending controls. It then uses transaction details, including the merchant, merchant type, and amount, to choose the most relevant budget.

Mercury also considers previous transaction reassignments to improve future matching.

If no budget is eligible, the transaction is declined.

Can I reassign a transaction to another budget?

Yes. Open the transaction from the Transactions page and select a different budget from the details panel.

If the reassignment would cause the new budget to exceed its limit, an admin must approve the change before it takes effect.

Enforcing spend policies with automatic card locking

Automatic card locking helps enforce your company’s spend policies by locking a cardholder’s card when a policy violation goes unresolved for a set number of days. This gives cardholders a clear deadline to resolve issues — like adding a receipt or transaction category — before losing access to their card.

Setting up automatic card locking

  • Go to Team Spend > Policies
  • Under Automatic card locking, click Enable
  • Configure the number of days a violation can remain unresolved before the card is locked
  • Optionally, create exemptions for specific employees or departments
  • Click Save to apply changes
What cardholders see

Cardholders can view lock warnings and locked card status from the Cards page on web and mobile.

  • If a violation is upcoming or unresolved, a warning icon appears on the card
  • If the card is locked, a notice indicates that the card is locked until policy violations are resolved
Notifications

Cardholders receive email notifications about upcoming and active card locks, depending on their notification settings:

  • 24 hours before a lock: an email warning that the card will be locked
  • At time of lock: an email confirming the card has been locked, with a link to resolve violations

To adjust notification preferences, go to Settings > Notifications.

Unlocking a card

To unlock a card, the cardholder must resolve all outstanding policy violations.

  • Go to the Cards page on mobile or web and click into the locked card
  • Click Unlock
  • Complete the requirements shown — for example, uploading a missing receipt or adding a transaction category

Non-admin cardholders can’t unlock a card themselves without resolving the violation — an admin can also manually unlock a card from the Cards page.

Requesting a receipt exception

If a receipt is required but unavailable, cardholders can request an exception instead of uploading one.

  • Click Don’t have it on the violation
  • Provide a reason for the missing receipt
  • Submit the request for admin review

If approved, a receipt will no longer be required for that transaction.

Temporary unlocks

In an emergency, a cardholder can temporarily unlock a card for 24 hours to continue using it while violations are pending resolution.

  • The first temporary unlock is self-serve
  • Any subsequent temporary unlocks must be requested and approved by an admin

Getting started with spend management

Mercury makes it easy to manage team spend without the mess. This guide will help you set up the right cards and controls to manage your team’s expenses.

Quick setup guide

Want a lightweight way to manage expenses? Here’s a simple setup most teams can start with:

  • Invite teammates to Mercury: Give them permission to spend without access to account balances or banking details
  • Set up spend policies: Set policies for card spend: receipt, category, and/or note requirements
  • Issue cards and set budgets: Create virtual or physical cards, then assign budgets for specific purposes like travel or software — Mercury sorts each purchase into the right budget automatically
  • Set up reimbursements: Allow team members to submit out of pocket expenses for reimbursements

Keep reading for the full guide to Mercury’s expense management tools, including accounting integrations, spend policies, and approvals for larger or more complex teams.

Invite your team and set permissions

The first step to enabling team spend is bringing the right people into your Mercury account, and we’ve designed that to be safe and flexible. You can invite teammates without giving them access to sensitive banking details, and assign only the visibility and permissions they need.

You can also automate access with an HR integration or manage it manually — and if you want to see exactly what they’ll experience, you can even preview what your employees can see before you officially invite them.

To get started, invite your team members and give them the right level of access.

  • Sync your HR and payroll system (like Gusto, Justworks, Deel, and more) to automatically onboard and offboard team members
  • Or invite them via email from the Team tab in your dashboard

As employees join, they’ll be automatically organized by department if you have your HR and payroll system integrated. If you invited them via email, you can add them manually to the correct department.

Set roles and permissions

Once you’ve invited your employees to Mercury, you can either choose to give them a default role (with pre-set permissions), or create custom roles with more granular permissions.

  • Default roles: Admin or Teammate
  • Custom roles: Create granular permission sets (e.g., card creation, spend approvals, accounting access, etc.)

Most users will be added as Teammates — a role designed for safe, limited access. Here’s what they can and can’t do:

  • Cards and reimbursements: Issue cards to employees and let them submit reimbursement requests
  • Visibility: Restricted from viewing account balances, routing details, or company-wide transactions
  • Access: Limited to their own cards and expenses — no visibility into other teammates’ activity

Set up budgets

Budgets let you assign a set amount of money to a specific purpose — like meals, travel, or office supplies — with rules for who can spend it, what it can be spent on, and how long it’s available. Instead of reviewing spend after the fact, you set the intent up front and Mercury routes each transaction to the right budget at the point of purchase.

  • Each budget has a per-person spend limit, a recurrence, and a list of team members it applies to
  • You can restrict spend to specific merchants or merchant types, or use the spend limit on its own
  • Budgets work with Mercury IO cards, and a single card can carry several budgets at once — Mercury assigns each purchase to the most relevant one
  • Admins and users with the manage spend permission create and manage budgets from the Team Spend page

Learn how to set up and manage budgets.

Issue cards and enable reimbursements

There are two ways team members can spend money in Mercury: by spending with their Mercury card or by submitting out-of-pocket expenses for reimbursement.

If a teammate makes recurring or predictable purchases — like travel, software, or supplies — it’s often easier to issue them a card upfront. Mercury offers both debit and credit cards, including the IO card, which lets you control spend limits and categories while earning 1.5% cashback on all credit purchases.

For one-off or unexpected expenses, reimbursement is a flexible way to keep things moving without needing to issue a card.

Issue team cards
  • Create virtual or physical cards in seconds in the Cards page of your dashboard
  • Set spending limits, lock cards to specific merchants (e.g., Figma, Google Ads), and pause access anytime
Enable reimbursements
  • Allow employees to submit out-of-pocket expenses for approval and reimbursement — They can upload receipts directly in Mercury, or simply email them to reimbursements@mercury.com.
  • Admins or managers can review and approve these requests from their dashboard

Create spend policies

Spend policies help guide employee behavior and keep your finances stay compliant and organized. In Mercury, you can set different requirements for cards and reimbursements to match your company’s needs — including requirements for receipts and expense categorization.

Require receipts
  • The IRS advises that all business expenses over $75 should have a corresponding receipt for tax filing purposes, so we’ve made it easy to require receipts in Mercury. You can also choose to require receipts for card spend
  • Employees can upload receipts directly in the app or simply forward them to receipts@mercury.com
Require categorization
  • For both reimbursements and card spend, you can create custom, employee-friendly categories so employees can specify what type of spend their transactions fall under
  • When you require categorization, employees will be prompted to set a category for certain transactions based on the rules you set, and when paired with accounting categorization rules, this will ensure they are properly coded for accounting
Simplify tracking and receipts

Your spend policies are only effective if your team can follow them. Mercury gives employees the tools to track their own spend, upload receipts, and categorize expenses — without the need for constant hand-holding. It’s a setup that saves your finance team time and reduces end-of-month surprises.

Once employees have card access and spend policies are in place, they can:

  • View their cards, limits, and recent transactions in one place
  • Upload receipts from their dashboard, forward them from email, or connect Gmail for automatic receipt scanning and matching
  • Receive SMS reminders when receipts are required and reply with a photo to submit by text
  • Easily tag expenses with the right category so your finance team can avoid guesswork

Automate your accounting

Mercury is designed to help your finance and ops teams move faster, not add more manual work. With direct integrations, custom rules, and AI-powered categorization, you can make expense data flow cleanly into your accounting system.

Connect your ERP
  • Integrate Mercury with QuickBooks, Xero, or NetSuite
  • Once you’ve integrated Mercury with your accounting software, you can import your GL codes
    • How to apply GL codes from QuickBooks
    • How to apply GL codes from Xero
    • How to import GL codes from NetSuite
  • We also recommend setting up custom categories your employees can select when submitting reimbursements or tagging card spend.
Create categorization rules

Mercury makes it easy to categorize transactions at scale by applying GL codes automatically based on rules you set.

In your accounting settings, you can create rules that map transactions based on specific attributes — like merchant, card, employee, or keyword. For example, you might automatically assign transactions from “United Airlines” to your “007 - Airfare” GL code.

Categorization rules follow a clear hierarchy — when more than one rule could apply, Mercury will use the most specific one:

  • Card-level rules
  • Employee-level rules
  • Merchant-level rules
  • Keyword-level rules

This lets you control spend categorization with precision — and ensures the right codes are applied, every time.

Use AI-powered auto-categorization

We pre-fill GL codes based on your categorization history and AI models. You can accept or overwrite them before syncing to your accounting software.

Sync transaction data to your accounting software
  • Once a transaction is ready to sync, click the “Mark as ready” action icon
  • Then click “Sync in the top right to sync the transactions you’ve marked as ready to your accounting software.

Set up approvals

The right controls give your team autonomy without sacrificing oversight. With Mercury, you can build approval flows that match your org structure and risk profile — from single-manager reviews to dual-approver setups.

  • Set approval flows for payments by navigating to the Approvals section in your team settings
  • Enable dual-approver workflows for added oversight

Managing card spend policies

As an admin, you can manage policies to control card spend from the Policies tab Team Spend.

Receipt requirements

  • Go to Team Spend > Policies
  • Click Enable in the Receipt requirement section. You will be prompted to set an amount threshold at which the receipts will be required.

The IRS advises that all business expenses over $75 should have a corresponding receipt for tax filing purposes.

  • Click Save to apply changes.
  • To make changes, click Edit or Disable to update or remove the requirement respectively.

Note: When setting up a new Mercury account, you may see a $75 receipt policy selected by default. You can adjust this policy during setup or edit or disable it later under Team Spend > Policies.

Receipt reminders

Cardholders will be notified that the policy has been added and they’ll be required to upload receipts. They’ll also get an email prompting them to upload receipts each time they complete a relevant transaction. For in-person transactions, if the cardholder has the mobile app, we’ll send them a push notification. At the end of each week, cardholders will be sent an additional email notification letting them know how many outstanding transactions still need receipts. These notifications are automatically enabled for cardholders, but they can be toggled off via Settings > Notifications.

Uploading receipts

To upload receipts, either follow the link provided in the email or push notification, or go to the Transactions page and click on the + button in the Attachments column.

Automatic receipt matching

To make staying compliant faster and easier, we’ll automatically match receipts to the right transaction when you upload them on the Transactions page or forward them to receipts@mercury.com.

Note requirement policies

  • Go to Team Spend > Policies
  • Click on Enable in the Notes requirement section. You will be prompted to set an amount threshold at which notes will be required.
  • Click Save to apply changes.
  • To make changes, click Edit or Disable to update or remove the requirement respectively.
Adding notes

To add notes on the desktop or mobile app, select the transaction and scroll to the Notes section. Similar to receipts, cardholders can go to the Transactions page and click on individual transactions to see which transactions require a note.

Category requirements for card spend

  • Go to Team Spend > Policies
  • Click on Enable in the Category requirement section
  • You will be prompted to select a dollar value, over which team members will be prompted that their transaction requires a category
  • Click Save to apply changes
  • To make changes, click Edit or Disable to update or remove the requirement respectively.

Tip: As an admin, enable automatic card locking to enforce spend policies automatically — cards lock when violations go unresolved for a set number of days. Learn more.

Category requirements for reimbursements

  • Go to Team Spend > Policies > Reimbursements
  • Click on Enable in the Category requirement section
  • You will be prompted to select a dollar value and the details of the policy enforcement under Restriction type:
    • Block will block transactions without a category
    • Allow will continue to allow reimbursement submissions with categorization, but warn your team member that it may be blocked
  • Click Save to apply changes
  • To make changes, click Edit or Disable to update or remove the requirement respectively

Receipt requirements

Enabling reimbursements

  • Click on Team Spend from your lefthand menu on Mercury web
  • Select Reimbursements > Get Started
  • Complete the steps in the enablement flow

Managing reimbursement source account

Managing rules for expense submissions

  • Navigate to Team Spend page on the lefthand menu on Mercury web
  • Select Policies and click the Reimbursements tab
  • View the list of active policies
  • Click Edit to manage an existing rule. These rules are guidelines for the expense information that team members must submit
    • Receipt requirement – Request that team members submit receipts above a custom dollar amount. You can choose to warn team members, which still allows them to submit an expense without a receipt attached, or block the submission outright if one isn’t attached.
    • Notes requirement – Same as above, you can either warn team members but still accept submissions without a note or block submission if the note isn’t included.
    • Category requirement – Require categories for expenses exceeding a custom dollar amount.

Requesting and approving spend requests

Team members can request new Mercury cards or higher spending limits on their existing cards, directly from their dashboard. Admins can review, approve, modify, or deny these requests.

This article covers how to submit and manage spend requests as a team member, and how to review them as an admin.

Submitting a spend request

Requesting a new card or a higher limit
  • From Home or the Cards page, click + Spend request. If you don’t have a card yet, click Request card
  • Under Spending method, choose an existing card or click New card. The dropdown defaults to the card you use most often
  • Enter the amount you need:
    • New card: The card’s spending limit
    • Existing card: The new total limit, not the amount to add
    • Existing card with budgets: The additional amount you need
  • Choose a Funds needed until date, or check I need these funds on a recurring basis
  • Describe why you need the funds, then click Submit request

You can also request a higher limit by opening a card and clicking the pencil icon next to its spending limit. This option isn’t available on cards with budgets or temporary limits.

New cards default to a virtual IO card if your company is eligible for IO, or a debit card otherwise. Admins can change the card type or issue a physical card when approving a request. If you need a physical card, mention it in your description.

Checking your request

Pending requests appear on your “Cards” page:

  • New card requests appear with a Requested status
  • Limit requests appear as a banner on the associated card

While a request is pending, you can click Edit request to change it or Cancel request to withdraw it.

You’ll receive an email when an admin approves or denies your request. Approved cards and updated limits appear on your “Cards” page. If you have questions about your request, reach out to an admin on file.

Reviewing spend requests as an admin

When a team member submits a spend request, you’ll receive an email notification, and the request will appear in your Tasks page for review. You can also find new card requests on the Cards page by filtering Status to Requested.

Open a request to review the amount, duration, and reason, then choose one of the following:

  • Approve: Issues the card or updates the limit as requested. For debit cards, you’ll choose which account the card draws from
  • Modify: Lets you change the details before approving. For new cards, you can change the card type, choose virtual or physical, and adjust the limit and spending controls. For existing cards, you can change the limit and how long it applies
  • Deny: Declines the request immediately and emails the team member

If the team member’s card uses budgets, you’ll approve the request by raising their individual limit in one of their budgets, or by assigning them another budget. The budget’s limit for other team members doesn’t change.

Temporary limit increases return to the card’s previous limit after the end date.

FAQs

How long does approval take?

Requests are reviewed by your company’s admins, not by Mercury. Approval times depend on your admins.

Why can’t I select a date after my card expires?

A temporary limit increase can’t last longer than the card. Choose an earlier date or request a new card.

Why don’t I see the Spend request button?

Spend requests are only available to team members with the Teammate role. If you don’t see the option, contact an admin on your account for help.

Which admin approves a request?

Any admin can approve or deny a request. Once an admin makes a decision, the request is removed from “Tasks” for everyone.

Why can’t I submit another request?

You can have one pending new card request and one pending limit request per card at a time. To submit another, cancel your existing request or wait for an admin to approve or deny it.

To make changes instead, open the request from your Cards page and click Edit request.

Can I submit or review spend requests in the Mercury mobile app?

Not yet. Spend requests aren’t currently available in the Mercury mobile app for iOS or Android. To submit, edit, or review a request, log in to Mercury from a web browser.

Team spend: “Mercury Gift” promotion terms

Eligible Mercury Business organizations may receive an ACH reimbursement of up to $10 for one eligible transaction made by an eligible IO cardholder when that transaction is categorized as “Mercury Gift” within 30 days of the user’s first IO Card being issued, regardless of whether that 30-day period extends beyond the promotion period.

How it works

  • Receive your first IO Card during the promotion period.
  • Make an eligible purchase using your IO Card.
  • Once your transaction has been posted, categorize it by selecting “Mercury Gift” as the transaction category in Mercury within 30 days of your first IO Card being issued.
  • We’ll reimburse your organization for that purchase, up to $10.

Eligibility

  • Open to eligible Mercury Business organizations participating in the promotion.
  • This promotion is available for up to five eligible team members per organization. To qualify, a team member must receive their first IO Card during the promotion period. Primary Admins are not eligible for the promotion..
  • Users must maintain an active IO Card and associated Mercury account in good standing to remain eligible.

How to Qualify

  • Limit one (1) reimbursement per eligible user.
  • Reimbursement is limited to up to $10 per eligible user, regardless of the transaction amount.
  • Make an eligible purchase using your IO Card.
  • Once your transaction has posted, categorize it as “Mercury Gift” in Mercury within 30 days of your IO card’s issuance.
  • Reimbursements will be deposited by ACH into the organization’s Mercury account.
  • Reimbursements are made to the organization, not the individual cardholder.
  • If you do not categorize an eligible transaction within 30 days of receiving your first IO Card, Mercury may automatically categorize one eligible transaction as “Mercury Gift” and apply the applicable reimbursement to the organization’s Mercury account.

Promotion Limits

  • Maximum reimbursement is $10 per eligible user.
  • Maximum reimbursement is $50 per organization (up to five eligible users).
  • This offer may not be combined with any other Mercury promotion or reimbursement unless otherwise specified.

Promotion Period

  • Promotion begins August 25, 2026, at 12:01 a.m. PT and ends September 21, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. PT, unless modified or terminated earlier by Mercury.
  • Eligible users must receive their first IO Card during the promotion period.
  • Once eligible, users have 30 days from IO Card issuance to categorize one eligible transaction as “Mercury Gift,” even if that 30-day period extends beyond the promotion end date.

Modifications & Termination

  • Mercury reserves the right to modify, suspend, or terminate this promotion at any time, including in cases of fraud, abuse, technical error, compliance with legal or regulatory obligations, or other circumstances affecting the administration or integrity of the promotion.
  • Fraudulent, abusive, or suspicious activity may result in disqualification from the promotion or other account action.
  • Mercury’s determinations regarding eligibility, qualifying transactions, reimbursements, and interpretation of these Promotion Terms are final.

Additional Terms

  • Participation in this promotion constitutes acceptance of these Promotion Terms.
  • This offer is non-transferable and has no cash value.
  • Void where prohibited or restricted by law.
  • Standard Mercury Terms of Use and the IO Corporate Charge Card Agreement apply.

Using SMS for receipt reminders and uploads

If your organization requires receipts for card transactions, you can receive SMS reminders and reply with a photo of your receipt to automatically match it to the correct transaction.

This article explains how to enable SMS receipt texting, receive receipt reminders, and submit receipts by text.

Enable SMS receipt texting

To enable SMS receipt texting:

  • Go to All Settings > Profile
  • Scroll down to “SMS receipt matching”
  • Add your country code and valid phone number
  • Click Opt In
  • You’ll receive a text message asking your to confirm SMS receipt reminders

We’ll send receipt-related text messages to the phone number listed on your Profile page.

Submit receipts by text

Once you’ve enabled SMS receipt texting, you can submit receipts in two ways.

Reply to a receipt reminder

After an in-person card transaction that requires a receipt, Mercury sends you a text reminder. Reply with a photo of your receipt, and Mercury automatically matches it to the correct transaction.

Text a receipt anytime

You can also text a receipt without waiting for a reminder.

Text receipt photos to: +1 (205) 973-5693

FAQs

Why didn’t I get a text reminder to upload a receipt for my purchase?

SMS receipt reminders are only sent for in-person card purchases. For online purchases, you’ll receive a task and be notified by email or push notification, depending on your notification preferences.

If you expected a text reminder for an in-person purchase, make sure:

  • SMS receipt matching is turned on under All Settings > Profile > SMS receipt matching
  • SMS notifications are enabled under All Settings > Notifications > Your spending
  • Your phone number is up to date in All Settings > Profile > Phone number
How do I stop SMS receipt texting?

Reply STOP to opt out of SMS messages at any time. Reply START to opt back in.

Message and data rates may apply. Mercury will never ask for passwords, one-time codes, or sensitive personal information over text. Reply STOP to opt out at any time.

How Mercury uses AI in Command (Business: Getting Started)

Mercury Command is powered by AI and designed to complete financial work for you. It retrieves information, stages actions, and executes — with your confirmation as the final step before anything changes in your account.

When you use Command, nothing ever happens without your explicit approval.

The AI’s role

When you send a message in Command, the AI interprets what you’re asking, retrieves the relevant information from your account, and prepares a response or stages an action for you to review.

The AI does the legwork — finding the right transactions, pre-filling the right fields, surfacing the right details — so that by the time you see a result, all you need to do is confirm or adjust.

Every Command response links directly to the underlying transaction, invoice, or account data behind it so you can verify the source before you act.

What the AI can see

Command authenticates through your existing Mercury session. This means it can only access the data and actions a user is already authorized to see and take in their Mercury account. There is no elevated access — if you can’t do something in the Mercury web or mobile product, Command can’t do it either.

The context shared with the AI for each session is limited by design. It includes basic session information like your first name, business name, and timezone. It does not include session cookies, authentication secrets, or API keys.

What the AI never sees

Sensitive personal and financial data is not transmitted to the AI model. This includes:

  • Card numbers
  • Social Security numbers
  • Dates of birth
  • Home addresses

When Command needs to reference something sensitive — like a card number — it passes the model a reference ID instead of the real data. The Mercury interface handles the conversion, so you see what you need to see, but the underlying data never passed through the AI.

Third-party AI providers

Mercury Command is powered by third-party AI providers. Some account data is shared with these providers to generate responses. Your conversations are not used to train their models, and sensitive financial data is never transmitted to them.

All AI vendors that power Mercury products go through a thorough security and privacy review before we engage them, and are contractually prohibited from using your data for any purpose beyond providing services to Mercury — including training their own models. We also review vendors on an ongoing basis to ensure they continue to meet our standards.

Every action requires your confirmation

Command can retrieve information and stage actions, but it cannot execute anything without your explicit approval. Before anything happens in your account, Command shows you exactly what it’s about to do and waits for you to confirm. You can also edit what’s been staged before approving.

There is no auto-approve under any circumstances.

AI features in Mercury are entirely optional. Your core account features — payments, cards, and account management — work exactly the same if you choose not to use Command.

Mercury Command overview (Business: Getting Started)

Mercury Command is a conversational interface built directly into your Mercury account. Instead of navigating between pages and dashboards, you can type what you need in plain language to get answers and take action — from checking your cash position to sending a payment to updating a card limit.

What you can do with Command

Command works across the products already in your Mercury account. You can:

  • Ask questions — check balances, find transactions, view account details and statements. Every answer is drawn from your live account data
  • Take action — send payments, freeze cards, categorize transactions, create and send invoices, and more. Command stages every action for your review first and does not execute until you confirm
  • Edit settings — update card limits, auto-transfer rules, user permissions, and similar account settings without navigating between pages
  • Verify responses — every answer links directly to the underlying transaction, invoice, or account data so you can check the source
  • Reach support — escalate any conversation and get routed to a real person on our support team without leaving the chat

Command can only perform actions that are already available to you in Mercury. It does not have elevated permissions. For example, if you have a monthly spend limit on your account, Command cannot override that permission. Every action is bound by these existing permissions and governed by the same approval policies and risk controls that protect your Mercury account.

How confirmation works

Command never takes action without your explicit approval. When you ask it to do something, it stages the action — pre-filling the details and showing you exactly what will happen — and stops. Nothing executes until you confirm.

You can also modify what Command has staged before approving, so it’s not just a simple accept or reject.

Your data and privacy

Command is designed to use only what it needs in order to respond to your prompts.

Sensitive personal and account information — including card numbers, SSNs, dates of birth, and home addresses — is never sent to the underlying AI model. When Command needs to reference something less sensitive (but something we believe the model doesn’t need to know, like a recipient’s name, account balances, or the email addresses of users on an account) we send an internal reference ID and only surface the real data to you directly in Mercury’s interface.

Command authenticates through your existing Mercury session. This means it can only access data that a user is already authorized to see. Likewise, it can only perform actions that a user is already authorized to perform inside their Mercury account. For example, if a team member can’t view account balances in Mercury, they can’t ask Command to surface them either.

Mercury Command is powered by third-party AI providers. In order to generate responses, some data is shared with these providers, but your conversations are never used to train their models.

Using Command is optional. You’re never required to use Command. Your core Mercury experience — payments, accounts, and cards — works the same as always whether you choose to use it or not.

Getting started

Command is available to all Mercury business and personal customers. You’ll find it in the bottom left corner of your Mercury dashboard.

  • “Show me software spend by vendor.”
  • “Find the wire details for our operating account.”
  • “Generate a custom bank letter for this account.”
  • “Show me all uncategorized transactions from April.”
  • “Create an invoice for [existing customer] for [amount].”
  • “Prepare an ACH payment to [recipient] for [amount].”
  • “Set up an auto-transfer rule to keep $25,000 in our operating account.”
  • “Show me card activity for employee this month.”
  • “Freeze the card ending [1234] until I review the charge.”
  • “Set a monthly spending limit for this card.”
  • “Invite [name, email] and assign the right role for a bookkeeper.”
  • “Summarize what needs my attention before month end.”
  • “Turn Mercury to dark mode.”
  • “How much interest have I earned on my savings this year?”
  • “Create a virtual card for my Netflix subscription with a $15 limit.”
  • “Move $1,000 from my business account to personal.”
