Business: Integrations

Connect your Mercury Business account to PayPal

You can connect your Mercury account to PayPal to transfer funds back and forth.

To do this, follow PayPal’s step-by-step instructions on how to link a bank account.

PayPal may ask for an eTeller ID, which Mercury accounts don’t have. Instead, you should be able to connect your accounts using the “two small deposits” method of verification.

These deposits take between 1-3 business days to reflect in your Mercury account, so it may take a little longer to complete the connection using this method.

Connect your Mercury Business account to Venmo

You can easily link Venmo to your Mercury account to send and receive funds.

  • Make sure you’ve created a Venmo account and downloaded the mobile app.
  • In the Venmo app, go to Settings > Payment Methods.
  • Tap Add a bank or card, then Bank.
  • Click Next to continue to Instant Bank Verification.
  • From the Select your bank screen, search for Mercury.
  • Tap Mercury’s name or logo, then enter your Mercury username and password to link your account.

Integrating your Mercury account with Slack

By connecting your Slack environment to your Mercury account, you’ll be instantly notified of payments that require your approval, and can review, approve or decline those payments directly from Slack. No more bouncing between environments to perform simple actions.

You can also check your Mercury account balances directly in Slack by using the /mercury-balance command.

We’ll continue adding new notifications into Slack in the coming months, making it easier than ever to manage your company’s finances!

What’s included?

  • Connect Slack to one or all of your Mercury organizations - you’re in control!
  • If you’re eligible to approve a payment, you will receive a notification within seconds, and be able to approve or decline
    • If another approver takes action, you’ll see the notification updated
  • You can check all your associated account balances directly from Slack by using the /balance command

How to enable the Slack integration

The initial set up will require that one admin installs the app in the Slack workspace from our Integrations page. Here are the steps:

  • Click on your company name in the top left-hand corner of your dashboard and click Settings.
  • From the sidebar under “Company”, select Integrations.
  • Click into Slack integration and click Connect where you’ll be prompted to log into Mercury via OAuth (email, password, and 2-factor authentication)
  • Review and Authorize Slack’s access to your selected Mercury account(s). Follow the prompt to head back to Slack where you’ll see that your “Mercury account was successfully connected”.

Once successfully connected, payments requiring approval will be sent to Slack for you to approve.

Additional admins can open the Mercury app in Slack to set up the integration on their end (step 4 onward).

How to disconnect

You can remove the app from Mercury or Slack:

  • Go to the Integrations page and click into the Slack integration
  • Click Disconnect for your connection
  • In Slack, navigate to the About tab in the Mercury app, then Configuration, then Revoke access

You can always view our up-to-date privacy policy at app.mercury.com.

Integration FAQs

Are you compatible with Zelle?

Not currently.

We do support payment processors like Stripe, Square, Shopify, and PayPal, or your customers can ACH or wire directly to your account. You can use your account details to link the Mercury account to those services.

Are you compatible with external payment processors?

Yes. We have many customers who use PayPal, Stripe, Shopify, Square, Kick.co, and other merchant services without issue. We also have quite a few users who have stores with Amazon, and we can accept Amazon payments.

To integrate with these services, you’ll need to take your Mercury account and routing number and add it as a payment account on the processor’s site. Make sure that you use your company’s legal name as the account holder name, because a payment sent to a name other than your company’s legal name may be returned due to the mismatch. We can show you how to update your Doing Business As name if need be.

Have a registered DBA or trade name? Reach out to our support team and we’ll add it to your account so you can receive payments under multiple names.

Linking external bank accounts (Business: Integrations)

We use Plaid to link U.S bank accounts to your Mercury account for easier transfers and money management.

How to link external accounts via Plaid

  • Click the blue Move Money button in the upper right corner, then select Transfer
  • Click on the Transfer From dropdown, then scroll to the bottom and click Link a Bank Account
  • Using the Plaid pop-up, find your bank and enter your credentials when prompted
    • If your bank is not selectable from the Plaid dropdown, we’re currently unable to support a connection (including a manual connection via micro-deposit). The good news is, you can still transfer funds between bank accounts via ACH and the Move Money flow
  • You’ll be prompted to select the type of external bank account that you’re linking (either business or personal). You’ll need to provide this information before you can make a transfer
    • The account type (business or personal) determines how the ACH transaction is sent between your linked accounts. This is called the SEC file type: WEB files for personal accounts or CCD files for business accounts
    • If you have an existing linked account, updating the account type may change how your transactions are sent. If your receiving bank flags the transaction for your review, you can let them know this was an expected change

Once the account is linked, you can view account details, manage the connection, and initiate new transfers by going to the Linked Accounts tab on your Accounts page.

If you receive an error when trying to log in, double-check that you’re using the correct login, password, and login method. It can also be helpful to log in to your bank directly and make sure there are no error messages or items you need to action before connecting.

At this time, we can only support linking U.S accounts. For transfers outside the U.S, we recommend initiating an international wire.

Initiating transfers between linked accounts

Once your external account is linked, you can transfer funds to or from it directly from your Mercury dashboard or mobile app.

Note: Transfers involving Plaid-linked accounts generally take longer to process. For more information, see our dedicated article on transfer timelines.

How to unlink external accounts via Plaid

On the Web:

  • Navigate to the Accounts page from the lefthand sidebar and look for the Linked Accounts tab
  • Find the account you want to remove, click on the three dots and select the option to Unlink account

On the Mercury App:

  • Open the Mercury app and head to the Accounts tab
  • Tap on the Linked Accounts account and select the external account you want to remove.
  • Look for the option to unlink the account.

Business: Invoicing

Accepting Credit Card, Apple, and Google Pay payments on invoices via Stripe

To accept card payments on your invoices and payment links sent from Mercury, you will need a Stripe account. This guide walks you through the setup and explains how card payments on invoicing works.

How to enable card payments for invoices and payment links

  1. Connect Stripe Payments to Mercury
  • Click your company name in the top left-hand corner of the dashboard
  • Go to Settings > Integrations
  • Locate the Stripe integration and click Connect
  • Click on Set Up On Stripe. You can create a new Stripe account, or, if you already use Stripe, you can link your existing account
  1. Complete the Stripe onboarding flow
  • It may take up to a few hours for Stripe to review and approve your account
  • Once Stripe is connected, you’ll see it on the Integrations page, in the “Active” section
  • Note: Once Stripe is connected, the checkbox to “Accept credit cards” becomes available when creating a new invoice and on payment links
  1. Check “Accept credit cards” when creating a new invoice or payment link
  • Check “Accept credit cards” if you want to allow card payments for this particular invoice or payment link. Your recipients will always have other options to pay as well - they can send an ACH or wire
  • You can enable or disable card payments on each invoice or payment link that you create
    • Note: The minimum payment Stripe will accept is $0.50

Only admins and users with the “Request payments” permission will be able to toggle on card payments.

How card payments work

  • When your payer pays an invoice or payment link by card, the payment will go to your Stripe account first
  • Stripe will charge a processing fee for each received card payment
    • The standard Stripe fee is 2.9% + $0.30 per successful charge for domestic cards (see complete list of Stripe fees here). If you connect an existing Stripe account with custom fees, those fees will also apply when using Mercury Invoicing
    • Mercury does not charge any card processing fees
  • The net amount received (what your payers pay minus Stripe fee) will be automatically sent from Stripe to your Mercury account each day. The frequency of disbursements can be edited in your Stripe account

Note: When you connect your Mercury account to Stripe and initiate your first payout, it’s important to know that Stripe has a mandatory 7-14 day waiting period, which you can read about here.

Managing Stripe payments

Stripe handles payments processing, disputes, and charges. You can manage Stripe payments (disputes, charges, refunds, etc) and view payout timelines directly through Stripe.

Creating and sending an invoice

Mercury’s invoicing tool lets you generate and send polished invoices directly from your dashboard. This guide covers how to create an invoice and customize its details before sending it to your customer.

How to create an invoice

1. Getting started
  • Go to the Invoicing tab in your Mercury dashboard on web
  • Click + Request Money in the top left
2. Add a customer
  • Choose an existing customer from the dropdown, or select Add new customer
  • You’ll need to enter a name and email (personal or business)
  • Optionally, include a mailing address
3. Select create an invoice
  • Select Create a one-time invoice to generate a formal invoice document with a built-in payment link
  • Select Recurring series to automatically generate multiple invoices on a set schedule (only available on the Pro plan)
  • If you need an informal, one-off request without an invoice, you can send a standalone payment link instead

Invoice set up

4. Add line items
  • For each line item, enter a description, quantity, and price
    • These can be one-off items, or you can select an item from your product catalog by clicking the line item field and choosing an existing item or clicking Add New Catalog Item to save a new one
  • The default quantity is 1, but you can edit any field
  • To apply a discount, enter a negative value as a line item
  • When you have more than one line item, click and drag to reorder them
5. Select currency
  • Select your desired currency to make it easy for your global customers
  • The payer will pay in that currency and funds will land in your Mercury account in USD automatically
6. Adjust totals
  • Your invoice total updates automatically based on the line items
  • Click Add sales tax to apply a tax rate if needed
  • Add an optional payer memo that will appear on the invoice
7. Choose your destination account
  • Select the account into which your customer payment will be deposited if they pay you through domestic wire, international wire, ACH, or credit card
  • Choose whether you’d like to use a secure virtual account number (preferred) or real account numbers
    • This helps prevent unauthorized withdrawals. Invoices and payment links sent to the same customer will display the same virtual account number

Set invoice details

8. Set invoice, PO numbers, and dates
  • An Invoice Number is generated automatically, but you can replace it with any combination of numbers and letters
  • You can also enter a PO (Purchase Order) number if your customer uses one
    • Purchase Orders are documents customers may provide to help them track their internal purchasing process
9. Select payment methods
  • Manual transfers (ACH/ Wire), Pay with Mercury, and International wires (USD only) are always available to your customers
  • If you have credit card payments setup via our Stripe integration, you can optionally enable or disable this per payment link
  • If you’re on our Pro or Plus plans, you’ll see an option to “Accept ACH debit”

Final steps

10. Review and send
  • On the confirmation screen, review your invoice
  • Mercury pre-fills your customer’s email, but you can review or add more customers to cc them
  • You can schedule an invoice to send at a future date. To do this, turn on Schedule send and choose the date you want. Scheduled invoices are sent at 9 AM ET on the selected day
  • Optionally, enable automated reminders so customers are automatically notified of upcoming and overdue invoices
  • Click Create Only to create the invoice or Create & Send to have the invoice sent immediately
  • You can download the invoice or copy a shareable link. All invoices can be viewed and managed from your Invoicing page

Customizing your invoicing template

Your invoice settings control the default details, branding, and payment preferences that appear on every new invoice. This article covers how to set up each section.

How to access invoice settings

  • Locate Invoicing on the left-hand side of your Mercury dashboard on web
  • Click Invoice settings near the top left of the page
  • A settings panel will open with three tabs: General, Branding, and Defaults
  • Review the live invoice preview on the right side of the screen as you make changes
  • Select Save to apply your settings

General settings

The “General” tab controls your invoice header information and integrations.

Invoice header
  • Company name — Select the company name to display on invoices (e.g. legal name or DBA)
  • Email — Enter the optional email address to include in the invoice header
  • Address — Toggle on to display your business address on invoices
  • Phone number — Toggle on to display an optional phone number on invoices
Integrations
  • Accept card payments — Connect or create a Stripe account to accept card payments. This can also be enabled on a per-invoice basis
  • Invoicing API — Use the Invoicing API to automate invoicing tasks and workflows. Select View API docs or click here to learn more
Configurations
  • Show service periods on invoices — Toggle on to display a service period field on each invoice
  • Show federal tax ID / EIN on invoice — Toggle on to include your EIN in the invoice header

Branding settings

The “Branding” tab lets you control the visual appearance of your invoices.

  • Color theme — Choose a color to apply to your invoice template
  • Company logo — Upload a logo to display on each invoice. The logo must be at least 256×256 pixels

Defaults settings

The “Defaults” tab sets pre-filled details that appear on every new invoice. These can be edited when creating an individual invoice.

  • Default memo — Add a memo that will pre-populate on each invoice
  • CC emails — Add email addresses to be copied on every invoice sent
  • Virtual account numbers — Toggle on to automatically enable virtual account numbers on each invoice

Getting paid through invoicing

Once you’ve sent an invoice or payment link to a customer, there are several ways they can pay you. This article walks through each payment method available through Mercury Invoicing and how to track or update their status.

Payment methods

  • Pay with Mercury: If the payer is a Mercury user and they are currently logged into their account, they will have the option to pay via internal transfer by selecting the account they wish the funds to be withdrawn from
  • Cards, Apple Pay, and Google Pay: If you’ve enabled card payments via Stripe for this invoice or payment link, the payer will be able to enter their card details to make a payment. You will be notified the moment you get paid
  • ACH or wire: The payer will receive a set of instructions they can use with their bank account in order to send payment via the ACH or wire network. If your customer pays using ACH or wire through their own bank, you won’t receive confirmation of payment until the payment is received by us. Payment timelines will depend on the sending bank in these instances
    • Note: Payers sending international wires should pay close attention to the available currency options (USD or non-USD) and the associated wire instructions.
  • [Mercury Plus/Pro subscribers only] ACH Debit: With the ACH Debit payment option, your payer can make a bank payment directly from your invoice or payment link. This eliminates the hassle of manually initiating a transfer from their own bank account, copying account and amount details and risking errors. Your customer simply creates a quick payer account, connects their bank through Plaid (first-time only), and confirms payment for your invoice or payment link - all directly from your invoice page. Learn more about the payer experience here.
    • ACH Debit fees may apply based on your Mercury subscription plan. Learn more here.

Once payment is received it will be deposited into the designated receiving account specific to each payer, and the invoice or payment link will be marked as paid. Reminder that payments follow our typical processing times.

Manually mark as paid

If you receive a payment for your invoice or payment link outside of Mercury (for example in the form of cash or check) you can manually mark them as paid:

  • Go to the Invoicing page in your Mercury dashboard
  • Find and select the relevant invoice or payment link in your invoicing table views
  • Select More from the detail panel on the right hand side of your Mercury account, followed by Mark as paid
  • Enter the date and type of payment to close out the invoice or payment link

Reverting to unpaid

If an invoice or payment link was erroneously marked as paid, you can unmatch the payment. Here’s how:

  • Navigate to the Invoicing page
  • Locate and select the invoice or payment link in your All or Paid Invoicing table views
  • Select Unmatch payment
  • Confirm that you want to revert the item to unpaid. Once confirmed, the invoice or payment link will now show up as unpaid

How to create a recurring invoice

A recurring series lets you automatically send invoices to the same customer on a set schedule—weekly, monthly, or custom. This article explains how to create a recurring series, view upcoming invoices, and manage or cancel a series when needed.

Recurring invoicing is only available for clients subscribed to one of Mercury’s paid plans.

Create a recurring invoice series

  • Click the dropdown next to the Invoicing tab on the left hand side of your dashboard on web and select Recurring
  • Click +Create series in the top left
  • “Create a recurring series” will be automatically selected
  • Follow the prompts to fill out the invoice details
  • Choose the send date, payment terms, and frequency
  • Review the series details and click Create Series

For detailed instructions on creating invoices, see Creating and sending an invoice.

Managing invoice series

To view or manage head to Invoicing > Recurring from the left hand side of your dashboard. From here, you can:

  • View invoice series by customer and series ID
  • See status, amount, and frequency of each series
  • Click into a series to view details such as:
    • Previously sent invoices
    • The next scheduled invoice (an editable draft)
    • A full series summary
Editing and other actions

Select a series that needs editing:

  • Click Edit series to update the schedule, payment methods, or prefix. This will update all future invoices
  • Click the Trash icon to cancel the series. This stops all future invoices. Completed or canceled series cannot be edited
  • Easily duplicate an existing series by clicking the the Copy icon
  • Click the ellipsis (…) next to the invoice number to:
    • Edit the queued (next scheduled) invoice
    • Send now
    • Skip an upcoming invoice

FAQs

Can I edit a recurring invoice after it’s been created?

Yes, you can edit the entire recurring series or just the next scheduled invoice (called the queued invoice). Editing the series updates all future invoices. Editing the queued invoice creates a one-time override.

What happens if I skip the next invoice?

You can choose to skip the next invoice to move to the following one in the series. Future invoices in the series will continue as scheduled.

What do the recurring series statuses mean?

  • Active: Series is ongoing with future invoices scheduled
  • Completed: All invoices have been created and sent (but may not be paid)
  • Canceled: The series has been stopped manually

Who can manage recurring invoices?

Admins and Custom roles with “Create Invoice” permissions can manage and edit recurring invoice series. You can read more about permissions and creating custom roles here.

How to create and send a payment link in Mercury

Payment links are an easy, informal way to collect money from customers. Instead of creating a full invoice, you can generate a quick link and share it with a customer when you just need a simple, lightweight way to get paid.

How to create a payment link

  • Go to the Invoicing tab in your Mercury dashboard
  • Click +Request Money in the top left
1. Add a customer
  • Choose an existing customer from the dropdown, or select Add new customer
  • You’ll need to enter a name and email (personal or business)
  • Optionally, include a mailing address
2. Select Request money without an invoice
  • You can create an invoice or request money using a standalone payment link
  • To create a payment link, Request money without an invoice

Fill out payment link details

3. Add the total amount you’d like to request
  • Payment links are designed for quick, one-off requests, so they don’t support line items or catalog selections like invoices do.
4. Add an optional memo for your customer
  • You can write a message to your customer that will be visible to them on the payment link
  • Additionally, you can add attachments for your customers
5. Select payment methods
  • Manual Transfers (ACH/ Wire), Pay with Mercury, and International Wires are always available to your customers
  • If you have credit card payments setup via our Stripe integration, you can optionally enable or disable this per payment link
  • If you’re on our Pro plan, you’ll see an option to Accept ACH debit
6. Choose your destination account
  • Select the account into which your customer payment will be deposited if they pay you through domestic wire, international wire (non-USD supported), ACH, or credit card
  • Payment links use a secure virtual account number to protect your account from unauthorized withdrawals. Showing real account numbers on payment links are not available
    • Additional payment links or invoices sent to the same customer will display the same virtual account number
7. Create and send
  • Select Create & Send to automatically send the payment link to your customers email address. You can also copy a shareable link.
  • Payment links will continue to remain active until you either cancel it or the customer pays the link.
  • All payment links and invoices can be viewed and managed from your Invoicing page

What your customer sees

Your customer will be given a standalone link via email. The email will contain: the requestor’s name, payment amount, and other info you included when creating the payment link.

  • If your customer also has a Mercury account, they’ll be able to send via Pay with Mercury and submit a payment immediately
  • If they don’t have a Mercury account, they’ll be provided with various payment options including manual transfers and international wires
  • If you enabled ACH Debit or Credit Card options on the payment link, these will also be available to your customers

Payment links use a secure virtual account number to protect your account from unauthorized withdrawals. The funds route through this account automatically and ultimately land in the account you selected when creating the request. For security reasons, showing real account numbers on payment links are not available.

Managing payment links

All payment links and invoices can be viewed and managed from your Invoicing page.

When you select a payment link, a detail panel opens where you can take actions like sending reminders, marking the link as paid, editing it, or canceling it. You can also view a timeline of all activity related to the link.

If you’ve sent both invoices and payment links, you can filter by “Type” and select Payment links to view only those.

Creating payment links on Mobile

Payment links can also be created and managed directly from the mobile app. To create a payment link on mobile:

  • Click the middle ⇄ icon on the bottom menu navigation bar (Move Money)
  • Select the Request button on either the Move Money page or under Invoicing
  • Choose an existing customer from the dropdown, or select Create Customer
  • Select Request money without an invoice to create a payment link
    • Note: Creating a full invoice is currently only available on web
  • Add the total amount you’d like to request
  • Choose your destination account
    • Reminder: Payment links use a secure virtual account number to protect your account from unauthorized withdrawals
  • Add an optional memo or attachment to your payment link
  • Select your payment methods. Manual transfers, Pay with Mercury, and International are always enabled. You can optionally add Card Payments via our Stripe integration, and ACH Debit if you’re on a Pro plan.
  • Review and confirm to automatically send the payment link to your customers email address. You can also copy a shareable link.

Managing invoices and payment links

Mercury’s Invoicing dashboard gives you a central place to track, organize, and take action on all your invoices and payment links. This article covers how to navigate the dashboard, manage individual items, and access Invoicing on mobile.

Accessing the Invoicing dashboard

On web, click Invoicing from the lefthand navigation menu on web. This opens your Invoicing dashboard.

At the top of the dashboard, you’ll see summary totals for:

  • Active items
  • Overdue invoices
  • Paid items

Each summary shows the total amount and the number of invoices or payment links in that category.

Only admins and custom roles with invoicing permissions can access the Invoicing page.

Viewing and sorting items

Your invoices and payment links appear together in a unified table. The table layout depends on what you’ve sent:

  • Payment links only — the table shows payment-link-specific fields only
  • Invoices only, or both — the table shows the full expanded view with all invoice and payment link fields

You can sort the table by customer, creation date, due date (invoices only), invoice number, amount, and status.

Payment links don’t have due dates. Their available statuses are: Active, Paid, Canceled, and Processing.

To narrow your view, click Filters to filter by status, customer, due date, and more. Canceled invoices are hidden by default — use the toggle within Filters to show them.

Managing invoices and payment links

Select any item from the table to open a details panel. From there, you can:

  • Leave internal notes for your records
  • Edit or cancel the invoice or payment link
  • Mark it as paid or unpaid
  • Make a copy
  • Send a payment reminder to your customer
  • Download a PDF (invoice only)
  • Access a shareable link
  • Edit invoice details (on Mercury web only)
Exporting your data

Click Export to download a CSV of all your invoices and payment links.

Managing invoices and payment links on mobile

You are able to manage your invoices and payment links directly from the Mercury mobile app. To find Invoicing on mobile:

  • Click the middle ⇄ icon on the bottom menu navigation bar (Move Money)
  • Select the Invoicing section to open up a full view of all invoices and payment links
  • The dashboard will show you filters and metrics to monitor your Invoicing activity
  • Click + to create a one-time invoice or payment link. Recurring invoice creation is only available via web

Taking action on an invoice or payment link

  • If you’d like to manage a specific Invoicing item, you can select it directly from the list to open a detail view
  • The detail view will have core invoice and payment link actions, a timeline of events, and details associated with the specific item
  • You can take actions including sending reminders, copying a shareable link, marking as paid and canceling the invoice or payment link

Managing your invoicing customers

You can easily view, edit, and delete invoicing customers from your Invoicing > Customers page. This guide walks you through adding new invoicing customers and editing existing ones.

Adding a new customer

  • Click Add Customer on your “Customers” page
  • Enter your customer’s information
    • You can enter their name, email, and physical address
  • Select Add Customer and you’re all set

Editing a customer

  • Click on the customer you would like to edit
  • Select Edit
    • If the customer has NEVER been sent an invoice or payment link and has no active items, you can edit their name, email, and physical address and click Update
    • If the customer has PROCESSING invoices or payment links you will need to wait for the pending status to resolve before you can edit the customer
    • If the customer has ACTIVE invoices or payment links you will have the choice to resend any active items so that they contain the new changes. If you’d like to resend the invoices or links with the updates, select the option to resend invoices and click Confirm Changes. Otherwise, you can click Confirm Changes without opting to resend them

Deleting a customer

  • Click on the customer you would like to delete
  • Select Delete
    • If the customer has NO open invoices or payment links, click Delete Customer
    • If the customer has ACTIVE invoices or payment links you can still click Delete Customer
      • Note: Deleting a customer with active invoices or payment links will cancel all the active items
    • If the customer has PROCESSING invoices or payment links you will need to wait for the items to process before you can delete the customer

Integrating with Accounting

Our standard bank feed imports will be available via QuickBooks, Xero, and NetSuite, which will automatically sync the payment records, once an invoice is paid, via a bank feed. However, it should be noted that your accounting system of choice won’t reflect the unpaid invoices, nor will journal entries update the financial statements.

Pricing

Customers can create, send, track, and receive payment on as many invoices as they’d like in the free version of Mercury. Advanced invoicing capabilities, such as sending recurring invoices, and invoicing with ACH debit, are available as part of our paid plans. Learn more about pricing here.

It’s free for customers to pay you by ACH transfers, wire, or through Mercury. If you connect a Stripe account, you can receive payments via credit card and Apple or Google pay. Stripe charges a processing fee for each credit card payment, which is typically 2.9% + $0.30. Mercury does not charge any additional fees for credit card payments.

Moving payment requests under invoicing

Payment Requests are getting a new home and a new name. We’re consolidating everything related to requesting payments into Invoicing, where you’ll now find a payment link - a cleaner, more flexible way to get paid.

If you’ve used payment requests before, this guide walks you through what’s changing, what stays the same, and how to close out any existing requests.

Why we’re making this change

Payment requests and Invoicing have always aimed to solve the same problem: helping you get paid quickly and reliably. Moving everything under one roof makes the experience more intuitive and gives you access to more capabilities, including:

  • A unified place to create invoices or quick payment links
  • Access to additional payment methods including ACH Debit
  • Better tracking across all incoming payments
  • Mobile support for monitoring both invoices and payment links
  • A cleaner more polished request pages for your customers

Think of payment links as the next version of payment requests. Same outcome, better experience.

What’s happening to your existing payment requests

If you’ve sent at least one payment request in the past, here’s what you can expect:

  • Your existing requests will remain visible and actionable in your legacy Requests page
  • All requests created before December 16 automatically receive a new 3-month expiry date, and now all expire on March 16, 2026
  • The Request button on the old Requests page is disabled and new requests can now only be created using Payment links on the Invoicing page by clicking + Request Money
  • We’ve generated a downloadable CSV archive of your past payment requests under the Documents page for easy reference anytime

We’ll notify you in app and website with banners and tasks when you visit your old Requests page so you know exactly what’s changing and where to go next.

All of this applies to the mobile app as well. Any requests made before December 16, 2025 will appear in a dedicated “Legacy” table beneath the Invoicing section. You’ll see a banner notification to make the transition clear and can access a downloadable CSV directly from the mobile app. These requests will also expire on March 16, 2026 and will be available for download on the Documents page.

Key dates to know

Now

  • Starting on December 16th 2025, you can create new payment links from Invoicing
  • Your legacy requests page is visible and any existing request made before December 16th is actionable
  • A CSV will be generated immediately of all existing and former payment requests for your reference. This can be accessed on the Documents page

A week before March 16, 2026

  • If you still have open payment requests, you’ll receive a final reminder that the page will be sunset soon
  • You’ll see a notice in your Tasks tab encouraging you to close out any last open requests

March 16, 2026

  • All old payment requests expire
  • Visiting the old page will show a final message directing you to Invoicing and your downloadable CSV

What you can do with payment links

Payment links combine the simplicity of a quick request with the flexibility of invoicing. Now all in one place.

From the Invoicing page, you can now:

  • Create polished one-time or recurring invoices
  • Send quick payment links for one-off informal payments
  • Track all outstanding payments in a single dashboard
  • Access everything from desktop or mobile

This consolidates tools you already use while giving you more clarity and smoother workflows.

Where to find your past request history

Your complete archive of past requests is available for export anytime:

  • Under your Mercury profile, navigate to the Documents & Data page and click “Other”
    • On mobile, you can find this in the org switcher menu
  • Navigate to “Payment Requests” to download a CSV of request history

Do I need to take any action?

Most customers won’t need to lift a finger. However:

  • If you have open payment requests that you expect to be paid after March 16, plan to close them or resend them as payment links via the Invoicing page before they expire on March 16
  • For your records, feel free to download the CSV archive of previous requests

Everything else will continue working as normal, and you can use Invoicing to send new payment links immediately.

What your customers will experience

Your customers will continue to see a simple, modern payment page that is now even more polished and flexible. Existing payment requests will work up until the final expiration date of March 16th. New links created via Invoicing will use the updated design.

No disruption on their side, just a cleaner experience.

Questions? We’re here to help

If you have any open payment requests or unique workflows you’d like guidance on, get in touch with us below. We’re happy to walk you through the transition.

Pay an invoice or payment link with ACH debit

Paying an invoice or payment link with ACH debit is only available where the invoice sender has enabled the “Accept ACH Debit” option on our Pro or Plus plans (learn more about plans and pricing here).

First time payer

You’ll receive an email indicating that you’ve been sent an invoice and payment links. To set up ACH Debit, follow these steps:

  • Click Pay Invoice for invoices or View Payment link for payment links
  • Select Create Payer Account
  • Fill in the prompted information
  • Click Set and Connect
  • Verify your email
    • You’ll receive an email at the address you used in step 3
  • Once verified, select Go back to complete your payment
  • Click Connect Bank Account
  • Follow Plaid’s prompts to connect your bank account
  • After your account is connected, click the check box to authorize Mercury to debit your account.
  • Select Send Payment

Returning payer

You’ll receive an email indicating that you’ve been sent an invoice or payment link.

  • Click Pay Invoice for invoices or View Payment link for payment links
  • Select Sign In
  • Enter your email and password and click Log In
  • Select the account from which you’d like to pay the invoice or payment link
  • Click the check box to authorize Mercury to debit your account
  • Select Send Payment

FAQs

What is ACH Debit?

ACH Debit is a payment method that enables funds to be withdrawn directly from a checking or savings account.

What are the benefits of ACH Debit?

You can pay directly from the invoice or payment link payment page. There is no need to go to your banking app, no need to copy and paste any information from the invoice or payment link, which results in fewer chances for errors to occur.

How long does an ACH debit take to post?

Incoming invoicing payments via ACH debit take 1-5 business days to post

How is my bank account information shared and used?

We securely store your information. The sender has no access to that data. Additionally, you need to authorize each payment, so you cannot be automatically charged without your approval.

How can I disconnect my bank account?

You can disconnect your bank account at any time by logging into your Mercury Payer account and disconnecting.

When will my invoice or payment link be paid?

The invoice sender can see you initiated the payment immediately, but the transaction may take up to five business days to settle in their account.

What if my bank does not support Plaid?

You can send the payment as an ACH or wire rather than an ACH Debit if your bank does not support Plaid.

Using the invoice catalog to organize your goods and services

When you regularly invoice for the same products or services, saving them as catalog items can help speed things up. This article covers how to create, manage, and reuse catalog items to simplify invoicing.

Save and manage catalog items

You can view and manage all your saved invoicing items from the Catalog page on Mercury web:

  • Click the Invoicing dropdown on the left side of your dashboard
  • Select Catalog
  • Click + Add item to create a new product or service
  • Click an existing item to view more details or take actions like Edit or Delete.
    • Deleting an item won’t affect existing invoices. If the item is already in use, it will remain on those invoices as a standalone line item.
    • Editing an item will apply to all future invoices and recurring series that use this item. Open invoices won’t be affected.

Add catalog items to an invoice

When creating an invoice, you can click into the “Item” field to choose from your catalog or select +Add New Catalog Item to create a new one on the spot.

The item’s details will auto-fill in the row. If needed, you can make custom adjustments to the quantity or price of that catalog item – any changes here won’t affect the original saved item.

Note: You can’t edit existing catalog items from the invoice builder. To update or delete saved items, go to your Catalog page.

Using virtual vs. real account numbers on your invoices

When sending an invoice through Mercury, you can choose between using a secure virtual account number (recommended) or your real account number in the payment instructions.

Virtual account numbers (recommended)

By default, invoices sent through Mercury display virtual account numbers. These are secure, system-generated account numbers that are different from your actual account numbers through Mercury. Payments made to the virtual account are automatically and immediately routed to the destination account you choose when creating the invoice.

Each customer you invoice will be assigned a unique virtual account number. This means:

  • All invoices sent to the same customer will show the same virtual account number. If a customer saves your payment details, they can reuse the same virtual number for future payments.
  • Different customers receive different virtual account numbers.
Benefits of virtual account numbers:
  • Enhanced security: Your real account numbers stay private, reducing the risk of unauthorized withdrawal attempts.
  • Public-friendly: Safe to display on your invoice payment page, even if it’s publicly accessible.
  • Simplified reconciliation: Helps Mercury automatically match incoming payments to the correct invoice.

Real account numbers

Some customers - particularly larger businesses - may require your real bank account details on invoices. This usually happens when your customer requires payment instructions to exactly match a bank letter or vendor portal registration, and these invoices are usually processed through their internal AP (Accounts Payable) system.

To meet these requirements, you have the option to display your real account number on the invoice.

Things to note when using real account numbers:
  • Real account numbers are only included in the PDF version of the invoice’s payment instructions. They will not appear on the invoice payment webpage on mercury.com for security reasons.
  • Automatic payment matching is not supported. You’ll need to manually mark these invoices as paid in Mercury once the payment is received.

Add and manage comments on your business transactions

You can leave comments on any transaction in Mercury to keep your team aligned, and make sure any relevant context stays with the transaction.

How commenting works

Anyone with access to a transaction can leave a comment and view the full comment history. This is useful for sharing context, asking questions, or flagging something for review.

To mention a teammate in a comment, type @ followed by their name. Only users who have access to the transaction can be tagged.

When a comment is added, the following people will be notified:

Notifications are sent via email, in-app updates, and the Mercury Slack App.

Note: Comments do not sync with your connected accounting software at this time.

How to set up ACH debits (also known as ACH pulls or direct debit)

  • If you do not have ACH authorization enabled on Mercury, skip to step two.
  • If you do have ACH authorization enabled on Mercury, you’ll need to authorize your payroll provider by adding their ACH Originator ID(s) (also known as ACH Company ID or Vendor ID) to your list of authorized parties — you also have the option of setting a transaction limit. (ACH Originator IDs are ten-digit codes used to identify payroll providers and other entities that collect payments via ACH debit. Similar to a mailing address, these IDs help ensure the ACH debit is delivered to the correct account holder. You can request them from your payroll provider.)
  • *Please note that if you do not authorize your payroll provider as a vendor or they initiate a transaction above the set transaction limit, one of your org admins will be notified to review the ACH pull. If that window expires without admin approval or rejection, the ACH pull will be auto-approved.
  • Did you know? ACH authorization ensures the fastest payroll funding. Learn how to set it up here.
  • Retrieve the account number and routing numbers for your Mercury payroll account. You can do this by clicking the account (located under your “Accounts” tab) and copying the numbers from the details card in the top right. Your payroll provider will need these to complete the ACH debit setup.
  • Follow the instructions from your payroll provider to complete the setup. Here are links to instructions from some common payroll providers that support ACH debit:
    • Gusto
    • Rippling
    • Deel
    • Justworks
    • Trinet
    • ADP
    • Intuit QuickBooks
    • Paychex (Make a client support request)
    • Oyster HR
    • Onpay Inc.
    • Remote

If you can’t find instructions for how to connect or change your linked bank account, you can try these steps:

  • Retrieve the account number and routing numbers for your Mercury payroll account. You can do this by clicking the account (located under your “Accounts” tab) and copying the numbers from the details card in the top right. We recommend using a checking account. Your payroll provider will need these to complete the setup.
  • Log in to your payroll provider portal and navigate to the settings page where you can connect or change your bank account information.
  • Verify your bank account. Plaid is usually the fastest way to verify your bank account. However, if Plaid is not an option, you can use manual verification — this usually takes 2–3 days and begins with the provider making 1–2 micro-deposits (random amounts that are typically less than $0.50) into your bank account that you will need to verify by logging in and inputting the amount. These deposits will be reversed after the verification process.
  • In your payroll portal, make sure you enable the correct settings for automatic processing from your bank account before the processing date.

Connecting Mercury to ChatGPT, Claude, and other AI tools (Business: Manage Money)

Connect Mercury to ChatGPT, Claude, or another AI tool that supports Model Context Protocol (MCP) to view account information and take actions like transferring money between accounts, paying existing recipients, and categorizing transactions.

You can request these actions through your AI tool, then review and approve transfers and payments in Mercury before money moves.

This article explains how to connect Mercury, approve requests, and manage connected AI agents.

Connect Mercury to an AI tool

To connect Mercury, add it to your AI tool and authorize access to your account. The steps may vary by tool.

  • Log in to your AI tool
  • Find Mercury using one of these options:
    • ChatGPT: Connect Mercury to ChatGPT
    • Claude: Connect Mercury to Claude
    • Other AI tools: Search for Mercury in the tool’s app or connector directory or connect manually.
  • Add Mercury from your AI tool
  • Enter your Mercury email and password, then select Next
  • Complete login verification and select Continue
  • On the Review permissions page, confirm which Mercury organization you’re connecting and review the requested permissions
  • Select Authorize to complete the connection

Once connected, try asking your AI tool, “What’s my Mercury account balance?” to confirm you’re accessing the intended account.

If you’ve connected Mercury to an AI tool before, you may need to disconnect and reconnect to enable certain actions.

Approve transfers and payments

You can request transfers between your Mercury accounts and payments to existing recipients through your AI tool. You’ll need to approve these requests in Mercury before money moves.

  • Ask your AI tool to initiate a transfer or payment
  • Review the details in the chat, including the recipient, amount, account, and payment method
  • Select Approve on Mercury to send the request to Mercury, or Cancel to stop
  • Open the verification notification in the Mercury app on web or mobile. The approval will also appear in your Tasks page
  • Review the transfer or payment details in Mercury
  • Approve or decline the request

Note: Selecting Confirm Request in your AI tool doesn’t authorize the payment. You must approve the request in Mercury before it can be initiated.

Approval requests expire after approximately 5 minutes. If yours expires, start a new request through your AI tool.

You can also categorize transactions and update supported transaction metadata through your AI tool. These changes don’t require additional approval in Mercury and take effect immediately.

Manage connected AI agents in Agent Controls

Admins can use Agent Controls to see which AI tools their team has connected to Mercury, review their permissions and recent activity, and disconnect connections.

To find Agent Controls:

  • Go to Settings
  • Under “Security & Controls,” select Agent Controls

For more information, see Managing AI agents connected to Mercury.

FAQs

What information can my AI tool access?

When you connect Mercury to an AI tool, you authorize it to access certain account information, which may include accounts, cards, transactions, categories, statements, and users.

You can review the requested permissions on the Review permissions page before selecting Authorize.

Information accessed through the connection may be processed by the AI tool’s provider according to its terms and privacy policy. We recommend reviewing the provider’s privacy settings before connecting.

Can I switch between Mercury organizations in my AI tool?

You can’t switch between Mercury organizations within an active AI tool connection.

If you have access to multiple Mercury organizations, your AI tool will only show information from the organization you authorized when connecting.

To access a different organization:

  • Disconnect Mercury from your AI tool
  • Reconnect Mercury using the steps above
  • Select and authorize the organization you want to access

Note: You can currently connect only one type of Mercury account: either personal or business, but not both.

Can my AI tool add a new recipient?

No. You can only request payments to recipients you’ve already added in Mercury. To pay someone new, add them as a recipient in Mercury first.

How do I disconnect Mercury from an AI tool?

You can disconnect Mercury at any time through the Agent Controls page in Settings. Find your connected agent, go to the agent detail page, and click Disconnect.

What other tools are supported?

Mercury MCP is available as an official integration with the following tools:

  • ChatGPT
  • Claude
  • Cursor
  • Perplexity
  • Gemini Enterprise
  • Microsoft 365 Copilot
  • Grok Bot
  • Notion
  • Replit

To connect, select a link above or search for Mercury in your tool’s connectors, plugins, or integrations directory. Then follow the prompts to connect your account.

For Claude Code, Codex CLI, or other MCP clients, see our API documentation for setup instructions.

Why was my AI tool disconnected from Mercury?

If an admin changes your role, or changes the permissions of a role you have, Mercury disconnects the AI tools you’ve connected. This happens even if your access increases, so an AI tool never has more access than you do. You’ll get an email listing the tools that were disconnected. To keep using a tool, reconnect it using the steps above and authorize it again. It will get access that matches your current role.

Why can’t I connect Mercury to my AI tool?

To connect Mercury to AI tools, you need the Use Mercury via MCP permission. If you don’t have it, request your admin to assign you to a different role.

Deposit checks to your Mercury Business account

This article explains how to deposit checks electronically through Mercury, along with the requirements your check needs to meet before you submit it.

Mercury can’t accept checks mailed to us or our banking partners, including checks sent through virtual mailbox or mail forwarding services, or any electronic or non-standard checks (including eChecks, credit card checks, courtesy checks, or temporary/starter checks). Any checks sent by mail will be destroyed or returned to the sender.

Before you get started

Make sure the check is issued by a U.S bank and made out to:

  • The legal name or DBA of the business on file
  • A business owner (for business accounts) or the account holder on file
Endorsing checks

Before uploading photos, a signatory (any team member with check deposit permissions) needs to endorse the back of the check.

Write your business name and “For mobile deposit only” underneath your signature. Use blue or black ink — pencil isn’t accepted. If you use a stamp, that’s fine as long as it includes the required endorsement text.

Missing or incorrect endorsements are a common reason check deposits are rejected.

Depositing from your dashboard

In the upper right corner of your dashboard, click Move Money > Deposit and select Check Deposit as the method. Follow the prompts to upload check photos and submit your deposit.

If you’re running into a deposit limit, you can request an increase by following the steps outlined here.

Depositing from the Mercury mobile app

You can deposit a check from the Mercury mobile app on iOS or Android:

  • Tap the double arrow icon in the bottom navigation
  • Depending on your device:
    • iOS: Tap +Deposit at the top of the screen, then follow the prompts to upload photos and submit your deposit
    • Android: Tap the paper plane icon, then tap +Deposit

Taking photos of your checks

Successful deposits rely on check images that are clear and legible. Here are our requirements:

  • Upload clear photos: Ensure both the front and back of your check images are clear, with all account information legible. Photos must be of the actual check, not a photo of a check image from a computer screen or another secondary source. Scanned checks are acceptable.
  • Background matters: Take the photos on a solid, dark, and non-reflective background. Avoid wood or busy backgrounds, as they can lead to poor image quality.
  • Flat surfaces only: In addition to solid backgrounds, ensure the check is completely flat. Do not take photos with the check in your hands or on your lap.
  • Lighting and focus: Capture the photos in a well-lit area, ensuring no shadows are cast on the check. Use a clean camera lens and avoid zooming in to maintain clarity.
  • Remove attachments: If your check has a pay stub or letter attached, remove them before taking photos.

If your check deposit is rejected

The check type isn’t supported

eChecks, courtesy checks, and temporary/starter checks won’t process, even if you resubmit them. Ask the sender for a standard check from a U.S. bank, or for another way to pay you. If there are no account, routing, and check numbers along the bottom of the check, it’s likely an eCheck.

The payee doesn’t match your account
  • Made out to a DBA that isn’t on your account: Add the DBA, then resubmit the check.
  • Made out to someone who isn’t a signatory or beneficial owner: Contact Support to add them. Resubmit once they’ve been added.
The photo couldn’t be read

Retake the photo using the tips above, and also check that:

  • The numbers along the bottom are sharp and fully in the frame
  • There’s a visible border around all four edges, so don’t zoom or crop too close
  • There’s no glare or wrinkles, and the photo isn’t too bright or too dark

When to expect funds

Checks are manually reviewed and once approved can take up to 5 business days to post. You may notice that funds have settled on the 6th business day if the check was submitted after our 12pm Pacific cutoff time.

Please keep the check for at least a week to make sure it clears without issue.

Depositing money overview

You have several options for funding your Mercury account: wiring money from an external account, sending an ACH transfer, depositing a check, creating a SAFE, or sending a payment request. All of these can be accessed from the Mercury dashboard through the Deposit flow. Below is an overview of the methods available, how they differ, and links for further information.

Note: Only users with full Move Money permissions will see all the options mentioned here.

Wiring from an external account

You can make a deposit by sending a domestic or international wire in USD to Mercury from an external account. Start by retrieving your Mercury account wire details, then log in to the external bank account you want to wire from and use those details. Incoming wires from a domestic account typically arrive in 0-1 business days and international wires in 1-4 business days.

Linking an external account

To add funds from another U.S. account, you can link that external account to Mercury via Plaid. Once linked, you’ll be able to pull in funds from external accounts via the Deposit flow. External transfers are sent via ACH and should arrive in 3-5 business days.

Depositing a check

To deposit a check, follow these instructions. Funds should appear in 1-5 business days.

Creating a payment request

To request a payment, follow these instructions. Arrival depends on your recipient’s payment method.

Creating a Mercury SAFE

To create a SAFE, follow these instructions. This is a common method for C-Corps.

Disputing an ACH pull

If you notice an ACH pull, also known as an ACH Debit, you don’t recognize or there’s an issue with the transaction, you can file a dispute from your Mercury dashboard or mobile app. Our Disputes team will review your case and guide you through the next steps.

This article covers what you can dispute, how to file, and how to withdraw an ACH pull dispute if needed.

What transactions can I dispute?

Not all transactions are eligible for dispute. Here’s what you need to know before filing:

  • Settled transactions only. Transactions must be fully completed and settled before they can be disputed. Pending, canceled, blocked, or failed transactions aren’t eligible because the funds haven’t fully left your account.
  • Eligible transaction types. Internal transfers between Mercury accounts, wire transfers, and other non-card and non-ACH pull transactions can’t be disputed through the self-service flow. Contact our support team for help with those.
  • Reporting windows. For most business accounts, disputes must be filed by 5:00 PM PT on the second business day after the transaction settles. For certain business transactions not subject to this window, the deadline is 5:00 PM PT on the 60th calendar day after settlement. Disputes filed after either deadline aren’t eligible for a return or credit. See your applicable Terms of Service agreements for details.
  • Written Statement of Authorized Debit (WSUD). For certain business transactions outside the two-day window, and for all personal banking transactions, a WSUD may be required. Your dispute investigator will send you the form once you file.
  • Nacha restrictions. Nacha guidelines don’t allow ACH returns for merchant disagreements, dissatisfaction with goods or services, undelivered goods, or a company’s bankruptcy or failure to meet contractual obligations.
  • Court-ordered transactions. Disputes aren’t accepted for state, federal, or court-ordered transactions, including levies, garnishments, child support, or tax payments.
Unauthorized ACH pulls

If you suspect unauthorized activity or notice a charge you didn’t authorize, we highly recommend replacing your account number to prevent any additional unauthorized ACH pulls from going through. If you want to change your account number, let your dispute investigator know or reach out to our support team.

Tip: The ACH authorization feature allows you to create a list of merchants that are pre-approved to perform ACH pulls from your account. You can learn more about ACH authorizations here.

How to dispute an ACH pull

You can file a dispute in your Mercury dashboard or mobile app.

  • Navigate to your Transactions page and select the transaction you wish to dispute
  • Click the flag icon at the bottom of the transaction details card
  • Follow the prompts to submit your dispute

Once submitted, a member of our Disputes team will review your case and follow up via email. The Disputes team operates via email, so all updates and next steps will be communicated by email only. If you have questions, would like to provide additional information, or need to respond to your dispute investigator, you can reply to the confirmation email you received after filing or directly to the email from your assigned investigator.

How to withdraw an ACH pull dispute

To withdraw a filed ACH pull dispute, reply to the confirmation email you received when the dispute was submitted.

Filing a Mercury Business card dispute: Eligibility and steps

If you notice a charge you don’t recognize or there’s an issue with a transaction, you can file a dispute from your Mercury dashboard or mobile app. Our Disputes team will review your case and guide you through the next steps.

This article explains which transactions are eligible and how to submit a dispute.

What types of transactions can be disputed?

In order to successfully file a card dispute, the transaction must meet our eligibility requirements:

  • Transactions must be completed and settled before they’re eligible for dispute. Pending, canceled, blocked, or failed transactions can’t be disputed because the funds haven’t fully left your account.
  • We’re unable to accept disputes for state, federal, or court-ordered transactions, including (but not limited to) levies, garnishments, child support payments, or tax payments.
  • Business transactions must be reported to Mercury within 60 days of the transaction settlement date to be eligible to dispute. For additional information on dispute reporting timeframe requirements, please refer to the applicable Terms of Service agreements.
  • Internal transfers between your Mercury accounts, wire transfers, and other non-card or non-ACH-Pull transactions aren’t eligible for disputes through the self-service flow. For assistance, please reach out to our support team.

If you need to file an ACH pull dispute, review the steps outlined here.

How to dispute a card transaction

If the issue is not related to an unauthorized transaction, we recommend contacting the merchant first. Merchants can often resolve billing errors, subscription issues, or product concerns more quickly than the formal dispute process. If we need to file a chargeback on your behalf, the Mastercard chargeback process can take up to 90 days.

If you’re unable to resolve the issue directly with the merchant, or if the charge was unauthorized, you can file a dispute in your Mercury dashboard or mobile app.

  • Go to your Transactions page on web or mobile app
  • Use filters to locate the transaction you want to dispute and click on it to open the transaction details
  • Click on the flag icon in the bottom left of the transaction details card to dispute the transaction
    • If you don’t see the flag button, ensure the transaction is eligible for a dispute
  • Follow the prompts to submit your dispute
    • If your dispute is eligible to include multiple transactions, you’ll have the option to add additional transactions after completing the initial prompts
Do I need to cancel my card?

Whether you need to cancel your card depends on the type of dispute:

  • Unauthorized charge: If you suspect unauthorized card activity or notice a charge you didn’t authorize, cancel your card to prevent additional charges.
  • Billing dispute or merchant disagreement (e.g., incorrect charge amount, undelivered goods or services, recurring subscription charged after cancellation, goods or services that don’t match their description): You do not need to cancel your card.
What happens after you file

After you submit your dispute, a member of our Disputes team will review your case and follow up by email.

  • The Disputes team communicates via email only. Updates, next steps and requests for additional information will come through via email.
  • To respond to your investigator or provide additional information, reply to the confirmation email you received after filing or directly to the email from your assigned investigator.
Requests for further information

If we need more details to process your dispute, we’ll contact you by email — either to the address on file or directly in reply to your original dispute confirmation email. We can only send and receive communications through verified email addresses associated with your account.

You can also check the status of your dispute in the disputed transaction widget on your home screen. If the status shows “On hold, information needed,” check your email and respond as soon as possible.

Per internal and Mastercard network guidelines, if we don’t receive a response by the deadline communicated via email, your dispute will be moved to an ineligible status and cannot be reopened — even if information is submitted later.

Note: We may need to file a chargeback to attempt recovery. The Mastercard chargeback cycle is a structured, multi-stage process that moves through phases of evidence submission and review. As we are strictly bound by the Mastercard Rules and Transaction Processing Guidelines, we must adhere to specific timelines and evidentiary standards at every step. Please keep in mind that filing a chargeback is not a guarantee of a refund, as the final decision rests on the validity of the provided evidence and the network’s specific guidelines.

Canceling or checking the status of a dispute

Once a dispute has been filed, you can manage disputes from your Mercury dashboard on web. You can read more about dispute statuses here.

How percentage-based auto transfer rules are calculated (Business: Manage Money)

Percentage-based auto-transfer rules let you distribute money automatically between accounts based on 1) a percentage of an account balance or 2) a percentage of an incoming transaction.

On May 8, 2026, Mercury is updating how percentage-based rules are calculated to make their behavior more consistent and predictable.

This article explains what’s changing, who is affected, and how to update your rules if needed.

Changes to percentage-based rules

Before May 8, each percentage rule calculated against the balance remaining after the previous rule ran. This meant multiple high-percentage rules could all execute — but each one would transfer a smaller amount than the last.

Starting May 8, every percentage rule calculates against your account’s starting available balance at the beginning of the day or the total amount of the incoming transaction.

What did not change: Rules still run in order. If there isn’t enough balance to fulfill a rule after earlier rules have run, that rule will fail.

Example: How the calculation changes

Say you have three rules on the same account, each set to transfer 50% of your balance. Your starting balance is $1,000.

BEFORE May 8 (legacy calculation):

Rule 1: 50% of $1,000 = $500 transferred | $500 remaining

Rule 2: 50% of $500 = $250 transferred | $250 remaining

Rule 3: 50% of $250 = $125 transferred | $125 remaining

Result: All three rules execute.

AFTER May 8 (new calculation):

Rule 1: 50% of $1,000 = $500 transferred | $500 remaining

Rule 2: 50% of $1,000 = $500 transferred | $0 remaining

Rule 3: 50% of $1,000 = $500 attempted — $0 available, rule fails

Result: Rules 1 and 2 execute. Rule 3 fails.

For incoming transaction rules, the same math applies. In the above example, an account with multiple incoming transaction rules on the same account would see the same result after an incoming transaction of $1,000.

Who is affected

You will only be affected if you have multiple, separate percentage-based rules on the same checking or savings account that run on the same day. The amount transferred may change, and if the combined percentages exceed 100% on any 1 account, some rules will fail. Example:

You are not affected by this change if you have one percentage-based rule on a checking or savings account, even if that rule distributes funds to multiple accounts. These rules are not impacted by this change. Example:

Options for updating your rules

Option 1: Reduce percentages so they total 100% or less to prevent rule failure

Option 2: Replicate the old cascading behavior manually

If you relied on the waterfall calculation, you can recreate it by adjusting each rule’s percentage relative to the starting balance.

Example — replicating three 50% rules on a $1,000 balance:

Rule 1: 50% (receives $500)

Rule 2: 25% (receives $250 — equivalent to 50% of the $500 that was left)

Rule 3: 12.5% (receives $125 — equivalent to 50% of the $250 that was left)

Option 3: Switch to fixed-amount rules

If your goal is to move a specific dollar amount each day regardless of your balance, fixed-amount rules aren’t affected by this change and may be a simpler fit.

How to edit your auto-transfer rules
  • On web, click Accounts on the left-hand menu and select the Auto-transfer rules tab
  • Click the three dots menu > Edit rule on the rule you want to change
  • Update the percentage, review the rule summary, and save

FAQs

Will my rules automatically update on May 8?

Yes. Your existing rules will be modified. If you take no action, rules that can’t be fulfilled due to insufficient balance will fail after May 8.

What happens when a rule fails?

No money is transferred for that rule. You’ll see it reflected in your transaction history. Your other rules won’t be affected.

Do I need to update all of my rules?

Only rules where multiple percentage rules on the same account are in place.

What if I have one percentage rule and one fixed-amount rule on the same account?

Fixed-amount rules are unaffected by this change. Only percentage-based rules are recalculated.

What if my rules run on different days?

If your percentage rules are scheduled on different days and never run on the same day, they won’t compete for the same balance. You likely won’t see any change.

How to check and manage your Mercury Business card dispute status

After submitting a card dispute, you can track its progress directly from your Mercury dashboard. The dispute tracker shows real-time status updates, flags any actions needed from you, and keeps a full history of your dispute from submission through final decision.

Checking the status of a dispute

  • Navigate to the Disputes widget on the homepage of your Mercury dashboard on web
  • If you have multiple disputes, scroll through the list and select the dispute you’d like to review
  • Hover over the status and click View Details to open the dispute and view more information about the dispute
  • On the details page, you will see the current status, a timeline of updates, and any required actions

You can also filter on disputed transactions from your Transactions page using the status filter.

Canceling a card dispute

  • Navigate to the Disputes widget on the homepage of your Mercury dashboard on web
  • If you have multiple disputes, scroll through the disputes and select the set of disputes you would like to cancel
  • Hover over the status and click View Details to open the dispute
  • Scroll to the bottom of the details card and click Withdraw dispute located on the bottom right
  • Provide a reason to submit your withdraw. We’ll email you to confirm the dispute has been canceled
What do the different dispute statuses mean?
  • Dispute received: The disputes team has received your dispute and started the investigation process.
  • On hold, information needed: We need more information from you to move forward. Check your email for a message from the Mercury Disputes team and respond as soon as possible.
    • Note: if we don’t receive a response by the deadline communicated in that email, your dispute will be moved to an ineligible status and cannot be reopened — even if information is submitted later.
  • Chargeback filed on your behalf: The chargeback has been filed and you are all set. We don’t need any more information. This tends to be a longer step in the process.
    • If we need to submit a chargeback to attempt to recover the funds, your dispute may remain in a “Pending Chargeback” status. The full dispute and chargeback process can take up to 90 days from the date the dispute is filed. This timeframe is set by Mastercard and allows the merchant a designated period to respond and provide supporting evidence.
  • Dispute complete: This means your dispute has been resolved or approved. You can click into this status to view more information.

FAQs

Who can view dispute statuses?

Anyone with access to the Transactions page can view dispute details, including the user who submitted the dispute, cardholders, Admins, and business owners.

How do I view the status of my ACH pull dispute?

Dispute statuses are currently only available for card transactions. For ACH dispute updates, reply to the original dispute-related email you received.

How do I update or add details to a dispute?

Reply to your confirmation email to ask questions or submit additional information. You’ll also receive updates and the final outcome of your dispute via email.

Insights page overview

Insights is a page within your Mercury account that shows real-time, customizable financial metrics, helping you understand and act on your finances. You can access Insights via the sidebar menu of your Mercury account.

On the Insights page, you will find:

  • An overview of cashflow with a filter menu that allows you to customize the data you’re reviewing. Drill down by category, GL code, accounts, counterparties, and more.
  • A built-in AI-powered financial recap module that automatically surfaces important trends and alerts in your data. You can click into any of them and ask our chatbot follow up questions like “Why did my software spend spike this month?”

You can quickly review Money in data by source, category, or GL code, and Money out data by recipient, category, GL code:

You can also click into any row to see the pre-filtered list of transactions behind it.

Customizing your Insights data

Filtering data

You can filter your data by GL code, category, bank account, and more. Select the desired filter from the drop down menu on the top left corner.

Excluding data from Insights

You can exclude certain transactions or transaction types from Insights — such as proceeds from an investment — so they don’t skew your day-to-day cash flow data. To get started, click the vertical dots (⋮) at the top of the Insights page to open Insights Settings, where you can also manage notifications, cashflow timeframes, and more:

Saving views

About the AI assistant in Insights

Insights includes a built-in AI-powered financial recap that automatically surfaces the most relevant cashflow changes, helping you interpret your financial data and take action if needed.

You can hover over any insight and “Ask Mercury AI” to dig deeper into the transactions behind it or click the ? in the bottom-right hand corner to start a new conversation.

Keep in mind that the assistant is designed to help with trend analysis - it’s not meant to replace formal accounting reports.

Insights FAQs

What is “runway”?

Runway is the number of months your business can keep operating with the money you currently have, if you keep spending the way you have been.

How do you figure out my cashflow, or burn rate?

We look back at your last few months of activity. By default, we use the last 3 full months of activity, but this can be changed by adjusting the time frame on your insights page in the top right corner.

  • Money in: all deposits you received during that time, excluding internal transfers.
  • Money out: all withdrawals/expenses during that time, excluding internal transfers.
  • We average this to get your monthly burn rate (how much you’re spending, on average, each month).

How do you calculate my runway from that?

We take your current available balance and divide it by your monthly burn rate. This includes any money you have in Treasury.

Why am I not seeing a runway number?

We don’t show a runway number if you’re making money (positive cashflow) or if the time range you’ve selected does not extend until today or the end of the most recent month. That’s because we assume runway is most relevant for you based on recent transaction data.

How are my transactions categorized?

Most transactions are automatically categorized by Mercury. You can always overwrite our suggested category by going into a transaction and selecting a new value from the drop down list. Learn more about auto-categorization here.
