Receiving real-time payments (RTP) (Business: Manage Money)

Real-time payments (RTP) allow you to receive money in seconds 24/7, including weekends and holidays. This article explains how real-time payments work on Mercury, who can send you these payments, and how to make sure you’re set up to receive them.

Real-time payments are only available to Mercury accounts provided through our partner, Column N.A.

Overview of real-time payments

RTP can occur via two payment networks operated by The Clearing House and the Federal Reserve that let participating banks and providers send funds instantly within the U.S. If someone sends you a payment via RTP, it can show up in your Mercury account in just a few seconds (though some may take up to 30 minutes, depending on the sender). Once completed, RTP transactions settle immediately and are generally irrevocable.

Eligibility and supported senders

The ability to receive RTP transfers depends on the sending institution’s participation in the applicable payment network. Receipt of RTP funds may be delayed or unavailable due to network interruptions, transaction limitations, risk or fraud screening, or other circumstances outside of Mercury’s control. RTP availability is not guaranteed for all transactions.

Currently, receiving RTPs is only available for Mercury accounts on our partner bank, Column N.A. You can receive real-time payments from participating providers, including:

  • Banks that support the ability to send RTP (many major banks do)
  • Payment processors like Stripe, Bill, Square, PayPal, Amazon Express Payout, and Venmo

Your sender’s bank or provider must support one of the RTP networks in order to be eligible to send RTP to your account. While Mercury does not charge you for receiving RTP, your sender’s bank/provider may charge fees for sending real-time payments — unfortunately, these are set by them and we can’t control or refund those charges.

How to receive RTP payments

As long as your Mercury account is on Column N.A., you don’t need to enable anything in your account in order to receive RTP. If a sender is eligible to send real-time payments and uses your Mercury wire details, the funds should arrive instantly.

To receive a real-time payment:

  • Log in to your Mercury account on web or mobile
  • Locate your wire/payment details
  • Share your account details with trusted senders and/or your payment processor

Most processors will automatically detect that your account can accept RTP. If they request verification, you can confirm that your account is with Column N.A., which supports RTP.

Note: If you already have a Mercury account on Column N.A. and would like to open additional accounts to receive RTP, you’ll first need to make sure that your preferred partner bank is set to Column N.A. (your preferred partner bank is usually set to whichever partner bank you most recently opened an account with).

If you need to confirm your preferred partner bank or switch it to Column N.A., just reach out to us below and we can update it for you. Then head to your Accounts tab and click the “Add Account” drop-down to open a new account on Column N.A. with its own account number.

Common processor setup guides

If you’re using RTP with an e-commerce or payment platform, check our setup tips here:

  • Stripe - Link your Mercury account and initiate Instant Payouts manually from the Stripe Dashboard or using the Stripe API
  • Bill - Enable and manage instant payments from your Bill settings menu
  • Square - Link your Mercury account and initiate transfers directly from Square
  • PayPal - When initiating a transfer, select the “in minutes” option
  • Amazon Express Payout - Log in to your Amazon Pay account and opt into Express Payout
  • Venmo - When initiating a transfer, select Instant as the transfer method

Note: We recommend reviewing any eligibility and setup instructions directly from the provider’s website, as details may change.

FAQs

What if the sender’s payment doesn’t process as an RTP?

If RTP isn’t available or fails, most providers will automatically send the payment as an ACH or wire transfer instead.

Why is the amount sometimes lower than expected?

Many providers deduct a processing fee (typically 1–2%) in order to send RTP as payments or payouts. Check with the sender or platform for fee details.

How can I recognize instant payout scams?

Be cautious if you’re asked to verify your account or share wire details unexpectedly. If you didn’t initiate a payout or don’t recognize a sender, don’t respond or provide sensitive account information.

How is RTP different from services like Zelle or Venmo?

Services like Zelle aren’t actually sending payments between banks, so they aren’t using the RTP network. They are performing what is called a book transfer, where funds are exchanged between banks and credit unions within their ecosystem, which allows money movement to be instant. On the other hand, the RTP network actually moves money between banks in real time.

Does Mercury support the ability to send real-time payments?

Yes, real-time payments are available for Mercury accounts provided through our partner, Column N.A.

For more information, see section 10.7 in the Column N.A. account agreement. To confirm whether your account is eligible to receive RTP payments, please contact Mercury support at help@mercury.com.

Real-Time Payments (RTP) are available only to Mercury customers whose accounts are provided through Column, N.A., Member FDIC. Third-party fees may apply. Setting up auto transfer rules

Auto-transfer rules help you move money between accounts automatically so you can manage cash flow, fund specific accounts, or streamline distribution of deposits without manual effort. You can create rules from scratch or use templates to get started faster.

How to find and manage rules

  • On the left-hand side of your dashboard, select Accounts
  • Click the Auto transfer rules tab
  • From here, you can:
    • Create new rules
    • View active rules
    • Edit or remove existing rules
  • Review your rule configuration
  • Optional: Add a nickname
  • Click Create rule to save

A few notes on rule creation:

  • Currently, you can only set up auto transfer rules between Mercury accounts
  • Only admins can create, edit, or remove rules. Bookkeepers and custom users will need to ask an admin for help

Creating a new rule

Choose from four suggested rule types designed around common goals, like distributing funds or maintaining a specific account balance. These give you a structured framework with fill-in-the-blank settings, so you don’t have to start from scratch.

Alternatively, click + Custom Rule to create an auto-transfer rule from scratch.

Not sure which rule to choose? Click + Create Rule and describe how you want your funds to move—we’ll use AI to suggest the right rule for you.

Using templates

Choose from four suggested rule types for common goals — structured starting points you can customize.

1 - Distribute funds across accounts

Split funds across multiple accounts on a schedule.

  • Choose to transfer by set amount or percentage
  • Decide if the rule runs on incoming funds or on a schedule
  • Add your destination accounts

Great for: Profit-first accounting, setting aside funds for taxes, or automating budgeting

2 - Maintain a target account balance

Move funds into or out of an account to stay within set limits.

  • Select a minimum, maximum, or both
  • Choose a supporting account
  • Set a frequency

Ideal for: Payroll accounts, keeping operational balances steady.

3 - Schedule recurring transfers

Send a set amount to a destination on a regular basis.

  • Choose your source and destination
  • Set the transfer amount
  • Pick a frequency

Helpful for: Vendor payments and routine funding.

4 - Redirect incoming funds

Clear the account by moving out 100% of incoming funds.

  • Automatically distributes all incoming funds (including internal transfers) to a chosen destination account

Useful for: Reducing account exposure, consolidating funds.

Custom rule options

Build rules from scratch with full flexibility — best if you have a specific setup in mind.

Maintain a target account balance

Automatically keep a selected account within a minimum, maximum, or target balance range.

  • Choose the target account to monitor
  • Set the desired behavior:
    • Keep the balance above a minimum: Funds will be added from another account whenever the balance falls below the set minimum.
    • Keep the balance below a maximum: Funds above the maximum will be moved into another account.
    • Keep the balance within a range: Funds will be added or removed whenever the balance falls outside the specified range.
  • Choose the supporting account to add funds from or move excess funds into
  • Set your frequency. Rules can run daily, weekly, monthly, or on specific days
Transfer funds to one or more accounts

​​Automatically move money to other accounts. Commonly used for budgeting or the profit first method.

  • Choose whether to move:
    • A set amount
    • A percentage of account balance
    • A percentage of incoming funds
  • Select the source/starting account
  • Input the amount or percentage that should be transferred
  • Add one or more destination accounts
  • Choose your frequency/how often you want the rule to run

Transfer settlement timing

  • Transfers between checking/savings happen instantly when triggered.
  • Transfers to/from Treasury settle in 0–2 business days depending on your portfolio.
  • Auto transfers from Treasury are limited to two transfers per month and the selected dates must be at least 7 calendar days apart.

FAQs

Can I set up multiple rules per account?

Yes. If you’re setting up multiple percentage-based rules on one account, ensure that the combined percentage to be transferred does not exceed 100%, or else some rules will fail. Learn more about how percentage-based auto-transfer rules are calculated.

When do auto-transfer rules run?

Rules on a schedule (daily, weekly, monthly, etc.) run at 15:00 UTC (6:00 AM PT). Rules between accounts at the same partner bank can run every day, including weekends. All other scheduled rules run on business days; if the date falls on a weekend or holiday, they run on the preceding business day.

Rules based on incoming funds run in real time whenever funds are deposited into the rule account.

You can view when a transfer is next scheduled to run from your Auto Transfers page.

Can I pause an active auto transfer rule?

Yes. You can pause existing rules from the main Auto transfer rules page. Click the pause toggle next to any active rule to pause it immediately — no deletion or reset required. Click the toggle again to resume right where it left off.

For more control, click the rule to open a details panel where you can set a specific auto-resume date so the rule restarts automatically when that date arrives.

Can I set up auto transfer rules with linked external accounts?

Can I set up auto-transfer rules with linked external accounts?

Yes. You can use an external account linked via Plaid as a destination for certain auto-transfer rules:

  • Distribute funds across accounts: Funds can be sent from Mercury to a linked external account
  • Maintain a target account balance: A linked external account can be used as the supporting account when funds are being sent out of Mercury

Auto-transfers to linked external accounts are sent via ACH and typically take 1–3 business days to arrive. Auto-transfers with linked external accounts are push-only, so funds can’t be pulled from an external account into Mercury.

What happens if my account doesn’t have enough money for a scheduled transfer?

If there aren’t enough funds to run a scheduled rule, we will simply skip it. You’ll receive an email notification, and the rule will continue running as usual for future auto transfers.

When creating a rule, how many accounts can I distribute funds to?

You can distribute funds into up to 20 accounts within a single rule.

How do I set up a Treasury rule to maintain a target balance?

You can use a Treasury rule to automatically manage the balance of a checking or savings account. This helps ensure you always have enough cash available for operations while putting excess funds to work.

To set it up, select “Maintain a target account balance” as the rule type. Then choose your rule account, set your balance parameters (minimum, maximum, or both) and select your Treasury account as the supporting account. Under “Repeat”, choose which dates to run the transfer — you can pick any two monthly dates.

What if I need to fund an account that has a “distribute incoming funds” rule?

Because internal transfers also count as incoming funds, sending money into an account with an active distribution rule will trigger funds leaving the account. You have two options:

  • Temporarily remove the rule: Delete the distribution rule, make the internal transfer, then recreate the same rule.
  • Leave some funds behind: Set your distribution rule to less than 100% so the account keeps a small balance from each deposit. You can then manually transfer any excess funds as needed.

Tracking missing payments (Business: Manage Money)

Different kinds of payments have different processing times, and if your transaction was just sent, it might not have been processed yet. Here’s more information on tracking details and how to find them once a transaction has been sent:

Outgoing Transactions

Log into your Mercury account and go to your Transactions page. Use filters to narrow down the transaction in question and locate the relevant tracking details. Tracking details (including trace IDs, IMADs, receipts, etc.) are typically available once a transaction has been sent and is no longer “Pending”:

For ACH payments
  • Click on the transaction and locate the “Transaction tracking number”
  • The ACH trace ID is a 15-digit transaction tracking number. Please share this with the beneficiary so that their banking institution can locate the funds
    • For outgoing ACH transfers, the Trace ID may not appear immediately after you initiate the payment. It typically becomes available after the transfer has been submitted to the ACH network, which may take until the next business day
  • An ACH payment may take 0-1 business days to arrive, so please inform us if the recipient has not received the funds by then
For domestic wires
  • Click on the transaction and find the “Transaction tracking number”
  • The transaction tracking number (or IMAD) is a unique number that identifies a wire transfer made through the Federal Reserve Bank’s Fedwire system
  • Share the IMAD with the recipient to track the funds. Domestic wires should only take 1 business day to arrive
For international wires
  • Click on the transaction and locate the “Tracking link” to see and share the wire’s status
  • Once generated, you can also download the SWIFT receipt under “Mercury-generated receipts” to review the wire instructions. Sharing this with the recipient can help the beneficiary’s institution locate the wire

Incoming Transactions

If it’s been longer than the expected processing times outlined here, you can track your incoming domestic or international wire here. Otherwise, please get in touch with us below with the following information:

For ACH payments
  • Date sent
  • Sender name
  • Amount
  • ACH trace ID (this is a transaction tracking number. You may have to ask the sender, but this will be the fastest way to locate the transaction)
For domestic wires
  • Date sent
  • Sender name
  • Amount
  • IMAD/OMAD (these are domestic wire tracking numbers and can be obtained by asking the sending bank)
For international wires

First, make sure that the sender followed our wire instructions; if the incorrect account details were used, the wire will be returned to sender.

If all information was entered properly, send us over the following so we can take a closer look:

  • Date sent
  • Sender name
  • Amount

Our support team will then share a secure link you can use to share a copy of your wire receipt or SWIFT confirmation (MT103 or pacs.008).

Understanding your Mercury balances

As you explore your Mercury dashboard, you’ll see a few different balance breakdowns to help you better understand how much money you have coming in, going out, and available to use.

Your Mercury balance

When you first log in to Mercury on the web or in the mobile app, you’ll see an amount called your “Mercury balance”. This is a birds eye view of available funds across all of your checking, savings, and (if applicable) Treasury accounts, including any pending transactions that are outgoing.

Click the table icon near your Mercury balance to see the detailed breakdown of available funds and pending transfers. You can quickly toggle between this and your balance graph.

Your available balance

Your available balance represents funds that can be used immediately.

  • On your homepage, you can find this in the detailed breakdown of your Mercury total. If you don’t have any pending internal transfers, your available balance and your Mercury balance might be the same.
  • On an individual account page, this is the balance at the top of the page.

Your pending balance

Your pending balance is the total of all pending outgoing transactions. The second a transaction begins to process, it’s subtracted from your Mercury and available balances since the funds are no longer available to use. Instead, we provide this total so you can get a quick sense of your outgoing cashflow.

  • On your homepage, you’ll see this in the breakdown of your Mercury balance. This shows you the total of outgoing funds across all accounts.
  • On an individual account page, you’ll find this near the available balance. This shows you the total outgoing transactions from the specific account you’re viewing.

Your Treasury balance

Your Treasury balance is the total of all your available and invested Treasury funds and doesn’t include pending deposits. It’s functionally very similar to an available balance on a checking or savings account, but because your Treasury funds may be invested and thus not immediately available in the same way, we gave it its own name. As a reminder, accessing these funds will require a transfer out of Treasury and can take 1-4 business days to liquidate.

You can view your Treasury balance in a few places: on your homepage by clicking into the table icon and clicking Treasury, your list of accounts in the sidebar and within your actual Treasury page.

Your IO credit balance

Your IO credit balance is the total amount you’ve currently spent on your IO card. Obviously, this balance is slightly different than the others in that it doesn’t represent funds you have available, but rather funds you need to pay back.

Also note: this balance includes pending charges before they’ve fully settled to give you a sense of overall spend. If a charge falls off or fails to complete, the balance will adjust accordingly. This balance can be viewed on your Credit page.

Using a Mercury Recipient Profile to receive payments

If a Mercury customer sends you a payment or requests your payment details, you may see an option to create a Mercury Recipient Profile. A Recipient Profile lets you track incoming payments, save your payout details, and generate invoices without opening a full Mercury account.

This article explains what a Recipient Profile is, how to set one up, and what you can do with it.

What is a Mercury Recipient Profile?

A Mercury Recipient Profile is a lightweight account for people who receive payments from Mercury customers. With a Recipient Profile, you can:

  • View incoming and past payments
  • Save and manage your payout details
  • Generate and share invoices for free
  • Upgrade to a full Mercury account at any time

A Recipient Profile does not include access to checking and savings accounts, cards, or other full account features.

For questions about payment status, timing beyond standard processing windows, or changes to manually entered payment details, please reach out directly to the business that sent the request.

How to create a Recipient Profile

When a Mercury customer sends you a request for payment details, you’ll receive an email requesting details and the option to create a profile.

To create a Recipient profile
  • Open the email requesting your payment details with the subject line “[Name] wants to send you money via Mercury”
  • Follow the email prompt to get started
  • Enter your basic information:
    • Name
    • Email
    • Business type (if applicable)
    • Company name (if applicable)
    • Password
  • Enter your payment details manually or link an external account via Plaid. Payments methods can include:
    • ACH
    • Domestic wire
    • Check
    • International wire

Once complete, you’ll be taken to your Mercury Recipient Profile dashboard where you can view and track incoming payments. If you have questions about the available payment options, reach out to the payment requestor.

If you already have a Recipient Profile

If your email is already associated with a Recipient Profile, you’ll be prompted to log into your account and verify payment details before funds are sent.

Navigating your Recipient Profile dashboard

Your Recipient profile dashboard is where you manage your payment activity. Your Lite dashboard allows you to:

  • View status of incoming transactions
  • Navigate to your Transactions page to track incoming transactions
  • Access Mercury’s Invoicing tool where you can generate invoices
  • View your profile information, payment details and linked account

FAQs

Do I need a full Mercury account to receive payments?

No, you do not need a full Mercury account or a Recipient profile to receive payments. However, a Recipient profile allows you to receive payments and track them without opening a full Mercury account. A Recipient profile does not include access to checking and savings accounts, cards, or other banking features.

How long does it take for a payment to post?

All funds follow our standard processing times. You can read more about timelines here or reach out to the requestor for more information.

Is creating a Recipient profile required?

No. You can skip this step and still provide your payment details and receive funds as usual without creating a profile.

Can I update my payment details later?

If you have a Recipient profile, you can do this with each new incoming payment request, or anytime from your dashboard by clicking the pencil icon beside “My payment details”.

Can I use a Recipient profile to send payments?

No. Recipient profiles are designed for receiving payments to the banking details you provide and generating invoices that you can save as a pdf and send.

Can I upgrade to a full Mercury account later?

Yes. You can apply for a full Mercury account at any time from the bottom-left of your Recipient Profile dashboard.

Using a third-party payroll provider

If you need to set up ACH debit configurations after moving your banking to Mercury, switching between Mercury’s partner banks, or for processing payroll, you’ll need to update your account details with relevant service providers.

This article covers connecting a third-party payroll provider — like Gusto, Rippling, or Deel — by ACH debit or reverse wire.

Using Mercury Payroll? Payroll is funded from your Mercury account automatically, so there’s nothing to connect. See Getting Started with Mercury Payroll instead.

The most common method for connecting payroll providers to Mercury is from a Mercury checking account via ACH debit, also known as ACH pull or direct debit (if outside of the U.S.). Some payroll providers also support reverse wires, also known as wire drawdowns. Which method you use will depend on what your payroll provider supports or requires from your company.

How to set up or update ACH debits

  • If you do have ACH authorization enabled on Mercury, you can add newly created checking accounts to existing authorizations from your Authorizations page.   • Please note that if you do not authorize your service provider as a vendor or they initiate a transaction above the set transaction limit, one of your org admins will be notified to review the ACH pull. If that window expires without admin approval or rejection, the ACH pull will be automatically approved or rejected, depending on your organization’s settings.
  • Did you know? ACH authorization ensures the fastest processing for recurring payments. Learn how to set it up here.
  • Retrieve the account number and routing numbers for your Mercury account. You can do this by clicking the account (located under your “Accounts” tab) and copying the numbers from the details card in the top right. Your service provider will need these to complete the ACH debit setup.
  • Follow the instructions from your service provider to complete the setup. Here are links to instructions from some common providers that support ACH debit:

If you can’t find instructions for how to connect or change your linked bank account, you can try these steps:

  • Log in to your service provider portal and navigate to the settings page where you can connect or change your bank account information.

However, if Plaid is not an option, you can use manual verification — this usually takes 2–3 days and begins with the provider making 1–2 micro-deposits (random amounts that are typically less than $0.50) into your bank account that you will need to verify by logging in and inputting the amount. These deposits will be reversed after the verification process.

How to set up reverse wires (also known as wire drawdowns)

Some service providers (primarily payroll) require companies to fund payments through a reverse wire (sometimes called wire drawdown). Follow the instructions here to set up your payments via reverse wires.

Using the Payments page

Your Payments page makes it easy to create, track, and manage both payments and bills. This article covers what you’ll see on the page, how to use the tabs, and where to manage settings like bill forwarding.

Overview of the Payments page

Your Payments page includes tabs that help you manage each step of your payment process:

  • Inbox: Forward or uploaded bills that haven’t been queued for approval, scheduling, or paid yet
  • Needs Approval: Payments awaiting admin review based on your approval rules
  • Scheduled: Payments that have been approved and scheduled
  • Paid: Completed payments that have been successfully sent

In each tab, you can Filter the list by Status (e.g. Overdue, Due in the next 7 days, Missing due date, etc.).

Depending on your role, you’ll see different options when you click into a payment:

Admins can:

  • Review payment details
  • Approve or Delete a payment pending approval

Submitters can:

  • Edit payment details
  • Cancel requests

Initiating payments

You can initiate payments in two main ways:

1. Send money (without attaching a bill)

Use this to send funds directly to a recipient. Click Send Money at the top of the Payments page to:

  • Search for an existing recipient or add a new one
  • Enter an amount and payment method
  • Schedule or send immediately
2. Upload bill

If you have a bill you want to attach, click Upload Bill instead. We automatically scan the bill and extract details using Optical Character Recognition (OCR) to fill out payment details. Once uploaded, the bill will appear in your Inbox and can be reviewed, approved, and scheduled.

You can read more about bill pay here.

Setting up bill forwarding

To save time, you can forward bills by email so they automatically land in your Inbox.

Finding your bill forwarding email

Your bill forwarding email appears at the top of the Payments page, next to the gear icon. You can click to copy or select the gear icon to edit the address if needed. Forwarded bills will appear in your Inbox and follow your normal approval flow once they have been reviewed.

Payments settings

Click the gear icon to access your Payments settings, where you can manage:

  • Bill forwarding email: View or copy your custom email address
  • Approval rules: Set thresholds for when admin approval is required
  • Approved senders: Prevent emails from unknown senders from being auto-processed
  • Accounting sync: Connect your accounting software to speed up reconciliation

Viewing cashflow and transactions data on your Transactions page

You can analyze cashflow, top spend, and transaction trends directly from your Transactions page. This guide shows how to use graphs, filters, and table tools to review your finances in real-time and speed up end of month close.

View your cashflow and top trends

At the top of the Transactions page, you’ll see two real-time graphs designed to help you understand how your money is moving:

  • Cashflow:
    • Displays money in and out over time, defaulting to the current month. View daily changes by hovering over the graph.
    • The graph is dynamic and will update based on any filters applied to the Transactions table – so whether you’re slicing by category, account, or timeframe, you’re always looking at the right data.
  • Top Money Movements:
    • Quickly identify your top five sources of cash inflows and outflows, ranked by volume. Use the dropdown in the top-left to group by Account, Card, Merchant Type, Category, and more.
    • Once selected, the graph will update to show the sources of the highest cash movement – green bars for money in, red for money out.

Filter, sort, and group your transactions

Use the Transactions table to explore or organize your financial data in more detail:

  • Quick Filters: Narrow down your view of transactions by Date, Amount, or Keyword
  • Advanced Filters: Click the Filters menu to apply more specific filters such as Category, Merchant Type, Team Member, Method, GL Code, and more.
  • Customize Menu: Allows you to:
    • Sort transactions by Date, Amount, Account and more
    • Group transactions by Merchant Type, Card, Category and more
    • Adjust the timezone used for displaying dates
    • Show or hide the graphs at the top of the page

Grouping transactions adds collapsible section headers with money in and money out totals, making it easier to review specific segments of spend. Grouping actions will also update the graphs to match.

Save and reuse filtered views

You can save a combination of filters as a Data View:

  • Apply any combination of filters in the table
  • Click Create View, give your view a name, and hit Save
  • Access your saved views anytime from the Data Views dropdown

We’ve created a few default views to help you get started, including:

  • My transactions
  • Monthly money in
  • Monthly money out

Edit and clean up transactions

The Transactions page lets you refine and enrich your transaction data quickly and accurately.

  • Inline Editing:
    • GL Codes: If you’ve connected an ERP, select a GL code from the dropdown to add it to a single transaction and sync it to your integrated accounting software.
    • Categories: Once categories are set up, you can assign them to transactions via the dropdown.
  • Bulk Editing: Select multiple rows using the checkboxes to the left of the Transactions table, then click Edit to bulk apply GL codes or categories across all selected items.

Business: Mercury Account

Account inactivity, restrictions, and closures (Business: Mercury Account)

If you received an email from Mercury about inactivity, your account has gone an extended period without qualifying activity. This article explains what counts as activity, what happens if your account remains inactive, and how to restore access if your account is restricted.

What counts as qualifying activity

Any one of the following counts as qualifying activity:

  • Add funds to your account via ACH, wire, or check deposit
  • Log in to Mercury at mercury.com or through the mobile app. For help logging in, visit our Security section
  • Initiate or receive an incoming or outgoing transaction
  • Contact Mercury Support

You only need to complete one of these activities at least once every 12 months to keep your account active.

If you no longer need your Mercury account, you can close it at any time by following the steps in Closing your Mercury account.

What happens if your account stays inactive

Your account is considered inactive after 12 consecutive months or more without qualifying activity.

Mercury regularly reviews accounts for qualifying activity to comply with state unclaimed property laws and banking partner requirements. This process applies to all Mercury accounts.

Taking any qualifying action reactivates your account. You don’t need to contact us to confirm—we’ll see the activity and update your account automatically.

What happens next depends on whether your account has a balance.

If your account has a $0 balance

An inactive account with a $0 balance will be closed if there’s no qualifying activity by the closure date in your email.

Before closure, we’ll email you with the subject “Your Mercury account will be closed due to inactivity” and include the date your account is scheduled to close.

Taking any qualifying action before that date keeps your account open.

If there’s no qualifying activity before the closure date, we’ll close the account and email you to confirm. Closed accounts can’t be reopened, but you can apply for a new account at mercury.com, subject to approval.

If your account holds a balance

An account with a balance remains fully functional when it first becomes inactive, and you may not receive a notification since no restrictions have been placed. If the inactivity continues, the account may later be restricted. At that time, we will notify you.

When your account becomes inactive

No restrictions have been applied at this point. Taking any qualifying action will reactivate your account.

When your account becomes restricted

If your account reaches 22 consecutive months without qualifying activity, we’ll restrict it and email you with the subject “Action Required: Your Mercury account is restricted due to inactivity.”

The email will include the date the restriction was applied and your current balance.

While your account is restricted:

  • Your funds remain secure
  • Your account data and history remain intact
  • You can’t send or receive payments, or initiate transfers

To restore access, log in to Mercury and complete any required account and identity verification as possible. We’ll review your information and contact you if we need anything else.

If you don’t want to complete verification, you’ll also have the option to close your account when you log in. You don’t need to complete verification to receive your remaining funds.

Unclaimed property and escheatment

If an account with a balance remains inactive long enough to pass the applicable State dormancy period, State unclaimed property laws may require Mercury to transfer the remaining balance to the State. This process is called escheatment.

State dormancy periods are typically three to five years from the last qualifying activity, depending on the State associated with your account.

Before your funds are transferred

Before your funds are remitted to the State, you will receive a letter with the date they’re scheduled to be transferred. The letter will be sent to the legal address on file.

Until that transfer occurs, you may still be able to reclaim your funds from Mercury by logging in and completing the required verification.

After your funds are transferred

Once the funds have been transferred, your Mercury account is closed and the funds are held by the State.

Your funds aren’t lost, but you’ll need to claim them from the State:

  • Visit the unclaimed property website for the State named in the notice we sent you
  • Search for unclaimed property under your legal name or business name (if you have a Mercury business account)
  • Follow the state’s instructions to file a claim

Claims typically take 30–90 days once filed, though timelines and documentation requirements vary by state.

If your account has a non-US address

The state that receives escheated funds generally depends on the address associated with the account.

For accounts without a US address, Mercury will remit the funds to Delaware, where Mercury is incorporated. If your funds have already been transferred, you can file a claim with Delaware’s unclaimed property office.

Add or change a custom logo on your Mercury account

You can personalize your Mercury account by adding a custom logo. The logo will appear throughout your dashboard and to other members of your team, internally.

Here’s how to add and edit a custom logo:

  • Click on your company menu in the top left-hand corner of your dashboard and select Settings.
  • Beside your company name, hover over the placeholder icon and click Add logo.
  • Drag and drop or click to upload a JPEG/JPG version of your logo.
  • Crop the logo if needed and click Save.

Adding or removing owners

Mercury requires information about anyone who owns 25% or more of your company. If your company’s ownership changes, an admin can request an update directly from your Mercury dashboard. You can add or remove owners, update ownership percentages, and submit supporting documents in one request for our team to review.

Requesting an ownership change

To add or remove an owner:

  • On your Mercury web, click your company name in the top-left corner and select All Settings
  • Under “Company profile,” find “Owners” and click Edit
  • Select the ownership changes you’d like to make, including adding or removing owners or updating ownership percentages
  • Enter the requested information and upload any supporting documents
  • Submit the request for review

If you don’t see the Owners > Edit option, contact our support team to request an ownership change. Include details about the owner you’re adding or removing, such as their name, email, title, and ownership percentage. Our team may request additional documentation to process the change.

What to have ready

Before starting, make sure you have the following information and documents ready:

  • Details of the owners you’re adding or removing
  • Updated ownership percentages, if applicable
  • Supporting documents related to the ownership change

Additional information or documentation may be requested during the review process.

FAQs

What if my company is owned by another business?

We require a real person to be listed as a beneficial owner. If your business is owned partially or wholly by another legal entity, you’ll need to include the individual(s) who own that entity as the beneficial owner. Anyone with significant ownership of the company (whether direct or pass-through ownership of the parent company) should be listed.

Do beneficial owners need account access?

No, it is not required that beneficial owners have account access. We understand that not all owners are managers of the business, and vice versa.

What if no individual owns 25% or more?

At minimum, we need to list owners with 25% ownership. If there is no individual party that owns 25% or more, we need to list at least one person with the highest ownership percentage or responsibility for managing the legal entity. This can include a senior executive or director, shareholder with the highest ownership, or other parties with significant influence over the company’s management and operations.

Consolidating your Mercury Business accounts

Our partner bank model

Mercury works with several FDIC-insured banks to provide essential banking services such as depository accounts, FDIC insurance through sweep networks, and the ability to send and receive money. Many Mercury customers have active checking and savings accounts with more than one of our partner banks. There are instances where customers may want or need to consolidate their accounts into one partner bank.

This article will walk you through the process of consolidating your accounts, including balances and financial activity, into one partner bank.

What does it mean to consolidate your accounts?

Consolidating accounts means transferring your deposited funds held at one of Mercury’s FDIC-insured bank partners to another, so that all of your balances and active accounts are with the same partner bank. You will still have access to the same Mercury experience and features.

How can I tell which partner bank each of my accounts are held with?

Log into your Mercury dashboard and open the Accounts page to view all of your accounts. Click into an account to view its details. On the right hand side of the screen, you will see the name of the Mercury partner bank associated with that account.

To consolidate your accounts, please follow the steps below.

1: Transfer funds into your accounts with the desired partner bank.

  • You can get started by clicking the Send Money button in the top right hand corner of your dashboard and clicking Transfer.
  • Transfers between Mercury’s banking partners typically take 1-2 business days.

2: Review any ACH debits you currently have set up in your old accounts.

  • Create a list of companies that initiate ACH debits from your old accounts, and provide them with your preferred account information so that payroll, benefits, taxes and similar expenses continue getting paid.
  • You can use filters on your Transaction page to review recent ACH debits.
  • For more information on looking up your account numbers and updating ACH debits, see here.

3: Review scheduled payments.

  • Recreate any scheduled payments tied to your old accounts. You can do this by navigating to your Scheduled tab of your Payments page. Click into each scheduled payment, note the details, and recreate the payment from your preferred account. When you are done, delete the scheduled payments in your old account.
  • More information on managing scheduled payments can be found here.
  1. Replace any physical and virtual debit cards.
  • Any debit cards tied to your old accounts will be canceled once they are closed. You can create replacement debit cards tied to your preferred accounts from your Cards page. More information on issuing new debit cards can be found here.
    • Please note that if you have any scheduled or recurring payments tied to your old debit cards, you will need to update them with your new card details.
  • Any IO credit cards will continue to work as normal. However, if IO payments were formerly made from one of your old account(s), you will need to update your credit autopay account to one of the account(s) into which you are consolidating your funds. You can do this by clicking Edit Autopay from your Credit Card page. More details on editing your autopay settings can be found here.

5: Review your auto-transfer rules.

  • Edit any rules that are tied to the old accounts to your preferred accounts. The partner bank is conveniently labeled for you to easily edit these.
  • Head to your Auto Transfers page, click the vertical ellipses (…) and then click Edit Rule to change the accounts.
  • More information on creating and managing auto transfers rules can be found here.

6: Review your payment requests.

  • Head to your Payment Requests page. Click into any outstanding request (these will be marked as Active or Overdue) and edit the “Destination account” to any of your preferred accounts.

7: Review any wire drawdown authorizations you currently have set up.

  • Create a list of companies that initiate wire drawdowns from your old accounts, and provide them with your preferred account information so that payroll, benefits, taxes and similar expenses continue getting paid.
  • Update your wire drawdown authorizations’ source accounts from your old accounts to new accounts here. You can also create additional authorizations for your new accounts while your drawdown beneficiaries which account they request from.
  • See more about wire drawdowns here

8: Close your old accounts.

  • Once you’ve completed these steps and your old accounts have a balance of $0, you can close them out by following the steps here.
    • You can also do this if there are duplicate or unnecessary accounts open on your preferred Mercury partner bank.
  • Once the old accounts have been closed, you’ll still be able to access statements and transaction history. However, new incoming and outgoing payments will fail, so please ensure you’ve followed the steps outlined above.

Earning referral bonuses for Mercury business accounts

Referral bonus qualifications

Linking and switching Mercury accounts (Business: Mercury Account)

If you have more than one Mercury account (or are on more than one team that uses Mercury), there are a few ways you can link accounts to easily switch between them without needing to log out and log in again.

Link more than one account to your profile

When you create or are invited to your first Mercury account, you create a profile that includes an email address, password, and some basic info like your name and 2FA preferences.

You’re able to link multiple Mercury accounts to a single profile so that you can seamlessly switch between different accounts without needing to log out and log in again. Linked accounts are only visible to you and can’t be seen by admins or anyone else using the Mercury account, so you can confidently link a side hustle or personal account as needed.

Applying for a new Mercury account using an existing profile

  • Click on your company name in the top left-hand corner of your dashboard
  • You’ll see the option to Apply for new account
  • You’ll be able to start a new application that uses an existing profile. If the application is approved, your new account will be automatically linked to the profile you used when applying. Alternatively, you can apply with a new and separate email address.
Joining another team’s Mercury account with an existing profile

Ask your contact or the admin who’s inviting you to add you to their Mercury account using your existing profile email. You’ll receive an email invite and the Mercury account will automatically be linked to your profile once you accept.

Linking an existing profile to share linked accounts

Until recently, you needed to create a new profile (and thus use a separate email) for every Mercury account you created or were invited to. You can now link your existing profiles to effectively link any associated accounts as well and switch seamlessly between them.

Here’s how to do it:

  • While logged in to one of the Mercury accounts you want to link, open your company menu in the top left corner of your dashboard
  • Select Link existing account
  • You’ll be prompted to log in with the profile associated with the other account
    • If that profile is already linked to others, you’ll see a list of all the Mercury accounts you’ll be able to switch between before you proceed
  • Enter your 2FA verification code, then click Log In & Link
  • If successful, you’ll be switched to your other Mercury account
Editing an existing email to link profiles

To edit an existing email to one that’s already in use, you’ll want to follow the steps of inviting yourself as a team member as opposed to editing your own email.

  • If you’re an admin, follow the steps listed here to invite yourself to the account under your preferred email
  • If you’re a non-admin, you’ll need to ask an admin on file to invite your preferred email

Once your preferred email has been added, the old profile can be removed from your Team page. Please note that any cards tied to the removed email will be automatically deleted so you’ll need to set those back up under the new profile.

Managing linked accounts and profiles

Go to your Profile settings. From here, you can view and un-link other Mercury profiles you’re linked to, and also view which Mercury accounts are directly linked to your current profile.

Note: Linked profiles are only visible to you. Other members of your organization can’t see that profiles are linked or view any details of the linked profile.

Managing AI agents connected to Mercury (Business: Mercury Account)

Agent Controls lets you view and manage the AI tools your team has connected to Mercury. You can see who connected each agent, review its permissions and activity, and disconnect agents when needed.

Who can use Agent Controls

Admins can access Agent Controls in Mercury on the web, including from a mobile browser. Agent Controls isn’t currently available in the Mercury mobile app.

What counts as an AI agent

An AI agent is a tool connected to Mercury through Mercury MCP, such as ChatGPT, Claude, or Cursor, or through the Mercury CLI.

Each time someone authorizes a tool, Mercury creates a separate connection. This means the same tool may appear more than once in Agent Controls.

API tokens and other integrations, such as accounting software, don’t appear in Agent Controls.

Finding Agent Controls

  • Go to Settings
  • Under “Security & Controls,” select Agent Controls

The “Agent Controls” page has three tabs: Agents, Activity, and Explore.

If no one on your team has connected an agent, the page opens on the Explore tab.

Viewing your team’s connected agents

The Agents tab shows a summary of your team’s agent connections, including:

  • Authorized connections: Total number of authorized agent connections
  • Users with agents: Number of team members who have connected agents
  • 3rd party tools: Number of third-party tools connected
  • All activity: Agent activity across your team

Below the summary, the “Connected agents” table lists each connection and its details:

  • Owner: The team member who connected the agent. Currently, only admins and custom roles with the permission to use Mercury via MCP can connect AI tools.
  • Agent: The AI tool and when it was last used or connected
  • Permissions: What the agent can view or do in Mercury

Agents can have two permission levels:

  • Read only: View information such as accounts, balances, transactions, and receipts
  • Read & write: View information, update transaction notes and categories, and prepare payments for approval

Note: Agents with Read & write access can’t move money on their own. Payments and transfers they prepare must be approved in Mercury before money moves, and your existing approval rules still apply.

Viewing an agent’s details and permissions

Select an agent from the “Connected agents” table to view its details, including:

  • Created by: The team member who connected the agent
  • Created on: When the connection was created
  • Last used: When the agent last accessed Mercury
  • Permissions: What the agent can view or do
  • Recent activity: Actions the agent has taken

The permissions table compares what the agent’s owner can do with what the agent can do, including:

  • Viewing accounts and balances
  • Downloading statements
  • Viewing transactions and receipts
  • Viewing recipients
  • Editing memos and attaching receipts
  • Categorizing transactions
  • Drafting payments for approval

An agent’s access is limited by its owner’s permissions. To reduce an agent’s access, you can change the owner’s role.

Changing the owner’s role also changes what they can do in Mercury and disconnects all of their agents.

Disconnecting an agent

To disconnect an agent from Mercury:

  • Open the Agents tab
  • Select the agent from the “Connected agents” table
  • Select Disconnect
  • Select Revoke to confirm

The agent loses access to Mercury immediately.

In some cases, disconnecting an agent also removes the owner’s other connections to the same tool. If this applies, you’ll see a message before confirming.

Disconnecting an agent doesn’t prevent its owner from connecting the tool again later. To prevent this, turn off Use Mercury via MCP in their role’s permissions (this also disconnects agents for everyone with that role), or assign them another role without the Use Mercury via MCP permission.

Reviewing agent activity

The Activity tab shows actions your team’s connected agents have taken in Mercury.

To review all activity across your account, select View all activities to open the Activity Log.

For more information, see Reviewing activity in your Mercury account.

Connecting a new AI tool

The Explore tab shows AI tools that work with Mercury MCP, along with how many people on your team have connected each tool.

Supported tools include ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor, Perplexity, Gemini Enterprise, Grok Bot, Microsoft 365 Copilot, Notion, Replit, Claude Code, Codex CLI, and other MCP clients.

To connect a tool:

  • Open the Explore tab
  • Select the tool you want to connect
  • Select Connect and follow the setup instructions

For more information, see Connecting Mercury to ChatGPT, Claude, and other AI tools.

FAQs

Why did an agent disappear from Agent Controls?

An agent is removed from Agent Controls when:

  • Someone disconnects it
  • Its owner’s role changes
  • The permissions associated with its owner’s role change
  • Its owner is removed from your team

The owner can reconnect the tool if they still have access to Mercury.

Can team members who aren’t admins use Agent Controls?

No. Only admins can access Agent Controls. Other team members can disconnect their AI tools through the tools’ own settings.

Does connecting an agent change anyone’s permissions?

No. An agent operates within its owner’s existing permissions and can’t do more than its owner can.

Managing emails (Business: Mercury Account)

You can add more than one email to your Mercury profile and log in with any of them.

This article explains how to add and remove emails, which email is used for logging in, security, and notifications, what admins can see, and how emails work when you belong to more than one account. You can manage your emails on the web or in the Mercury app for iOS and Android.

Email types at a glance

Email type

What it’s used for

How many

Log in emails

Log in to Mercury and reach all your accounts

Every verified email on your profile is a log in email.

Security email

2-Factor Authentication (2FA) reset codes, password resets, account recovery, security notices, and replies from our support team

Exactly one per profile. It’s the same in every account.

Notification email

Notifications for one accounts

One per account. By default, it’s the email you were invited with.

One email can have more than one type. For example, the same email can be your security email and the notification email for your business.

Logging in

You can log in with any verified email on your profile. Your password and passkey are the same no matter which email you use.

After you log in, you’ll land in the account you used last. To go to a different one, select the account switcher in the upper left corner.

Adding and verifying an email

On the web

  • Go to Settings, then select Profile
  • Under Emails, select Edit emails
  • Select Add email and enter the email
  • Select Save

In the Mercury app

  • Go to Settings and select your profile
  • Select Edit
  • Under Login emails, select Add email, enter the email, and confirm
  • Save your changes: select Done on iOS or Save on Android

You can add up to 5 emails at a time. You may be asked to confirm it’s you before your changes are saved.

Next, check the inbox for each new email. Open the verification email from Mercury and select the link.

Until you verify an email, it shows Needs verification. You can’t log in with it, or choose it as your security or notification email, until it’s verified.

Note: Verification links expire after 30 days. To get a new one, find the email in your list of emails, open its options, and select Resend verification email.

You can’t add an email that:

  • Is already on your profile or on another Mercury profile
  • Has a pending invite to one of your accounts
  • Is used for receipt forwarding. See Receipt forwarding below
Removing an email
  • Open your list of emails:
    • On the web: go to Settings › Profile and select Edit emails
    • In the app: go to Settings, select your profile, then select Edit
  • Select the email, then select Delete login email. For an email you haven’t verified yet, select Delete
  • Confirm, then save your changes

You can remove any of your emails, with some exceptions:

  • Your security email. Choose a different security email first, then remove the old one. That also means you can’t remove your only email.
  • A notification email. You can remove it, but we’ll warn you first: that account’s notifications will go to your security email instead, and its admins will be able to see your security email.
Security email

Your security email is where we send anything related to keeping your profile safe: 2-Factor Authentication (2FA) reset codes, password resets, account recovery, and security notices.

Note: Replies from our support team also go to your security email. You can write to us from any verified email, but if you write from a different one, you’ll get an automatic reply letting you know where we’ll respond.

Your security email is also the backup for your notification emails. If you remove an account’s notification email, that account’s notifications go to your security email.

Changing your security email
  • If the email you want isn’t on your profile yet, add and verify it first
  • Go to Settings, then select Security
  • Select Security email. On the web, select Edit
  • Choose one of your verified emails, then save

You’ll always have exactly one security email. It stays the same no matter which account you’re working in. Your previous security email stays on your profile as a log in email; remove it if you don’t need it anymore.

Admins can’t see or change your security email. The only exception: if an account falls back to your security email for notifications (see Removing an email), that account’s admins can see it.

Notification emails

You have a notification email for each account you belong to. It’s where we send the notifications you’ve turned on for that account. Because it’s set per account, you can send each one somewhere different, like your work email for the company you work at and your personal email for a side business.

By default, it’s the email you were invited to that account with. You can change it to any verified email on your profile.

Admins of that account can see it. They can’t see your other emails. An admin chooses this email when they invite you, but after that only you can change it.

Changing a notification email
  • Switch to the account you want to change the notification email for
  • Go to Settings, then select Notifications
  • Select Notification email. On the web, select Edit email
  • Choose one of your verified emails, then save

Changing it only affects the account you’re in. Your other accounts keep their own notification emails.

Receipt forwarding (business accounts only)

Receipt forwarding emails and log in emails are separate:

  • Adding an email for receipt forwarding doesn’t let you log in with it.
  • You can’t add an email as a log in email while it’s being used for receipt forwarding. To use it for logging in, remove it from receipt forwarding first.

Read more about receipt forwarding here.

What admins can see and do

Admins can see only your notification email for that account. They can’t see your security email or your other log in emails. The exception is when you remove your notification email: your security email becomes the fallback, and that account’s admins can see it.

Admins choose your email when they invite you. After that, they can’t change it.

If you belong to more than one account

Your emails belong to you, not to an account, so they work across every account you’re part of.

Switching accounts: Log in with any verified email and you’ll land in the account you used last. To switch, select the account switcher in the upper left corner, then select the account you want.

Joining another account: If you’re invited with an email that’s already on your profile, log in and accept the invite. The account is added to your existing profile, and you don’t need a new password. If you’re invited at with an email that isn’t on any Mercury profile yet, you can log in first and add it to your existing profile when you accept, or create a new profile with it.

If you’d like to keep your emails separate but easily switch between Mercury accounts see our Linking and switching Mercury accounts article.

Managing your notification settings

Team members can customize the alerts they receive for account activity, payments, balances, and more. Notification settings are personal — each team member manages their own preferences and are dependent on their permissions and account access.

Where to find your notification settings

You can access your notification settings from two places in the Mercury dashboard:

  • Your personal profile: Click your personal logo in the top right corner, then select Notifications
  • Company settings: Click your company name in the top left corner, select Settings, and scroll to Notifications

What you can control

Notifications are organized into two groups: important alerts that may require action, and general account updates.

Important updates and actions to take

These notifications cover high-priority activity across your account:

  • Cash flow — tracks money moving in and out of your account (Email & push)
  • Suspicious activity — alerts you to anything irregular (Email & push)
  • Tasks and approvals — notifies you of pending requests and to-dos (Email & push)
General updates about your account

These notifications keep you informed about specific features and activity, including spending, account balances, reimbursement, team changes and more. You can turn each category on or off independently.

How to update a notification

  • Navigate to your Settings > Notifications
  • Locate the notification category you want to update
  • Click the arrow ( > ) next to the current delivery method
  • Toggle your preference depending on the options available: Email, Push, or Off
  • Click Done to save your changes

Push notifications are sent to the phone number we have on file. You can confirm and manage phone numbers from Settings > My Profile.

Delivery methods

Available delivery options vary by notification category. Head to your Notifications page to confirm and configure your selections.

Mercury account types

Business accounts

Simplify your finances with powerful business banking*. Mercury’s business accounts allow you to efficiently manage your business’ banking and financial operations from a single dashboard.

Individual accounts

Individual Mercury Personal accounts are owned by a single individual account holder. Key characteristics include:

  • Account in the account holder’s name
  • Full control over funds
  • Up to $5 million FDIC insurance** coverage
  • Payments must be sent and received in the name of the account holder

These accounts are ideal for personal finances.

Joint accounts

Joint Mercury Personal accounts are co-owned by two or more individual account holders. They offer:

  • Account in all account holder’s names
  • The ability to receive payments in the name of any account holder
  • Increased FDIC insurance (up to $5 million** per account holder)
  • Automatic transfer to surviving account holders upon death

Joint accounts are common for couples or situations where it’s advantageous to have shared finances.

FAQs

How do I pay for a Mercury subscription?

Payments to Mercury subscriptions are withdrawn from your primary account balance. Therefore, it is important to ensure you have sufficient funds each month, your account will be in a 7-day grace period until the payment is made. Afterwards, you will be unsubscribed from the plan and lose access to any features.

When am I charged for my subscription?

The billing cycle begins on the first of the month, so monthly subscriptions renew on the first of the next month and annual subscriptions renew on the first of the same month, next year. If you subscribe or upgrade after the first of the month, you’ll be charged immediately for a pro-rated amount based on the remaining days in the current billing cycle.

If you start a Mercury Plus free trial, you aren’t charged when the trial starts. When the trial ends, you’re charged a prorated amount for the rest of that month, then the regular $35 on the 1st.

Why was I charged twice after my Mercury Plus free trial?

Two charges close together after a Mercury Plus free trial are expected. The first is a small prorated charge when your trial ends, covering the rest of that month. The second is the regular $35 monthly charge on the 1st.

What happens when I unsubscribe or downgrade?

Unsubscribed or cancelled accounts will have access to the plan until the end of the term (month or year depending on the plan). Downgraded accounts will also have access to the plan until the end of the term, and will be moved to the new plan at the start of the new billing cycle.

Please note that any time-based features associated with your plan, such as recurring invoices, will be cancelled once you’ve unsubscribed. Please plan accordingly to avoid any disruption.

Why am I paying sales tax for my subscription?

Certain states require sales tax on software-as-a-service that is delivered. If your legal address on file is in one of these states, you will see a sales tax on your monthly invoice. You can read more about sales tax here.

How are overages or fees charged?

Any overages or fees on top of your monthly/annual subscription (e.g. ACH debit transactions are $1/mo on Mercury Plus), you will see the total on the next monthly billing statement.

Ownership disputes

If you’re an account owner and are wondering if you’ve been removed from your Mercury account, here are few questions you can ask yourself to confirm that you’ve been removed:

  • Have you received an email informing you that you’ve been removed from your Mercury account?
  • When you login to your account, do you see the following error?: “Sorry, access to your account has been restricted. Contact us at help@mercury.com if you have questions.”

If neither of the above apply to you but you’re still having trouble logging in, we recommend the following:

  • Verifying that you are an owner of the account. Mercury considers any person with 25% or more ownership of a company to be an owner.
  • In the case that there are multiple administrators on the account, contact them in order to gain access?

If you’re still having trouble accessing your account, please contact our team at help@mercury.com. In order for our team to quickly identify your request, please use the subject line Help: Reinstate Account Access and provide as much detail as possible about your situation, including documentation that proves your ownership such as:

  • Operating Agreement
  • Articles of Organization
  • Initial Resolutions
  • Articles of Amendment
  • Notice of Sell of Ownership
  • Board Resolution (Corporate Resolution)
  • Corporate Bylaws
  • Articles of Incorporation

Please note that if an ownership dispute is identified, your account will be locked during the investigation process.

Request closure of your Mercury Business account

Our team is here to support you to make closing your account as smooth as possible.

Preparing to close your account

When preparing to close your account, please ensure these actions are taken in advance in order to avoid processing delays:

  • If you have an IO credit account with an outstanding balance, pay off the balance as soon as possible
    • Go to your Credit Account page
    • Near the top, select the Pay button
    • Select your payment amount and the account you want to pay from, then select Review and Confirm Payment
  • If you have a remaining deposit balance, transfer your funds to another financial institution
    • You can do this via ACH, wire transfer, or physical check, depending on account eligibility, or via linked account. Keep in mind that this process can take several days depending on the method you choose, so you’ll need to wait until those transfers have settled to close the account. If the account is closed with a positive balance, funds will be sent via check to either the shipping or legal address on file.
    • If you have investments in Mercury Treasury, you need to liquidate the funds and transfer them out of the Treasury account, then transfer them elsewhere via ACH or wire.
  • Ensure all pending incoming and outgoing transactions are settled. Any incoming payments to your account after it is closed will be canceled
  • Migrate any recurring transactions to another financial institution and update your vendors. You can view your current recurring transactions here, as well as your card subscriptions here to see what you will need to update
  • Download relevant account statements. Most account statements (including an account closure letters) will be available for you to access upon login even after your account is closed, but we recommend downloading necessary statements before then for your own reference
    • Note: To access Treasury statements post-closure, please reach out to our Support team.

Requesting account closure

You can initiate the account closure process from your Mercury dashboard as long as you meet the following criteria:

  • You’re a beneficial owner on the account
  • The account has no pending transactions
  • The total Mercury balance is $0.00, which means you’ve transferred all funds out of checking, savings, and other accounts. Please see the previous section, “Preparing to close your account” for more detail

Please note – you’ll need to either be a listed owner on the account or include a listed owner on the email to verify the account closure. We only need one owner to verify the closure, so please make sure to notify any other owners that you’re taking this action before proceeding.

Once the above criteria are met, here’s how to initiate the process of closing your Mercury account:

  • Log in to your Mercury account on the web
    • This flow is not currently available through the mobile app – it must be initiated through the web dashboard
  • Go to Settings > Company Profile
  • Scroll to the bottom of the page where it says “Close Account” and click Start Request
  • Review the information provided, then click Continue. If you still have a balance or any pending transactions, we’ll let you know that you can’t proceed
  • You’ll be asked to provide a reason for closing the account and given a chance to share any feedback about your Mercury experience
  • Finally, you can review your selections, and then submit your request by clicking Request to Close
  • Once submitted, your request will be reviewed by our team within 2 business days and the account will be closed. We’ll send you an email confirming everything’s good to go once it’s officially closed

Reviewing activity in your Mercury account (Business: Mercury Account)

The Activity Log shows a timeline of actions taken in your Mercury account, whether by your team, Mercury, or AI agents working on your team’s behalf.

Who can use the Activity Log

The Activity Log is available in Mercury on the web, including from a mobile browser.

Admins can view activity across the organization. Other team members can view their own activity.

Finding the Activity Log

  • Go to Settings
  • Under “Security & Controls,” select Activity Log

Viewing activity

The Activity Log groups activity by time, such as Today, Yesterday, and This week. Each entry shows what happened and when.

If an AI agent performed an action, the entry identifies the agent, such as via Mercury CLI, via Mercury Command, or the name of the connected AI tool.

Select an entry to view more details, including:

  • Actor: Who performed the action
  • When: When the action occurred
  • Agent: Which AI agent performed the action, if applicable
  • IP address: The IP address associated with the action
  • Device: The device associated with the action

New activity may take some time to appear. The timeline shows when it last synced.

Filtering activity

Select All filters to narrow the activity shown in the timeline.

You can filter by:

  • Keyword: Matches whole words in activity titles
  • Category: Accounts, Budgets, Cards, Recipients, Invoices, Payments, Team, Roles, Company settings, Security, API tokens, and Command
  • Actor (admins only): A specific team member, or No actor for actions without an associated team member
  • Platform: Command, MCP, CLI, Web, iOS, Android, or Public API
  • Agent: Activity from specific agent connections
  • Date: All dates, a recent month, or a Custom range

Admins can also switch between Org-Wide and Personal views.

Viewing routine login activity

Routine sign-ins, session refreshes, and account switches are hidden by default.

Turn on Routine Logins to include these events in the timeline. New-device, two-factor authentication, and password events always appear.

Exporting activity

To export activity as a CSV file:

  • Apply any filters you want
  • Select Export or Export filtered
  • Select Export CSV
  • When the file is ready, select Download CSV

Exports include all events matching your filters, including events that haven’t loaded in the timeline.

Download links expire. If your link has expired, select Refresh download link to generate a new one.

Note: If too many events match your filters, narrow the date range or adjust your filters and try again. You can’t combine the Agent and Actor filters in an export yet.

FAQs

How can I tell what an AI agent did in my account?

Filter by Agent or by Platform (MCP or CLI). Activity entries associated with an agent show its name.

Admins can also review each agent’s recent activity in Agent Controls.

Why don’t I see something that just happened?

The Activity Log syncs regularly, so new activity may take some time to appear. Check the last sync time shown in the timeline.

Sales Tax FAQ

What is this charge for?

With the launch of Mercury Invoicing on August 20, 2024, we are now considered to be a Software as a Service (SaaS) company. In certain states, SaaS products and services have sales tax obligations.

What is a SaaS company?

Software as a Service (SaaS) is traditionally considered a cloud-based software model that delivers applications to end-users through an internet browser. SaaS vendors host services and applications for customers to access on-demand. There are a handful of states that have sales tax obligations for SaaS products and services by state.

Why didn’t you charge me this before?

Prior to the launch of our new invoicing product on August 20, 2024, we were not considered as a Software as a Service provider.

Why wasn’t I notified of this change?

The T&Cs in the subscription agreement discusses that applicable taxes apply.

I am not based in the US. Why do I have to pay sales tax?

If you are not based in the U.S., you are not subject to U.S. sales tax rules.

I am tax-exempt. How can I update my tax status?

If you believe you are tax-exempt, please get in touch with us to submit your tax exemption certificate. If you are unsure of your tax status, please contact your tax advisor with any questions about a tax exemption.

I am tax-exempt. Why did you charge me for this? How can I get a refund?

If you believe you are tax-exempt, get in touch with us to submit your tax exemption certificate. We will issue a refund to you once we validate your tax exemption status.

Do I need to submit anything to the IRS?

No, this pertains to state and local jurisdictions. Mercury will collect your sales tax and submit it to the state and local taxing authorities as applicable.

Does Mercury do tax reporting? How does this affect my business?

Yes, once Mercury collects the sales tax from our customer, we will file the sales tax returns with the appropriate state and local taxing authorities.

How do I change the state I am taxed in?

The default billing address we use to determine the sales tax rate is based on your legal address under your customer profile. If that information is incorrect, please update your address.

Which states require the collection of sales tax?

Currently, 26 states or jurisdictions require the collection of sales tax. They are: Alaska; Arizona; Colorado; Connecticut; District of Columbia; Hawaii; Iowa; Chicago, Illinois; Kentucky; Louisiana; Maryland; Massachusetts; New Mexico; New York; Ohio; Pennsylvania; Puerto Rico; Rhode Island; South Carolina; South Dakota; Tennessee; Texas; Utah; Vermont; Washington; and West Virginia.
