Checkbooks overview

Mercury checkbooks let you write and manage physical checks directly from your account. This article covers when to use checkbooks, how to order one, and how to review and manage check activity from your dashboard. This is separate from the mailed checks you can send via the Send Money flow.

Use cases for issuing physical checks

Although most payments are sent via ACH or wire, sometimes you just need a physical check. This can be helpful when:

  • You need to pay someone on the spot
  • A payment requires accompanying paperwork
  • You need to provide a voided check, usually for someone to verify your account information
  • A recipient can’t accept ACH, wire transfers, or card payments

If you only need to send the occasional check, you can use the Send Money flow to have a paper check printed and mailed on your behalf. Read more about these one-off check payments here.

Ordering your checkbook

Please note that ordering checkbooks is restricted to admin users, and checkbooks can only be shipped to addresses within the United States and its territories.

  • Go to the left-hand menu on your Mercury dashboard on web, click Payments > Checkbooks
  • Click Order Checkbook
  • Enter these details for your checkbook:
    • Account: This indicates the specific checking account you want to enable for this checkbook. Note that each checkbook can only be assigned to one enabled checking account. However, enabled checking accounts can have multiple assigned checkbooks.
    • Your check nickname
    • Your checkbook number start number — since each Mercury checkbook includes 25 sheets, the full range will go from your start number up to the next 24 numbers. Be sure to use a start number where the range will not overlap with any existing check numbers you’ve already ordered from Mercury or a third party provider
    • Your shipping address — this is set to your company mailing address on file by default, but you can pick a different one. As a reminder, checkbooks can only be shipped to addresses within the United States and its territories.
  • Click Next
  • Choose your default check review setting:
    • Approve check: Check deposits will be automatically approved after the 24-hour review window expires
    • Reject check: Check deposits will be automatically rejected after the 24-hour review window expires
  • Review your selections, agree to the terms and conditions, and click Confirm

The final page will confirm your checkbook’s estimated shipping time. You’ll also receive an order confirmation and an update when the checkbook ships via email. The typical delivery time to expect is 10-14 business days.

You can also order a checkbook from a checking account page. To get there, head to your Accounts tab.

Navigating the Checkbooks page

Once you’ve ordered a checkbook, all check deposit attempts will show up on your Checkbooks page. You’ll be able to see:

  • Check no.: The unique check number on that particular check
  • Date: The date your recipient deposited your check
  • Amount: Amount on the check
  • Pay from: The check-enabled Mercury account you are paying from.
  • Review status: Pending checks will indicate the amount of time remaining in your review window before the default review action is applied

Click into any pending checks to see more details and take action. Please note that once a check has been approved or rejected, it will technically clear from the Checkbooks page and appear in your Transactions (rejected checks will show up as “blocked”).

In the bottom right, you can click View all check payments. This will show you your Transactions tab filtered for check payments. This shows:

  • Approved checks
    • Checks that were manually approved by your business during the checkbook review window
    • Checks that were approved via default review action after the review window expired
  • Failed checks
    • Checks that were manually rejected by your business during the checkbook review window
    • Checks that were rejected via default review action after the review window expired
    • Checks that were rejected because of insufficient funds

How does check review protect your account?

Whenever there is an attempted check deposit on one of your enabled check-issuing accounts, you’ll receive an email notification to review that check within ~24 hours and decide whether to approve or reject it. If the 24-hour window passes without a decision, your default check review action will apply.

Learn more in our check review article.

In the top right-hand corner, you’ll also see a Settings icon you can click to manage:

  • Which accounts are enabled for check issuing — enabling an account allows you to order Mercury checkbooks from them, as well as issue checks from 3rd party providers
  • Your default check review action
  • Your business’s checkbook order history

FAQs

Who can order checkbooks and enable accounts for checkbooks?

Only account admins can order checkbooks and edit which accounts are enabled for checkbooks.

What gets printed on each check?

The following details are included on each check:

  • The check number
  • The associated account number and routing number
  • Your legal business name
  • The legal address we have on file for your business

Can I print my DBA company name or a different address on my checks?

At this time, Mercury checkbooks cannot be printed with your DBA company name or a custom address. You can order checks from a third-party provider that allows you to customize these fields.

How do I order checks from a third party provider?

To order checks from a third party provider for your Mercury checking account, you’ll need to enable the account details. You can do this by heading to your Checkbooks page and clicking Settings. From there, you should be able to edit your enabled accounts. When you order checks through the third party, you can provide the account and routing numbers for the enabled account.

We recommend using the legal business name on your Mercury account when ordering checks through a third-party provider to avoid potential payment issues. Mercury is not responsible for any checks ordered through third-party providers.

Can I cancel my checkbook?

If you want to cancel your checkbook before it gets to you, reach out to help@mercury.com. If the checkbook hasn’t been mailed, we are able to cancel the checkbook. If it’s already been mailed, you will need to request a stop payment on the checkbook number range you ordered — our team can help you with this, or you can follow the instructions in our Stop payments article.

How long do checks take to show up on the Checkbooks page?

Deposited checks will usually appear on your Checkbooks page the same or next business day after your recipient deposits them. Please note that only deposited checks will show up on your Checkbooks page — if your recipient hasn’t deposited them yet, that record won’t appear in Mercury.

Will checks in the Send Money flow show up for review on the Checkbooks page?

No. Only physical checks you write will appear for review and on your Checkbooks page. Checks sent through Mercury’s Send Money flow are pre-approved — you can learn more about them here. Mailed checks can be viewed from your Transactions page.

What are common check terms I should be aware of?

Here are some of the terms people often see when dealing with checks and checkbooks, and what they mean:

  • Item: Any single check transaction, often referring to a check being processed.
  • Memo / Memo line: A note field on a check that can be used for reference. Doesn’t affect the payment.
  • Check review: Mercury’s fraud prevention service that matches checks presented to a list provided by the issuer. Also known as ‘Positive Pay’. Endorsement: When the recipient signs the back of the check, allowing it to be deposited.
  • Non-Sufficient Funds (NSF) / bounced check: A check that is returned unpaid due to the funding account lacking sufficient funds.
  • Deposited: The recipient’s bank has accepted the check.
  • Stop Payment: A stop payment prevents a check you’ve written from being deposited.

What if I don’t have enough funds in my account to cover a check payment?

Check payments are only processed if the associated Mercury account has sufficient funds. Avoid failed payments by:

  • Keeping an eye on account balances to make sure you have enough to cover your outstanding or upcoming check payments
  • Turning on notifications for low-balance alerts
  • Using auto-transfers to maintain minimum funds in your dedicated check-enabled account

How can I avoid errors or fraud when writing a check?

Always write the amount in both words and numerals, ensuring they match, and complete all fields (including date, payee, and signature). Avoid leaving blank spaces where extra text could be added. Use permanent, non-erasable ink, and keep a record of your check numbers for future reference.

Is there a maximum amount I can send by check?

Yes — each check item must be under $1 million. Any checks over this amount will be rejected.

Are checkbooks available for Mercury Personal?

No, only business checking accounts on Mercury are eligible for checkbooks at this time.

Covering recipient fees for USD international wires (Business: Send Money)

While Mercury doesn’t charge fees to send an international wire in USD, other banks might. When sending in USD, you can optionally choose to cover these fees for your recipient when sending a payment.

Understanding international wire fees

When an international wire is sent, it often passes through multiple intermediary banks before ultimately hitting your recipient’s account. If one bank in the chain doesn’t have a relationship with the next, they may charge an additional fee for their services.

Those fees are paid in one of two ways, depending on how the wire is coded.

  • If the wire is coded as Charges Shared (SHA), the fees are deducted directly from the wire amount. So if you sent $1000, and intermediary bank charges were $50, your recipient would end up with only $950 when all was said and done.
  • If the wire is coded as Charges Ours (OUR), the intermediary bank fees are covered by the payer and the recipient gets the full amount. The payer or payment provider pays a higher upfront cost to use this method.

How Mercury handles these fees

You have two options when it comes to sending international wires in USD:

  • Send the wire as a SHA payment. This option is free for you, as Mercury will cover the outgoing payment fees, but any intermediary bank fees will be absorbed by your recipient
  • Send the wire as an OUR payment for a flat $15 fee to cover any additional intermediary fees for your recipient.*

There’s not a lot of transparency built into this system, so it’s hard to predict the number or amount of fees your recipient might encounter when sending a wire as SHA. That’s why we allow you the option to send the payment as OUR, with the $15 flat fee going towards the higher upfront costs associated with this wire type.

We usually recommend choosing that option for high value transactions (such as contracts, invoice payments, etc) where you want to make sure there’s no question how much your recipient will get.

*This covers any fees that may occur while in transit between banks. Mercury does not reimburse fees charged by the receiving bank when accepting a wire.

How to cover your recipient’s fees

As long as you’re sending in USD, you can cover your recipient’s fees. Here’s how:

  • Create a new international wire by clicking the Move Money button in the upper right corner of your dashboard and selecting Pay Someone.
  • Fill out your recipient details.
  • When asked How do you want to pay?, select International Wire.
  • Below the Recipient Gets field, you’ll see a check box labeled Cover recipient’s fees. Check this box to add the coverage.
  • Once it has processed, the $15 fee will show up as a separate transaction on your Transactions page.

Fixing undeliverable addresses

When sending a payment or issuing a card, we use address verification software called LOB to verify the recipient’s address is valid. This data is tied to the United States Postal Service and ensures that cards can be delivered successfully within estimated delivery times and payments are going to legitimate recipients.

If you get an error message that says “That doesn’t seem to be a deliverable address,” there are a couple of things you can check to try and fix the issue yourself.

  • First, verify that the address meets the following criteria.
    • It only contains Latin characters and no special characters.
    • It’s a physical address and not a PO box.
    • Each address line is shorter than 35 characters.
  • Google the address. This sounds basic, but there should be a Google Maps link tied to the address if it’s valid. If you try street view and it’s an empty field, alley, or something similar, you may have an incorrect address and should confirm with the recipient.
  • Try the address directly in LOB. Go to lob.com, scroll down to “Try it Out,” and select either the Domestic US or International tabs. Enter the address and click Verify Now.
    • LOB may automatically correct small errors like street address typos. You can then copy the corrected address back into Mercury.
    • Since LOB data is tied to the USPS, it sometimes flags newer addresses that may not be in the system yet.
  • If nothing else works, contact our Support team. We may be able to override the error, but will need the following information in your email in order to help:
    • A link to the Google Maps results and/or a copy of the recipient’s wire details with address included (usually a PDF or screenshot).
    • The full address in this exact format:
    • Address Line 1 (Street):
    • Address Line 2 (Apt/Unit Number):
    • City:
    • State / Province / Region:
    • Zip / Postal Code:
    • Country:

Forwarding invoices to your Mercury account

You can forward invoices directly to your Payments page using a custom forwarding address to quickly pay invoices from your team and external vendors.

Forwarding an invoice

  • From the org menu in the top-right corner of your dashboard, click Settings > Company Profile
  • Scroll to locate your “Bill forwarding email”
  • From your email client (e.g. Gmail), use that address in the “To” field, then attach your invoice and click Send
    • Individual invoices must be less than 20MB each, and the total attachment size must be less than 35MB
    • Invoices should be jpg, .jpe, .jpeg, .png, .gif, .pdf, .txt, .htm, .html, .zip, .heic, .heif, .avif, .webp, or .ofd
    • You don’t need to use a specific subject line or body. Any text in the body will be converted to an attachment for review in your Mercury dashboard
  • Once received, you can view, edit, discard, or pay the invoice from your Payments page

Adding approved senders

By default, all team members on your Mercury account can forward invoices without limitation. You can also add external vendors or your existing accounts payable (AP) email address to your approved senders list.

Here’s how:

  • Go to your Payments page
  • Click the gear icon beside your forwarding email address to open your Payment settings
  • Beside “Approved senders” click Edit
  • Enter as many email addresses as you’d like, then click Save
    • You can edit or remove addresses later from this same location

Reviewing flagged and failed invoices

To prevent bad actors from spoofing emails on your approved senders list (and keep your Payments page clear of spam), we make use of Sender Policy Framework (SPF) Records and DomainKeys Identified Mail (DKIM) checks. If you’re already using a custom domain or a major email provider like Google or Office, you most likely make use of these already.

If a forwarded invoice or email doesn’t pass our checks, we’ll alert you on your Payments page with an Unverified status, at which point you can choose whether to add the email to your approved senders or discard the invoice.

Changing your forwarding address

You can change your forwarding address anytime from your dashboard. Here’s how:

  • Go to Settings > Company Profile
  • Next to the Bill forwarding email, click Edit
  • Enter your new email. It can be anything you like, but it will always end in @ap.mercury.com

Setting up auto-forwarding for Gmail

Before you can set up auto-forwarding, certain email clients (like Gmail) require you to verify the linked email address. Here’s how to do this:

  • Complete the necessary steps in Gmail first. This will trigger Gmail to send a verification email
  • Go to your Payments page. Once the verification email is received, a banner will appear on your Payments page
  • Click the link in the banner and complete the steps to finish verification

How ACH transfers and domestic wires work in the US

If you’re sending money within the U.S., it’s helpful to understand the differences between ACH transfers and domestic wires. This article covers how ACH transfers work, when to send a domestic wire, and what to expect from ACH processing.

What are ACH transfers and domestic wires?

Automated Clearing House (ACH) transfers and domestic wires both move money electronically between financial institutions in the U.S. The main difference is how they’re processed:

  • ACH transfers are processed in batches through the ACH network, so they typically take longer to complete
  • Domestic wires are processed individually and typically arrive the same business day when sent before the institution’s cutoff time.

To send either type of payment, you’ll generally need the recipient’s:

  • Routing number: Identifies the receiving financial institution
  • Account number: Identifies the recipient’s account
  • Full name as stated on their account: Used to identify the recipient
  • Amount: The amount being sent

For ACH transfers, you’ll also need the recipient’s account type, such as personal checking. This is a Nacha requirement that determines routing, return windows, and protections for the transaction.

Some financial institutions use different routing numbers for ACH transfers and domestic wires. Confirm the correct routing number with the recipient before sending your payment.

How long outgoing ACH transfers take

ACH transfers move money electronically between U.S. financial institutions through the ACH network.

Unlike domestic wires, ACH transfers are processed in batches rather than individually. ACH transfers can be standard or same-day, and processing times can also vary when a transfer involves a Plaid-linked external bank account.

For specific ACH and domestic wire timelines, see Processing times for payments.

FAQs

When should I send a domestic wire instead of an ACH transfer?

ACH transfers are a good option for most payments that aren’t time-sensitive. Consider sending a domestic wire instead when:

  • The recipient’s financial institution requires a wire for the type of payment you’re making
  • You need funds to arrive by a specific deadline, such as for a closing or settlement

To learn how to send an ACH transfer or domestic wire from your Mercury dashboard or the Mercury app, see Sending money overview.

How do I track an ACH payment?

Every ACH transfer receives a 15-digit Trace ID that financial institutions use to locate the payment within the ACH network.

If you need to track an incoming or outgoing ACH transfer, provide the Trace ID, along with the payment details to Mercury Support or the receiving financial institution.

For outgoing ACH transfers, the Trace ID may not appear immediately after you initiate the payment. It typically becomes available after the transfer has been submitted to the ACH network. To find the Trace ID for an outgoing ACH transfer, open the payment from your Transactions page and look for the “Transactions tracking number”.

How do I track a domestic wire?

Every domestic wire has a unique transaction tracking number, known as an IMAD, that identifies the transfer in the Fedwire system. The IMAD is formatted as YYYYMMDD ABCDXXXX 012345 and includes a date, source routing identifier, and number.

To find the IMAD for an outgoing domestic wire, open the payment from your Transactions page and look for the Transaction tracking number. If you need to track an outgoing domestic wire, provide the IMAD to the recipient for them to check with their financial institution.

You can read more about tracking payments and information needed to troubleshoot missing payments in our Tracking missing payments article.

Can I use the same routing number for ACH and wire transfers?

Not always. Some financial institutions use separate routing numbers for ACH transfers and domestic wires. Confirm the correct routing number with the recipient before sending your payment.

Are ACH transfers and domestic wires free?

Mercury doesn’t charge fees for incoming or outgoing ACH transfers or domestic wires. However, other financial institutions may charge fees for sending or receiving wires. Mercury can’t reimburse fees charged by another institution, so we recommend confirming any applicable fees with the sender or recipient before initiating a transfer.

Linking and transferring between Mercury accounts across organizations (Business: Send Money)

You can link Mercury accounts across organizations, so you can move funds between them more easily. This article covers how to set up a link between Mercury accounts, how to send a transfer, and how to troubleshoot common issues.

Before you begin

Linking accounts across Mercury has specific eligibility requirements. Review these before starting.

To create or delete a link, you must:

  • Be an admin on both organizations
  • Have shared ownership between the two orgs — someone must be listed as an owner on both

If you’re linking a Mercury Personal account:

  • The person creating the link must be both an admin and an owner of the Mercury Personal account

To send money to a linked account, you must have:

  • Send money permissions or be an admin on the account you’re sending from

How linking works

No sensitive information is shared or visible between linked accounts — linking only enables transfers.

Account links are one-directional. When you link two accounts, you can only push funds from the originating account to the linked account — you cannot pull funds from the linked account.

Linking Mercury accounts:

To link a Mercury account to another Mercury organization:

  • Click Accounts on the left-hand side of your Mercury dashboard on web
  • Navigate to the Linked accounts tab
  • Select Link Mercury account or click the dropdown next to “Create account” and click Link Mercury account
  • Choose the organization you want to link to — only eligible organizations will appear
  • Review the permissions summary and select Confirm link
Transferring funds to a linked account

Once the link is created, team members with send money permissions can start transferring funds to the linked account from the Transfer funds flow. You can read more about how to transfer funds between accounts here.

Transfer speeds will follow our regular timelines. Exact timing depends on whether both accounts share the same partner bank:

  • Same partner bank: Transfers typically take a few minutes.
  • Different partner banks: Transfers are processed via ACH and can take 1–3 business days

Troubleshooting

I don’t see the Mercury account I want to link

If an organization doesn’t appear when setting up a link, one of the following eligibility requirements likely isn’t met:

  • You are not an admin on both organizations
  • There is no shared ownership between the organizations — no single person is listed as an owner on both
  • For personal accounts: you are not both the admin and owner of the personal account

The dashboard only surfaces organizations you’re eligible to link with. If an org is missing, it’s because an eligibility condition hasn’t been met.

I’m an admin on both accounts but still can’t link

If the organizations don’t share an email address, Mercury may not be able to identify the connection between them without an existing profile link. Try linking your profiles first, then return to this flow.

If profiles are already linked, a data mismatch may be preventing the connection. Common causes include:

  • Name changes (such as after marriage)
  • Spelling variations between accounts
  • Outdated beneficial owner records

If you believe there’s a data mismatch on your account or still experiencing issues, contact Mercury support.

FAQs

Can I link a personal Mercury account to a business account?

Yes. To link a personal account, you must be both the admin and owner of the personal account, and shared ownership must exist between the two organizations.

Can I set up automatic transfers to a linked account?

Yes. You can use linked accounts as a destination for certain auto-transfer rules:

  • Distribute funds across accounts: Funds can be sent from Mercury to a linked external account
  • Maintain a target account balance: A linked external account can be used as the supporting account when funds are being sent out of Mercury

Auto-transfers to linked external accounts are sent via ACH and typically take 1–3 business days to arrive. Auto-transfers with linked external accounts are push-only, so funds can’t be pulled from an external account into Mercury.

What are the transfer limits for linked account transfers?

​​Linked account transfers have their own limits, separate from ACH limits. If a transfer exceeds your limit, you’ll be notified in the transfer flow and given the option to request an increase.

Can I link accounts at external banks?

To link an external bank account, you’ll need to do so via Plaid. You can read more about this here.

Processing times for payments (Business: Send Money)

Payments on Mercury process at different speeds depending on the type. This guide explains how long each payment type typically takes and what to expect for incoming and outgoing transactions. If you’re still missing a payment that you should have received based on this, check out our guide on tracking missing payments.

With the exception of real-time payments, transactions only process on working/business days (Monday through Friday), and not on holidays or weekends. If a transaction is created on a weekend, it will usually be processed on the next business day.

These timelines are general estimates. Some wires may take longer if they require manual review or if a bank holiday occurs during processing.

ACH processing times

ACH transactions are U.S-specific intra-bank transfers that only occur on business days.

Incoming ACH
  • Typically arrive within 0-2 business days and post around 9-11am PT, Monday-Friday. If you’re expecting an ACH credit and it’s before this time, it likely hasn’t arrived yet
  • Transfers from Plaid-linked accounts to Mercury take 3 business days and typically post around 3pm PT
  • Incoming invoicing payments via ACH debit, take 1-5 business days to arrive
Outgoing ACH
  • Once sent from your account, typically arrive with the recipient in 0-1 business days
  • Sent via same-day if sent prior to 12pm PT and less than $1,000,000 USD, otherwise, sent as next day and will arrive with the recipient the following business day
  • Transfers from Mercury to Plaid-linked accounts take 0-1 business days
  • Posting times will vary by receiving bank but typically same-day ACH transactions post later that afternoon

Domestic wire processing times

Domestic wires are ideal for sending large amounts quickly. These are same-day transactions, but not instant.

Incoming domestic wires
  • Typically arrive the same business day if sent before the sending bank’s wire cutoff time, otherwise, arrive next business day
  • Exact timing varies by sending bank. For example: Wells Fargo: received around 6:00pm PT, Bank of America: received around 9:00pm PT
Outgoing domestic wires
  • Our daily domestic wire cutoff is 1:30pm PT. If your wire is created before this time, your recipient should have their wire by evening that same day. If it was created after this time, your recipient will receive it the following business day.

Real-time payment (RTP) processing times

Incoming RTPs

Real-time payments (RTP) allow you to receive money in seconds 24/7, including weekends and holidays, from participating institutions — though some may take up to 30 minutes depending on the sender. You can learn more about receiving real-time payments here.

Outgoing RTPs

Real-time payments are designed to settle in seconds, but instant delivery is not guaranteed in every situation. If an RTP does not arrive immediately, see our guide for Sending real-time payments for more information.

Real-time payments are only supported for accounts provided through our partner, Column N.A.

International wire processing times

International wire times vary widely as payments are not standardized across country borders. There are also often many parties involved. It’s like a flight for your money—if they’re large banks on either end, you can have a direct transfer that will be quicker. If you’re sending from or to a smaller bank, there may be “layovers” (in this case, correspondent/intermediary banks) for your funds to go through that can make it take a little longer.

Incoming international wires
  • Typically take up to 4 business days to reach your Mercury account with possible delays if information is incomplete or incorrect. Be sure your sender follows wire instructions carefully.
Outgoing international wires
  • Processed and sent by Mercury within 1-3 business days from when they’re requested. In general, these can take up to 5 working days to reach your recipient if all information is correct. Make sure you include a purpose/reason for your wire to ensure it processes quickly.

We recommend checking the status of your international wire from your Transactions page on the web. Simply click into the payment and you’ll see the option to Track this wire. This will provide a more accurate timeline and the option to share the tracking link with your recipient.

Check payment processing times

Check payment processing times vary between incoming and outgoing. Incoming check payments go through risk review, while outgoing payments cover both our mailed check product (accessible via the Send Money flow), as well as physical checks.

Incoming check payments
  • Check deposits: Checks are manually reviewed and once approved can take up to 5 business days to post. You may notice that funds have settled on the 6th business day if the check was submitted after our 12pm Pacific cutoff time.
Outgoing check payments
  • Mailed checks: These are mailed on a customer’s behalf via USPS and typically arrive in 7–10 business days (1-2 days to print, then delivery). The check will remain pending until it’s deposited. If not deposited within 90 days, it will automatically cancel.
  • Physical checks/checkbooks: When you order a Mercury checkbook, it should reach you within 10-14 business days. From there, since you are in possession of your checkbook, the timing will be dependent on your personal delivery method.

Real-Time Payments (RTP) are available only to Mercury customers whose accounts are provided through Column, N.A., Member FDIC. Third-party fees may apply. Mercury is a fintech company, not an FDIC-insured bank. Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Members FDIC.

Receiving non-USD payments

Customers on either of our partner banks, Choice Financial Group or Column N.A., Members FDIC, can accept international wires in non-USD currencies. In both cases, the funds are automatically converted to USD before they hit your account. Column N.A. converts incoming funds to USD at the mid-market rate. Choice Financial Group uses third-party intermediary banks that typically add a 2–3% markup to the exchange rate. Mercury doesn’t control these conversions, set the rates, or profit from them.

To receive non-USD wires successfully, make sure the sender includes all required details. For accounts held with Choice, that means including Remittance Information (Section 70), to avoid delays or returns. Here’s how to find your wire instructions. Be sure to view and download the Foreign Exchange instructions for non-USD wires.

Note: While you can receive international payments in supported currencies, Mercury only supports USD accounts. Funds are automatically converted to USD before they reach your account—we cannot hold or maintain non-USD balances.

Requesting higher payment limits (Business: Send Money)

When you open a Mercury account, you’re assigned certain limits for ACH payments, wire payments, and check deposits. If you encounter one of these limits when trying to send a payment or deposit funds, you can request a temporary limit increase directly from your dashboard.

Here’s how:

  • Start your payment, transfer, or deposit as normal
  • If you enter a payment or deposit amount that’s above your limit, an alert will show up. Click Request a temporary limit increase
    • Note: Only admins can request higher limits. If you don’t see the Request a temporary limit increase option, it may be due to your permissions. Reach out to an admin to request higher limits
  • You’ll be asked to provide some info about the check deposit or transfer, along with pictures of the unendorsed check (if applicable) and any other invoices or paperwork that provide additional context
  • After submitting, our team will review the request and get back to you within 1-2 business days.

If you need to increase the spending limit on an individual debit card, you can do that from your dashboard by visiting your Cards page and clicking the card that needs editing.

Mercury is a fintech company, not an FDIC insured bank. Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Members FDIC.

Scheduling payments (Business: Send Money)

If you make similar payments on a regular basis, you can set up a recurring payment to handle them automatically.

Here’s how to do it:

  • Click the Move Money menu in the upper right corner of your dashboard and select Send.
  • Enter your recipient’s information and select your payment method and amount
  • On the “Amount” screen you’ll see the option to click the toggle next to “Repeat this payment”
    • You’ll be able to choose a payment frequency and decide when you’d like the payments to end. You can cancel this payment schedule at any time
  • Once enabled, these will begin processing at 9am EST on the specified date

Payments scheduled on the weekend or a holiday will begin processing on the nearest business day before the scheduled date.

Scheduling non-USD (FX) international wires

When you send an international wire in a non-USD currency, two things are factored into the final amount:

  • The exchange rate between USD and the destination currency (we use a market-leading rate)
  • A currency exchange fee of 1% on the USD amount you’re sending

We apply the exchange rate at the time your scheduled payment is processed. While we can’t predict what that rate will be in advance, you’ll see an estimated exchange rate when setting up the payment and can always check the Scheduled tab of your Payments page for an updated estimate based on current market rates.

You can read more about sending non-USD wires here.

Managing your scheduled payments

You can view and edit upcoming scheduled and recurring payments from your Payments page on the left-hand menu on web.

Click on the “Scheduled” tab and select the payment that needs editing to view scheduling details. Click Edit to make changes to the date, amount, or similar. If you need to delete the payment entirely, you can do so by clicking Delete Payment.

Notes on editing scheduled payments:

  • Non-USD wire amounts can’t be edited. To change the amount, delete the scheduled payment and create a new one.
  • If your organization uses multi-admin approvals, you can only change the funding account. To change the date or amount, cancel the payment and create a new one.
  • Editing requires permission to edit scheduled payments; ask an admin if you don’t see the Edit option.

Sending checks from your Mercury account

Mercury offers multiple ways to send and manage checks. This article explains how to send mailed checks, order a Mercury checkbook, and enable your account to order checks from a third-party provider.

Types of checks available:

  • Mailed checks that are printed and mailed on your behalf via the Send Money flow
  • Physical checkbooks that you can order from the Checkbooks page

Additionally, you can enable your Mercury checking account and routing numbers to order checks from third party providers.

How to send a mailed check

You can send a paper check to recipients within the United States and its territories from your Mercury dashboard.

  • Click Move Money, then select Send
  • Choose or add a recipient, or upload a bill to start
  • Select Check as the payment method
  • Fill in the required payment details and follow the prompts
  • (Optional) Upload up to 6 pages of attachments in PDF, PNG, or JPG format
    • Files must be exactly 8.5” x 11” at 300 DPI
    • HTML files will be rendered and paginated automatically
    • If you’re attaching a PDF form, flatten the file before uploading by using Print > Save as PDF to prevent formatting issues during printing
Delivery time

Checks are mailed via USPS and typically arrive in 7–10 business days (1-2 days to print, then delivery). The check will remain pending until it’s deposited. If not deposited within 90 days, it will automatically cancel.

Canceling mailed checks

If you want to cancel a mailed check before it has been deposited, you can click into it on your Transactions page and select the “Cancel check payment” icon.

How to order a Mercury checkbook

To order a Mercury checkbook so you can send physical checks personally, follow these steps. Please note that ordering checkbooks is restricted to account admins, and checkbooks can only be shipped to addresses within the United States and its territories.

  • Go to the left-hand menu on your Mercury dashboard on web, click Payments > Checkbooks
  • Click Order Checkbook
  • Enter the details for your checkbook then click Next
  • Choose your default check review setting:
    • Approve check: Check deposits will be automatically approved after the 24-hour review window expires
    • Reject check: Check deposits will be automatically rejected after the 24-hour review window expires
  • Review your selections, agree to the terms and conditions, and click Confirm
  • The final page will confirm your checkbook’s estimated shipping time. You’ll also receive an order confirmation and an update when the checkbook ships via email.

You can also order a checkbook from a specific checking account page. To get there, head to your Accounts tab.

Since you are in possession of your checkbook, timing will depend on your method of delivery. Checks deposited by your recipient will usually appear on your Checkbooks page the same or next business day after your recipient deposits them. Please note that only deposited checks will show up on your Checkbooks page — if your recipient hasn’t deposited them yet, that record won’t appear in Mercury.

Want to learn more about Mercury checkbooks? Click here.

Important notes about third party checks

If you want to enable your Mercury checking account and routing numbers to order checks from a third party provider, you can head to your Checkbooks page, click Settings in the top right corner, and choose which checking accounts you want to enable.

You can also use the routing number or account details printed on your Mercury checkbooks for direct deposits or account verification. If a vendor asks for a check to verify your account, you can also usually provide a bank letter. Download one from the Documents & Data page under Bank Letters.

Want to learn more about check deposits? Click here.

Creating a payment from your dashboard

  • In the “Details” step, you can include optional additional details related to the payment such as memos or attachments

iOS

Sending international payments (Business: Send Money)

On Mercury, you can send payments to 200+ countries and regions, in 40+ local currencies. This article covers how to send an international wire, track its status, and understand eligibility and restrictions.

Initiating an international wire

  • Go to Move Money in the upper-right corner of your dashboard and select Send
  • Choose a recipient:
    • Upload a bill, select an existing recipient, or create/invite a new recipient
  • If creating a new recipient:
    • Add their name and basic info
    • Click Create Recipient
  • Enter the payment details:
    • Select International Wire as the payment method
    • Choose your currency (USD or one of 40+ supported local currencies) from the dropdown
  • Review or enter bank details:
    • Start with the recipient’s SWIFT code. The form will update based on country-specific requirements
    • If prompted, add the IBAN (International Bank Account Number)
    • (Optional) Add a correspondent or intermediary bank’s SWIFT code. Only include this if the recipient instructs you to—extra details may cause rejections
    • Review these details and ensure information is accurate. Errors may delay or block the transfer
  • Click Next
Filling out “Amount” details
  • Enter the payment amount
  • Choose the fee structure:
    • SHA – Recipient absorbs potential intermediary bank fees and fees are deducted directly from the wire amount
    • OUR – The intermediary bank fees are covered by the payer and the recipient gets the full amount
    • You can read more about fee structures here
Confirming “Source account” and schedule
  • Choose your source account
  • Set the send date (today or scheduled)
  • (Optional) Set up a recurring payment
Additional details and finalizing
  • If you use an accounting integration, select the relevant GL codes
  • In the Details step:
    • Describe the purpose of the wire
    • Add optional memos, attachments, or recipient email addresses for receipts
    • For countries that require documentation, you may need to select “I’d like to provide additional information” and fill out a description of the payment reason, indicate whether or not you plan to pay this recipient in the future, and upload any supporting documentation such as an invoice or a contract
  • Click Next to review everything. Double-check recipient details—incorrect info will cause the wire to be rejected and returned

Tracking your payment

Wires usually process within 1-3 days of the scheduled payment date, and can take up to 5 working days to reach your recipient.

Once sent, you should be able to view details (reflecting the USD amount deducted from your account) from your Transactions page.

Sending money overview

You can send payments from your Mercury account using the Send Money flow in your dashboard — this is where you’ll start most outgoing payments from Mercury, including ACH transfers, domestic wires, international wires, real-time payments, and mailed checks.

The only exception is physical checkbooks, which are ordered and managed separately.

When you send money, you can add or select a recipient, choose an available payment method, enter the amount and timing, then review and submit your payment.

Domestic payment methods

ACH payments

ACH payments are electronic transfers between U.S. bank accounts. They’re commonly used for standard domestic payments, like paying vendors, contractors, employees, or external accounts.

ACH payments are free to send on Mercury. If submitted before the ACH cutoff and eligible for same-day processing, funds typically post the same business day. Otherwise, ACH payments are processed the next business day.

Domestic wires

Domestic wires allow you to send money in USD to a recipient at a U.S. bank. They’re typically used for larger or time-sensitive domestic payments.

Domestic wires are free to send on Mercury. If submitted before the domestic wire cutoff and eligible for same-day processing, funds typically post the same business day. Otherwise, domestic wires are processed the next business day.

Real-time payments (RTP)

Real-time payments (RTP) allow you to send payments that arrive within seconds.

Real-Time Payments are free to send on Mercury and work 24/7, including weekends and holidays. Availability depends on your Mercury account, the recipient’s bank, and the payment details. If your account is eligible, you’ll see Real-Time Payment as an available option in the Send Money flow.

Real-time payments are only supported for accounts provided through our partner, Column N.A.

Mailed checks

Mailed checks let you send a paper check to a U.S.-based recipient without writing or mailing it yourself. Mercury prints and mails the check on your behalf.

Mailed checks are free to send on Mercury. They’re typically printed within 1 business day, then sent via USPS. Checks can take up to 10 business days to arrive.

Physical checkbooks

Physical checkbooks are separate from the Send Money flow. If your account is eligible, you can order a checkbook from your Mercury dashboard and write checks manually.

Use a mailed check payment in Send Money if you want Mercury to print and send a check for you. Use a physical checkbook if you want to write and mail checks yourself.

International payment methods

International wires in USD

USD international wires let you send U.S. dollars to recipients outside the U.S. This can be useful if your recipient wants to receive USD or has provided USD wire instructions.

USD international wires are free to send on Mercury. They’re typically processed and sent by Mercury within 1–3 business days from when they’re requested. In general, international wires can take up to 5 business days to reach your recipient if all information is correct.

International wires in non-USD (FX)

Non-USD international wires allow you to send money to recipients outside of the United States in 40+ local currencies.

Non-USD international wires include a 1% currency exchange fee on the USD amount to account for the conversion handled as part of the payment flow. You’ll be able to review the exchange rate, applicable fees, and final amount before submitting the payment.

Non-USD international wires are typically processed and sent by Mercury within 1–3 business days. Arrival timing can vary based on the destination country, currency, recipient bank, intermediary banks, and any routine payment review.

Sending a payment

To send a payment:

  • In your Mercury dashboard on web, go to Move Money > Send
    • On mobile, tap the middle ⇄ icon on the of your bottom menu bar, then tap Send
  • You can either start by adding a new recipient/selecting an existing one or uploading a bill to pay directly
  • Choose an available payment method
  • Enter and confirm the amount, funding account, and send date
  • Review the payment details
  • Submit the payment

A note on timing and errors

Processing times can vary based on cutoff times, weekends, holidays, payment review, recipient bank processing, intermediary banks, and whether all payment details are complete and accurate.

For international wires, Mercury may process and send the payment before the recipient receives it. Intermediary or recipient banks may take additional time to deliver the funds.

If you’re encountering errors with a failed/returned payment, we recommend locating the payment on your Transactions page and looking for a failure reason.

Sending non-USD international wires

You can convert USD to one of 40+ supported currencies when sending an international wire. The exchange includes a 1% currency conversion fee.

Note: We only support sending wires in the currencies listed below. If a currency isn’t supported, the wire will need to be sent in USD.

How exchange rates work

On available business days, funds are exchanged at the current mid market rate. On weekends and holidays, we provide you with the stored/cached rate from the previous business day.

So if you create the payment on a Saturday, you will see the rate from Friday. This is a secured rate and will be the rate used when the payment is processed on the following business day.

Sending a wire with currency exchange/FX

Follow the steps outlined here to send an international wire in non-USD. Select “International Wire” as the payment method, then choose your currency from the dropdown menu.

If a currency isn’t listed, the wire will need to be sent in USD.

Don’t see this feature on your dashboard? Reach out to us. Our team can review your Mercury account to determine if you’re eligible.

FAQs

Why are weekend rates cached?

Financial markets are not typically open on weekends and holidays. To ensure a smooth experience, we use the last available rate before markets close so that you can make your transfer knowing the specific rate that will be used the following business day.

Is the exchange fee negotiable?

If your business is exchanging more than $200,000/month, please reach out to us. A member of our team will follow up with you to learn more.

Are there any wire limits?

There are upper limits based on currency pairs, as well as some that may be tied to your account. If you run into a limit issues, you may need to request higher limits.

How do I monitor for a specific exchange rate?

At this time, we are unable to alert you on specific rates as we get live rates when you go through the wire flow.

Please be sure to select the appropriate currency for your recipient’s bank details, in order to see the currency rate.

Can I create a recurring payment with currency exchange?

Yes, you can schedule a recurring payment as normal, but recurring payments will be processed at the exchange rate on the date the payment is actually processed. In other words, we can’t guarantee a set rate.

How do returns work?

To prevent returns, we encourage users to confirm payment details before making a payment.

If your payment is returned by the receiver’s bank, the funds will be redeposited to your Mercury account for the USD equivalent of the return. It will appear as a new transaction and be labeled “wire return.”

Can I receive non-USD and convert it to another currency?

Currently, only Mercury customers that are on our partner banks, Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Members FDIC, can accept international wires in non-USD currencies. In both cases, the funds are automatically converted to USD before they hit your account. Column N.A. converts incoming funds to USD at the mid-market rate. Choice uses intermediary banks for currency conversion, which means the rates can vary.

What is the cutoff time for non-USD payments?

There isn’t a daily cutoff for payments. They are processed throughout the day.

Will holidays affect my ability to use currency exchange?

You should be able to retrieve a quote and create new transfers any time day or night. On weekends and holidays, you’ll receive a cached exchange rate from the previous business day. If you want a live rate, you will need to wait until the next business day.

If the receiving bank has a local bank holiday, this may also impact the delivery estimate of the payment.

I’m getting an error when trying to make a conversion. Why?

You may be getting an error due to invalid bank details. Please confirm that the currency quote you’re trying to pull matches the receiver’s bank currency. You will receive an error if you try to pull a CAD quote if the receiver’s bank account is based in Germany.

If you’ve received a rate drift error, this means there was a change in the exchange rate between the time the payment was created and when it reached our payment provider for processing. If the exchange rate shifts by more than 1% from the originally quoted value, the payment will automatically fail to prevent unintended discrepancies. We recommend trying the payment again. We’ve seen higher success rates for wires initiated during business hours (9 am–5 pm ET) on weekdays.

Sending real‑time payments (Business: Send Money)

Send money instantly — and know it arrived. Real-time payments (RTPs) are electronic transfers that complete in seconds, 24/7/365, giving you more certainty and cash flow clarity, while helping you avoid follow-ups and late fees. Real-time payments are only available to Mercury accounts provided through our partner, Column N.A. This article explains how sending RTPs works on Mercury.

What is a real-time payment (RTP)?

In the U.S., real-time payments (RTPs) move funds over networks operated by The Clearing House (the RTP® network) and the Federal Reserve (the FedNow service). Because RTPs settle instantly, these payments are typically irreversible once submitted.

When might a real-time payment not arrive instantly?

  • The recipient’s bank is experiencing delays or a maintenance window
  • Network delays between participating institutions or payment processors

How to send a real‑time payment

As with any payment, real-time payments should only be sent to people or businesses you know and trust – always double-check recipient account details before sending:

  • Go to Move Money > Send (on web) or tap the ⇄ icon in the bottom navigation bar (on mobile)
  • Create a new recipient or select an existing one
  • Select Real‑Time Payment as the payment method
  • Add or confirm your recipient’s account details (routing and account number)
    • If the receiving account can’t receive RTPs, you’ll be prompted to choose another method
    • Before sending, check with your recipient to make sure their bank can receive real-time payments
  • Enter the payment amount, set the send date or schedule a recurring payment (optional), and add any optional details (like memos or internal notes)
    • You can schedule a payment for a future date, and we will attempt delivery on that date, subject to bank/network availability
    • You can also set up a recurring payment that repeats on a weekly, monthly, or custom schedule
  • Review and confirm the payment

Once your recipient’s bank receives your real-time payment, it may be coded as a real-time payment, “instant payment”, “instant transfer”, or something similar.

How to view outgoing real-time payments

You can check the status of your real‑time payments anytime from your Transactions page. Use filters and select Real-Time Payment Out as the payment method. The statuses include:

  • Sent: The payment was delivered successfully. You’ll see the delivery timestamp in the transaction details.
  • Pending: The payment has been submitted and is still processing. Status will update once it’s delivered or fails.
  • Failed: The payment didn’t go through. If a failure reason is available, you’ll see it in the transaction details.
Troubleshooting
Payment failure reasons

If a real-time payment fails, a failure reason will be stated when available. Common failure reasons include:

  • Recipient’s bank account does not support real‑time payments
  • Recipient’s account is closed
  • Account or routing numbers were entered incorrectly

Here are some best practices to help you avoid real-time payment failures:

  • Double-check your recipient’s account and routing numbers before you confirm a payment
  • Save recipients only after you verify their details
  • Confirm that your recipient’s bank can receive real-time payments before sending one
Payments sent in error

Real‑time payments are designed to be final and irrevocable once submitted. In general, since settlement happens immediately, they cannot be canceled or reversed by the sender.

If an RTP was sent in error:

  • Try to resolve the issue directly with the recipient
  • If that’s not possible, contact Mercury support

While we can’t revoke an RTP once it has been submitted, we can send a return request through the payment network to ask the recipient’s bank to return the funds. Return requests are not guaranteed and depend on the recipient bank’s response.

FAQs

I don’t see the option to send a real-time payment. Why?

If RTP (Real-Time Payments) isn’t appearing as an option when you go to send money, it may be because of one of the following reasons:

  • Your account is on Choice rather than Column. Real-time payments are only supported for accounts provided through our partner, Column N.A.
  • The recipient’s bank or routing number isn’t RTP or FedNow eligible. Even when RTP is supported on your end, the receiving institution has to support the RTP network or FedNow. If the recipient’s routing number isn’t eligible, RTP will be hidden or blocked for that payment.
  • Consider checking with your recipient to make sure their institution is able to receive real-time payments.

Will recipients always receive their funds instantly?

In most cases they will, but instant delivery is not guaranteed. Processing times can vary and some transfers may take longer to complete. Once your recipient’s bank receives your real-time payment, it may be coded as a real-time payment, “instant payment”, “instant transfer”, or something similar.

Can I cancel an RTP after it’s sent?

RTPs are designed to be final once submitted. If you made an error, contact the recipient first to resolve it directly, and then Mercury support. We can request a return request to the recipient’s bank, but returns are not guaranteed.

Are real-time payments only for U.S. accounts?

Yes — real-time payments move funds between U.S. banks/payment providers that participate in the RTP® network and/or the FedNow service.

Does Mercury support receiving real-time payments?

Yes, and can read more about receiving RTP here.

Setting up wire drawdowns

A wire drawdown, also known as a reverse wire, is a type of wire payment initiated by your recipient to withdraw funds from your account. Wire drawdowns are most commonly used for payroll and allow for fast, secure transfers with no action needed on the sender’s end once they’re set up.

To set up a new wire drawdown, you’ll need to create an authorization on your Mercury dashboard. Any incoming wire drawdown request that doesn’t match one of your wire drawdown authorizations in Mercury will be automatically rejected.

Please note that wire drawdowns can’t be created with Mastercard at this time.

If you’re trying to set up payroll on Mercury via ACH debit (also known as ACH pull or direct debit), click here.

Creating an authorization on your Mercury dashboard

  • From your Payments tab on the left hand side of your dashboard, select Wire Drawdowns
  • Click Create authorization to get started
  • On the first screen, select Payroll/Benefits and then choose the name of your payroll provider from the dropdown. If you don’t see your recipient in the list, select Custom to manually input your vendor’s payment information. Once you’re done, click Next
  • On the “Source Account” screen, choose the account you want to pay from. Click Next
  • You’ll be asked if you want to set a drawdown limit. This is optional, but allows you to limit how much money can be requested from your provider. If you don’t want to set this up, click Skip limits & review. Otherwise set up your limits and then click Review
  • Review everything one last time and click Authorize
  • Once set up, the authorization will remain active until you cancel it in Mercury. You can view and edit all active authorizations from the Wire Drawdowns tab on your Payments page.

Finish setting up with your recipient

Once you’ve created the authorization on Mercury’s end, you’ll need to complete a few additional steps on your recipient’s side before drawdowns can be processed.

  • If you’re setting up with Gusto, please follow their guide on setting up and running reverse wire payrolls.
  • If you’re setting up Sequoia One, TriNet, ADP, Namely or any other partner, please reach out to your contact and they’ll be able to help you figure out the final steps to get up and running.

Stopping a check payment

If you’ve written a check that hasn’t been deposited yet, you can request a stop payment from Mercury to prevent the funds from leaving your account.

Note: If you want to cancel mailed checks created through the Send Money flow, you can do so on your Transactions page.

What is a stop payment?

A stop payment prevents checks from being processed before they’re deposited. They can be applied to any checks/checkbooks assigned to your enabled Mercury accounts, including physical checks ordered from third-party providers.

When to request a stop payment

You might want to request a stop payment if:

  • You sent a check to the wrong recipient
  • A check was lost, stolen, or voided
  • You changed your mind about making the payment
  • You issued a replacement payment and need to cancel the original check

You may also decide after ordering a checkbook that you no longer need it. If this is the case, message us — our team can help you cancel that checkbook if it hasn’t been mailed yet. Otherwise, you will need to request a stop payment on the checkbook number range you ordered by following the instructions in the section below.

Tip: If you still have the check in hand, write “VOID” on it to prevent misuse.

If a check deposit appears for review in your Checkbooks page and you don’t want to honor it for any of the reasons above, you can reject it via check review — no need to submit a stop payment.

How to request a stop payment

Note: Only account admins can request stop payments for physical checks.

Head to your Payments page or Checkbooks page and click the chat icon in the bottom right corner to start a new conversation. You should see a “Stop Check Payment” option, which will lead to you a form to fill out these details:

  • The issuing checking account
  • The check number or check number range (matching the checks you ordered exactly, e.g., “001-025” is not the same as “1-25”)
  • (Optional) any additional notes for context on why you’re stopping the check
  • (Optional) the check amount

Once submitted, we’ll block processing of any checks matching those details for 180 days. You’ll also receive a confirmation email when your stop payment is created.

After submitting a stop payment

Next steps:

  • Check your email for a confirmation of the stop payment
  • If the check does go through within the 180-day stop payment window, notify us immediately by replying to the confirmation email
  • Monitor your account in case of any processing delays

Understanding check review

Check review is a fraud prevention feature that allows you to review checks written from your check-enabled checking accounts at the moment they are deposited. You’ll have a ~24-hour window to approve or reject each check before any money leaves your account.

Learn more about setting up checkbooks in our overview article.

How check review works

Whenever someone attempts to deposit a check written from one of your check-enabled checking accounts, Mercury flags it and gives you a 24-hour review window.

You’ll be notified of pending checks in a few ways:

  • Email: Includes check number, amount, last four numbers of the associated Mercury checking account, and the number of pending transactions. Multiple checks may be grouped into a single email.
  • Push notifications: You will get in-app push notifications, directing you to the Tasks page.
  • Tasks: Flagged checks appear in your Tasks tab on both desktop and mobile. The task will then link you to the Checkbooks page.

If you don’t act within the review window, the check is automatically accepted or rejected based on your default review action settings (see next section).

In rare instances, a check may be processed the same day, which could shorten or eliminate your chance to review it beforehand. You can always dispute a check after it’s been processed by reaching out to our team.

If someone tries to deposit a check from one of your Mercury accounts that is not enabled, it will be returned automatically. Be sure to review all enabled accounts from your Checkbooks > Settings page.

Choosing your default check review action

When you are setting up your Checkbooks page, you will be asked to choose either “approve check” or “reject check” as your default review action.

  • Approve check: Check deposits will be automatically approved after the review window expires
  • Reject check: Check deposits will be automatically rejected after the review window expires

If you want to change your default review action, click the Settings icon in the top right corner of your Checkbooks page.

FAQs

Who can approve and reject checks during check review?

Only admins are able to review checks and adjust the default check review action.

If someone attempts to deposit a check drawn from a Mercury checking account that isn’t enabled for check issuing, will it be flagged for review?

No. If a check is deposited from a Mercury account that isn’t enabled for check issuing, the deposit will be returned automatically. Be sure to review all enabled accounts from your Checkbooks > Settings page.

Mercury is a fintech company, not an FDIC insured bank. Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Members FDIC.

Why did I get a notification of change (NOC)?

What is a NOC?

When you send a successful ACH payment, Mercury will sometimes receive what’s called a notification of change (NOC) from your recipient’s bank. An NOC tells us that previously valid ACH information has changed and needs to be updated. When Mercury receives an NOC, we make the necessary changes to meet the requirements set by the ACH network.

How do I see the changes?

When Mercury receives an NOC, you’ll be notified by email and in your action bar. While there is no action needed by you, you may want to review your recipient’s updated ACH details.

  • From any page in the Mercury dashboard, click the button in the top right of your screen with the bell icon to open your action bar. If you have any unactioned items there will be a red dot on top of the button.
  • Look for the notification in the action bar that says your recipient’s ACH details were updated.
  • Click View Changes to see the updated ACH details in green.

What are some common NOCs?

These are the most common reasons we receive a notification of change, which can occur individually or in combination with one another:

Incorrect bank account number

The recipient’s account number doesn’t match what the receiving bank expects. This can happen due to a number of reasons, including incorrect data entry, a bank merger, or the changing or closing of a bank branch.

Incorrect routing number

The information for the recipient’s transit/routing number was different from what the receiving bank expected. This can happen if your recipient’s bank is undergoing a merger or recommends a different preferred routing number for its account holder.

Bank account name change

The receiving bank’s name is different from what was in the recipient details. If the name of the bank changes (usually due to a rebranding effort by the bank), you may get this error.

Incorrect payment code

The bank account type for your recipient was different from what their bank expected. This usually translates to changing from savings to checking, personal to business, or vice versa.

Incorrect company name

The name of the company you’re dealing with has changed. You’ll need to update your recipient’s name to reflect the change.

Editing team members

You can update a team member’s permissions, account access, and work details from their profile. To make changes, you need to be an admin or have the User management permission.

Editing permissions and account access

A team member’s role determines their permissions and which accounts they can access:

  • Permissions determine what actions a team member can take, such as sending money
  • Account access determines which accounts a team member can view and interact with, based on their permissions

For example, if they have access to Account X and the Send money permission, they can send money from Account X. Without access, the account details and balances are hidden and they’re unable to interact with the account.

Note: Users with the Teammate role cannot access or view any account details, balances, or transactions, other than their own transactions.

To change a team member’s permissions or account access, you can switch them to an existing role or create a new role with the settings they need.

For more information, see Understanding roles and permissions.

How to edit permissions and account access

  • Go to All Settings > Team
  • Select the team member’s name to open their profile
  • Find the Permissions section and click on the edit icon
    • If your organization is using Mercury Payroll, you’ll find this section under the “Details” tab
  • Review that role’s permissions and account access. You can also view other roles’ permissions and account access by selecting them from the role dropdown
  • Choose how you’d like to update their role:
    • Switch to an existing role : Select the role that fits, then click Save
    • Create a new role: In the role dropdown, select Create new role. When you’re done, you’ll return to the team member’s profile. Open Permissions again, select the new role, then select Save

Notes:

  • If your organization has dual admin approval on, and you give a team member Send money permissions or want to make them an admin, the change will require another admin to approve.
  • Account access doesn’t affect cards. If a team member loses access to an account, cards linked to that account stay active.
  • Changing a team member’s role disconnects any AI tools they’ve connected to Mercury, like ChatGPT or Claude, even when you give them more access. They’ll need to reconnect each tool afterward. If the change needs another admin’s approval, the tools are disconnected once it’s approved.
