Enforcing separation of duties for per-payment approvals

Separation of duties (also known as segregation of duties) for payment approvals ensures that team members can’t approve payments they’ve created. This control helps organizations strengthen internal oversight, reduce fraud risk, and meet audit or compliance requirements.

What is separation of duties?

By default, Mercury allows the same person to both create and approve a payment if per-payment approvals are enabled. If a team member is in the approval chain, they automatically fulfill their own approval. This is fast and convenient for small teams, but doesn’t work for organizations that need stricter oversight.

With separation of duties enabled, the person who initiates a payment can no longer approve it, even if they are listed as an approver.

How it works

When the toggle is OFF (default)

  • Payment creators will automatically approve their own payments, if they’re in the per-payment approval chain (either named individually, or as “Any Admin”)

When the toggle Is ON

  • The creator is excluded from approving the payment
  • If they were the only approver, Mercury blocks the payment from being submitted for approval
  • Creators won’t receive approval notifications for their own payments

To enable separation of duties, head to Settings > Approvals and navigate to the Per-payment page.

Why it matters

Separation of duties is a key financial control for:

  • Reducing fraud or error by requiring a second set of eyes on every payment
  • Aligning with audit and compliance expectations (e.g. SOX for public companies)
  • Unlocking the most commonly requested approval flow: “No matter who submits a payment, at least one other person must approve it.”

If you’re a growing organization, or already operate under formal financial policies, this helps you scale your controls. To learn more about how approvals work and the controls available, read more here.

Who can use separation of duties?

  • Only admins can turn this setting on or off
  • If you have dual admin approval enabled, changing this setting will require approval from a second admin

FAQs

Does separation of duties apply to reimbursements or daily max limits?

Not at this time. It currently applies only to per-payment approvals.

Will this change existing approvals or past payments?

No, separation of duties only applies to payments created after it’s turned on.

Can I apply separation of duties to only certain users or payment types?

Not yet. This is a global toggle for all payments in your organization.

HR & payroll system (HRIS) integration

Integrating your HR and payroll systems with Mercury simplifies team management by automating team invites, card issuance, and offboarding.

Supported providers

  • ADP Run
  • BambooHR
  • Deel
  • Gusto
  • Justworks
  • Paycor
  • QuickBooks Online Payroll
  • Square Payroll
  • Workday

For Rippling customers: Rippling does not provide open API access and imposes prohibitive ongoing costs, preventing us from offering an integration. We recommend reaching out to your Rippling account manager to request a Mercury integration.

How Mercury integrates with your HR System

Mercury provides HRIS integrations through Finch, a third-party API aggregator. Finch encrypts all data and has been thoroughly reviewed by our information security team. Visit their site or reach out to Mercury support for more details on their security policies.

How to integrate

Initial connection:
  • Navigate to Settings > Integrations and click “Your payroll or HR system”
  • Choose your provider and log in
  • Select one or more entities you’d like to connect
  • Depending on your provider and the number of employees, data retrieval may take up to 30 minutes
    • If you only have a few employees, you might be able to go straight through the flow
    • If it looks like it will take more than ~5 minutes, we’ll email you once it’s complete
  • Choose which active employees to invite to Mercury, and offboard any terminated employees
  • Once you’ve selected which employees to invite, you can bulk issue them cards and assign them the appropriate roles and permissions
Ongoing syncing:
  • As long as your connection remains active, employee data will update in Mercury automatically within 24 hours of your HR system updates
  • If you add or remove users in your HR system, you’ll be prompted to invite or remove them in Mercury via Settings > Users
  • Mercury will never automatically invite or remove a user but will flag users in the Team page for necessary action
    • If an employee is terminated in your HR system, we’ll sync the data and update their status on the Teams page “To be offboarded”, recommending their removal from your Mercury account
  • When a Mercury user is linked via your HR integration, certain fields like job title must be edited in your HRIS and cannot be modified in Mercury
Disconnecting:
  • You can remove the connection at any time through the Integrations or Users pages with a single click.

Data We Fetch

Mercury only fetches the data necessary to create and update your team members, including:

  • Legal name
  • Address & Date of Birth (DOB)
  • Job title
  • Manager
  • Department
  • Employment status
  • Start date & End date

Mercury does not fetch sensitive employee information like Social Security number, or income or payroll data. For additional details on Mercury’s data security, refer to our Trust Center.

Troubleshooting

If you experience issues with your HR/payroll integration, consider the following:

  • Authentication errors: Ensure login credentials are correctly entered and your provider is not blocking integrations.
  • Data sync delays: Remember, it may take up to 24 hours for updates in your HR system to show up in Mercury.
  • Missing employee data: Confirm that records in your HR system are saved to the corresponding employee.
  • Access Issues: Check permissions within your HR system.

For further assistance, reach out to our support team.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who can set up this integration?

The Mercury user must be an Admin or a Custom user with “Manage Team” permissions, and be an Admin in the HR system.

How often does the system sync with my HR provider?

Syncing occurs once every 24 hours.

Can I integrate multiple payroll providers at once?

Currently, we support one integration per account at a time.

Is there an additional cost for HR integrations?

No - integrating your HR system is available at no extra cost.

What happens if my HR provider updates their API?

Finch works closely with providers to monitor API changes and updates all our integrations accordingly.

Navigating approvals (Business: Team)

To increase visibility and oversight over outgoing funds (including external transfers and when paying bills), you can use approval rules to:

  • Set amount-based thresholds for payment approvals
  • Assign specific and/or multiple team members as approvers
    • Add a department lead as an approver step in your approval rules
  • Limit how much a team member can send in a day
  • Require dual admin approvals for sensitive actions
  • Prevent users from approving payments they initiated by enabling separation of duties

To get started, head to Settings > Approvals or read on to learn more.

Per-payment approvals

Per-payment approvals let you require review before a payment is sent, based on the payment amount. This ensures the team members approve transactions before funds leave your account. You can even create multiple rules with custom thresholds and stack them for multi-level review.

How they work
  • Rules apply when a payment meets or exceeds the set amount (depending on how the rule is set up)
  • If multiple rules apply, all required approvers must review the payment
  • If the requester is also an approver, they’re skipped and count toward approval by default unless you have separation of duties enabled
Setting up per-payment approvals
  • Click your org name in the top-left hand corner of your dashboard and click Settings > Approvals
  • Under “Per-payment approvals”, click + Create rule to get started or Edit to stack existing rules
  • Configure dollar amounts and required approvers (Any Admin, department lead, or choose a specific team member)
  • Click Save

Note: Only admins can edit or remove approval rules. Changes apply to all new payments after the update.

Department approvals

You can add a department lead as an approver step in a rule. Rather than assigning a specific person, select Department lead as the approver type — approval routes automatically to the lead of whatever department is tagged on the payment.

  • Payments with no department tag, or tagged to a department with no assigned lead, will skip department approval — all other rules still apply
  • Department leads don’t need banking access to approve — they can hold any role, including Teammate
  • Department leads can see recipient info and non-sensitive account details for payments they’re asked to approve

A note on account access: Designated team members can only approve payments from accounts they have access to, unless they are a department lead. When a payment is submitted, Mercury checks that at least one approver can access the funding account. If no assigned approvers have access to the funding account, the payment can’t be approved and may be blocked.

Daily maximum

Set a daily limit on the total amount a team member can send, ensuring any payments exceeding the amount set requires approval.

This means if a team member’s cumulative payments (including any pending payments) exceed the daily maximum, additional payments will need to be reviewed before they are sent.

Both Payment Approvals and Daily Maximum rules can coexist. If a payment already requires review under a per-payment rule, the Daily Maximum will not add another approval. Instead, it acts as a safety net — ensuring users can’t send many smaller payments under the per-payment threshold without oversight (though this should be unusual).

Admins reviewing Payment approvals would also satisfy the “Any Admin” approvers on the Daily Maximum rule. Admins can act as approvers. If the payment requester is also an assigned approver, they’ll be skipped in the approval process and count as an approver.

Dual admin approvals

If you have multiple admins on your team, this setting requires that two admins approve certain requests.

You’ll need two admins on file before you can enable the policy. If you’re currently the only admin, you’ll need to either invite a new team member or update permissions for an existing team member.

Actions initiated by an admin will require one other admin to approve and all other roles require two admins to approve each request.

Requests that require additional approvals include:

  • Managing team members with elevated permissions
    • Inviting or removing an Admin
    • Changing an Admin’s role
    • Inviting a user with send money permissions
    • Granting send money permissions to an existing user
  • Resetting 2-factor-authentication
  • Enabling or editing approval rules

Removing a team member

If a team member leaves your company or no longer needs access to Mercury, you can remove them from your account as long as you have team management permissions. This article walks through the steps and important things to know before you do.

How to remove a team member

  • Find the team member in the list and select their name
  • In the top right corner of their profile, select Manage, then Remove
  • Confirm the removal
    • If your organization has dual admin approval on, and you want to remove an admin, the removal will require another admin to approve. To remove an owner, see below
    • If applicable, we’ll flag:
      • Automatic cancelation of any debit or credit cards assigned to the team member
      • Any ongoing subscriptions detected on those cards, that you might want to move to a different card

Removing an owner

If you don’t see the option to remove an account owner or team member, contact our support team. To remove an owner, you’ll need to provide formal documentation outlined here confirming the change in ownership.

Reminders

  • You can’t re-add a removed user using the same email address. Instead, you’ll need to locate the removed user and reactivate them
  • Removing a user does not reset their 2FA. To reset 2FA, follow the steps outlined here

Reusing email addresses (Business: Team)

Mercury no longer requires the use of unique email addresses. If you’ve used placeholder email(s) in the past, you can now use one profile to manage your various accounts.

Editing your email

You can now convert profiles attached to your old placeholder email(s) to your preferred/main email. To do this, you’ll need to invite yourself to the account using your preferred email by following the steps below.

Note: You won’t be able to edit your email from the Settings page — you will receive an error that the “Email is already taken”. Instead, you’ll need to follow the steps below.

  • Navigate to your company menu in the top left corner of your dashboard and click Settings and then select Team.
  • Near the top of the Team page, click Invite.
  • Input your first name, last name, and preferred email.
  • Assign yourself a role and click Next.
  • Review the details of the invite, ensuring details are correct and click Invite.
  • Check your inbox for an email from hello@mercury.com. Click the Accept Invitation button in the body of the email
  • Use your existing login credentials for that profile to login. You’ll be welcomed to the team and prompted to Accept Invite.

Once accepted, you’ll be logged into the newly invited account. Any accounts that share that email will appear in your profile icon in the lower left hand corner of your dashboard. From here, you’ll be able to easily switch between accounts without needing to log in and out. You can learn more about account linking and switching here.

If you’re a non-admin, reach out to an admin on file and ask them to invite your preferred email address to the account. Follow the same steps above to accept the invite.

You can head back to your Team page to remove any old placeholder emails that are no longer needed. If you’re a company owner, reach out to help@mercury.com so we can ensure we have your preferred email listed as the primary user.

Important items to note
  • Removing the old email will also remove any permissions, data and most importantly, cards associated with that account. Cancelled cards will need to be recreated and will have new card numbers. Be sure to check any subscriptions tied to the old cards and decide if this action is right for you.
  • This is a manual process, meaning if you have multiple Mercury accounts and placeholder emails, you’ll need to add yourself to each account using the steps above.

Applying for a new account

To apply for a brand new account using an email address we already have on file, log into the existing profile to get started. If you’re not logged in, you’ll run into an “Email already exists” error message.

Upon login, head to your company menu in the top left-hand corner of your dashboard where you’ll see the option to “Open new account”. This profile will share basic information like name, email and 2-factor authentication.

During the onboarding process, you’ll be asked to provide company details but we’ll pre-fill basic information like your name and email.

Once approved, the accounts will be linked and you’ll be able to easily switch between them from your menu.

Setting up custom roles

You can use custom roles to assign permissions to groups of users based on their responsibilities. Instead of configuring permissions for each user individually, you can now create reusable roles that reflect real responsibilities in your company, and assign those roles to as many users as you need.

This simplifies user management, improves visibility, and scales as your team grows.

Why use custom roles?

Previously, if you wanted to give a team member access to certain features (like viewing accounts, depositing checks, or managing payments), you had to assign those permissions manually through the “Custom User” role, one person at a time.

Instead of managing access one user at a time, you can now:

  • Name roles based on your team’s actual responsibilities (e.g. “AP Clerk”, “Finance Lead”, “Read Only”)
  • Add descriptions so roles are easy to understand across your org
  • Assign permissions to multiple users at once
  • Edit a role to update access for all users assigned to it

How custom roles work

Each Custom Role you create has two components:

  • Permissions: What users can do (e.g. send payments, deposit checks, manage team members)
  • Account access: Which accounts they can access (e.g. specific accounts or all accounts)

Once a role is created, you can assign it to as many users as you’d like. If you later update the role, those changes will automatically apply to all users with that role.

Changing a role’s permissions or account access also disconnects any AI tools connected by people assigned to it, and they’ll need to reconnect. Before you save, Mercury shows how many members the change will affect.

We’re phasing out the old “Custom User” role. All team members with custom permissions will be migrated. We’ll automatically group users with identical permissions into shared roles. You’ll still be able to edit, rename, or delete those roles later.

How to create and manage roles

You can create and manage roles from the Roles page:

  • Click your company name in the top-left corner of the dashboard
  • Select Team
  • Click the Roles button > Create role
    • Start from scratch or choose from the templated options — templates provide a starting set of common permissions that you can customize
  • Enter the role’s name, description, permissions, and account access
  • Click Save role

You can also assign roles when:

  • Inviting users (including bulk invites) — Select an existing role or create a new role
  • Issuing cards
  • Setting up users after your account’s been approved

Tips for using custom roles effectively

  • Keep it simple — most organizations don’t need more than 3–6 roles
  • Use clear names that match your team’s terminology (e.g. “Controller”, “Read Only”, “AP Manager”)
  • Use descriptions to explain what a role is for—this helps everyone on your team understand what access others have

What roles are templated?

We’ve converted common permission sets into templates. You can use these as-is when creating a role and modify them to match your org’s needs:

  • Finance Lead
  • Read Only
  • Money Mover

What About Admin, Teammate, and Bookkeeper roles?

Admin and Teammate remain standard roles. The former Bookkeeper role is now a templated Custom role (“Accountant”) with permissions that can be adjusted, including the ability to view and code transactions.

You can read more about these role types here.

Setting up departments

Departments let you organize your team in Mercury the way it’s structured in real life. You can create departments directly in Mercury, or sync them automatically from your HR or payroll system. Once set up, departments help you track spend by team, tag payments, and route approvals through department leads.

Note: Looking to tag transactions with accounting departments from NetSuite or QuickBooks Online? See Using classes, departments, and locations in Mercury. Team departments and accounting departments are separate and aren’t linked

Where to find departments

Navigate to your company name in the top left-hand corner of your dashboard and select Settings > Departments to create and manage your organization.

Creating and managing departments

You can create departments directly in Mercury:

  • Add departments and sub-departments
  • Assign leads to departments
  • Add users to departments manually or through invites

Departments can be rearranged at any time, and sub-departments can be nested to reflect the way your org is structured.

When viewing a department, click Manage to edit members and details, update the department name, or add sub-departments.

Syncing departments from your HR/payroll system

Departments can also be synced automatically via our HRIS integrations. When you connect your provider, we’ll ingest:

Using departments

Once your departments are set up, you can track spend and manage approvals by department.

You can tag a payment to a department in two places:

Department leads

Department leads can be added as an approver step in your approval rules. Admins select Department lead as the approver type in the rule builder, and approval routes automatically to the lead of whatever department is tagged on the payment.

To assign a department lead, click Manage when viewing a department. For more, see Navigating approvals.

FAQs

Who can create or manage Departments?

Admins and Custom Users with “Manage Team” permissions.

Can I create sub-departments?

Yes. Departments can be nested under parent departments to mirror your org structure.

What happens if I change a department in my HR system?

Departments and reporting chains will update automatically in Mercury within 24 hours. Department leads need to be assigned in Mercury.

Can I assign more than one lead to a department?

At launch, each department has a single lead, but one user can lead multiple departments.

What does this mean for my team today?

Departments currently help you structure your team in Mercury. The biggest impact will come as upcoming features (like manager-first approvals and department-based budgets) launch later this year.

Understanding roles and permissions in Mercury business

When you invite someone to your team on Mercury business banking*, you assign them a role that determines what they can see and do in your Mercury organization. Roles help you control access to money movement, accounts, cards, and sensitive settings while giving teammates the tools they need to do their job.

This article explains the differences between Teammate, Admin, and Custom roles, what permissions each role includes, and where to find the most up-to-date roles and permissions in our demo environment.

Role types at a glance

When you invite a team member, you assign them a role. Each role comes with its own set of permissions. Some roles are fixed; others can be created and edited to match your team’s needs.

Role

Access Level

Customizable

Teammate (formally known as, Employee)

Assigned cards and reimbursements only. No visibility into bank accounts, balances, or account numbers

No

Admin

Has full access to the account, settings, users, and controls

No

Accountant

Can view all accounts, transactions, and manage books

Yes — permissions can be adjusted

Custom roles

Defined by the permissions and account access you configure

Yes — fully configurable

Teammate role capabilities

The Teammate role is designed for teammates who need to spend company funds or submit expenses without visibility into sensitive banking information.

Teammates can:
  • Be issued debit and/or credit cards
  • View and manage their own cards
  • View their own transactions
  • Submit reimbursements (based on your expense settings)
Teammates cannot:
  • View account balances or account numbers
  • See company-wide transactions
  • View other team members’ activity
  • Move money between accounts
  • Send payments or manage recipients
  • Access accounting, user management, or security settings
  • Connect their AI tools to use Mercury via MCP

This role is best for team members who need limited, task-specific access without exposure to financial controls.

Admin capabilities

Admins have the highest level of access in Mercury. They’re considered super users because they can manage the account’s structure, security, and financial controls end to end. Admins have all of the capabilities below by default, without additional configuration.

Note: Any permission with an asterisk (*) is available to admins only and aren’t configurable via Custom role

Account and security management
  • Update core account settings*
  • Create and manage checking and savings accounts
  • Link external bank accounts
  • Receive and manage security alerts
  • Create API tokens*
  • Approve 2FA reset requests*
  • Request changes to payment limits*
Team and role management
  • Invite and remove team members
  • Manage roles and permissions for all users (including other Admins on the account*)
  • Assign and revoke Custom roles
Money movement and approvals
  • Send money and pay bills
  • Approve payments (when approval rules are enabled)
  • Initiate internal transfers
  • Create auto transfer rules*
  • Manage payment recipients
  • Create invoices and request payments
  • Deposit checks
  • Manage spend including policy management and approvals
Policies and controls
  • Manage ACH authorizations
  • Configure approval policies for payments and account changes*
Automations
  • Connect AI tools to use Mercury via MCP
  • Manage AI agents connected to Mercury across the organization

Note: Depending on your org’s approval rules, some payments and actions may require approval. Approval rules help add oversight by defining approvers, thresholds, and controls like dual admin approval. Learn more about approvals here.

Custom roles

Custom roles let you define reusable permission sets that reflect real responsibilities in your organization. Any changes you make to a custom role automatically apply to everyone assigned to it. Changing a custom role’s permissions or account access also disconnects any AI tools connected by people assigned to it, and they’ll need to reconnect. Changing only the role’s name doesn’t disconnect anything.

Custom roles are created by selecting which permissions to grant and choosing which accounts the role can access.

You can start from scratch or use templates as a starting point. Templates feature common permission sets but can be edited as needed:

  • Finance Lead: Broad non-admin access across payments, cards, users, accounting, expenses, and documents
  • Read-only: View-only access to accounts and transactions, with optional card issuance
  • Money mover: Ability to initiate payments and transfers and manage recipients

Custom roles can also include the Use Mercury via MCP permission, found in the Automations section when building a role. Users with this permission can connect their AI tools to Mercury. Turning the permission off for a role disconnects any agents connected by everyone assigned to that role.

For step-by-step instructions, see Setting up custom roles.

Configurable permissions

When building a Custom role, you’ll select which permissions make up the Custom role and determine what actions users in that role can do.

1 - Select which money movement actions the role can perform:
  • Send money (subject to approval policies if enabled)
  • Add, edit, and remove payment recipients
  • Initiate internal transfers
  • Create invoices and payment links
  • Deposit checks
2 - Select which operational actions the role can take:
  • Managing ACH authorizations
  • Managing users (anyone except admins)
  • Managing accounting tasks such as categorizing transactions and managing accounting integrations and 1099 filings

3 – Select the role’s spend management and policy permissions:

  • Select whether the role can manage spend
    • This includes managing budgets and issuing and managing cards
  • Select the role’s expense and policy permissions:
    • Reimbursement submission only
    • Reimbursement view only
    • Reimbursement approval and submission
    • Policy management, reimbursement approval, and submission
4 - Specify which accounts the role has access to. At least one account must be selected.
Permissions only apply to the accounts a user has access to. For example, a user may have permission to send money, but if they don’t have access to a specific account, they won’t be able to send funds from that account or view its details.

Business: Treasury & Vault

Changing your Treasury portfolio

You can change your Treasury portfolio at any time from the Treasury page. Some changes take effect within a day or two with nothing sold. When a change means holding fewer Treasuries, you choose how to get there: gradually, as rungs mature, or immediately, by selling. This article walks through both.

Making a change

  • Go to Treasury and select Edit portfolio
  • Edit your current targets or choose a preset
  • If you want a new recommendation, you can also update your monthly cash outflows and investment objective
  • If your change reduces your ladder, choose how to transition (see below)
  • Confirm

The same guardrails from How Mercury builds your Treasury portfolio apply: at least three months of cash in Near-term, at least $1,000 per rung, and up to 36 rungs.

Changes that don’t sell Treasuries

Adding a ladder, adding rungs, or moving cash into your ladder involves buying Treasuries rather than selling them, so there’s no early-sale risk. New rungs fill automatically with cash from dividends or later deposits, so you don’t need to do anything. Purchases happen over the next trading day or two once the cash is available. If you extend your ladder further than your current cash can fill, the new rungs show as empty until dividends, deposits, or maturing rungs provide the cash.

Changing your monthly cash outflows figure doesn’t sell Treasuries either. Your Near-term and Reserve targets adjust to match, and your fund holdings are rebalanced right away. Raising the figure tops up your funds. Lowering it trims them, and the excess moves to your ladder.

Reducing your ladder: Two ways to get there

When a new target means holding fewer Treasuries (smaller rungs or no ladder at all), you choose how to transition.

Gradually (recommended)

Your targets update immediately, but nothing is sold. As each rung matures, the cash flows into Near-term and are invested per the new targets. Removing four rungs takes about four months. Deposits and maturing rungs move the portfolio toward the new target along the way, and fund dividends are reinvested in the fund that paid them. Because no rung is sold before maturity, this path doesn’t realize a market gain or loss.

Rebalance now

Mercury immediately sells the rungs needed to reach your new targets. We’ll sell the rungs that no longer fit your new ladder, starting with those furthest from maturity.Treasuries sold early go at current market prices rather than face value, so this can realize a gain or a loss. You’ll see an early-sale warning before you confirm, and confirming is a separate extra step so it can’t happen by accident.

Gradually is the default. Rebalance now is for when you need the cash sooner and accept that trade-off.

A few things to know

  • One change at a time. You can start a new change once the previous one has been processed.
  • Existing Treasury customers. If your portfolio was set up as a percentage split between funds, your first edit moves you to a months-based portfolio. See Mercury Treasury tax FAQs for what changes and what doesn’t.

How Mercury builds your recommended Treasury portfolio

Mercury Treasury, offered by Mercury Advisory, LLC, an SEC-registered investment adviser, recommends a portfolio based on how your company uses cash. Instead of asking you to pick a percentage split between funds, we look at how many months of cash outflows your deposit covers and match each month to the right holding. This article explains how the recommendation is built. The recommended portfolio can always be customized to fit your business needs.

What we ask you

Your recommendation is built from three inputs:

  • Monthly cash outflows. What your company spends in a typical month, across all of its accounts, not just Mercury.
  • The amount you’re moving into Treasury.
  • Your investment objective.
    • Prioritizing stability keeps the more liquid part of your portfolio heavily weighted towards a government money market fund.
    • Prioritizing yield adds a greater weight in the more liquid part of your portfolio to an ultra short-term bond fund. This fund can have small price fluctuations, also called a variable NAV (net asset value).

Dividing your deposit by your monthly cash outflows gives your months of cash coverage. That number drives your portfolio recommendation.

The three parts of a Treasury portfolio:

Part

What it holds

Liquidity

What it’s for

Near-term

State Street Institutional U.S. Government Money Market Fund: Mercury Class (MRGXX)

Same day, before 3pm ET on business days

Cash you’ll need in the short term

Reserve

Morgan Stanley Ultra-Short Strategy Portfolio: Mercury Class (MCRYX)

1 to 2 business days

Cash you’ll need in coming months

Long-term

A ladder of individual US Treasuries, one maturing each month

Returns as each Treasury matures; can be sold earlier at market value with 1-2 day liquidity

Cash you don’t expect to need for a year or more

How the recommendation is built

  • Your first three months of cash go to Near-term.
  • Months four through twelve go to Reserve if you chose Prioritize yield. If you chose Prioritize stability, they stay in Near-term.
  • Everything beyond twelve months goes into a Treasury ladder, one rung per month of cash, up to 12 rungs. Past 24 months of cash, each rung gets larger rather than the ladder getting longer.

The order reflects Mercury Advisory’s investment priorities: protect your principal first, keep cash available when you’ll need it second, and pursue additional yield only with money that clears those two bars.

An example

Say your company spends $50,000 a month and moves $1,000,000 into Treasury. That’s 20 months of cash.

Part

Objective: Prioritize stability

Near-term

None

8 months ($400,000) in 8 rungs of $50,000

If your deposit covers 12 months of outflows or less, the recommendation won’t include a ladder. A company that may need all of its cash within a year risks having to sell rungs of the ladder early, possibly losing principal.

Choosing something different

The recommendation is a starting point, and nothing is invested until you approve it. Alongside Recommended, you can choose Stay liquid (everything in the government money market fund), Remain balanced (everything in the ultra short-term bond fund), or Custom, where you set months per part and the number of rungs. If your deposit covers fewer than four months of outflows, a ladder isn’t possible and Custom isn’t offered. A few guardrails apply in Custom:

  • At least three months of cash stay in Near-term. This buffer keeps cash on hand for everything else you do in Mercury, so you never have to sell Treasuries early to cover spending. A portfolio can’t be 100% US Treasury ladder.
  • Each ladder rung is equal to or greater than your monthly cash outflows in $1,000 increments.
  • A ladder can have up to 36 rungs. Later rungs will be empty if your deposit is insufficient to fill in all the rungs.

Whatever you choose, you approve every target before anything is traded, and Mercury Advisory only trades toward the targets you approved.

Keeping your recommendation current

Your monthly cash outflows figure stays as you set it until you change it. If your spending changes meaningfully, revisit it from Edit portfolio on your Treasury page.

How net yield is calculated in Mercury Treasury

Mercury Treasury is offered by Mercury Advisory, an SEC-registered investment adviser. To help you understand how your return is calculated, this article explains the yield figure we use for each holding in your portfolio, two mutual funds and, if you hold a Treasury ladder, individual US Treasuries, and how they combine into the net yield displayed in your dashboard.

What net yield represents

Net yield is an annualized estimate of the return you may earn from your Mercury Treasury portfolio, net of Mercury Advisory’s fee, based on the current yield of each holding. Mercury refreshes this figure each business day. For the funds, it reflects their publicly reported yields; for US Treasuries, it reflects the prior day’s closing prices.

It’s an estimate, not a guarantee. Fund yields vary with market conditions, so your net yield will move over time. A Treasury’s yield is set by the price you paid and doesn’t change if you hold it to maturity, but its market value moves daily, and as rungs mature and are reinvested at current rates, your ladder’s overall yield changes too.

Why each holding uses a different yield measure

A Treasury portfolio can hold up to three types of investments: a government money market fund, an ultra short-term bond fund, and individual US Treasuries. Each has an industry-standard way of measuring yield, and Mercury Advisory uses the standard measure for each so our reporting matches how fund managers and the bond market describe performance:

State Street Institutional U.S. Government Money Market Fund: Mercury Class (MRGXX)

Money market funds report a 7-day Effective SEC yield, which reflects the annualized measure of the fund’s income over the previous 7 days, including dividend reinvestment. The 7-day Effective SEC yield is updated at the end of each business day.

Morgan Stanley Ultra-Short Strategy Portfolio: Mercury Class (MCRYX)

Non-money market funds, such as this bond fund, report a 30-day effective yield, which measures the fund’s income over the most recent 30 days, including dividend reinvestment.

US Treasuries in your ladder

Individual Treasuries are measured by yield to maturity (YTM): the annualized return you’d earn by holding the Treasury until it matures, given its current market price and its scheduled payments, and reinvesting any coupon payments along the way. Mercury calculates each rung’s YTM from the prior day’s closing price, net of the transaction cost built into that price. Your ladder’s yield is the average yield to maturity across its rungs.

YTM is different from a Treasury’s coupon rate. A Treasury bought below face value yields more than its coupon; one bought above face value yields less. Treasury bills have no coupon at all, so their yield comes entirely from the discount to face value. See Understanding Treasury ladders for more on coupons and yield.

How we calculate the net yield shown in your dashboard

  • We refresh the yield for each holding: 7-day Effective SEC yield for MRGXX, 30-day effective yield for MCRYX, and yield to maturity for each US Treasury based on the prior day’s closing price
  • We weight each yield by the dollars in that part of your portfolio
  • We subtract Mercury Advisory’s annualized fee to arrive at your displayed net yield

The yield you see before you fund your portfolio

When Mercury recommends a portfolio, the yield shown is indicative. It’s calculated the same way as above, using the prior day’s closing prices for the Treasuries that would fill each rung. Estimated net yield is inclusive of empty rungs that you may have customized. The actual yield on each rung is set by the price at which it’s bought, which can differ slightly. Once your portfolio is funded, your dashboard shows the yield of the Treasuries you actually hold.

How your Treasury fee is calculated

Your fee for Treasury investments is calculated daily and charged monthly. This means that your fee will be based on the amount invested each day, with the accumulated total charged in a lump sum each month.

To review your monthly fees, find the “Treasury fee” line in your Activity table on the Treasury page. Fees now appear as their own line item, separate from your dividends. This isn’t a new fee. It was previously deducted from your earnings in a combined “Net return” entry.

The fee tiers are based on your total deposits at Mercury across all of your accounts (including Treasury). The higher your total deposits are on Mercury, the lower your fee is.

Here is a breakdown of the tiers:

  • More than $20m total deposits = 0.15% (15 bps) fee
  • $10m-$20m total deposits = 0.25% (25 bps) fee
  • $5m-$10m total deposits = 0.35% (35 bps) fee
  • $2m-$5m total deposits = 0.45% (45 bps) fee
  • $0-$2m total deposits = 0.60% (60 bps) fee

Your fee is charged only on your investments in Treasury. Please note these rates are hypothetical and subject to change.

How to calculate fees

For every day of the month, we gather your positions and overall Mercury deposits. Then we compute fees daily as follows:

Positions * fee [in bps] / (10,000 [conversion from bps]*365 [annualizes])= Fee for the day

For example, a customer that has an investment position with a value of $1.5 million and a total of $2.5 million in deposits in Mercury would have a fee of 45 bps (.45%) according to their tier. Therefore, their calculation would look like this:

1,500,000 * 45 / (10,000 * 365) = $18.49 (rounding down to the nearest cent).

What your Treasury fee covers

Your Treasury fee gives you access to institutional-grade mutual funds and share classes that typically carry minimums well beyond what most businesses could access directly.

It also comes with one integrated platform. Treasury sits alongside your Mercury checking, cards, and payments, so there’s no separate brokerage relationship to manage.

We’re continuing to invest in the product, including Mercury-exclusive funds and fixed income ladders. These aren’t live yet, but we’ll share updates as they become available.

Here’s what to expect when funding, withdrawing, reallocating, or viewing statements for your Treasury account.

Funding your Treasury account

Withdrawing from Treasury

Funds typically settle in 0–2 business days, depending on your portfolio:

Closing a Treasury account

Closing a Treasury account requires a few steps before our team can process the request.

Note: Once a Treasury account is closed, it cannot be reopened on your existing Mercury account. If you’d like to access Treasury again in the future, you would need to open a brand new Mercury account and apply for Treasury from there.

To close your Treasury account, first bring your balance to $0. To withdraw funds, transfer them to a Mercury account; direct transfers from Treasury to an external account are not supported.

If your portfolio includes a Treasury ladder, bringing your balance to $0 means either letting each Treasury mature or selling them early at market prices, which can result in a gain or loss. You’ll see the early-sale warning before you confirm.

If you held funds during the month, a final net return may post within the first 5 business days of the following month. Net returns are automatically reinvested, so be sure to move those funds out right away; waiting could result in another return posting.

Once the balance is fully zeroed, the account holder on file can contact our team for help closing the Treasury account.

Mercury Treasury tax FAQs: Tax year 2025

Mercury Advisory LLC is providing the following Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) regarding the upcoming 2025 tax reporting season on behalf of its Treasury partner Apex Clearing Corporation* (Apex).

What tax forms does Apex generate and when will they be delivered?

Based on your Treasury activity, Apex will create the following tax forms. Absent an extension, Apex is required to deliver these forms to the account holder by the regulatory due dates, below. All tax forms will be loaded to Mercury’s website and made available when provided to Mercury by Apex.

Correction runs are tentatively scheduled in two-week intervals starting April 15th, 2026 and are based on need. Issuers of securities held may publish income reclassification instructions after the original 1099 has been delivered. You may receive a corrected Form 1099 which could impact your tax returns and filing dates.

Please note the collection and application of income reclassification instructions is compulsory for information reporting agents such as Apex. In order to better service our customers and provide a better experience for your account holders, Apex may place a hold on issuing amended tax forms to consolidate these instructions and lessen the number of amended forms provided to your customers. Mutual funds offered as part of Treasury are included in the list of securities subject to reclassification. This list is a guide based on previous years reclassifications. As such, this security listing is a best effort and there is no guarantee that these securities listed will reclass again in 2025 or that the list is 100% accurate.

Form

Who receives a Consolidated 1099?

A consolidated 1099 is a grouping together into one statement of all the 1099 tax information for an account provided by Apex Clearing to be used in preparation of your annual tax return. All individuals receive a Consolidated 1099 if they are United States citizens or legal residents and have had reportable tax activity. In some cases, exempt recipients will receive a Consolidated 1099 if charged backup withholding on activities during the year. These amounts must be reported to the customer and the IRS.

Why wasn’t a 1099 generated for activity in a particular account?

If the activity in your accounts did not meet certain reporting thresholds set by the IRS, a tax form will not be issued. De minimis values differ by form and income type. For dividends and interest, de minimis is $10.00; for Cash In Lieu $20.00 and for miscellaneous income $600.00. Additional details regarding de minimis values have been provided with the forms identified in the next section of this FAQ.

What is reported on the different forms?

1099-B

A Form 1099-B reports all sales or redemptions of securities, futures transactions, commodities, options and barter exchange transactions. Cash in Lieu may be subject to a de minimis reporting if under $20.00.

As a reminder, closing transactions for identical securities and for orders with the same disposition dates will be combined into fewer transactions. This change simplifies the presentation of the information being reported on Form 1099-B. A Form 1099-B will be filed for any person for whom Apex withheld any federal tax under the backup withholding rules regardless of the amount.

1099-DIV

A 1099-DIV reports distributions such as dividends, capital gain distributions, or nontaxable distributions, that were paid on stock and liquidation distributions if any of the following applies:

  • Received $10.00 or more in dividends, including capital gains, exempt interest and other stock distributions.
  • Had any withholding amounts or any foreign tax on dividends and other distributions on stock.
  • Received any payments of at least $600 as part of the liquidation process.
1099-INT

Form 1099 INT reports interest income including taxable and tax-exempt interest dividends from mutual funds paid during the year. De minimis amount is $10.00 or more and are reported in boxes 1, 3 and 8. Tax-exempt interest is generally not subject to federal taxation. If you own municipal bonds, then interest on bonds from your home state is generally not subject to state tax. However, municipal interest from other states is taxed in your home state. Interest payments received on interest producing securities loaned out are reported as substitute payments in lieu of interest on Form 1099-MISC.

Form 1099-INT will be issued for any person for whom you withheld and paid any foreign tax or from whom you withheld (and did not refund) any federal income tax under the backup withholding rules regardless of the amount.

1099-MISC

1099 Misc reports substitute payments in lieu of dividends or interest received in your account, stock or cash rewards, stock loan fees received and royalty payments. Payments of royalties are generally from investments in natural resource companies.

Threshold amounts are amounts greater than $10.00 in royalty payments, rewards, in lieu of dividends or interest and $600.00 or more of miscellaneous income.

A new section will be present on corrected Form 1099-Comp forms that detail the change that resulted in a corrected tax form. Previous value, new value, and the delta of the change will be shown.

Distribution Code Y7 - A charitable contribution is a donation or gift to, or for the use of, a qualified organization. It is voluntary and is made without getting, or expecting to get, anything of equal value.

Moving money in and out of Treasury

Money moves into and out of a Mercury Treasury portfolio in a fixed order where your Treasury ladder is the last thing touched. This article explains how deposits are put to work, how withdrawals are funded, what Mercury’s daily rebalancing does and doesn’t do, and how auto transfer rules interact with a ladder.

Deposits

When you move money from your Mercury checking or savings account into Treasury, it arrives in Near-term first, on the same business day. Mercury allocates it toward your targets in order:

  • Near-term, up to its target.
  • Reserve, up to its target, if your objective includes it.
  • Long-term ladder: first refilling any rungs that are underweight or empty in order of maturity date, then spreading out excess cash across rungs starting from rungs with the closest maturity date.Treasuries are bought on business days while the bond market is open, in $1,000 increments. Any remainder under $1,000 stays in Near-term.

For deposit timing, see Managing your Treasury account.

Large deposits

A deposit that’s large relative to your current portfolio usually means something has changed, such as a fundraise or a large customer payment, for example. Rather than pour it straight into targets set for a smaller balance, we’ll ask you to take a quick look at your portfolio first. When you start a large transfer into Treasury, you’ll be prompted to confirm or update your monthly cash outflows and review the updated recommendation before the deposit goes through.

Withdrawals

Withdrawals are funded from the most liquid part of your portfolio first and the ladder last, in this order:

  • Near-term (MRGXX). Same-day availability if requested before 3pm ET on a business day.
  • Reserve (MCRYX). Typically settles in 1 to 2 business days.
  • Long-term ladder, only if the first three can’t cover the request. Rungs are sold closest to maturity first, and proceeds settle the next business day.
When a withdrawal reaches your ladder

Before you confirm a withdrawal that would sell any part of your ladder, you’ll see a warning.

Selling the rung closest to maturity keeps the sale price close to the Treasury’s face value, because a Treasury’s price moves toward its face value as maturity approaches. A rung within one business day of maturing can’t be sold; Mercury waits for it to mature and then releases the cash.

Automated rebalancing

Mercury Advisory reviews every Treasury portfolio each market day. It acts in two situations:

  • Near-term exceeds its target by one month of cash or more, because of a deposit, maturing rungs, or fund dividends. The excess moves to Reserve and then to your ladder.
  • Near-term falls below its target by two months of cash or more, and you don’t hold a ladder. Reserve is sold to bring Near-term back to its target.

Mercury Treasury will never sell a ladder rung through daily rebalancing. If your ladder is above its target, we let rungs mature and redirect the cash rather than selling early. A rung is only sold if you make a withdrawal large enough to reach it, or if you change your portfolio in a way that requires it.

Your portfolio will not trade just because market moves shifted a percentage point or two. Fund dividends, coupons, and maturing rungs all flow through the same order above, so small drifts close on their own.

Auto transfer rules and your ladder

Auto transfer rules that move money out of Treasury draw from Near-term, the same-day part of your portfolio. Keeping at least three months of cash there, which is the default, means most rules run without ever getting near your ladder.

If a transfer rule needs to sell a ladder rung to complete, the rung will be sold at market prices so the transfer can go through, which may result in a gain or loss. We’ll send you an email once a rung has been sold. To avoid early sales, review your transfer rules and keep enough in Near-term and Reserve to cover them.

U.S. Treasury securities held in a Treasury ladder fluctuate in market value before maturity as interest rates change. Selling a Treasury ladder before its maturity date may result in a gain or loss. Mercury Advisory’s portfolio management is designed to avoid selling Treasury ladders before they mature.

Understanding Mercury Treasury

Mercury Treasury helps you earn yield on idle cash by investing it in a portfolio built around your company’s cash flow. It includes a government money market fund for the next few months, an ultra short-term bond fund for the months after that, and a ladder of US Treasuries for cash you won’t need for a year or more. Here’s how it works and why teams use it.

How Treasury earns yield

  • Cash in Mercury Treasury is invested in mutual funds and, for longer-term cash, individual US Treasuries, all of which seek to generate yield
  • These holdings typically provide higher yields than traditional savings accounts, though yields vary and are not guaranteed
  • You can view the latest yields anytime at mercury.com/treasury. The yield shown in your dashboard is net of Mercury Advisory’s fee; see How net yield is calculated in Mercury Treasury

You can learn about eligibility in our Qualifying for a Treasury account article.

Once you’ve approved your targets, Mercury Advisory trades toward them each market day, and automated rebalancing never sells a Treasury rung before it matures to reach a target, protecting your principal.

The recommendation itself is only a starting point: you can change any of it at any time from your Treasury page > Edit portfolio.

How your portfolio is built

Most tools for investing business cash start by asking for a split: 40% here, 60% there, held steady from then on. Mercury Treasury starts with understanding when you expect to spend your money.

Mercury Advisory recommends a portfolio based on three things you tell us: your monthly cash outflows, how much you’re moving into Treasury, and whether you want to prioritize stability or yield. Dividing your deposit by your monthly outflows gives your months of coverage. Each month of coverage is then assigned to the part of your portfolio that matches when you’re likely to need that money, starting with the most liquid:

Near-term: State Street Institutional U.S. Government Money Market Fund: Mercury Class (MRGXX)
  • Holds the cash you’ll need soonest: your first three months of outflows, or your first twelve if you prioritize stability
  • A fund that seeks income with same-day liquidity* and principal stability
  • Invests at least 99.5% of its total assets in cash, U.S. government securities, and/or repurchase agreements that are collateralized solely by U.S. government securities or cash
  • Liquidity: 0-1 business days*
  • View MRGXX prospectus

*“Same-day withdrawals” only applies to funds invested in the State Street Institutional U.S. Government Money Market Fund: Mercury Class. Cutoff for transfers to settle same-day is 3pm ET each business day, subject to partner processing times. Read fund prospectus for additional information.

Reserve: Morgan Stanley Ultra-Short Strategy Portfolio: Mercury Class (MCRYX)
  • Holds months four through twelve of your outflows when you prioritize yield
  • An ultra-short bond fund made up of cash equivalents and short-term assets such as commercial paper and certificates of deposit
  • Liquidity: 1-2 business days
  • View MCRYX prospectus
Long-term: US Treasuries
  • Holds cash beyond your first twelve months of outflows, in a ladder of individual Treasury bills, notes, and bonds with one maturing each month around the 15th
  • Each Treasury returns its face value as cash on its maturity date; it can be sold earlier at market value, settling the next business day
  • Market value moves daily with interest rates, so selling before maturity can result in a gain or loss
Why months instead of percentages

A percentage-based portfolio

Mercury Treasury

You set

A percentage split between funds

Months of your spending in each part

A deposit

Is split across your allocation

Fills the most liquid part first, then the next

Rebalancing

Sells whatever has grown past its share

Never sells a Treasury before it matures

A percentage doesn’t know what your company spends. Twenty percent in a money market fund is a comfortable buffer for one business and a thin one for another. Months of coverage carry that information directly: three months in Near-term means three months of your outflows, and when your spending changes, you update one number and every target moves with it.

It also decides what happens when money moves. Nothing is split proportionally. A deposit fills Near-term to its target before any of it reaches Reserve, and fills Reserve before any of it reaches your ladder. Withdrawals draw in that same order with your ladder last, so the Treasuries in it can be left alone to mature.

Where a deposit goes, for a company spending $50,000 a month. Near-term is a month short of its three-month target, so it’s topped up first. Reserve comes next. Only what’s left over reaches the ladder, filling the three empty rungs before spreading across the rest.

Your recommendation is a starting point

You can accept the recommendation, choose a preset, or customize the months in each part and the number of rungs in your ladder, within a few guardrails. Nothing is invested until you approve. Once you’ve approved your targets, Mercury Advisory trades toward them each market day, and automated rebalancing never sells a Treasury rung before it matures to reach a target, protecting your principal. You can change any of it at any time from Edit portfolio.

Learn more in How Mercury builds your Treasury portfolio and Understanding Treasury ladders.

Access to your funds

  • You can withdraw money from your Mercury Treasury account at any time. How long it takes depends on where the money is invested: same day from the money market fund (before 3pm ET), 1 to 2 business days from the bond fund, and the next business day for any Treasuries that have to be sold
  • Withdrawals come from the money market fund first, then the bond fund, and only then from your Treasury ladder, closest to maturity first. You’ll see a warning before any Treasury is sold early
  • Delays may occur due to account standing
  • Treasury deposits and withdrawals typically take 0–2 business days

You can learn more about timelines in our Managing your Treasury account article, and about how deposits, withdrawals, and rebalancing work in Moving money in and out of Treasury.

Why teams use Treasury

  • Convenience: Keep all your cash management in one place
  • Built around your business: Portfolios are sized in months of your spending, not percentages, so cash is where you’ll need it when you’ll need it
  • Smarter automation: Automatically transfer idle cash between accounts with customizable twice-monthly transfer dates
  • Peace of mind: Your cash is held in lower-risk investments, funds managed by State Street and Morgan Stanley plus US Treasuries, in a portfolio built to protect principal first

Understanding Treasury ladders

A Treasury ladder is a set of individual US Treasuries that mature one after another, so a portion of your cash comes back on a predictable schedule. In Mercury Treasury, the ladder is the long-term part of your portfolio: the cash you don’t expect to need for a year or more. This article covers what Treasuries are, how your ladder works day to day, what happens when a rung matures, and the limits that apply.

What US Treasuries are

US Treasuries are debt securities issued by the US government. When you buy one, you’re lending to the US Treasury Department in exchange for repayment of the security’s par value on a set date, its maturity date. They come in three forms:

  • Treasury bills mature in one year or less. They don’t pay interest along the way. You buy them below face value and receive full face value at maturity; the difference is your return.
  • Treasury notes mature in two to ten years and pay a fixed interest payment, called a coupon, every six months.
  • Treasury bonds mature in more than ten years and also pay a semiannual coupon.

Your Mercury ladder can hold any of the three. What matters for each rung is how much time is left until it matures, not what it was called when it was issued. A 30-year bond with seven months left behaves much like any other security with seven months left to maturity.

Treasuries in your Mercury portfolio are held in an account in your company’s name at Apex Clearing Corporation, Mercury Treasury’s custodian, and are covered by SIPC protection.

How a ladder works

A ladder spreads your Treasury investment across staggered maturities instead of concentrating them on one date. Mercury builds yours with one rung per month, each maturing on or around the 15th.

Here’s a 12-rung ladder for a company that spends $100,000 a month and has $1,200,000 to put into the long-term part of its portfolio:

Rung

Matures

Face value

1

15th of month 1

$100,000

2

15th of month 2

$100,000

3

15th of month 3

$100,000

4

15th of month 4

$100,000

5

15th of month 5

$100,000

6

15th of month 6

$100,000

7

15th of month 7

$100,000

8

15th of month 8

$100,000

9

15th of month 9

$100,000

10

15th of month 10

$100,000

11

15th of month 11

$100,000

12

15th of month 12

$100,000

Each month, one rung matures and $100,000 returns as cash plus interest. Over a year, the whole ladder cycles through. That gives you two things:

  • Predictable cash. You know what’s coming back and when, which is designed to help you avoid selling a Treasury before it matures.
  • Spread-out reinvestment. Because rungs mature at different times, you’re never reinvesting everything at one moment’s interest rate.

Mercury sizes each rung to about one month of your cash outflows. Rungs are bought in $1,000 increments of face value, and anything left over stays in Near-term.

Why your ladder’s value changes every day

Your ladder is shown at market value, updated each day using the bond market’s prior-day closing prices. Between the day a Treasury is bought and the day it matures, its price moves for two reasons: changes in interest rates, and a gradual pull toward its face value as maturity approaches. At maturity, you receive the full face value.

  • When rates rise, the price of a Treasury you already hold generally falls. Newer Treasuries pay more, so yours is worth a little less to a buyer today.
  • When rates fall, the reverse happens and your Treasury is worth a little more.
  • The further a rung is from maturity, the more its price moves with rates. Your nearest rung barely moves; your twelfth moves the most.

None of this changes what a Treasury pays at maturity. Each rung is scheduled to return its full face value on its maturity date. The daily fluctuation only becomes a realized gain or loss if a rung is sold before it matures, which is why Mercury’s portfolio logic avoids selling rungs whenever possible.

What happens when a rung matures

On the maturity date, the Treasury pays its face value and the cash is swept into in your Near-term holding (MRGXX) at the end of the day. From there, Mercury’s daily portfolio review puts it to work in a fixed order:

  • If Near-term is below its target, the cash stays there to refill it.
  • If Reserve is below its target, the cash moves there next.
  • Otherwise, it’s reinvested as a new rung at the far end of your ladder, keeping the ladder rolling.

Coupon payments from notes and bonds follow the same path. Cash from a matured rung is available to withdraw the next business day.

If you’ve reduced or removed the ladder from your targets, maturing rungs flow back into Near-term and Reserve instead of being reinvested. See Changing your Treasury portfolio.

Minimums and limits

  • Per rung: $1,000 minimum, in $1,000 increments. Treasuries are purchased as whole bonds in $1,000 units of face value.
  • Smallest practical ladder: about $12,000 for 12 rungs. There’s no separate balance requirement for a ladder beyond the standard Treasury account requirements of $250,000.
  • Near-term buffer: at least three months of cash. A ladder is only possible when your deposit covers at least four months of outflows, and a portfolio can’t be 100% ladder.
  • Recommended rungs: up to 12. In Custom you can create up to 36.
  • No upper limit on ladder size. Very large orders may take more than one trading day to fill.

Standard Treasury eligibility still applies. See Qualifying for a Treasury account.

Transferring a ladder from another brokerage

Moving existing Treasuries into Mercury in kind (an ACATS transfer) isn’t available as a self-serve option. The simplest path is to let them mature or sell them, then transfer the cash. If you hold a large ladder at another institution and want to talk through options, reach out to your relationship manager or message Mercury support.

Why a Treasury’s coupon is different from its yield

Coupon is the fixed interest rate set when a note or bond is issued, paid as a percentage of face value. It never changes. Bills have no coupon at all.

Yield is what you earn, annualized, given the price you paid.

Mercury shows yield rather than coupon because yield is what determines your return. Specifically:

  • The yield shown for your ladder is yield to maturity: the annualized return if you hold each Treasury until it matures and, for notes and bonds, reinvest the coupons along the way.
  • Your ladder’s overall yield is net of fees, including Mercury Advisory’s annual fee and transaction costs built into each Treasury’s price. Individual rung yields include transaction costs but not the advisory fee.
  • It’s indicative and as of a date. Ladder yields shown before funding are estimates based on the prior day’s closing prices, and they refresh daily. Treasury prices, and so their yields, move throughout the trading day. The yield on each rung is set by the price at which it’s actually bought.
  • Once bought, your yield to maturity is locked in. If you hold a Treasury until it matures, you’ll earn the yield set at purchase, whatever happens to market prices along the way. Daily price changes affect your return only if you sell before maturity, when you’d get the market price at that time, which could be more or less than you paid.

For how the yields on all three parts combine into your portfolio’s net yield, see How net yield is calculated in Mercury Treasury.

Closing a Treasury account that holds a ladder

Closing your Treasury account requires bringing the balance to $0. If you hold a ladder, every Treasury in it will be sold at market prices before the account closes, which can result in a gain or loss. This applies whether you choose to close your account or Mercury closes it. See Managing your Treasury account for the full closure steps.

Closing the Books

Creating and managing journal entries

A journal entry is the double-entry record behind everything in your books. Most are created for you — by transactions arriving, invoices posting, and payroll syncing. You create one by hand when you need to record something that doesn’t come from a bank feed: an accrual, a depreciation entry, a reclass, or an opening balance.

Where journal entries come from

Most of your journal entries are created automatically:

  • Transactions. Every transaction in your books has a journal entry behind it. You edit it by editing the transaction — see our Categorizing and splitting transactions article
  • Invoices and bills. Posting an invoice or bill on accrual books creates its journal entry. On cash books, the entry is created when you match the payment
  • Payroll. Each completed Gusto payroll run posts as a balanced journal entry

Creating a journal entry

  • Go to Journal Entries in the left-hand menu of Books
  • Click Create Journal Entry
  • Set the date and input a description
  • Add a line item for each account the entry touches, with the ledger account, a memo, and the amount. You need a minimum of two line items to create a journal entry.
  • Confirm that the sum of debits = sum of credits
  • Post the entry by clicking Save

Tip: To bring in a longer entry, paste the rows straight from a spreadsheet into the journal entry screen rather than typing each line.

Exporting your journal entries

Manual journal entries can be exported to XLSX from the Journal Entries page by clicking the download icon.

Reconciling accounts in Mercury Books

Reconciling is the check that your books match reality — that every transaction on your bank statement is in your books, and nothing is in your books that isn’t on the statement.

Your Mercury accounts reconcile automatically, with no user intervention required. External accounts — anything linked through Plaid, Stripe, or a manual account you import by CSV — need to be reconciled manually.

How reconciliation works in Books

Reconciliation is configured one period at a time, in order. You choose the end date of each window, so it can cover whatever your statement covers — a calendar month, or any other range. Windows are contiguous and never overlap: each entry belongs to exactly one window, and a new one starts where the last one ended.

Mercury accounts reconcile automatically

Your Mercury accounts live in the same system as your books, so Books does this for you: as each monthly statement generates, it creates the reconciliation, marks every entry in the period reconciled, and records the statement ending balance. When you open Reconciliation for a Mercury account, you’re looking at work that’s already done.

Reconciling external accounts

Accounts linked through Plaid and Stripe, and manual accounts you import by CSV both reconcile in Books, but you drive the process: you get the statement from your bank, then work through the window in Books against it.

Reconciling an external account
  • From your Books menu, select Reconciliation
  • Select the account you want to reconcile from the account dropdown
  • Click Start reconciliation
  • Choose how you’d like to start your reconciliation:
    • Start from statement: Upload a PDF statement from your external account. Mercury will automatically extract the ending date and ending balance and create the reconciliation for you
    • Manual: Enter the statement’s Ending date and Ending balance, then click Start
  • Compare the transactions in the reconciliation window against your statement for that period
  • Resolve any discrepancies (see below)
  • Complete the reconciliation
When your balance doesn’t match

Work through these in order:

  • Check for missing transactions. Confirm the account is syncing and its connection is healthy on the Accounts page. For a manual account, check whether the CSV you imported covers the whole month
  • Check for duplicates. An account imported by CSV and also linked automatically will have the same transactions twice
  • Check the dates on transactions near the edges of the window. Books dates transactions from a linked account by when they were authorized; your statement dates them by when they posted. A charge authorized July 19 and posted August 3 sits in July in Books and in August on your statement. Edit the date on the entry to match your statement
  • Check your opening balance. If the first month of an account has never reconciled cleanly, the opening balance is the likely cause
  • Check for skipped entries. Look at your unreconciled entries for something that belongs in the window
  • Check both sides of transfers. A transfer whose other side isn’t in your books leaves a gap. See our Matching transfers between accounts article
Canceling a reconciliation in progress

You can cancel a reconciliation any time before you complete it by clicking the gear icon. Nothing is marked as reconciled, and your entries stay where they are.

Transactions that arrive after you’ve reconciled

A completed reconciliation stays as you completed it. If your bank returns a transaction later that’s dated inside a period you’ve already reconciled, Books leaves that period alone rather than reopening it — so that transaction won’t show up in your books for that period. To include it, delete the reconciliation for that period, add the transaction, and reconcile again.

Deleting a reconciliation

You can delete a completed reconciliation if you need to redo it by clicking the gear icon.

Note: Deleting a reconciliation also deletes every reconciliation after it. If you delete March, you’re also deleting April onward. The transactions included in the period are not deleted.

Understanding reports in Mercury Books

Mercury Books produces four reports from your books: a Profit & Loss, a Balance Sheet, a Cash Flow analysis, and a General Ledger. This article explains what each one shows, how to set the period, and how to drill in and export.

The reports

Go to Reports in the left-hand menu of Books and select the report you want.

Profit & Loss. Your revenue and expenses for a period, and the resulting net income. Built from your revenue and expense accounts.

Balance Sheet. What you own, what you owe, and your equity as of a point in time. Built from your asset, liability, and equity accounts, including Retained Earnings and Current Year Earnings.

Cash Flow. An analysis of cash coming in and going out over the period.

General Ledger. Every line entry posted to every account, in order. This is where you go to see the detail behind a figure on any other report. The general ledger is read-only — to change an entry, edit the transaction or journal entry behind it.

Setting the period

Each report has a period selector supporting:

  • Monthly, Quarterly, and Annual columns
  • A custom date range
  • Multi-year ranges, so you can compare across years in one view

Note: Periods that fall entirely before your entry start date are hidden from the selector and excluded from report output, because there’s no data in your books for them. The month, quarter, or year containing your entry start date remains available.

Filtering by tag

Every report page can be filtered by tag, so you can pull a Profit & Loss for a single department. Combine the tag filter with the period selector to compare a department across periods.

See our Tagging transactions in Books article.

Drilling into a figure

Click a period on a report to open a report drilldown for that period, where you can see every entry behind the number. From there, click into an individual entry to open its side panel and see the transaction, invoice, or journal entry that created it.

Exporting a report

Reports export to XLSX. Set your period and any filters first, then export — the file reflects what’s on screen, with an “as of” header showing the date.

This is the usual way to hand something to your accountant, your board, or a lender.

Making sure your reports are accurate

A report is only as good as the books behind it. Before you rely on one:

  • Clear your uncategorized transactions from the Transactions page
  • Reconcile the accounts and periods the report covers
  • Check your unreconciled entries for anything that belongs in the period
  • Confirm invoices and bills are matched to their payments, so your receivable and payable balances are current

FAQs

Is the Cash Flow report a statement of cash flows?

It’s a cash flow analysis — a view of cash in and cash out over the period.

Can I compare two periods side by side?

Yes. Use the monthly, quarterly, or annual column view, or a multi-year range, to see periods next to each other.

Can I build a custom report?

Not currently. The four reports can be filtered by tag and set to any period, and the General Ledger export gives you the underlying detail to work from in a spreadsheet.

Can I see my reports on the other accounting basis?

No. Your reports reflect the accounting method your books are set up on. See our Choosing your accounting method article.

Why is an account showing a zero balance?

Accounts with no activity in the selected period show as zero rather than disappearing, so the report keeps a consistent shape month to month.
