Understanding your Books home page

Your Books home page is where Mercury Books opens. It gives you your cash position, revenue, and expenses for a period you choose, so you can see where your business stands without pulling a report. This article explains what each figure means and how the date range works.

Setting the date range

Use the date selector at the top of the page to choose the period you’re looking at. You can pick a preset range or set a custom one.

The charts adjust their detail to the range you choose:

  • A range of a month or less plots a point per day
  • A longer range groups into weeks
  • A longer range still groups into months, then quarters

Hover any point on a chart to see the exact dates it covers and its value.

Note: Every figure on the page reflects the date range you’ve selected, not today’s date — with one exception, noted under burn rate below.

Cash

Your total cash across every account in your books. Bank account balances count positively, credit card balances count against them, and payment processor balances are included — so this is your net cash position, not just what’s in your Mercury accounts.

The accompanying chart shows how that balance moved over the period.

Burn rate and runway

Burn rate is your average monthly net cash outflow, calculated from your last three completed months. It deliberately ignores the date range you’ve selected, so the number stays stable as you move around the page.

Runway is how long your current cash lasts at that burn rate.

A few things to know:

  • Burn rate appears once you have three completed months of activity in your books. Before then you’ll see a message telling you when it will appear
  • If your cash flow is net positive over those three months, there’s no burn to report and the figure shows as unavailable

Revenue

Your total revenue for the selected period, with a trend chart and a Revenue sources breakdown split across your revenue accounts.

The breakdown lists every revenue account in your chart of accounts, so accounts with no activity in the period show as zero rather than dropping out.

Expenses

Your total expenses for the selected period, broken down by account.

Two numbers appear per category, and they measure different things:

  • The percentage next to each category is that category’s spend as a share of your revenue — the standard way to read an expense on an income statement
  • The bar underneath compares that category to your largest expense category. Your biggest category fills the bar, and everything else is drawn relative to it

Categories accounting for less than one percent of revenue show as <1%.

Keeping the numbers accurate

These figures come straight from your books, so uncategorized transactions leave gaps in them. If a period has transactions still waiting to be categorized, the page tells you how many and links you to them.

For the full detail behind any figure here, go to Reports. See our Understanding reports in Mercury Books article.

FAQs

Why is my revenue here different from my Profit & Loss?

Check that the date range matches. If it does, the likely cause is uncategorized transactions — categorize them and both will agree.

Why don’t I see a burn rate?

Either you don’t yet have three completed months of activity in your books, or your cash flow was net positive across those three months.

Does the cash figure include my Treasury balance?

No. Treasury activity isn’t part of your books.

Can I change which figures appear here?

Not currently. For a specific view of your numbers, use Reports, where you can set any period and filter by tag.

Connecting Your Accounts

Connecting accounts and integrations

Everything that feeds your books is managed from the Accounts page in Mercury Books. That’s where you link external bank accounts and credit cards, connect Stripe, PayPal, and Gusto, add manual accounts, fix broken connections, and check what’s syncing.

What connects automatically

Your Mercury accounts don’t need to be connected. Mercury checking, savings, and credit accounts in your organization syncs to Books automatically, including accounts you’ve closed — so your history stays complete.

Note: All of your Mercury accounts are included in your books by design. There’s no way to exclude an individual Mercury account.

Adding an account

  • Go to Accounts in the left-hand menu of Books
  • Click Link account
  • Choose what you’re connecting:
    • Bank account — an external checking or savings account, linked through Plaid
    • Credit or other account — an external credit card or other account, linked through Plaid
    • Payroll or payment processor — Stripe, PayPal, or Gusto
    • Click Add account — for anything you’ll bring in by CSV via manual linking
  • Follow the prompts to sign in and authorize access

Note: Linking or reconnecting a bank or credit account requires external account permissions, and connecting payroll requires team management permission. If an option is greyed out, hover over it to see which permission you’re missing, then ask an admin on your team.

Finishing setup

Some connections need one more step before anything syncs.

  • Stripe and PayPal ask you to map your revenue, fee, and refund ledgers, so Books knows where sales, processing fees, and refunds should post. Until that’s done, the connection stays pending and no transactions come through
  • Gusto asks for a start date, then backfills your completed payroll runs from that date forward

Tip: Finish the mapping step in the same sitting as the connection. It’s the most common place setup stalls, and nothing syncs until it’s complete.

Reading account statuses

Each row on the Accounts page shows a status:

  • Auto-synced — connected and transactions are flowing
  • Setup needed — the connection exists but setup isn’t finished
  • Sync paused — syncing was stopped for this account
  • Connection lost — the connection needs to be re-established

Use the filter tabs above the table to narrow to All, Mercury, Bank, Credit, or payroll accounts.

Fixing a feed that looks out of date

Connections break — usually after a password change, a multi-factor authentication reset, or when your bank requires you to re-authorize access. When that happens the row shows Connection lost.

  • Go to Accounts
  • Click Reconnect on the affected row
  • Sign in again and re-authorize

If a feed looks stale but the status is healthy, check whether setup is complete on that account. A last-synced date can appear while a connection is still waiting on its mapping step.

For more, see our Why some transactions are missing from Books article.

Pausing sync and removing an account

To stop an account from syncing, open the ⋯ menu on its row and choose to stop syncing. The status changes to Sync paused.

To remove an account entirely, open the ⋯ menu, go to Account settings, and click Delete account at the bottom.

Note: Deleting an account isn’t reversible. Its transactions and reconciliations are removed from your books along with it.

When your bank can’t be linked

Not every institution can be linked through Plaid. If yours isn’t available, or the connection won’t hold, add a manual account and bring transactions in with a CSV instead. See our Importing transactions with a CSV article.

FAQs

How often do accounts sync?

Bank and credit accounts sync throughout the day. Stripe and PayPal post activity as it happens. Payroll syncs run every 15 minutes.

Can I connect more than one bank?

Yes. There’s no limit on how many external bank or credit accounts you link.

Do I need to connect accounts to Books separately from my banking dashboard?

External accounts you link for Books are managed on the Books Accounts page. Your Stripe connection for Books is separate from a Stripe connection used for Mercury Invoicing — if Stripe activity isn’t reaching your books, connect it from the Accounts page in Books.

Which integrations does Books support?

See our Integrations Mercury Books supports article for the full list.

Importing transactions with a CSV

If an account can’t be linked automatically — a bank Plaid doesn’t support, an international account, or a closed account from a previous bank — you can bring its transactions into Mercury Books with a CSV. This article explains how.

Adding a manual account

Before you import, create an account for the transactions to post to.

  • Within Books, go to Accounts
  • Click Add account
  • Choose to add a manual account
  • Give it a name that matches how you’ll recognize it on your statements, and save

Importing your transactions

  • Within Books, go to Transactions
  • Click Import transactions
  • Select the account you’re importing into
  • Upload your CSV or paste the transaction details
  • Map your file’s columns to the fields Books expects — date, description, and amount
  • Review the transactions on the import screen
  • Click to complete the import

Tip: Starting the import from the Reconciliation page pre-selects the account for you, which saves a step when you’re importing to close out a period.

Preparing your file

Most banks let you export transactions as a CSV directly. A few things to check before you upload:

  • One row per transaction, with a header row at the top
  • Dates in a single consistent format
  • Amounts as numbers, with outflows and inflows clearly distinguishable
  • Remove running balance columns, subtotals, and any summary rows your bank added
  • Trim the date range to the period you actually need, so you don’t import overlapping transactions

Note: Transactions dated before your entry start date aren’t brought into your books, even in an import. Check your entry start date if part of your file doesn’t appear.

Correcting an imported transaction

Transaction amounts can’t be edited after they’re in your books. If an amount is wrong, delete the transaction and import it again with the correct value.

Descriptions and categories can be edited normally from your Transactions page within Books.

Integrations Mercury Books supports

Mercury Books connects to your Mercury accounts automatically and to a set of outside services so your sales, fees, payroll, and external bank activity post to your books without manual entry. This article lists what’s supported and what each connection brings in.

What’s supported

Connection

What it brings into Books

Mercury accounts

Every checking, savings, and credit account in your organization, including closed accounts. Connected automatically, with continuous auto-reconciliation

External bank accounts

Transaction feed from an outside checking or savings account, linked through Plaid

External credit cards

Transaction feed from an outside credit card or other account, linked through Plaid

Stripe

Sales, refunds, processing fees, taxes, and payouts

PayPal

Sales, refunds, fees, taxes, and payouts

Gusto

Completed payroll runs, posted as balanced journal entries

Mercury Invoicing

Your invoices and customers, with payment matching synced both ways

Mercury Bill Pay (Cash-basis only)

Your bills and vendors with payment matching synced both ways

Manual accounts

Anything you bring in by CSV, for accounts that can’t be linked

What each one gives you

Mercury accounts. Nothing to set up. Transactions arrive with their notes and receipts from your banking dashboard attached, and reconciliation happens continuously in the background.

External bank and credit accounts. Linked through Plaid. Books pulls the transaction feed from your entry start date forward and creates a source account for it in your chart of accounts.

Stripe and PayPal. After you map your revenue, fee, and refund ledgers, sales and fees post to a dedicated account for that processor. When a payout lands in your bank account, Books links the two sides so revenue isn’t counted twice. See our Using Stripe with Mercury Books and Using PayPal with Mercury Books articles.

Gusto. Completed payroll runs post as balanced journal entries with wages, taxes, and reimbursements mapped to the right accounts. Works on both cash and accrual. See our Using Gusto with Mercury Books article.

Mercury Invoicing. Once you’ve mapped your ledgers, invoices sync between Books and Invoicing in near real time. You can edit invoice details from inside Books, and a payment matched in either product shows as matched in both.

What isn’t supported

  • Other payroll providers. Gusto is the only payroll integration today
  • Other payment processors. Stripe and PayPal are supported; other processors aren’t
  • Stripe Connect and Stripe Express accounts. Only your own Stripe account’s activity is brought in
  • Stripe subscriptions. Books reads Stripe transactions, not subscription records, so there’s no revenue recognition from Stripe billing
  • Non-USD accounts and invoices. Books works in USD
  • QuickBooks Online, Xero, and NetSuite. Books is an accounting system in its own right rather than something that syncs to another one. See our Using Mercury Books alongside another accounting systems article

Does Books sync out to QuickBooks or Xero?

No. Books is your accounting system, not a feed into another one.

Can I connect two Stripe accounts?

My bank isn’t on the list.

Using Gusto with Mercury Books

Connecting Gusto to Mercury Books turns your completed payroll runs into balanced journal entries automatically, with wages, taxes, and reimbursements posted to the right accounts. This article explains how to set it up and how payroll behaves in your books.

Connecting Gusto

  • Go to Accounts in Books
  • Click Link account > Payroll or payment processor and choose Gusto
  • Authorize Mercury to read your Gusto payroll data
  • Set the date you want Books to start pulling payroll from

Books then backfills your completed payroll runs from that date forward.

Note: Connecting payroll requires team management permission, which admins usually have. If the option is greyed out, hover over it to see what’s missing and ask an admin on your team.

What comes in

Books pulls completed payroll runs — runs that have been processed and paid. For each one it creates a balanced journal entry covering wages, employer taxes, employee tax withholding, and reimbursements, mapped to the matching accounts in your chart of accounts.

Payroll works on both cash and accrual books.

Where to find your payroll

Go to Payroll in the left-hand menu of Books. Each row is a payroll run, with its period start and end dates.

Click a run to open it. The side panel gives you three views:

  • Details — what the payroll is made up of, line by line
  • Payment matching — what a bank transaction can settle against
  • Journal entries — what actually posted to your books

Matching payroll to your bank transactions

Gusto usually debits your bank account more than once for a single payroll run — typically one debit for net pay, another for payroll taxes, and sometimes another for reimbursements or benefits. You match those debits to the payroll lines they settle.

  • In Books, go to Transactions (or the account under Reconciliation) and open the Gusto debit
  • Click Match payroll (on accrual-basis Books it’s under Match payment → Match payroll)
  • Select the payroll run(s) the debit covers
  • Click Complete

Which lines you can match depends on your accounting method:

  • On cash books, you match the expense lines — earnings, employer taxes, and employer benefit contributions.
  • On accrual books, wage and reimbursement expense was already recognized when the payroll synced, so you match against the payable lines instead — wages payable and payroll tax payable.

Regardless of your accounting method, you are only required to match the lines that are included in Payroll Cash Requirement.

  • Wages
  • Employer Taxes
  • Employee Taxes
  • Reimbursements

Benefits and some jurisdictional taxes can have varying payment schedules, such as quarterly or bi-annually, that don’t match with a bi-weekly or monthly payroll model. As long as you match payments made to the cash requirement lines, the payroll run will be marked as Fully Matched.

Troubleshooting

Payroll is stuck finishing setup. Certain payroll runs — corrections, reversals, and true-ups with negative amounts — can hold up the initial backfill. Contact support with your Gusto connection and we’ll clear it.

A payroll run won’t fully match. Check whether a benefits amount is missing from the journal entry. You can also record an adjustment while matching, then clear it with a manual journal entry.

A payroll debit is in my bank feed but not matched. Payroll debits aren’t matched automatically. Open the transaction and match it to the payroll lines it covers.

FAQs

Does Books pull payroll runs that haven’t been paid yet?

No. Only completed runs come in.

Does Gusto get anything back from Books?

No. The connection is read-only.

Are other payroll providers supported?

Gusto is the only payroll integration today. For other providers, record payroll with manual journal entries.

Using PayPal with Mercury Books

Connecting PayPal to Mercury Books brings your sales, refunds, fees, and payouts into your books automatically. This article explains what comes in, how it posts, and what to watch for.

Connecting PayPal

  • Go to Accounts in Books
  • Click Add account and choose PayPal
  • Authorize Mercury to read your PayPal data
  • Map your ledgers — pick or create a revenue account, a fee account, and a refund account
  • Set the date you want Books to start pulling PayPal activity from

Books creates an account in your chart of accounts representing your PayPal balance. Sales and fees post there until the money is paid out to your bank.

Note: Nothing syncs until the ledger mapping step is complete.

What comes in

  • Sales — posted as revenue
  • Refunds — posted to your refund account
  • Fees — posted to your fee account
  • Taxes collected through PayPal
  • Payouts — transfers from your PayPal balance to your bank account

The connection is read-only. Books reads from PayPal and never writes back.

Avoiding a duplicate PayPal account

PayPal can also be linked as a bank account through Plaid. Don’t do both — linking PayPal through Plaid and through the PayPal integration creates two separate accounts in your books, and your PayPal activity gets recorded twice.

Use the PayPal integration from Accounts > Add account. If you already have PayPal linked through Plaid, remove that connection first.

Reconciling PayPal

Your PayPal account in Books reconciles like any other account, on monthly windows, against your PayPal balance for the period. Your bank account reconciles against your bank statement, where payouts appear as linked deposits.

See our Reconciling accounts in Mercury Books article.

Troubleshooting

PayPal is connected but nothing is syncing.

The ledger mapping step isn’t finished. Go to Accounts, open your PayPal row, and complete it.

My PayPal activity appears twice.

You likely have PayPal linked through both Plaid and the PayPal integration. Remove the Plaid connection and delete the duplicate account.

A payout deposit is categorized as revenue.

Give it a day — Books recategorizes it as a transfer once the payout event arrives. If it doesn’t resolve, categorize it as a transfer between accounts yourself.

FAQs

Will connecting PayPal change anything in PayPal?

No. The connection is read-only.

Can I match PayPal payments to invoices?

Yes. Open the transaction and match the payment to the invoice it settles. See our Matching payments to invoices, bills, and payroll article.

Can I change which accounts PayPal posts to?

Yes. Open your PayPal connection from the Accounts page and update the ledger mapping.

Does Books support PayPal in currencies other than USD?

Not currently. Books works in USD.

Using Stripe with Mercury Books

Connecting Stripe to Mercury Books brings your sales, refunds, processing fees, and payouts into your books automatically, so you don’t have to enter them by hand or work backward from your bank deposits. This article explains what comes in, how it posts, and how to sort out the most common issues.

Connecting Stripe

  • Go to Accounts in Books
  • Click Link account > Payroll or payment processor and select Stripe
  • Authorize Mercury to read your Stripe data
  • Map your ledgers — pick or create a revenue account, a fee account, and a refund account
  • Set the date you want Books to start pulling Stripe activity from

Books also creates an account in your chart of accounts representing your Stripe balance. Sales and fees post there until the money is paid out to your bank.

Note: Nothing syncs until the ledger mapping step is complete. If you connected Stripe and your books are still empty, this is almost always why.

What comes in

  • Charges — your sales, posted as revenue
  • Refunds — posted to your refund account
  • Processing fees — posted to your fee account
  • Taxes collected through Stripe
  • Payouts — the transfers from your Stripe balance to your bank account

The connection is read-only. Books reads from Stripe and never writes back.

How it posts to your books

Stripe activity doesn’t post to your bank account — it posts to your Stripe account in Books, which works like a clearing account:

  • A customer pays you. The gross sale posts as revenue, the processing fee posts as an expense, and the net sits in your Stripe balance
  • Stripe pays out to your bank. The payout leaves your Stripe balance and the deposit arrives in your bank feed
  • Books recognizes the two sides as the same money and links them as a transfer between accounts, so the deposit isn’t counted as additional revenue

This is why your Stripe revenue and your bank deposits won’t match line for line — the deposit is a transfer, not income.

Tip: A payout deposit can be categorized as revenue for a short time before Books receives the payout event and links it. If a deposit looks miscategorized, check it again the next day before you change it by hand.

Reconciling Stripe

Your Stripe account in Books reconciles like any other account, on monthly windows. Reconcile it against your Stripe balance for the period.

Your bank account reconciles against your bank statement, where payouts appear as deposits linked to your Stripe activity.

See our Reconciling accounts in Mercury Books article.

Matching Stripe payments to invoices

If you invoice customers who pay through Stripe, you can match the payment to the invoice so your accounts receivable clears. Open the transaction, choose to match the payment, and select the invoice — Books suggests a likely match automatically.

See our Matching payments to invoices, bills, and payroll article.

Troubleshooting

Stripe is connected but nothing is syncing.

The ledger mapping step isn’t finished. Go to Accounts, open your Stripe row, and complete it.

I don’t see the Stripe integration I set up.

Stripe appears in a few places across Mercury — a Stripe connection used for accepting card payments on Mercury invoices is separate from the Books integration. Connect Stripe from Accounts > Add account in Books.

Older payouts aren’t linked to their deposits.

Payout linking applies to payouts that arrive after your connection is set up. For earlier ones, categorize the deposit as a transfer between accounts yourself.

My revenue looks too high.

If you were categorizing Stripe deposits as income before you connected Stripe, those deposits and your new Stripe sales both count. Recategorize the earlier deposits as transfers between accounts.

FAQs

Does Books pull my Stripe subscriptions?

No. Books reads Stripe transactions rather than subscription records, so there’s no revenue recognition schedule from Stripe billing.

Does Books support Stripe Connect or Express accounts?

Not currently. Only your own Stripe account’s activity is brought in.

Will connecting Stripe change anything in Stripe?

No. The connection is read-only.

Can I change which accounts Stripe posts to?

Yes. Open your Stripe connection from the Accounts page and update the ledger mapping.

Getting Started

Eligibility for Mercury Payroll

Most Mercury customers are eligible to use Mercury Payroll. Eligibility can depend on factors such as your industry, business structure, and where your business is based.

This article covers factors that may affect your eligibility and what to expect during setup.

Mercury Payroll has separate eligibility requirements

Eligibility for Mercury Payroll is separate from eligibility for a Mercury account. This means some Mercury customers may not be eligible to use Payroll.

Industry eligibility

Mercury Payroll isn’t currently available to businesses in certain regulated or restricted industries, including:

  • Gambling and gaming, including lotteries, games of chance, and fantasy sports
  • Cannabis sales and dispensaries
  • Sales of firearms or ammunition
  • Sales of flammable or combustible substances
  • Drug paraphernalia
  • Adult entertainment
  • Virtual currency and related services

This list isn’t exhaustive, and eligibility can vary depending on your business. If you have questions, we can help review your eligibility, and we’ll also confirm it as part of the Payroll setup process.

Business structure and payroll arrangements

Mercury Payroll also isn’t currently available to:

  • Government agencies and federal contractors
  • Certain entity types and payroll arrangements, including common paymaster arrangements

Business location

Mercury Payroll is only available for US based customers. We’re unable to onboard businesses based in or have employees in Puerto Rico or other US territories.

Checking your eligibility

If you’re unsure whether your business is eligible for Mercury Payroll, contact us before starting setup.

Otherwise, we’ll review your eligibility after you complete setup and contact you if anything affects your ability to use Payroll. See Setting up payroll.

For more information about what you’ll need to use Mercury Payroll, including a Mercury Business account, an EIN, and someone authorized to sign for your company, see What is Mercury Payroll.

Mercury Payroll is offered by Mercury Technologies, Inc. Certain services are provided by Central Benefits and Insurance Services LLC, a Mercury affiliate, and by third-party partners, including Check Technologies, Inc. and Check Payments LLC.

Setting up Mercury Payroll

Mercury Payroll lives inside your existing Mercury account. There’s no separate app or login. Our Sales and Implementation teams guide you through setup, from confirming your company details to running your first payroll.

Getting started

  • Use the account switcher in your left-hand menu to select Payroll or visit mercury.com/payroll.
  • Fill out a short form about your team: how many people you’ll pay, whether they’re W-2 employees, contractors, or both, and when you plan to start running payroll.
  • Connect with our Sales team. A member of our Sales team will be in touch to walk you through Mercury Payroll, learn more about your needs, and help you get started.

On the call, we’ll learn more about your team. If Mercury Payroll is a fit, we’ll guide you through onboarding.

  • You’ll need a Mercury business account. Payroll is funded from a Mercury account. External bank accounts aren’t supported at launch.
  • You’ll need a verified EIN. Payroll can’t be set up while an EIN application is still pending.
  • We’ll need to verify your company documents. Payroll has additional federal and state compliance requirements, so we’ll need your Articles of Incorporation and IRS EIN confirmation letter (CP 575 or Letter 147C) to complete setup. We may already have these documents from when you opened your Mercury account. If not, we’ll ask you to provide them.
  • The person setting up payroll becomes your signatory by default. The signatory is authorized to sign offer and tax documents and to manage payroll funds. If you’re not authorized to sign for your company, ask an admin who is to join setup.
  • Some industries aren’t eligible. A few industries that Mercury supports for banking aren’t supported for payroll. You can ready more about eligibility here.

How onboarding works

  • Your call with Sales. On your call with Sales, we’ll review your payroll needs and walk you through how Mercury Payroll works. If you decide to move forward, we’ll begin setting up your company together. If additional time is needed, we’ll schedule a follow-up call to complete the setup
  • Meet your Implementation Manager. Once setup is complete, Sales will introduce you to your Implementation Manager, who will be your main point of contact through your first successful payroll run.
  • Activation and team onboarding. Your Implementation Manager will work on activating your company for payroll while you onboard your team.
  • First payroll review. Once your company is activated and your team is fully onboarded, you’ll meet with your Implementation Manager to review your payroll dashboard, walk through your upcoming pay run, and go over everything you need to know before running your first payroll.
  • Your first payroll. Your Implementation Manager will send you a reminder ahead of your first payroll’s auto-submission deadline and monitor your pay run through payday.
  • Ongoing support. After your first successful payroll, Mercury Support becomes your point of contact.

What you’ll confirm during company setup

  • Company details. Your company’s legal name, filing address, entity type, and EIN are filled in from your Mercury banking* application. You’re responsible for making sure these details are accurate. Incorrect entity information can delay state tax registrations and lead to refiling fees. If anything needs correcting, select “I need to update something” or let your Mercury contact know.
  • Company officers. Choose who holds the CEO, CFO, and Secretary roles from your existing admins and owners. One person can hold more than one role. You can also add someone who isn’t on the list, as long as they’ve completed KYC. Not every admin automatically qualifies. If you’re not sure who to assign, check your Articles of Incorporation.
  • Pay frequency. The options are:
    • Weekly (Fridays)
    • Every two weeks (every other Friday)
    • Twice a month (the 15th and the last day of the month), which is the default
    • Monthly (the last day of the month)
  • First payday. You’ll see four valid dates based on the frequency you chose. Mercury handles banking-day and quarter-end timing for you.
  • Funding account. Your Mercury primary checking account is selected by default. You can choose a different Mercury account or create a new one.
  • Authorizations. The last step is signing your debit and filing authorizations and the terms of service.

*Mercury is a fintech company, not an FDIC-insured bank. Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Members FDIC.

What is Mercury Payroll

Mercury Payroll* lets you pay and manage your team from the Mercury account you already use, without a separate app or login. This article covers what’s included, what you need to run payroll, and how pricing works.

What’s included with Mercury Payroll

Payroll processing

Mercury Payroll supports:

  • Payroll processing for W-2 team members and domestic contractors
  • Direct deposit for your team
  • Federal, state, and local tax payments
  • Payroll tax filings for payroll periods run on Mercury
  • Year-end W-2s and 1099s
  • Automated state payroll tax and unemployment insurance registrations
  • Multi-state payroll and multiple pay schedules
  • Downloadable payroll reports for your books
Hiring and team management

You can manage your team and their payroll details in Mercury, including:

  • Hiring, pay changes, offboarding, and rehiring
  • Offer letters and confidentiality agreements as part of the hiring flow
  • Self-onboarding for new hires to enter their own tax and bank details
  • A single record for each team member with their personal, employment, and pay details
  • Payroll permissions to control who can view and manage payroll
Benefits

Benefits are offered through a licensed broker and include:

  • Health, dental, and vision coverage in all 50 states
  • Support from a licensed broker to choose a plan, enrol new hires, and manage coverage changes
  • 401(k) plans provided via Human Interest and Vestwell**

Once set up, you can view your benefits details from within Mercury Payroll.

Tax and compliance support

Mercury Payroll helps manage tax and compliance requirements associated with employing people in all 50 states, including:

  • Filing and remitting federal and state payroll taxes
  • Preparing year-end W-2s and 1099s
  • Creating accounts with state unemployment and revenue departments
  • Identifying requirements when you hire in a new state, including workers’ compensation coverage, and helping set them up
  • Triaging the notices states send you and handle workers’ compensation and benefits audits

Pricing

Mercury Payroll is free for 2026. After that, Mercury Payroll costs $100/month plus $50 for each person paid that month, with no annual contract. For more information, see Mercury Payroll pricing.

Note: You would still be responsible for government fees and taxes that will be passed on to you as well as costs incurred for workers compensation, insurance, and benefits provided by third parties.

FAQs

Do I need a Mercury account to use Mercury Payroll?

Yes. You need Mercury banking*** to access and use Mercury Payroll. Payroll runs directly from your Mercury account, so there’s no separate payroll login or need to transfer payroll funds to an outside provider before payday.

During onboarding, you’ll confirm information Mercury has on file, including your EIN, legal entity details, and account information.

Please confirm this information is current and accurate during onboarding to help prevent downstream filing issues, particularly if your legal name, address, EIN, or entity type has changed.

What do I need to run payroll?

Before you can run payroll, you’ll need:

  • An admin who can sign on behalf of the company: Your company signatory must complete setup and tax authorizations
  • A Mercury Business account: Payroll is funded from a Mercury account; external bank accounts aren’t supported
  • An EIN: Your EIN must be issued before you can set up payroll
  • Up-to-date business information: Confirm that your business ownership, legal entity, and address information is accurate in your Payroll Settings. Inaccurate information can cause issues with payroll setup and tax filings
Can I connect Mercury Payroll to a non-Mercury account?

No. Mercury Payroll can only be used with your Mercury account. You can’t connect an external or non-Mercury bank account to fund payroll.

Can I run payroll in multiple states?

Yes. Mercury Payroll includes multi-state payroll in your subscription and can help with state payroll tax and unemployment insurance registrations when you hire in a new state.

Does Mercury Payroll support contractors?

Yes. Mercury Payroll supports W-2 team members and domestic contractors, including year-end W-2s and 1099s. International contractors aren’t supported yet. Until international contractor support is available, you can pay them directly from your Mercury account outside of Payroll.

How do I get started with Mercury Payroll?

To get started with Mercury Payroll, log in to Mercury on web and select Payroll from the left-hand product switcher. You can also get started here. Our team will reach out to learn about your payroll needs and walk you through setup.

Getting Started With Books

Choosing your accounting method

Mercury Books supports both cash and accrual accounting. You choose your accounting method during setup, and it applies to your whole set of books. This article explains where the setting lives, what changes depending on which method you’re on, and how to change it if you need to.

Where your accounting method is set

You select your accounting basis during Books setup. To see which method you’re on afterward, go to Settings > Accounting basis.

What each method does in Books

The difference comes down to when revenue and expenses.

  • Cash basis records income when money arrives in your account and expenses when money leaves it. If you’ve sent an invoice or received a bill but the money hasn’t moved yet, your reports don’t show it. Learn more here.
  • Accrual basis records income when you earn it and expenses when you incur them, whether or not. the money has moved. Your reports reflect the invoice revenue or bill expense on the date the invoice or bill was issued. Learn more here.

Changing your accounting method

Your accounting method is set when your books are created and can’t be switched on your own.

If you need to change it, head to Settings > Accounting basis to contact support.

FAQs

Which method should I choose?

Which method is right for your business depends on your size, your industry, your investors, and your tax situation. If you’re unsure which method to use, consider working with one of our Accounting Partners.

Can I see my reports on both bases?

Not currently. Your reports reflect the accounting method your books are set up on.

Getting started with Mercury Books

Mercury Books is a full double-entry accounting solution built into your Mercury account. It brings your transactions, journal entries, reconciliations, and financial reports into the same place you already do your banking*.

This article explains what Books does, how to set it up, and how to decide whether you want to run your books yourself or work with a bookkeeper.

What Mercury Books does

  • Supports cash and accrual accounting on a full double-entry ledger
  • Syncs every Mercury checking, savings, and credit account automatically — including closed accounts, so you have your full history
  • Connects to external bank and credit card accounts through Plaid
  • Connects to Stripe, PayPal, and Gusto so sales, fees, payouts, and payroll post to your books without manual entry
  • Pulls in your Mercury invoices and bills, and keeps payment matching in sync between Books and Mercury Invoicing
  • Auto-reconciles your Mercury accounts continuously, because they live in the same system as your books
  • Categorizes transactions automatically using AI, similarity matching, and rules you define
  • Produces a Profit & Loss, Balance Sheet, Cash Flow, and General Ledger you can filter, drill into, and export

Getting into Books

Books appears in the left-hand menu of your Mercury dashboard. You can also go straight there at app.mercury.com/books.

To move back to your banking dashboard, use the product switcher in the top left corner.

Getting started with Books

Getting started with Books is near instant after making two decisions:

  • Select your accounting basis — cash to track money when it moves, or accural to track revenue and expenses when they’re earned or incurred.
  • Choose a chart of accounts template based on your entity type, or import your own as a CSV

Mercury will automatically set your start date: Nearest date between Jan 1 2025 or date of incorporation. This can be edited via Settings post-set up.

Note: You need a role with the all accounts, accounting, invoice creation, and recipient management permissions. The first two are required to open Books at all; without the other two, payment matching and vendor records won’t work. See our Sharing access to your books article.

Once setup is complete, Books opens on your home page with your cash, revenue, and expense insights for the period.

Finalizing Books set-up

After getting into Books, there are a few additional steps to pull in non-Mercury data and invite any bookkeeper users who you’d like to collaborate with.

Bringing your non-Mercury data over

Books is designed around a clean cutover rather than a full historical migration. The recommended approach is to close your last period in your current system, set your entry start date to the first day of the period you want to start in Books, and bring over your chart of accounts.

  • Import your chart of accounts as a CSV during setup, or start from one of Mercury’s templates
  • Import transactions for accounts Books can’t connect to directly using Transactions > + Import transactions
  • Record opening balances as of your cutover date with a manual journal entry

For a step-by-step walkthrough, see our Moving to Books from QuickBooks Online or Xero article.

Do you need a bookkeeper?

No. Plenty of founders run Books entirely on their own, and the product is built to work that way. Choose whichever path fits how you work today:

  • Do it yourself — you categorize transactions, create journal entries, reconcile, and pull your own reports
  • Bring your own bookkeeper — you invite the bookkeeper or accountant you already work with into your Mercury account
  • Get matched with a bookkeeper — Mercury introduces you to a partner bookkeeping firm that fits your business

The path isn’t permanent. You can start on your own and add a bookkeeper later, or bring one in from the start and take more of it on yourself over time. Learn more in our Working with a bookkeeper in Mercury Books article.

Note: If you get matched with a bookkeeping firm, that firm sets its own pricing and you pay the firm directly. Bookkeeping services aren’t included with Mercury Books.

FAQs

Does Books replace my accountant?

Depends how comfortable you are. Books does the mechanics well enough that a lot of founders handle it themselves. For the judgment calls — unusual transactions, accounting method, taxes — most people still want an accountant in the loop.

Can I use Books if I bank somewhere else too?

Yes. You can link external bank accounts and credit cards through Plaid, and import transactions by CSV for any account Plaid doesn’t support.

Does Books support multiple currencies?

Not currently. Books works in USD, and non-USD invoices don’t sync into Books.

Can I use Books for more than one business?

You can access Books for every business that has a business banking account with Mercury.

How much does Books cost?

Books is free through December 31, 2026. Starting January 1, 2027, Books will cost $35/month. It’s a separate subscription — not included in Mercury Plus or Mercury Pro. See mercury.com/books for details.

Can I see a demo of Books before committing?

Yes. You can explore Books in a Mercury demo environment to see how it works before getting started: demo.mercury.com.

Moving from QuickBooks Online (QBO) to Mercury Books

This guide will walk you through how to bring your QBO chart of accounts and trial balances to Mercury Books.

When you’re done here you’ll have:

  • Your QBO chart of accounts in Books.
  • Your opening balances from QBO to Books.
  • Mercury and external bank and card accounts synced as of your start date.
  • A clean starting point to begin using Mercury Books!

Note: Detailed transaction history, vendor info, invoices, and customer lists are currently unable to be migrated to Books. Should you wish to access this data, it is recommended that you maintain read access to your QBO account and/or export any relevant data you may need to access. It is recommended that you consult with your accountant to ensure you are capturing the data you need.

Time required to migrate: 30 - 45 mins

Before you begin migrating

In order to begin setup, you will need to have/know the items below:

  • Will you be using cash or accrual basis accounting?
  • The date you will close your QBO books and switch to Mercury Books: this determines your Books start date.
    • Books defaults to a January 1, 2026 start date, so a switch-over date of December 31, 2025 is recommended but not required.
    • Switching mid-year (ex: June 30) requires one more step (refer to step 7 below).Reconcile QBO through your switch-over date to close out you can refer to the QuickBooks help article here.
  • Download the Chart of Account Conversion Tool → Link here
    • If you’re signed into a Google account, select File > Make a copy
    • Otherwise, select File > Download to save the spreadsheet
  • Start with a new Books instance. This guide assumes you’re starting from the Books onboarding screen. If you have already begun onboarding, reach out to us via customer support and we can reset your account to start fresh.

Have questions? It is recommended you consult your accountant before completing the steps below.

Part 1: Chart of accounts

1. Export your Chart of Accounts (CoA) from QuickBooks

In QuickBooks, go to Settings (gear icon) → Chart of accounts → Run report, then export to Excel or CSV.

2. Convert the CoA for Books

Books uses different account types than QuickBooks and requires that all GL accounts need a number. The CoA converter allows you to quickly map QBO accounts into Books for a seamless import.

  • Open the converter file
  • Paste all rows from your QuickBooks’ export into the Input tab. Don’t paste headers
  • Download the Export tab as a CSV

Existing account numbers carry over as 5-digit codes, and missing ones are generated. You can change any number later in Books.

3. Import your CoA into Books

From the Books onboarding screen, choose Import custom chart of accounts and upload your CSV export from the converter file.

4. Resolve any errors

Books will highlight rows with errors in red. The most common are:

  • Missing or duplicate account numbers
  • Account numbers: Books already uses for default and required accounts (i.e. Accounts Receivable, Retained Earnings). An account type Books doesn’t recognize

Once all errors are resolved, you are ready to import your Chart of Accounts into Books.

Part 2: Beginning Balances

5. Your Books Start Date

Your Books start date is the day after your switch-over date, and Mercury accounts sync automatically from it. The default is January 1, 2026, or your incorporation date if later.

If you’re switching on a different date, change it in Settings → Books details so Mercury transactions already in QuickBooks aren’t counted twice.

Start date can only be moved to an earlier date in time (example: 1/1/2026 → 8/1/2025). If you need to move the start date to a later date in time, reach out to customer support.

6. Enter your opening balances

In QuickBooks, run a Balance Sheet report as of your switch over date. Eg. Balance sheet as of 12/31/2025 if Books start date is 1/1/2026.

Then, in Books, go to Chart of Accounts, edit each account, and enter its balance from the report as the opening balance.

Skip these accounts to avoid counting them twice:

Skip

Why

Mercury accounts

They sync automatically from your Books start date.

Other banks and credit cards you’ll connect via Plaid

You’ll set these balances when you connect them (step 8).

7. Switching mid-year? Add your year-to-date income and expenses

Skip this step if your switch-over date is your fiscal year-end.

In QuickBooks, run a Profit and Loss report from the start of your fiscal year to your switch-over date. Enter each income and expense account’s total as its opening balance, as in step 7.

Books now has everything you’ve recorded in QuickBooks.

Part 3: Connect your other accounts

8. Connect your other banks and cards

From the setup checklist on your Books home page, connect each non-Mercury bank and credit card account via Plaid. For each one:

  • Start date: your Books start date
  • Opening balance: the closing balance from the day before your start date. e.g., For a July 1 start, use the June 30 balance

Confirm your Books opening balances match QBO

In the left side panel in Books, select Chart of Accounts and check that each account’s opening balance matches your ending balances in QBO. For Plaid-connected accounts, you will want to reconcile the balances to the balances the day before your start date.

If you work with an accountant, have them review. Then you can set QuickBooks to read-only and keep it for your records.

FAQs

Will my transaction details move to Books?

No. Individual transaction details before your start date will not transfer from QBO.

Will open invoices and bills transfer over fromQuickBooks?

Mercury bills and invoices after your start date will sync to Books; external invoices will not.

Can I change account numbers after importing?

Yes, you can edit account numbers and names at any time.

My balances don’t match. What should I check first?

Look for an account that has an opening balance from step 6 and was also connected via Plaid, or a start date that isn’t the day after your switch-over date. Both cause double counting.

Setting your entry start date

Your entry start date determines how far back Mercury Books pulls in your account activity and which periods are available in your reports. This article explains how your entry start date works, how to choose or change it, and what happens when you move it to an earlier date.

What your entry start date controls

  • How far back transactions sync. Books pulls transactions dated on or after your entry start date from every connected account — Mercury accounts, external accounts linked through Plaid, and your Stripe, PayPal, and Gusto integrations. Anything dated before it isn’t brought in
  • Which periods your reports cover. Months, quarters, and years that fall entirely before your entry start date are hidden from the period selector on your reports and excluded from report output

Choosing a date

Pick the first day of the first period you want to keep in Mercury Books. In practice, that’s usually the day after the last period you closed in your previous system.

For example, if your 2025 books are closed in QuickBooks Online and you want to start doing your bookkeeping in Mercury Books for 2026, choose January 1, 2026.

Books defaults your entry start date to your business’s date of incorporation or January 1, 2025, whichever is more recent. A few things to consider when deciding whether to change it:

  • Starting at incorporation gives you the most complete picture, and is the right choice if you’ve never kept formal books
  • Starting at a clean period boundary is usually simpler if you already have closed books elsewhere — you avoid duplicating work and reconciling periods twice
  • An older start date means more historical transactions to review and categorize before your reports are accurate

Tip: Choose a date that lines up with the start of a month, quarter, or year. Reconciliation in Books runs on monthly windows, so a mid-month start date leaves you with a partial first period.

Changing your entry start date

You can change your entry start date via Settings > Books Details.

When your entry start date moves earlier, Books backfills the older transactions from your connected accounts. Two things to expect while that happens:

  • Reconciliation windows you’ve already completed can temporarily show as out of balance while older transactions arrive. This resolves on its own once the backfill finishes
  • Newly arrived historical transactions need to be reviewed and categorized like any others

FAQs

Can I pull in transactions from before my entry start date?

Not without changing the date itself. Transactions dated before your entry start date aren’t brought into your books, including through a CSV import. If you need older history, contact support to have your entry start date moved earlier.

Why can’t I select last year on my Profit & Loss?

Periods that fall entirely before your entry start date are hidden from the report period selector. The month, quarter, and year that contain your entry start date remain selectable.

Does my entry start date have to match my fiscal year?

No. It’s independent of your fiscal year — it only controls how far back data syncs.

I set the date too recently and my books look empty. What now?

This is the most common cause of missing transactions. See our Why some transactions are missing from Books article, then change date in the Books Details tab.

Understanding your chart of accounts

Your chart of accounts is the list of accounts your bookkeeping is organized around — your revenue accounts, expense accounts, assets, liabilities, and equity. In Mercury Books, these are called Ledger accounts. When you categorize a transaction in Books, you’re selecting a ledger account from your chart of accounts.

How your chart of accounts gets created

During setup you either choose a Books template or import your own chart of accounts as a CSV.

To see your chart of accounts, go to Chart of Accounts in the left-hand menu of Books.

Reading the page

Each row is a ledger account with:

  • An ledger code — the number used to sort and group accounts, like 1000 for assets or 4000 for revenue
  • A ledger account — what you’ll see in the category dropdown when you categorize a transaction
  • A type — asset, liability, equity, revenue, or expense, which determines where the account appears on your reports
  • An opening balance, the beginning balance of the account on your Books start date where one applies

Every Books accounts includes a set of system ledger accounts that can’t be deleted.

Making changes

Adding, renaming, and removing individual accounts is straightforward.

To add an account:

  • In Books, go to Chart of Accounts
  • Click the Add ledger account button
  • Enter the ledger code, name, and type
  • Click to save

To rename or edit an account, click the row to open it, make your change, and save. Renaming an account updates it everywhere, including on transactions already categorized to it and on past reports.

To delete a ledger account, open it and click the delete. .

Note: An account can’t be deleted if it has any line entries posted to it. If you see “Can not delete ledger with line entries,” recategorize the transactions to a different account first, then delete it.

Why some transactions are missing from Books

If a transaction isn’t showing up in Books, it’s usually one of three things: the account hasn’t finished setup, the transaction is older than the window your connection can import, or it’s dated before your books begin. Here’s how to tell which.

Check the account’s setup status

Linking an account and finishing its setup are two separate steps. An account can appear on your Accounts page while still waiting on the rest of its configuration — and nothing syncs until that’s done.

Go to Accounts and check the status on each row:

  • Auto-synced — the account is connected and transactions are flowing
  • Setup needed — setup isn’t finished yet. Select the account to complete it
  • Sync paused — syncing was stopped for this account
  • Connection lost — the connection needs to be re-established

For Stripe and PayPal, setup includes mapping your revenue, fee, and refund GL accounts. Until that’s complete, the connection stays pending and no transactions come through.

How far back each connection imports

When you first connect an account, Books imports history up to a limit set by each provider. It can’t pull transactions older than that window:

Connection

How far back it imports

Connected external bank accounts

Up to 2 years

Payment platforms (e.g. Stripe, PayPal)

Up to 2 years

Payroll providers (e.g. Gusto)

Back to January 1 of two years ago

These limits come from our integration partners or the providers themselves, so anything older won’t be available to import.

Other reasons a transaction might not appear

Even inside that window, Books won’t add a transaction if:

  • It’s dated before your books’ start date. Books only tracks activity from the start date you set. Transactions before it are skipped.
  • It falls in a closed period. Once you’ve reconciled and closed a period, new transactions dated within it won’t be added automatically, so your reconciled numbers don’t change.
  • The account’s sync start date is later than the transaction. Anything before that date won’t import.
  • The import is still finishing. After you connect an account, your transaction history can take a while to arrive. Give it some time and check back.
  • It’s still pending. Pending transactions may not appear until they clear.

What to do next

  • On the Accounts page, confirm the account shows Auto-synced. If it says Setup needed, finish setup first.
  • Check the transaction’s date against the limits above.
  • Confirm your books’ start date under Settings > Books details.
  • Confirm the account’s sync start date on the Accounts page.
  • Still missing? If the account shows Auto-synced and the transaction is dated within the last 2 years, after your books’ start date, and outside any closed period, contact Support with the account name and the transaction’s date and amount.

FAQs

How long should a sync take?

After sign up

  • Your Mercury transactions appear in Books within seconds. Transactions from external accounts — banks, payment platforms, and payroll — typically start syncing within a few minutes of finishing setup. A first-time import of a long history can take longer to fully arrive.

On an ongoing basis

  • Mercury transactions appear within seconds of posting.
  • External bank and payment platform transactions sync as soon as the provider sends an update — usually several times a day.
  • Payroll syncs run hourly minutes.

Managing Your Team

Adding someone to payroll

When you add a teammate to payroll, you can set up their pay and employment details, send offer documents, assign their role, and issue a card if they need one. After you send the invite, they’ll complete their personal, tax withholding, and bank account details themselves.

This article covers how to add a teammate to payroll and what happens after you send their invite.

Adding a teammate to payroll

Both team members and contractors must be based in the US to be added to payroll. You’re responsible for making sure their employment and pay details meet applicable requirements.

Add their details
  • From your Payroll home page, scroll to the Team section
  • Select Add teammate
  • Search for an existing Mercury teammate, or select Invite a new teammate
  • Enter their name, email, job title, personal email, and whether they’re a team member or contractor. You can also add their manager and department
  • Select Next
Set up their employment and pay
  • Choose their work location: Select an existing office or enter their state if the team member is remote
  • Set their pay type: Choose from the available options based on whether they’re a team member or contractor
  • Enter their pay details: Add their pay rate and scheduled hours, if applicable, then complete any optional fields for signing bonuses, overtime eligibility, or contract documents (if applicable)
Add offer documents
  • Under “Offer Documents”, select Add offer letter to send a default offer letter for e-signature. You can also add a standard confidentiality agreement.
  • Preview offer documents before sending or select X to remove them.

Note: We’ll collect I-9s by default but if you choose to collect them elsewhere, you can unselect this document.

Assign a role and card
  • Select Next, assign the teammate a role, then select Next
  • Choose whether to issue them a card. If you do, select the card type and set their spend controls
  • Select Next
Review and send the invite
  • Review the teammate’s details before sending their invite

Note: You’re responsible for confirming that your teammate’s employment and pay details comply with applicable laws and requirements. This includes, but isn’t limited to:

  • Their pay meets minimum wage requirements for their work location

  • They’re correctly classified as a team member or contractor

  • They’re at least 18 years old

  • Their pay frequency meets applicable state requirements

  • Once you’ve reviewed their information, select Send Invite

After you send the invite

Your teammate will receive an email asking them to create an account and complete their onboarding. They’ll be able to sign their offer letter or confidentiality agreement and provide their:

  • Personal info
  • I-9 verification (if applicable)
  • Bank account for receiving pay
  • Tax withholding information
  • Benefits elections (if applicable)

Managing someone’s payroll details

From your Payroll homepage, find someone in the Team section and select their name to open their profile. From there, you can manage how they’re paid and view their payroll information.

Changing someone’s pay

The Pay tab shows someone’s current compensation, including whether they’re salaried or hourly and when their current compensation took effect.

To make a change:

  • Select Manage pay
  • Select Edit compensation
  • Make your changes, then select Save changes

Keep in mind:

  • You can set an effective date in the past. The new rate applies from that date, but paychecks that have already been processed aren’t changed
  • If the effective date falls in the middle of a pay period, that period is split between the old and new rates, so the next paycheck may not reflect a full period at the new rate

Viewing someone’s pay history

Select Manage pay, then View compensation history to see previous changes to someone’s pay and when each change took effect.

Compensation history is a record and can’t be edited.

Adding a recurring earning

A recurring earning is an amount added to someone’s paycheck on top of their base pay. Someone can have multiple recurring earnings at once.

To add one, select Manage pay, then Add recurring earning. Choose the appropriate earning type and enter the details of the payment.

Earning types include:

  • Bonus (supplemental wages) and Commission — supplemental wages that are taxed differently from regular wages
  • Regular allowance — a taxable cash allowance, such as a car or remote-work allowance
  • Reimbursement — a recurring expense reimbursement, such as a phone or internet stipend
  • Group term life and Other imputed income — imputed income that increases taxable wages without being paid out. For group term life, enter the imputed cost rather than the coverage amount
  • 2% shareholder benefits and 2% shareholder HSA — for S-corp shareholders with more than 2% ownership

The tax treatment of an earning can depend on the circumstances. Make sure you select the earning type that applies to the payment.

Adding a deduction

Deductions are recurring amounts withheld from a team member’s pay after tax. They’re only available for team members and can’t be added for contractors.

Select Manage pay, then Add deduction and choose the appropriate type:

  • Miscellaneous — deductions that aren’t garnishments, such as union dues, donations, or loan repayments
  • Garnishment — wage garnishments calculated using disposable income, such as tax liens or student loans
  • Child support — child support garnishments ordered by a state authority

For miscellaneous deductions, percentage-based deductions are calculated from gross pay. For garnishments, they’re calculated from disposable income. You can also set limits and, for garnishments, a priority when someone has multiple orders.

Child support requires information from the order, including the case and issuing state. You can also choose whether the payment is remitted through payroll or paid separately by your company.

Keep in mind:

  • Child support is withheld before other garnishments, subject to each order’s disposable-income limit
  • If someone’s pay can’t cover all garnishments, child support is withheld first, followed by other garnishments from oldest to newest. Any amount that can’t be withheld in full is flagged on the pay run

Garnishment and child support requirements can vary. Review each order carefully to make sure the information entered in Mercury is accurate.

Changing someone’s pay schedule

Someone’s “Pay” tab shows their current pay schedule and next payday.

Select Manage pay, then Manage pay schedule to move them to another schedule. See Understanding pay schedules for more information.

When you move someone to a new pay schedule, their pay, recurring earnings, deductions, and benefits move with them.

For salaried team members, their salary is divided across the new schedule’s pay periods. Because pay accrues daily, no days go unpaid and a separate catch-up run isn’t needed. If the change takes effect in the middle of a pay period, that period’s salary is split between the old and new schedules.

Viewing their details and documents

The “Details” tab shows someone’s personal and work information, along with their payroll permissions.

Payroll documents, including I-9 and tax withholding forms, are at the bottom of the “Pay” tab and can be downloaded from there.

Managing someone’s email addresses

The “Details” tab shows two emails for each team member:

  • Work email — managed by your company and used for payroll
  • Personal email — an address they control, so they keep access to their pay stubs and tax documents after they leave your company

Team members can update their own personal email from their profile. Only admins can change a work email.

To make a change:

  • On the “Details” tab, select Edit next to Work email or Personal email
  • Enter the new address, then select Save

Keep in mind:

  • We send a verification email to the new address and notify the team member at their login email that a change was requested. The team member needs to be logged in to Mercury and open the link to confirm it. Until they do, the current email stays in place. If the new address is already verified on their Mercury profile, the change takes effect right away.
  • Verification links expire after 30 days. While a change is pending, you can Resend verification email or Delete it, and only one change per email can be pending at a time.
  • An email already used by another Mercury profile can’t be added, and changing a work or personal email doesn’t change the email they log in with.

Removing someone from payroll

Removing someone from payroll sets their last day and creates their final payroll. After they leave, they’ll retain access to their pay records. You can also remove their access to your Mercury business banking* account as part of the same process.

You can edit or cancel a removal until their final payroll is submitted.

This article covers how to remove someone from payroll, what happens to their pay and access, how to reverse a removal, and how to rehire someone.

Remove a teammate

To remove a teammate from payroll:

  • From your Payroll home page, scroll to the “Team” section. You can filter by status to show active teammates only
  • Find the teammate and select Options next to their name
  • Select Remove team member to start offboarding
    • Remove all business banking access is selected by default. Uncheck it if they should keep their Mercury banking* access, then select Continue
  • Enter their last day and select whether they’re leaving voluntarily or involuntarily
  • Choose when they should receive their offboarding notification
  • Confirm their personal email and, optionally, add an internal reason for the removal. The teammate won’t see this reason
  • Select Review removal
  • Review the details, then select Remove team member

What happens to their access

The teammate’s access changes on their last day, not when you schedule their removal.

After their last day, they’ll retain read-only access to:

  • Paystubs
  • Tax documents
  • Personal details

They’ll lose access to everything else in Payroll.

Their profile and removal details will remain available to your company, including if you rehire them later.

Access to year-end tax documents

After leaving, teammates can still access their tax documents and paystubs. Their offboarding email explains how to access them.

Their W-2 or 1099 for their final year will be issued the following January using their selected delivery method. To request a paper copy, they must contact Mercury support by December 31 of that tax year.

Admins can also access the teammate’s tax documents through Documents and share a copy if needed.

What happens to their pay

Removing a teammate creates a final payroll, which runs separately from your regular payroll schedule.

Their final payroll may include:

  • Wages they’ve earned but haven’t been paid
  • Bonuses, commissions, and other earned compensation
  • Unused time off, if your PTO policy provides for a payout
  • Pending reimbursements for you to review
  • Applicable benefits deductions, garnishments, and taxes
If there’s enough time to process their final pay

Their final paycheck will arrive on their last day, and the final payroll will submit automatically.

If their last day is approaching

Final-pay deadlines vary by state and may depend on whether the teammate is leaving voluntarily or involuntarily. If the teammate’s last day doesn’t leave enough time for Mercury to process their payment by the applicable deadline, you’ll see a notification before completing the removal.

You’ll be able to choose how to handle their final payment:

  • Direct deposit: Mercury processes the payment through Payroll for the earliest available payday
  • Pay them directly: You pay their net wages by cash, check, or electronic transfer while Payroll calculates, withholds, and remits applicable taxes and deductions

You’ll also be able to review the final payroll before it’s submitted.

Mercury doesn’t provide legal advice. You’re responsible for complying with applicable final-pay requirements. Consult your employment counsel if you’re unsure which requirements apply.

Keep in mind
  • You can resend the offboarding email after it’s been sent
  • If a previous pay run includes days after the teammate’s last day, Mercury will notify you during removal. You may need to recover an overpayment outside of Mercury

Benefits and Mercury banking* access

Benefits

For team members actively enrolled in benefits, coverage ends at the end of the month in which their last day occurs.

Mercury banking* access

Removing someone from Payroll doesn’t automatically remove their Mercury banking* access. During the removal flow, you can select Remove all banking access to schedule both for their last day.

Existing Mercury banking* access rules still apply:

  • Only admins can remove other admins
  • Beneficial owners can’t be removed from Mercury banking*, but they can be removed from Payroll
  • If your organization requires dual-admin approval, removing banking* access requires approval from another admin. Payroll removal doesn’t require a second approver
  • Their cards are canceled, removed or transferred

If you cancel the payroll removal before the final payroll is submitted, the pending banking removal is also canceled.

Rehire someone you’ve removed

Rehiring someone adds a new employment period to their existing profile rather than creating a new record. Their pay history, paystubs, and tax documents remain together, and their profile shows their original hire date and latest rehire date.

To rehire someone:

  • Open their profile
  • Select Manage
  • Select Rehire

If they were never on Payroll, you’ll see Reactivate instead. Both options open the teammate setup flow with information Mercury already has pre-filled.

When rehiring someone:

  • Their earliest start date is the day after their previous last day
  • Their previous pay and pay schedule are provided as a starting point and can be changed
  • Their worker type can change between team member and contractor
  • They’ll complete onboarding again using their existing login and review their pre-filled information
  • Any final pay from their previous employment period will continue processing

Some information doesn’t carry over:

  • One-time pay items, such as signing bonuses or backpay
  • A fixed-term end date from their previous employment period
  • Previous admin roles
  • Their previous card(s)

If their Mercury banking* access was removed, rehiring them restores their access, but you’ll need to issue a new card.

If you try to add a teammate whose legal name matches someone you’ve previously removed, Mercury will prompt you to rehire them instead to help prevent duplicate records.

Tip: If someone is rehired within the same calendar year, their pay will be included on the same W-2 or 1099. If they’re rehired in a later calendar year, their new employment period will be reflected in that year’s tax documents.

What team members see during payroll onboarding

When you add a team member to Payroll, they complete the rest of their setup themselves, including entering their Social Security number, bank details, and tax withholdings.

This article covers what they’ll be asked during setup, what they can view and change afterward, and where they can find their documents.

Before they start

New team members on Payroll receive an email at the personal email address you entered, with a link to create their account and begin onboarding.

Their progress is saved as they go. If they stop partway through, they can use the same link to pick up where they left off.

What they’re asked depends on whether you added them as a W-2 employee or a contractor.

What they’ll do during onboarding

1. Sign their offer letter

If you attached an offer letter, they’ll review it, enter their full legal name, and type their name to sign electronically.

If you also attached a confidentiality and invention assignment agreement, they can list any prior inventions or agreements before signing it the same way.

Both signed documents are saved to their record.

2. Create their account

They’ll review or enter:

  • Name
  • Preferred name
  • Personal email
  • Date of birth
  • Password

Most of this information is pre-filled based on what you entered when adding them, and they can correct it if needed.

3. Enter their personal details

They’ll enter:

  • Phone number
  • Residential address
  • SSN or ITIN

Employees are also asked for their sex assigned at birth, which is required for tax filings, and an emergency contact.

4. Add Form I-9 details

If you elected to have Mercury handle I-9 verification, this step will allow them to fill out their Form I-9 details, upload verification documents, and elect a verifier to verify their documents.

5. Add a bank account
  • Mercury Personal: They can link an existing Mercury Personal account or sign up for one with their $240/year subscription covered while they’re on an active payroll account. If signing up, they’ll connect another bank account to receive paychecks until their Mercury Personal account is ready. They’ll receive an email to complete their application, and deposits will switch once their account is open
  • Another bank account: They can connect an account instantly through Plaid or manually enter their routing and account numbers
6. Complete their tax withholdings

They’ll first answer a few questions about their citizenship or visa status. Their answers determine whether they’re exempt from Social Security and Medicare taxes.

They’ll then complete the forms required for their worker type:

  • Employees: A federal W-4 and any applicable state withholding form. State forms are based on their work address, or home address if they work remotely. If they live in a state without income tax, they’ll only complete the W-4
  • Domestic contractors: W-9 details, including their legal or business name, entity type, and tax ID

Everything is completed using form fields in Mercury. There’s nothing to download, print, or upload.

Submitting a form signs it, so there’s no separate signature step.

7. Benefits

If you elected to offer benefits through Mercury, this step will allow them to choose their medical, vision, and dental insurance.

8. Complete security and spend setup

They’ll complete the standard Mercury setup for new team members, including two-factor authentication and card setup if you’ve given them a card.

When they’re done

Once onboarding is complete, they’ll see a summary of what happens next, including their first day of work and first scheduled payday.

No further action is required on your end at this time.

Check their onboarding status

Until a team member finishes onboarding, they’ll appear as Onboarding incomplete in your Team list. Their profile will also show a banner indicating that they haven’t completed payroll onboarding.

From their profile, you can:

  • Send reminder
  • Cancel their onboarding

If they haven’t accepted their offer yet, they’ll appear as Pending offer instead. You can resend, edit, or rescind their offer.

It’s worth checking their status before their first payday, particularly if you’re adding yourself to Payroll.

What team members can view and change

Once they’re set up, team members can view their pay and tax details from the My Payroll page.

They can view:

  • Compensation — their pay rate, the date it took effect, and any recurring earnings or deductions
  • Direct deposit — the bank account their pay is sent to
  • Work details — their employment type, job title, manager, work location, and start date
  • Federal and state tax — their withholding details and the form each comes from
  • Documents — their pay statements, tax documents, and employment documents
What they can change

Team members can update:

  • Direct deposit by selecting Edit on their direct deposit details. They should make changes well before payday. If a pay run has already started processing, that payment will still go to their previous account
  • Tax withholding by selecting Edit on their federal or state tax details and re-signing the updated form

Team members can view their compensation and work details, but can’t change them. You can manage those details instead — see Managing someone’s payroll details.

Contractors can’t update their tax details themselves after onboarding. Ask them to contact our support team instead.

Where team members can find their documents

Team members can find and download their documents at the bottom of My Payroll.

Documents are organized into three groups:

  • Pay statements — a pay stub for each time they’ve been paid
  • Taxes — tax forms including their W-4, state withholding form, and year-end W-2 or 1099
  • Employment — their I-9 and offer letter

Who can manage payroll details

You can view a team member’s payroll details and documents from the Team page. Anyone else with permission to manage Payroll or team members can also view this information.

Some information can only be changed by the team member:

  • Team members can change their own direct deposit and tax withholding
  • Team members can view their compensation and work details, but can’t edit them themselves
