Cancel scheduled or pending payments in Mercury Personal

You can easily cancel scheduled payments or payments pending approval from your Payments page.

Canceling a payment you just sent

ACH and domestic wire payments are processed almost immediately and thus unable to be canceled after the fact.

If you sent a payment by check, you can cancel it on your end as long as it hasn’t been deposited yet. Simply head to your Transactions page, open the payment that needs canceling and click the cancel icon.

Canceled checks can take 0-3 business days to reflect in your account. You can review the status of the cancelation on your Transactions page. Note: Checks may still be printed and mailed to the recipient even if they are already cancelled. They will not be deposited successfully.

Canceling a scheduled payment

  • As an admin, go to Payments from the left sidebar menu on your dashboard.
  • Under Payments, click on the Scheduled tab.
  • Select the payment you want to cancel and click on the trash icon.
    • If you need to skip a single payment in a recurring payment, you’ll need to cancel the entire series and recreate it.
  • You’ll be able to review details of the scheduled payment and confirm you want to cancel.

Canceling a payment pending approval

  • Go to your Payments page.
  • Click on the Needs approval tab.
  • If you’re an approver, click the payment you want to cancel and click Decline.
  • If you created the payment, click the payment and click Cancel Request.

Canceling an international wire you just sent

You can cancel an international wire sent from your personal account wizthin 30 minutes of creating it—either from the confirmation screen or your Transactions page. After that, the wire is final and can’t be canceled. Learn more about cancelations and disputes here.

Canceling payments on mobile

For scheduled payments:

  • Click the middle ⇄ icon on the bottom menu navigation bar (Payments)
  • Under “Scheduled Payments”, select the payment you want to cancel and you’ll be able to review details of the scheduled payments
  • Click Cancel Payment to confirm you want to cancel

For payments pending approval:

  • Click the first 🏠 icon on the bottom menu navigation bar (Homepage)
  • Under “Tasks”, select the payment you want to cancel and you’ll be able to review details of the payment request
  • If you’re an approver, click the payment you want to cancel and click Decline
  • If you created the payment, click the payment and click Cancel Request

Categorizing transactions on Mercury Personal

Transaction categories let you label your spending and income so it’s easier to track trends, review your finances, and stay organized. This article explains how to manage your categories and apply them to transactions.

Managing your categories

Mercury Personal includes a default list of categories you can use as-is or customize to fit your needs. You can add new categories, edit existing ones, or delete any you don’t need from your Mercury dashboard on web.

To access your categories:

  • Click your name in the top-left corner of your dashboard
  • Select Settings
  • Choose Categories from the left-hand sidebar

From here, click Create category to add a new one, or use the pencil and trash icons to edit or delete existing ones.

  • Edited category names will update across all previously categorized transactions
  • Deleted categories won’t be available for future transactions, but will remain assigned to historical transactions

Categorizing transactions

You can categorize transactions from two places: inline on the Transactions page or by clicking into a transaction and opening the detail panel.

From the transactions table
  • Navigate to the Transactions page
  • Click the dropdown on the transaction you want to categorize
  • Select a category from the list
    • If you don’t see a category available, create a new one by clicking Add category from the dropdown
Automated categorization (Beta)

Mercury automatically suggests categories for your transactions using AI. If you notice a category applied to a transaction that you didn’t set, automated categorization added it to help you organize and track spend.

You can override suggestions at any time using the category dropdown. The system learns from your selections and improves over time.

FAQs

Can I apply more than one category to a transaction?

Each transaction can have one category applied at a time.

Will editing a category name change it on past transactions?

Yes. When you edit a category name, it updates across all transactions that were previously labeled with that category.

What happens to transactions if I delete a category?

Deleted categories are removed from your category list and won’t be available for new transactions. However, they will remain visible on any transactions they were previously applied to.

Connect cards from other banks and analyze your spending with Command

You can connect credit cards from other banks to Mercury Personal, see their balances, limits, and transactions in one place, and ask Command, your Mercury agent, questions about your spending across your connected cards.

This article covers how to:

  • Connect cards from other banks. See each card’s balance, limit, and recent transactions under Linked Accounts.
  • Ask Command about your spending. Get a visual answer based on your actual transactions, such as your top merchants or how this month compares with last month.
  • Start from a suggested prompt. Command shows prompts you can tap once you’re ready to ask.

Note: This feature is available for Mercury Personal.

Connect a credit card

You can connect a card from Command or from Linked Accounts.

  • Open Command (>_) and choose the suggestion to connect an account, or ask: “Help me add a credit card from another bank.” You can also select Link account from your Accounts page.
  • Search for your bank and sign in through the secure connection window. Mercury uses Plaid to connect your accounts.
  • Select the card you want to connect.
  • Wait for your transactions to load. They may take a few minutes to appear after you add a card.

Once the card is connected, it appears under Linked Accounts and Command can answer questions about it.

View your linked cards and transactions

Linked checking, savings, and credit card accounts appear together under Linked Accounts. Expand a card to see:

  • Balance and limit: your current balance and your credit limit.
  • Last updated: the date your balance and transactions were last pulled from your bank.
  • Transactions: merchant, date, amount, and whether each one is pending or posted.

Ask Command about your spending

Open Command and ask a question in your own words, or tap a suggested prompt. Command answers with a short takeaway and a chart, plus supporting transactions where they help. Here are some questions to start with:

Ask

What you get

“What are my top five merchants across my linked credit cards? Show the transactions behind it.”

A ranked chart of merchants and up to five representative transactions

“Am I spending more than usual this month? Compare to the same point last month and tell me what changed.”

Weekly lines for this month and last month, with a takeaway on the difference

“Which of my linked credit cards am I using the most over the last 30 days?”

A bar chart comparing spending by card

“Did I pay off more than I spent on my linked credit cards over the last 60 days?”

Weekly purchases as money out and payments or refunds as money in

Command answers questions about your spending. It doesn’t give financial advice.

Joint accounts and team access

Linked accounts belong to your Mercury organization, not to the person who connected them.

  • For joint Mercury Personal accounts, both owners and full admins see the same list of linked accounts and transactions, including accounts the other owner connected.
  • Linked accounts can show Linked by with the name of the person who connected them. Older connections may not show a name.
  • Team members with restricted access only see the accounts they’re authorized to access.
  • Command follows the same access. It can answer questions about any linked account you can see.

Manage your linked accounts

  • Reconnect: if a connection goes stale, Mercury prompts you to sign in to your bank again to refresh it.
  • Rename: give a linked account a name that’s easy to recognize.
  • Unlink: remove a linked account you no longer want in Mercury.
Good to know
  • Transactions can take a few minutes to appear after you add a card.
  • Command is not a financial advisor. It answers questions about your spending and doesn’t give financial advice.
  • AI-generated responses may vary and aren’t guaranteed. Review outputs before you take action.
  • Category breakdowns are estimates. Command infers broad categories, such as travel, shopping, and dining, from merchant names.
  • Command looks at spending. It uses the transactions from the cards you’ve connected and the data your bank shares.

Connecting Mercury to ChatGPT, Claude, and other AI tools (Personal: Manage Money)

Connect Mercury to ChatGPT, Claude, or another AI tool that supports Model Context Protocol (MCP) to view account information and take actions like transferring money between accounts, paying existing recipients, and categorizing transactions.

You can request these actions through your AI tool, then review and approve transfers and payments in Mercury before money moves.

This article explains how to connect Mercury, approve requests, and manage connected AI agents.

Connect Mercury to an AI tool

To connect Mercury, add it to your AI tool and authorize access to your account. The steps may vary by tool.

  • Log in to your AI tool
  • Find Mercury using one of these options:
    • ChatGPT: Connect Mercury to ChatGPT
    • Claude: Connect Mercury to Claude
    • Other AI tools: Search for Mercury in the tool’s app or connector directory or connect manually.
  • Add Mercury from your AI tool
  • Enter your Mercury email and password, then select Next
  • Complete login verification and select Continue
  • On the Review permissions page, confirm which Mercury organization you’re connecting and review the requested permissions
  • Select Authorize to complete the connection

Once connected, try asking your AI tool, “What’s my Mercury account balance?” to confirm you’re accessing the intended account.

If you’ve connected Mercury to an AI tool before, you may need to disconnect and reconnect to enable certain actions.

Approve transfers and payments

You can request transfers between your Mercury accounts and payments to existing recipients through your AI tool. You’ll need to approve these requests in Mercury before money moves.

  • Ask your AI tool to initiate a transfer or payment
  • Review the details in the chat, including the recipient, amount, account, and payment method
  • Select Approve on Mercury to send the request to Mercury, or Cancel to stop
  • Open the verification notification in the Mercury app on web or mobile. The approval will also appear in your Tasks page
  • Review the transfer or payment details in Mercury
  • Approve or decline the request

Note: Selecting Confirm Request in your AI tool doesn’t authorize the payment. You must approve the request in Mercury before it can be initiated.

Approval requests expire after approximately 5 minutes. If yours expires, start a new request through your AI tool.

You can also categorize transactions and update supported transaction metadata through your AI tool. These changes don’t require additional approval in Mercury and take effect immediately.

Manage connected AI agents in Agent Controls

Admins can use Agent Controls to see which AI tools their team has connected to Mercury, review their permissions and recent activity, and disconnect connections.

To find Agent Controls:

  • Go to Settings
  • Under “Security & Controls,” select Agent Controls

For more information, see Managing AI agents connected to Mercury.

FAQs

What information can my AI tool access?

When you connect Mercury to an AI tool, you authorize it to access certain account information, which may include accounts, cards, transactions, categories, statements, and users.

You can review the requested permissions on the Review permissions page before selecting Authorize.

Information accessed through the connection may be processed by the AI tool’s provider according to its terms and privacy policy. We recommend reviewing the provider’s privacy settings before connecting.

Can I switch between Mercury organizations in my AI tool?

You can’t switch between Mercury organizations within an active AI tool connection.

If you have access to multiple Mercury organizations, your AI tool will only show information from the organization you authorized when connecting.

To access a different organization:

  • Disconnect Mercury from your AI tool
  • Reconnect Mercury using the steps above
  • Select and authorize the organization you want to access

Note: You can currently connect only one type of Mercury account: either personal or business, but not both.

Can my AI tool add a new recipient?

No. You can only request payments to recipients you’ve already added in Mercury. To pay someone new, add them as a recipient in Mercury first.

How do I disconnect Mercury from an AI tool?

You can disconnect Mercury at any time through the Agent Controls page in Settings. Find your connected agent, go to the agent detail page, and click Disconnect.

What other tools are supported?

Mercury MCP is available as an official integration with the following tools:

  • ChatGPT
  • Claude
  • Cursor
  • Perplexity
  • Gemini Enterprise
  • Microsoft 365 Copilot
  • Grok Bot
  • Notion
  • Replit

To connect, select a link above or search for Mercury in your tool’s connectors, plugins, or integrations directory. Then follow the prompts to connect your account.

For Claude Code, Codex CLI, or other MCP clients, see our API documentation for setup instructions.

Why was my AI tool disconnected from Mercury?

If an admin changes your role, or changes the permissions of a role you have, Mercury disconnects the AI tools you’ve connected. This happens even if your access increases, so an AI tool never has more access than you do. You’ll get an email listing the tools that were disconnected. To keep using a tool, reconnect it using the steps above and authorize it again. It will get access that matches your current role.

Why can’t I connect Mercury to my AI tool?

To connect Mercury to AI tools, you need the Use Mercury via MCP permission. If you don’t have it, request your admin to assign you to a different role.

Deposit checks to your Mercury Personal account

You can deposit checks electronically from your dashboard or the Mercury mobile app.

Mercury can’t accept checks mailed to us or our banking partners, or any electronic or non-standard checks (including eChecks, credit card checks, courtesy checks, or temporary/starter checks). Any checks sent by mail will be destroyed or returned to the sender.

Before you get started

Make sure the check is issued by a U.S bank and made out to the account holder on file.

Before you upload photos, make sure to add your signature to the back of the check in pen and include “For mobile deposit only” underneath.

Depositing from your dashboard

In the upper right corner of your dashboard, click Move Money > Deposit and select Check Deposit as the method. Follow the prompts to upload check photos and submit your deposit.

If you’re running into a deposit limit, you can request an increase by following the steps outlined here.

Depositing from the Mercury mobile app

Tap the double arrow icon in the bottom panel of your iOS or Android app and select Deposit. Follow the prompts to upload photos and submit your deposit.

Taking photos of your checks

Successful deposits rely on check images that are clear and legible. Here are our requirements:

  • Upload clear photos: Ensure both the front and back of your check images are clear, with all account information legible. Photos must be of the actual check, not a photo of a check image from a computer screen or another secondary source.
  • Background matters: Take the photos on a solid, dark, and non-reflective background. Avoid wood or busy backgrounds, as they can lead to poor image quality.
  • Flat surfaces only: In addition to solid backgrounds, ensure the check is completely flat. Do not take photos with the check in your hands or on your lap.
  • Lighting and focus: Capture the photos in a well-lit area, ensuring no shadows are cast on the check. Use a clean camera lens and avoid zooming in to maintain clarity.
  • Remove pay stubs: If your check has a pay stub or letter attached, remove them before taking photos.

When to expect funds

Checks are manually reviewed and once approved can take up to 5 business days to post. You may notice that funds have settled on the 6th business day if the check was submitted after our 12pm Pacific cutoff time.

Please keep the check for at least a week to make sure it clears without issue.

Disputing & canceling international wires sent from your personal account

You can dispute or cancel international wires sent from your Personal Mercury account but only within specific timeframes. This article explains how to cancel a wire shortly after sending, how to dispute a wire due to an error, and what to expect from a wire recall.

This guidance only applies to wires sent from personal accounts. Wires sent from business accounts are not eligible for cancellation or dispute.

Canceling an international wire

You can cancel an international wire sent from your personal account within 30 minutes of creating it. After that, the wire will be sent to the beneficiary and cannot be canceled.

To cancel a wire:

  • From the payment confirmation screen, click Cancel payment if you see a Made a mistake? prompt or go to your Transactions page, find the wire, and click into the transaction to open the details
  • Select Cancel payment
  • Confirm the cancellation

If the cancellation is successful, the wire will not be sent and the funds will return to your available balance.

Disputing an international wire

You can dispute a wire within 180 days of delivery if a processing error occurred.

Disputes are only valid if the issue was caused by Mercury or a provider. Errors made by the sender such as incorrect recipient details or accidentally sending the wrong amount are not eligible for dispute and need to be recalled and resolved with the beneficiary.

Valid reasons for dispute:
  • Incorrect amount paid – You were charged or sent more/less than authorized
  • Funds not delivered – The recipient didn’t receive the full amount
  • Late delivery – Funds arrived after the promised date
  • Wrong recipient account – The wire was sent to the wrong recipient due to provider error
  • Unauthorized transaction – You didn’t authorize the payment
  • Missing or inaccurate disclosures – Disclosures about fees or FX rates were missing or incorrect
  • Incorrect exchange rate or fees applied – Fees or exchange rates didn’t match what was disclosed
To submit a dispute:

Email personalwires@mercury.com from the email address associated with your personal account. Please include:

  • A brief description of the issue
  • Beneficiary name
  • Amount
  • Date of the transaction

Requesting a wire recall

If a wire was sent in error and is no longer cancelable, our Support team can help you request a recall. However, wire recalls are not guaranteed, and the beneficiary’s bank may reject the request. For recalls, please reach out to personal@mercury.com.

Note: Wires are considered final after the 30-minute cancellation window passes. Mercury cannot guarantee successful recovery once a wire is sent.

Generate and send a payment link from Mercury Personal

Payment links are an easy, informal way to collect money from your contacts. You can generate a quick link and share it with a contact when you just need a simple, lightweight way to get paid.

Creating a new payment link

  • Open the Move Money menu in the upper right corner of your dashboard, then Request Money
  • Select a contact you’ve previously sent to or input details of a new one
  • Input the amount, add an optional note, or attachment, and select which account you want to receive the payment. Once complete click Create & Send
  • A shareable link will be automatically generated and sent to your contact

What your contact sees

Your recipient will be given a standalone link with the payment amount, deadline, and other info you included when creating the payment link.

  • If they also have a Mercury account, they’ll be able to select an account to pay from and submit payment immediately
  • If they don’t have a Mercury account, they’ll be provided with ACH/Wire and International Wire details to submit payment

The account and routing numbers displayed are not your actual account and routing numbers. When you create a payment link, it also creates a unique “routing” account with its own account and routing numbers so your actual account information remains hidden. The funds route through this account automatically and ultimately land in the account you selected when creating the link.

Managing payment links

Go to your Payments page, then select payment links to view all of your active and canceled payment links.

Click any of these line items to open up the link details. From there, you can re-copy the payment link, send a reminder, cancel the link, or mark the payment link as paid.

High-yield savings with Mercury Personal

Every Mercury Personal account includes access to high-yield savings earning a competitive 3.50% Annual Percentage Yield (APY*) with no minimum balance required.

Once your application is approved, you can open a savings account and begin earning interest.

Below are the basics of how high-yield savings works at Mercury.

What is a high-yield savings account?

A high-yield savings account (HYSA) works like a regular savings account, with one difference: it pays a higher interest rate.

Your money stays flexible. You can deposit and withdraw whenever you need to, while it earns more than it would in a traditional savings account.

At Mercury, a personal high-yield savings account includes:

  • A 3.50% APY, with no minimum balance to open or to earn
  • FDIC insurance up to $5M per depositor**, per insured bank

How you earn interest

Interest is calculated on your daily balance and paid to your account at the start of each month.

There is no minimum balance requirement and no deposit limit, so any funds in your savings account earn interest automatically.

The rate is variable, so the APY may change over time as market rates move.

Interest rate vs. APY

A savings account often lists two rates: the interest rate and the APY.

  • Interest rate is the base percentage your balance earns.
  • APY (annual percentage yield) is the total you earn in a year once compounding is included. Compounding means the interest you earn is added to your balance and then earns interest of its own.

APY is always slightly higher than the interest rate, and it is the more accurate measure of what your savings will earn.

For example, a $10,000 balance at 3.50% APY earns about $350 over a year.

Opening a savings account

Every Mercury Personal customer can earn high-yield savings once their application is approved.

You can even open more than one savings account to organize your money by goal, such as an emergency fund or an upcoming trip.

To learn more, see Managing checking and savings accounts.

*Annual Percentage Yield (APY) is accurate as of 09/21/2026. This is a variable rate account. The interest rate and annual percentage yield may change at any time and without prior notice. Fees may reduce earnings.

How percentage-based auto transfer rules are calculated (Personal: Manage Money)

Percentage-based auto-transfer rules let you distribute money automatically between accounts based on 1) a percentage of an account balance or 2) a percentage of an incoming transaction.

On May 8, 2026, Mercury is updating how percentage-based rules are calculated to make their behavior more consistent and predictable.

This article explains what’s changing, who is affected, and how to update your rules if needed.

Changes to percentage-based rules

Before May 8, each percentage rule calculated against the balance remaining after the previous rule ran. This meant multiple high-percentage rules could all execute — but each one would transfer a smaller amount than the last.

Starting May 8, every percentage rule calculates against your account’s starting available balance at the beginning of the day or the total amount of the incoming transaction.

What did not change: Rules still run in order. If there isn’t enough balance to fulfill a rule after earlier rules have run, that rule will fail.

Example: How the calculation changes

Say you have three rules on the same account, each set to transfer 50% of your balance. Your starting balance is $1,000.

BEFORE May 8 (legacy calculation):

Rule 1: 50% of $1,000 = $500 transferred | $500 remaining

Rule 2: 50% of $500 = $250 transferred | $250 remaining

Rule 3: 50% of $250 = $125 transferred | $125 remaining

Result: All three rules execute.

AFTER May 8 (new calculation):

Rule 1: 50% of $1,000 = $500 transferred | $500 remaining

Rule 2: 50% of $1,000 = $500 transferred | $0 remaining

Rule 3: 50% of $1,000 = $500 attempted — $0 available, rule fails

Result: Rules 1 and 2 execute. Rule 3 fails.

For incoming transaction rules, the same math applies. In the above example, an account with multiple incoming transaction rules on the same account would see the same result after an incoming transaction of $1,000.

Who is affected

You will only be affected if you have multiple, separate percentage-based rules on the same checking or savings account that run on the same day. The amount transferred may change, and if the combined percentages exceed 100% on any 1 account, some rules will fail. Example:

You are not affected by this change if you have one percentage-based rule on a checking or savings account, even if that rule distributes funds to multiple accounts. These rules are not impacted by this change. Example:

Options for updating your rules

Option 1: Reduce percentages so they total 100% or less to prevent rule failure

Option 2: Replicate the old cascading behavior manually

If you relied on the waterfall calculation, you can recreate it by adjusting each rule’s percentage relative to the starting balance.

Example — replicating three 50% rules on a $1,000 balance:

Rule 1: 50% (receives $500)

Rule 2: 25% (receives $250 — equivalent to 50% of the $500 that was left)

Rule 3: 12.5% (receives $125 — equivalent to 50% of the $250 that was left)

Option 3: Switch to fixed-amount rules

If your goal is to move a specific dollar amount each day regardless of your balance, fixed-amount rules aren’t affected by this change and may be a simpler fit.

How to edit your auto-transfer rules
  • On web, click Accounts on the left-hand menu and select the Auto-transfer rules tab
  • Click the three dots menu > Edit rule on the rule you want to change
  • Update the percentage, review the rule summary, and save

FAQs

Will my rules automatically update on May 8?

Yes. Your existing rules will be modified. If you take no action, rules that can’t be fulfilled due to insufficient balance will fail after May 8.

What happens when a rule fails?

No money is transferred for that rule. You’ll see it reflected in your transaction history. Your other rules won’t be affected.

Do I need to update all of my rules?

Only rules where multiple percentage rules on the same account are in place.

What if I have one percentage rule and one fixed-amount rule on the same account?

Fixed-amount rules are unaffected by this change. Only percentage-based rules are recalculated.

What if my rules run on different days?

If your percentage rules are scheduled on different days and never run on the same day, they won’t compete for the same balance. You likely won’t see any change.

Linking external bank accounts (Personal: Manage Money)

We use Plaid to link U.S bank accounts to your Mercury account for easier transfers and money management.

Here’s how to link an external account:

  • Click the blue Move Money button in the upper right corner, then select Transfer.
  • Click on the Transfer From dropdown, then scroll to the bottom and click Link a Bank Account.
  • Using the Plaid pop-up, find your bank and enter your credentials when prompted. If your bank is not selectable from the Plaid dropdown, we’re currently unable to support a connection (including a manual connection via micro-deposit). The good news is, you can still transfer funds between bank accounts via ACH and the Move Money flow.
  • You’ll be prompted to select the type of external bank account that you’re linking (either Business or Personal). You’ll need to provide this information before you can make a transfer.
    • The account type (business or personal) determines how the ACH transaction is sent between your linked accounts. This is called the SEC file type: WEB files for personal accounts or CCD files for business accounts.
    • If you have an existing linked account, updating the account type may change how your transactions are sent. If your receiving bank flags the transaction for your review, you can let them know this was an expected change.

Once the account is linked, you can view account details and certain transaction history, manage the connection, and initiate new transfers by going to the Linked Accounts tab on your Accounts page.

If you receive an error when trying to log in, double-check that you’re using the correct login, password, and login method. It can also be helpful to log in to your bank directly and make sure there are no error messages or items you need to action before connecting.

At this time, we can only support linking U.S accounts. For transfers outside the U.S, we recommend initiating an international wire.

Managing checking and savings accounts

You can open additional checking and savings accounts in Mercury to organize your finances—for example, by merchant, expense type, or savings goals. These accounts can be nicknamed, paired with virtual debit cards (checking only) or set up with auto-transfer rules to manage balances.

Below are steps to open and remove accounts right from your dashboard.

Creating a new checking or savings account

If you’re an admin on the account, you can create a new checking or savings account right from your main dashboard on web. Here’s how:

  • From your Accounts table, click on the + to add a new account
  • Select either Checking or Savings
  • (Optional) Add a nickname for your account and click Create
  • The new account should appear in your list after a few moments, and you can click into it to copy your new account number

Removing an account

Before you can remove a checking or savings account, make sure its balance is $0. Then:

  • On web, click Accounts in the left sidebar of your dashboard to open the Accounts page
  • Select the account you’d like to remove
  • Select the Manage dropdown in the top right (only visible once the account has been zeroed out)
  • Click Close account
  • Confirm you’d like to close the account

Once removed, the account will be permanently deleted and can no longer transact, but you can still see previous statements.

To close your Mercury Personal account entirely, you’ll need to reach out to a specialized team (personal@mercury.com).

Tips for managing your accounts

Your Accounts page is customizable. From here you can:

  • Customize the order in which your accounts appear by reordering them based on personal preference. Simply drag and drop the order. The new order will appear on your Accounts overview page, on the main dashboard, mobile apps and account dropdowns

Receiving real-time payments (RTP) (Personal: Manage Money)

Real-time payments (RTP) allow you to receive money in seconds 24/7, including weekends and holidays. This article explains how real-time payments work on Mercury, who can send you these payments, and how to make sure you’re set up to receive them.

Receiving RTPs is currently only available to Mercury customers with accounts that are provided through our partner bank Column, N.A. For questions about access, reach out to personal@mercury.com.

Overview of real-time payments

RTP can occur via two payment networks operated by The Clearing House and the Federal Reserve that let participating banks and providers send funds instantly within the U.S. If someone sends you a payment via RTP, it can show up in your Mercury account in just a few seconds (though some may take up to 30 minutes, depending on the sender). Once completed, RTP transactions settle immediately and are generally irrevocable.

Eligibility and supported senders

The ability to receive RTP transfers depends on the sending institution’s participation in the applicable payment network. Receipt of RTP funds may be delayed or unavailable due to network interruptions, transaction limitations, risk or fraud screening, or other circumstances outside of Mercury’s control. RTP availability is not guaranteed for all transactions.

Currently, receiving RTPs is only available for Mercury accounts on our partner bank, Column N.A. You can receive real-time payments from participating providers, including:

  • Banks that support the ability to send RTP (many major banks do)
  • Payment processors like PayPal and Venmo

Your sender’s bank or provider must support one of the RTP networks in order to be eligible to send RTP to your account. While Mercury does not charge you for receiving RTP, your sender’s bank/provider may charge fees for sending real-time payments — unfortunately, these are set by them and we can’t control or refund those charges.

How to receive RTP payments

As long as your Mercury account is on Column N.A., you don’t need to enable anything in your account in order to receive RTP. If a sender is eligible to send real-time payments and uses your Mercury domestic transfer details, the funds should arrive instantly.

To receive a real-time payment:

  • Log in to your Mercury account on web or mobile
  • Locate your wire/payment details
    • RTP uses the same transfer details as ACH and domestic wires
  • Share your account details with trusted senders and/or your payment processor

Most processors will automatically detect that your account can accept RTP. If they request verification, you can confirm that your account is with Column N.A., which supports RTP.

Common processor setup guides

If you’re using RTP with a payment platform, check our setup tips here:

  • PayPal - When initiating a transfer, select the “in minutes” option
  • Venmo - When initiating a transfer, select “Instant” as the transfer method

Note: We recommend reviewing any eligibility and setup instructions directly from the provider’s website, as details may change.

FAQs

What if the sender’s payment doesn’t process as an RTP?

If RTP isn’t available or fails, most providers will automatically send the payment as an ACH or wire transfer instead.

Why is the amount sometimes lower than expected?

Many providers deduct a processing fee (typically 1–2%) in order to send RTP as payments or payouts. Check with the sender or platform for fee details.

How can I recognize instant payout scams?

Be cautious if you’re asked to verify your account or share wire details unexpectedly. If you didn’t initiate a payout or don’t recognize a sender, don’t respond or provide sensitive account information.

How is RTP different from services like Zelle or Venmo?

Services like Zelle aren’t actually sending payments between banks, so they aren’t using the RTP network. They are performing what is called a book transfer, where funds are exchanged between banks and credit unions within their ecosystem, which allows money movement to be instant. On the other hand, the RTP network actually moves money between banks in real time.

For more information, see section 10.7 in the Column N.A. account agreement. To confirm whether your account is eligible to receive RTP payments, please contact personal@mercury.com.

Setting up auto transfer rules on Mercury Personal

Auto-transfer rules help you move money between accounts automatically so you can manage cash flow, fund specific accounts, or streamline distribution of deposits without manual effort. You can create rules from scratch or use templates to get started faster.

How to find and manage rules

  • On the left-hand side of your dashboard, select Accounts
  • Click the Auto transfer rules tab
  • From here, you can:
    • Create new rules
    • View active rules
    • Edit or remove existing rules

You can set up auto-transfer rules between Mercury accounts, and also from Mercury to a Plaid-linked external account. Only admins can create, edit, or remove rules. Custom role users will need to ask an admin for help.

Creating a new rule

Choose from four suggested rule types designed around common goals, like distributing funds or maintaining a specific account balance. These give you a structured framework with fill-in-the-blank settings, so you don’t have to start from scratch.

Alternatively, click + Custom Rule to create an auto-transfer rule from scratch.

Using templates

Choose from four suggested rule types for common goals — structured starting points you can customize.

1 - Distribute funds across accounts

Split funds across multiple accounts on a schedule.

  • Choose to transfer by set amount or percentage
  • Decide if the rule runs on incoming funds or on a schedule
  • Add your destination accounts

Great for: profit-first accounting, setting aside funds for taxes, or automating budgeting

2 - Invest extra funds

Move excess funds from a checking account into savings or your Invest account.

  • Set a target max balance
  • Transfer any amount above that to your Invest account
  • Customize the frequency to twice a month on days that work for you
3 - Schedule recurring transfers

Send a set amount to a destination on a regular basis.

  • Choose your source and destination
  • Set the transfer amount
  • Pick a frequency

Helpful for: vendor payments and routine funding.

4 - Maintain a target account balance

Move funds into or out of an account to stay within set limits.

  • Select a minimum, maximum, or both
  • Choose a supporting account
  • Set a frequency

Ideal for: payroll accounts, keeping operational balances steady.

Custom rule options

Build rules from scratch with full flexibility — best if you have a specific setup in mind.

Maintain a target account balance

Automatically keep a selected account within a minimum, maximum, or target balance range.

  • Choose the target account to monitor
  • Set the desired behavior:
    • Keep the balance above a minimum: Funds will be added from another account whenever the balance falls below the set minimum.
    • Keep the balance below a maximum: Funds above the maximum will be moved into another account.
    • Keep the balance within a range: Funds will be added or removed whenever the balance falls outside the specified range.
  • Choose the supporting account to add funds from or move excess funds into
  • Set your frequency. Rules can run daily, weekly, monthly, or on specific days
Transfer funds to one or more accounts

​​Automatically move money to other accounts. Commonly used for budgeting or the profit first method.

  • Choose whether to move:
    • A set amount
    • A percentage of account balance
    • A percentage of incoming funds
  • Select the source/starting account
  • Input the amount or percentage that should be transferred
  • Add one or more destination accounts
  • Choose your frequency/how often you want the rule to run

Transfer settlement timing

  • Transfers between checking/savings happen instantly when triggered
  • Transfers to Plaid-linked external accounts settle in 1-3 business days, depending on the destination bank.
  • Transfers to/from Invest settle in 1-3 business days
  • Auto transfers from Invest are limited to two transfers per month and the selected dates must be at least 7 calendar days apart

FAQs

Can I set up multiple rules per account?

Yes. If you’re setting up multiple percentage-based rules on one account, ensure that the combined percentage to be transferred does not exceed 100%, or else some rules will fail. Learn more about how percentage-based auto-transfer rules are calculated.

When do auto-transfer rules run?

Rules on a schedule (daily, weekly, monthly, etc.) run at 15:00 UTC (6:00 AM PT). Rules between accounts at the same partner bank can run every day, including weekends. All other scheduled rules run on business days; if the date falls on a weekend or holiday, they run on the preceding business day.

Rules based on incoming funds run in real time whenever funds are deposited into the rule account.

You can view when a transfer is next scheduled to run from your Auto Transfers page.

Can I set up auto-transfer rules with linked external accounts?

Can I set up auto-transfer rules with linked external accounts?

Yes. You can use an external account linked via Plaid as a destination for certain auto-transfer rules:

  • Distribute funds across accounts: Funds can be sent from Mercury to a linked external account
  • Maintain a target account balance: A linked external account can be used as the supporting account when funds are being sent out of Mercury

Auto-transfers to linked external accounts are sent via ACH and typically take 1–3 business days to arrive. Auto-transfers with linked external accounts are push-only, so funds can’t be pulled from an external account into Mercury.

What happens if my account doesn’t have enough money for a scheduled transfer?

If there aren’t enough funds to run a scheduled rule, we will simply skip it. You’ll receive an email notification, and the rule will continue running as usual for future auto transfers.

When creating a rule, how many accounts can I distribute funds to?

You can distribute funds into up to 20 accounts within a single rule.

What if I need to fund an account that has a “distribute incoming funds” rule?

Because internal transfers also count as incoming funds, sending money into an account with an active distribution rule will trigger that rule.

You have two options:

  • Temporarily remove the rule: Delete the distribution rule, make the internal transfer, then recreate the same rule.
  • Leave some funds behind: Set your distribution rule to less than 100% so the account keeps a small balance from each deposit. You can then manually transfer any excess funds as needed.

Understanding your Insights page on Mercury Personal

Insights is a page within your Mercury account that shows real-time, customizable financial metrics, helping you understand and act on your finances. You can access Insights from the sidebar menu of your Mercury account on web.

Insights page overview

On the Insights page, you’ll find:

  • Overview tab: a quick snapshot of your financial health, including your net cash flow and top spending categories.
  • Money in / Money out: tabs that break down inflows and outflows, so you can see which paychecks, subscriptions, or spending categories are growing or shrinking over time

You can quickly review Money in and Money out data by Merchant/Recipient and Category:

Customizing your Insights data

Excluding data from Insights

You can exclude certain transactions or transaction types from Insights so they don’t skew your day-to-day cash flow data. To get started, click the vertical dots (⋮) at the top of the Insights page to open the Settings module where you can search transactions to exclude:

Insights FAQs

How is my cash flow calculated?

We look at your income and spending over the last few months. By default, we use the last 3 full months of activity, but you can adjust this using the timeframe selector in the top right corner.

  • Money in: all deposits received during that time, excluding internal transfers.
  • Money out: all withdrawals and expenses during that time, excluding internal transfers.
How are my transactions categorized?

Mercury runs each transaction through our categorization engine (currently in beta) and assigns a category when it’s confident enough. If anything looks off or uncategorized, open the transaction and update it from the dropdown. Your corrections help the engine improve over time. Learn more about categorization here.

Why am I not seeing certain data?

Some metrics may not appear if your selected time range doesn’t include recent enough activity. For the most accurate view, make sure your timeframe extends through today or the end of the most recent month.

Account inactivity, restrictions, and closures (Personal: Mercury Account)

If you received an email from Mercury about inactivity, your account has gone an extended period without qualifying activity. This article explains what counts as activity, what happens if your account remains inactive, and how to restore access if your account is restricted.

What counts as qualifying activity

Any one of the following counts as qualifying activity:

  • Add funds to your account via ACH, wire, or check deposit
  • Log in to Mercury at mercury.com or through the mobile app. For help logging in, visit our Security section
  • Initiate or receive an incoming or outgoing transaction
  • Contact Mercury Support

You only need to complete one of these activities at least once every 12 months to keep your account active.

If you no longer need your Mercury account, you can close it at any time by following the steps in Closing your Mercury account.

What happens if your account stays inactive

Your account is considered inactive after 12 consecutive months or more without qualifying activity.

Mercury regularly reviews accounts for qualifying activity to comply with state unclaimed property laws and banking partner requirements. This process applies to all Mercury accounts.

Taking any qualifying action reactivates your account. You don’t need to contact us to confirm—we’ll see the activity and update your account automatically.

What happens next depends on whether your account has a balance.

If your account has a $0 balance

An inactive account with a $0 balance will be closed if there’s no qualifying activity by the closure date in your email.

Before closure, we’ll email you with the subject “Your Mercury account will be closed due to inactivity” and include the date your account is scheduled to close.

Taking any qualifying action before that date keeps your account open.

If there’s no qualifying activity before the closure date, we’ll close the account and email you to confirm. Closed accounts can’t be reopened, but you can apply for a new account at mercury.com, subject to approval.

If your account holds a balance

An account with a balance remains fully functional when it first becomes inactive, and you may not receive a notification since no restrictions have been placed. If the inactivity continues, the account may later be restricted. At that time, we will notify you.

When your account becomes inactive

No restrictions have been applied at this point. Taking any qualifying action will reactivate your account.

When your account becomes restricted

If your account reaches 22 consecutive months without qualifying activity, we’ll restrict it and email you with the subject “Action Required: Your Mercury account is restricted due to inactivity.”

The email will include the date the restriction was applied and your current balance.

While your account is restricted:

  • Your funds remain secure
  • Your account data and history remain intact
  • You can’t send or receive payments, or initiate transfers

To restore access, log in to Mercury and complete any required account and identity verification as possible. We’ll review your information and contact you if we need anything else.

If you don’t want to complete verification, you’ll also have the option to close your account when you log in. You don’t need to complete verification to receive your remaining funds.

Unclaimed property and escheatment

If an account with a balance remains inactive long enough to pass the applicable State dormancy period, State unclaimed property laws may require Mercury to transfer the remaining balance to the State. This process is called escheatment.

State dormancy periods are typically three to five years from the last qualifying activity, depending on the State associated with your account.

Before your funds are transferred

Before your funds are remitted to the State, you will receive a letter with the date they’re scheduled to be transferred. The letter will be sent to the legal address on file.

Until that transfer occurs, you may still be able to reclaim your funds from Mercury by logging in and completing the required verification.

After your funds are transferred

Once the funds have been transferred, your Mercury account is closed and the funds are held by the State.

Your funds aren’t lost, but you’ll need to claim them from the State:

  • Visit the unclaimed property website for the State named in the notice we sent you
  • Search for unclaimed property under your legal name or business name (if you have a Mercury business account)
  • Follow the state’s instructions to file a claim

Claims typically take 30–90 days once filed, though timelines and documentation requirements vary by state.

If your account has a non-US address

The state that receives escheated funds generally depends on the address associated with the account.

For accounts without a US address, Mercury will remit the funds to Delaware, where Mercury is incorporated. If your funds have already been transferred, you can file a claim with Delaware’s unclaimed property office.

Add or remove a Payable on Death (POD) beneficiary

Mercury Personal supports adding up to five individuals or one trust as a payable on death (POD) beneficiary on your account. In the event that all account holders pass away, your checking and savings account balances will be evenly split among the POD beneficiaries you designate. This arrangement allows for a seamless transition of the account’s deposits without going through the probate process.

How do I add a beneficiary?

You can add up to five individuals or one trust as a payable on death (POD) beneficiary to your Mercury Personal account. To do so:

  • Navigate to your main menu in the top left corner of your dashboard and click Settings and then Account Settings
  • Scroll down to the beneficiaries section
  • Click Add a Beneficiary
  • Input your beneficiary’s information and click Add Beneficiary

When naming an individual as a beneficiary, you’ll need their full name, date of birth, home address, and optionally their social security number (for identity verification purposes only). If you add more than one beneficiary, your checking & savings account balances will be evenly split among all of your beneficiaries.

When naming a trust as a beneficiary, you’ll need the trust’s Legal Name and Tax Identification Number.

How do I remove a beneficiary?

You can remove a payable on death (POD) beneficiary from your Mercury Personal account at any time. To do so:

  • Navigate to your main menu in the top left corner of your dashboard and click Settings and then Account Settings
  • Scroll down to the Beneficiaries section
  • Under the list of beneficiaries on your account, click Edit. You’ll see a list of beneficiaries on your account. Click Edit next to the name of the beneficiary you’d like to remove.

At the bottom of the beneficiary information form, click Remove Beneficiary

What’s the difference between a POD beneficiary and a trust account?

A payable on death (POD) beneficiary designation allows funds in your Mercury Personal account to pass directly to your named beneficiaries after death.

A trust account, on the other hand, is owned and managed by a trust during your lifetime and operated by trustees.

These are different ownership structures and may have different tax, probate, and FDIC insurance implications.

Learn more about Trust Accounts at Mercury.

Convert your Mercury Personal account to a joint account

You can apply to convert your individual Mercury Personal account into a joint account by inviting additional account holders.

If you have an active Invest account, converting to a joint account isn’t supported. We recommend opening a new joint account instead.

Here’s how to get started:

  • Click Settings in the top-left menu
  • Under the Account type section, click Convert to joint account
  • Invite the person(s) you’d like to add as joint account holders and click Send Invite

What happens next?

  • Each invited joint account holder must submit an application for approval.
  • While their applications are being reviewed, invitees will have access to your individual account, but you will remain the sole owner until all applications are approved.
    • You can view the status of their applications and account conversion from your Settings page.
  • If and when all of the invitees’ applications are approved, your individual Mercury Personal account will be converted to a joint account, and you and the new co-owners will have equal ownership of the account.

If an application is denied:

  • If any of the invitees’ applications are denied, the conversion will be canceled, and your account will remain as an individual account.

For more details, check out how joint accounts work.

Linking and switching Mercury accounts (Personal: Mercury Account)

If you have more than one Mercury account (or are on more than one team that uses Mercury), there are a few ways you can link accounts to easily switch between them without needing to log out and log in again.

Link more than one account to your profile

When you create or are invited to your first Mercury account, you create a profile that includes an email address, password, and some basic info like your name and 2FA preferences.

You’re able to link multiple Mercury accounts to a single profile so that you can seamlessly switch between different accounts without needing to log out and log in again. Linked accounts are only visible to you and can’t be seen by admins or anyone else using the Mercury account, so you can confidently link a side hustle or personal account as needed.

Applying for a new Mercury account using an existing profile

  • Click on your account name in the top left-hand corner of your dashboard.
  • You’ll see the option to Open new account.
  • You’ll be able to start a new application that uses the same basic profile info. If the application is approved, your new account will be automatically linked to the profile you used when applying.

Joining another team’s Mercury account with an existing profile

Ask your contact or the admin who’s inviting you to add you to their Mercury account using your existing profile email. You’ll receive an email invite and the Mercury account will automatically be linked to your profile once you accept.

Linking an existing profile to share linked accounts

Until recently, you needed to create a new profile (and thus use a separate email) for every Mercury account you created or were invited to. You can now link your existing profiles to effectively link any associated accounts as well and switch seamlessly between them.

Here’s how to do it:

  • While logged in to one of the Mercury accounts you want to link, open your org menu in the top left corner of your dashboard.
  • Select Link existing account.
  • You’ll be prompted to log in with the profile associated with the other account.
    • If that profile is already linked to others, you’ll be able to review a list of all the Mercury accounts you’ll be to switch between before you proceed.
  • Enter your 2FA verification code, then click Log In & Link.
  • If successful, you’ll be switched to your other Mercury account.

Editing an existing email to link profiles

To edit an existing email to one that’s already in use, you’ll want to follow the steps of inviting yourself as a team member as opposed to editing your own email.

  • If you’re an admin, follow the steps listed here to invite yourself to the account under your preferred email
  • If you’re a non-admin, you’ll need to ask an admin on file to invite your preferred email

Once your preferred email has been added, the old profile can be removed from your Team page. Please note that any cards tied to the removed email will be automatically deleted so you’ll need to set those back up under the new profile.

Managing linked accounts and profiles

Go to your Profile settings. From here, you can view and un-link other Mercury profiles you’re linked to, and also view which Mercury accounts are directly linked to your current profile.

Managing AI agents connected to Mercury (Personal: Mercury Account)

Agent Controls lets you view and manage the AI tools your team has connected to Mercury. You can see who connected each agent, review its permissions and activity, and disconnect agents when needed.

Who can use Agent Controls

Admins can access Agent Controls in Mercury on the web, including from a mobile browser. Agent Controls isn’t currently available in the Mercury mobile app.

What counts as an AI agent

An AI agent is a tool connected to Mercury through Mercury MCP, such as ChatGPT, Claude, or Cursor, or through the Mercury CLI.

Each time someone authorizes a tool, Mercury creates a separate connection. This means the same tool may appear more than once in Agent Controls.

API tokens and other integrations, such as accounting software, don’t appear in Agent Controls.

Finding Agent Controls

  • Go to Settings
  • Under “Security & Controls,” select Agent Controls

The “Agent Controls” page has three tabs: Agents, Activity, and Explore.

If no one on your team has connected an agent, the page opens on the Explore tab.

Viewing your team’s connected agents

The Agents tab shows a summary of your team’s agent connections, including:

  • Authorized connections: Total number of authorized agent connections
  • Users with agents: Number of team members who have connected agents
  • 3rd party tools: Number of third-party tools connected
  • All activity: Agent activity across your team

Below the summary, the “Connected agents” table lists each connection and its details:

  • Owner: The team member who connected the agent. Currently, only admins and custom roles with the permission to use Mercury via MCP can connect AI tools.
  • Agent: The AI tool and when it was last used or connected
  • Permissions: What the agent can view or do in Mercury

Agents can have two permission levels:

  • Read only: View information such as accounts, balances, transactions, and receipts
  • Read & write: View information, update transaction notes and categories, and prepare payments for approval

Note: Agents with Read & write access can’t move money on their own. Payments and transfers they prepare must be approved in Mercury before money moves, and your existing approval rules still apply.

Viewing an agent’s details and permissions

Select an agent from the “Connected agents” table to view its details, including:

  • Created by: The team member who connected the agent
  • Created on: When the connection was created
  • Last used: When the agent last accessed Mercury
  • Permissions: What the agent can view or do
  • Recent activity: Actions the agent has taken

The permissions table compares what the agent’s owner can do with what the agent can do, including:

  • Viewing accounts and balances
  • Downloading statements
  • Viewing transactions and receipts
  • Viewing recipients
  • Editing memos and attaching receipts
  • Categorizing transactions
  • Drafting payments for approval

An agent’s access is limited by its owner’s permissions. To reduce an agent’s access, you can change the owner’s role.

Changing the owner’s role also changes what they can do in Mercury and disconnects all of their agents.

Disconnecting an agent

To disconnect an agent from Mercury:

  • Open the Agents tab
  • Select the agent from the “Connected agents” table
  • Select Disconnect
  • Select Revoke to confirm

The agent loses access to Mercury immediately.

In some cases, disconnecting an agent also removes the owner’s other connections to the same tool. If this applies, you’ll see a message before confirming.

Disconnecting an agent doesn’t prevent its owner from connecting the tool again later. To prevent this, turn off Use Mercury via MCP in their role’s permissions (this also disconnects agents for everyone with that role), or assign them another role without the Use Mercury via MCP permission.

Reviewing agent activity

The Activity tab shows actions your team’s connected agents have taken in Mercury.

To review all activity across your account, select View all activities to open the Activity Log.

For more information, see Reviewing activity in your Mercury account.

Connecting a new AI tool

The Explore tab shows AI tools that work with Mercury MCP, along with how many people on your team have connected each tool.

Supported tools include ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor, Perplexity, Gemini Enterprise, Grok Bot, Microsoft 365 Copilot, Notion, Replit, Claude Code, Codex CLI, and other MCP clients.

To connect a tool:

  • Open the Explore tab
  • Select the tool you want to connect
  • Select Connect and follow the setup instructions

For more information, see Connecting Mercury to ChatGPT, Claude, and other AI tools.

FAQs

Why did an agent disappear from Agent Controls?

An agent is removed from Agent Controls when:

  • Someone disconnects it
  • Its owner’s role changes
  • The permissions associated with its owner’s role change
  • Its owner is removed from your team

The owner can reconnect the tool if they still have access to Mercury.

Can team members who aren’t admins use Agent Controls?

No. Only admins can access Agent Controls. Other team members can disconnect their AI tools through the tools’ own settings.

Does connecting an agent change anyone’s permissions?

No. An agent operates within its owner’s existing permissions and can’t do more than its owner can.

Managing emails (Personal: Mercury Account)

You can add more than one email to your Mercury profile and log in with any of them.

This article explains how to add and remove emails, which email is used for logging in, security, and notifications, what admins can see, and how emails work when you belong to more than one account. You can manage your emails on the web or in the Mercury app for iOS and Android.

Email types at a glance

Email type

What it’s used for

How many

Log in emails

Log in to Mercury and reach all your accounts

Every verified email on your profile is a log in email.

Security email

2-Factor Authentication (2FA) reset codes, password resets, account recovery, security notices, and replies from our support team

Exactly one per profile. It’s the same in every account.

Notification email

Notifications for one accounts

One per account. By default, it’s the email you were invited with.

One email can have more than one type. For example, the same email can be your security email and the notification email for your business.

Logging in

You can log in with any verified email on your profile. Your password and passkey are the same no matter which email you use.

After you log in, you’ll land in the account you used last. To go to a different one, select the account switcher in the upper left corner.

Adding and verifying an email

On the web

  • Go to Settings, then select Profile
  • Under Emails, select Edit emails
  • Select Add email and enter the email
  • Select Save

In the Mercury app

  • Go to Settings and select your profile
  • Select Edit
  • Under Login emails, select Add email, enter the email, and confirm
  • Save your changes: select Done on iOS or Save on Android

You can add up to 5 emails at a time. You may be asked to confirm it’s you before your changes are saved.

Next, check the inbox for each new email. Open the verification email from Mercury and select the link.

Until you verify an email, it shows Needs verification. You can’t log in with it, or choose it as your security or notification email, until it’s verified.

Note: Verification links expire after 30 days. To get a new one, find the email in your list of emails, open its options, and select Resend verification email.

You can’t add an email that:

  • Is already on your profile or on another Mercury profile
  • Has a pending invite to one of your accounts
  • Is used for receipt forwarding. See Receipt forwarding below
Removing an email
  • Open your list of emails:
    • On the web: go to Settings › Profile and select Edit emails
    • In the app: go to Settings, select your profile, then select Edit
  • Select the email, then select Delete login email. For an email you haven’t verified yet, select Delete
  • Confirm, then save your changes

You can remove any of your emails, with some exceptions:

  • Your security email. Choose a different security email first, then remove the old one. That also means you can’t remove your only email.
  • A notification email. You can remove it, but we’ll warn you first: that account’s notifications will go to your security email instead, and its admins will be able to see your security email.
Security email

Your security email is where we send anything related to keeping your profile safe: 2-Factor Authentication (2FA) reset codes, password resets, account recovery, and security notices.

Note: Replies from our support team also go to your security email. You can write to us from any verified email, but if you write from a different one, you’ll get an automatic reply letting you know where we’ll respond.

Your security email is also the backup for your notification emails. If you remove an account’s notification email, that account’s notifications go to your security email.

Changing your security email
  • If the email you want isn’t on your profile yet, add and verify it first
  • Go to Settings, then select Security
  • Select Security email. On the web, select Edit
  • Choose one of your verified emails, then save

You’ll always have exactly one security email. It stays the same no matter which account you’re working in. Your previous security email stays on your profile as a log in email; remove it if you don’t need it anymore.

Admins can’t see or change your security email. The only exception: if an account falls back to your security email for notifications (see Removing an email), that account’s admins can see it.

Notification emails

You have a notification email for each account you belong to. It’s where we send the notifications you’ve turned on for that account. Because it’s set per account, you can send each one somewhere different, like your work email for the company you work at and your personal email for a side business.

By default, it’s the email you were invited to that account with. You can change it to any verified email on your profile.

Admins of that account can see it. They can’t see your other emails. An admin chooses this email when they invite you, but after that only you can change it.

Changing a notification email
  • Switch to the account you want to change the notification email for
  • Go to Settings, then select Notifications
  • Select Notification email. On the web, select Edit email
  • Choose one of your verified emails, then save

Changing it only affects the account you’re in. Your other accounts keep their own notification emails.

Receipt forwarding (business accounts only)

Receipt forwarding emails and log in emails are separate:

  • Adding an email for receipt forwarding doesn’t let you log in with it.
  • You can’t add an email as a log in email while it’s being used for receipt forwarding. To use it for logging in, remove it from receipt forwarding first.

Read more about receipt forwarding here.

What admins can see and do

Admins can see only your notification email for that account. They can’t see your security email or your other log in emails. The exception is when you remove your notification email: your security email becomes the fallback, and that account’s admins can see it.

Admins choose your email when they invite you. After that, they can’t change it.

If you belong to more than one account

Your emails belong to you, not to an account, so they work across every account you’re part of.

Switching accounts: Log in with any verified email and you’ll land in the account you used last. To switch, select the account switcher in the upper left corner, then select the account you want.

Joining another account: If you’re invited with an email that’s already on your profile, log in and accept the invite. The account is added to your existing profile, and you don’t need a new password. If you’re invited at with an email that isn’t on any Mercury profile yet, you can log in first and add it to your existing profile when you accept, or create a new profile with it.

If you’d like to keep your emails separate but easily switch between Mercury accounts see our Linking and switching Mercury accounts article.

Managing your joint account

How can I add a joint account holder?

You can add additional account holders to your existing individual account by following the instructions in this article.

How can I remove a joint account holder?

  • Ask the joint account holder to reach out to personal@mercury.com to request their own removal.
  • In case of death of a joint account holder, any joint account holder can reach out to personal@mercury.com to request their removal.

The options above are the only way that an account holder may be removed. Other than in the case of death, a joint account holder may not request that a fellow joint account holder be removed from the account.

Can I convert a joint account to an individual account?

No, at this time we don’t support conversion from a joint account, to an individual one.

This means that if a joint account has two joint account holders, and one account holder removes themself, the remaining account holder will have to close the joint account and open a new individual account to continue using Mercury Personal. But if a joint account has more than two joint account holders, and only one joint account holder removes themself, you can continue using the joint account when one of the account holders is removed, as long as the account has two or more joint account holders after the removal.

How can I close my joint account?

Any joint account holder can reach out to personal@mercury.com to close a joint account. You’ll need to withdraw all funds before closing your account.

Mercury Personal Subscription

Each Mercury Personal subscription includes one individual account, one joint account, and one trust account.

When you invite someone to your joint account, they will become a co-owner of the joint account only. Should they also want another account, they can open one separately for the annual subscription fee of $240.

FAQs

I have an individual account on Mercury Personal and paid a subscription fee already. Will I get charged another $240/year for opening a joint account?

No, your $240/year subscription to Mercury Personal includes access to one individual and one joint account.

I received an invitation to join a joint account on Mercury from someone with a Mercury Personal account. Am I going to be charged $240/year?

No. If one of the joint account holders has an active Mercury Personal subscription on their individual account, the joint account will not incur an annual fee, as it is included in that individual account subscription.

If neither of the joint account holders has an active Mercury Personal subscription on their individual accounts or doesn’t have an individual account open at all, the subscription will be charged to the joint account.

Does my Mercury Personal subscription include a trust account?

Yes. Each Mercury Personal subscription includes one trust account in addition to one individual account and one joint account. Trust accounts are available for eligible revocable living trusts and require trust-specific onboarding and approval. You can learn more here.

I opened a joint account on Mercury, and I don’t have an individual account. Will I get charged an annual subscription if I open an individual account?

The first account holder to open an individual account will have their subscription waived, as it will be included in the joint account subscription.

For example, say you open a joint account with your spouse, and neither of you have individual accounts: if your spouse opens an individual account in addition to the joint account, your spouse won’t be charged $240. If you open an individual account after your spouse opens an account, you will be charged $240. After that, joint account holders who open individual accounts will each be charged $240/year.

The same applies to trust accounts. If you already have an active Mercury Personal subscription through an individual, joint, or trust account, opening another included account type will not result in an additional annual subscription fee.

Open and manage a Mercury Personal joint account

Joint bank accounts are accounts shared by two or more account holders. All account holders are named on the account and have full control over the account and the funds in it. This includes the ability for joint account holders to receive payments and deposit checks in their own name.

Please note: all account holders will also have the ability to withdraw account funds and/or close the joint account at any time, and we only support accounts where all joint owners have equal access to the funds.

You may have up to four account holders on a Mercury Personal joint account at this time.

How do I open a joint account?

Follow the steps outlined here. You can also convert your existing individual account to a joint one by following the steps outlined here.

How does a joint account subscription work?

Each Mercury Personal subscription includes one individual and one joint account. When you invite someone to your joint account, they will become a co-owner of the joint account only. Should they also want another account, they can open one separately for the annual subscription fee of $240. More information on how Mercury Personal subscription works can be found here

Can I deposit a check in one of the joint account holder’s names?

Under the joint account, you can deposit checks in either joint account holders’ names or all of the names present.

How does FDIC insurance work for joint accounts?

Mercury checking and savings deposits are FDIC-insured up to $5 million* through our partner bank and use of sweep networks. You can learn more about FDIC insurance here.

Since FDIC insurance is given to each account holder, a joint account with two joint account holders would be eligible for up to $5 million* in FDIC insurance, each (for a total of up to $10 million).

How much FDIC Insurance do I have if I have an individual and a joint account on Mercury?

FDIC Insurance applies to each account holder for each account ownership category. Therefore, as an individual and joint account holder, you would be eligible for up to $5 million* in FDIC insurance for your individual account and $5 million* in FDIC insurance for your joint account(s), for a total of up to $10 million for a single account owner.

How is my money FDIC insured?

Deposits at banks are eligible for $250K in FDIC insurance. To make your funds eligible for up to $5 million* in FDIC insurance per account type (joint and individual), your funds are automatically allocated across our partner banks’ sweep networks. Learn more here.

Can I add a trust as a joint account holder?

No, we only allow individuals to be joint account holders.

Can I issue a check in my name?

You can only send a check with names of all joint account holders present on the check.

Reviewing activity in your Mercury account (Personal: Mercury Account)

The Activity Log shows a timeline of actions taken in your Mercury account, whether by your team, Mercury, or AI agents working on your team’s behalf.

Who can use the Activity Log

The Activity Log is available in Mercury on the web, including from a mobile browser.

Admins can view activity across the organization. Other team members can view their own activity.

Finding the Activity Log

  • Go to Settings
  • Under “Security & Controls,” select Activity Log

Viewing activity

The Activity Log groups activity by time, such as Today, Yesterday, and This week. Each entry shows what happened and when.

If an AI agent performed an action, the entry identifies the agent, such as via Mercury CLI, via Mercury Command, or the name of the connected AI tool.

Select an entry to view more details, including:

  • Actor: Who performed the action
  • When: When the action occurred
  • Agent: Which AI agent performed the action, if applicable
  • IP address: The IP address associated with the action
  • Device: The device associated with the action

New activity may take some time to appear. The timeline shows when it last synced.

Filtering activity

Select All filters to narrow the activity shown in the timeline.

You can filter by:

  • Keyword: Matches whole words in activity titles
  • Category: Accounts, Budgets, Cards, Recipients, Invoices, Payments, Team, Roles, Company settings, Security, API tokens, and Command
  • Actor (admins only): A specific team member, or No actor for actions without an associated team member
  • Platform: Command, MCP, CLI, Web, iOS, Android, or Public API
  • Agent: Activity from specific agent connections
  • Date: All dates, a recent month, or a Custom range

Admins can also switch between Org-Wide and Personal views.

Viewing routine login activity

Routine sign-ins, session refreshes, and account switches are hidden by default.

Turn on Routine Logins to include these events in the timeline. New-device, two-factor authentication, and password events always appear.

Exporting activity

To export activity as a CSV file:

  • Apply any filters you want
  • Select Export or Export filtered
  • Select Export CSV
  • When the file is ready, select Download CSV

Exports include all events matching your filters, including events that haven’t loaded in the timeline.

Download links expire. If your link has expired, select Refresh download link to generate a new one.

Note: If too many events match your filters, narrow the date range or adjust your filters and try again. You can’t combine the Agent and Actor filters in an export yet.

FAQs

How can I tell what an AI agent did in my account?

Filter by Agent or by Platform (MCP or CLI). Activity entries associated with an agent show its name.

Admins can also review each agent’s recent activity in Agent Controls.

Why don’t I see something that just happened?

The Activity Log syncs regularly, so new activity may take some time to appear. Check the last sync time shown in the timeline.
