Scheduling payments (Personal: Send Money)

If you make similar payments on a regular basis, you can set up a recurring payment to handle them automatically.

Here’s how:

  • Click the Move Money menu in the upper right corner of your dashboard and select Send.
  • Either upload a bill you’d like to pay upfront, or directly select/create/select a recipient.
  • In the “Recipients” section, select your payment method (ACH, check or wire) from the dropdown.
  • In the “Amount” step, set your amount and payment account. If you toggle “Repeat this payment,” you can set up a recurring payment that will automatically process on a schedule of your choosing.
    • You’ll be able to choose a payment frequency and when you’d like the payments to end. You can also manually cancel the payments at any time if you choose Never as the end date.
  • Once enabled, these will begin processing at 9am EST on the specified date.

Payments scheduled on the weekend or a holiday will begin processing on the nearest business day before the scheduled date.

Note: If you schedule a wire in a non-USD currency, the funds will be converted when the wire is processed. The exchange rate at that time will determine the final USD amount debited.

Managing your recurring payments

You can view and edit upcoming scheduled and recurring payments from your Payments page. Click on the “Scheduled” tab and locate the payment that needs editing. Select the pencil/edit icon to make any necessary changes to the date, amount, or similar. If you need to delete the payment entirely, you can do so by clicking the trash icon.

How to send a mailed check

Sending international payments in non-USD

When sending an international wire, you can choose to convert USD to one of 40+ non-USD currencies for a 1% exchange fee.

On available business days, funds are exchanged at the current mid market rate. On weekends and holidays, we provide you with the stored/cached rate from the previous business day.

So if you create the payment on a Saturday, you will see the rate from Friday. This is a secured rate and will be the rate used when the payment is processed on the following business day.

Frequently asked questions

Why are weekend rates cached?

Financial markets are not typically open on weekends and holidays. To ensure a smooth experience, we use the last available rate before markets close so that you can make your transfer knowing the specific rate that will be used the following business day.

Are there any wire limits?

There are upper limits based on currency pairs, as well as some that may be tied to your account. If you run into an upper limit that you would like to change or learn more about, please reach out to our team at personal@mercury.com.

How do I monitor for a specific exchange rate?

At this time, we are unable to alert you on specific rates as we get live rates when you go through the wire flow.

Please be sure to select the appropriate currency for your recipient’s bank details, in order to see the currency rate.

Can I create a recurring payment with currency exchange?

Yes, you can schedule a recurring payment as normal, but recurring payments will be processed at the exchange rate on the date the payment is actually processed. In other words, we can’t guarantee a set rate.

How do returns work?

To prevent returns, we encourage users to confirm payment details before making a payment.

If your payment is returned by the receiver’s bank, the funds will be redeposited to your Mercury account for the USD equivalent of the return. It will appear as a new transaction and be labeled “wire return.”

Can I receive non-USD and convert it to another currency?

Currently, only Mercury customers that are on our partner banks, Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Member FDIC, can accept international wires in non-USD currencies. In both cases, the funds are automatically converted to USD before they hit your account. Column N.A. converts incoming funds to USD at the mid-market rate. Choice uses intermediary banks for currency conversion, which means the rates can vary.

What is the cutoff time for non-USD payments?

There isn’t a daily cutoff for payments. They are processed throughout the day.

Will holidays affect my ability to use currency exchange?

You should be able to retrieve a quote and create new transfers any time day or night. On weekends and holidays, you’ll receive a cached exchange rate from the previous business day. If you want a live rate, you will need to wait until the next business day.

If the receiving bank has a local bank holiday, this may also impact the delivery estimate of the payment.

I’m getting an error when trying to make a conversion. Why?

You may be getting an error due to invalid bank details. Please confirm that the currency quote you’re trying to pull matches the receiver’s bank currency. You will receive an error if you try to pull a CAD quote if the receiver’s bank account is based in Germany.

If you’ve received a rate drift error, this means there was a change in the exchange rate between the time the payment was created and when it reached our payment provider for processing. If the exchange rate shifts by more than 1% from the originally quoted value, the payment will automatically fail to prevent unintended discrepancies. We recommend trying the payment again. We’ve seen higher success rates for wires initiated during business hours (9 am–5 pm ET) on weekdays.

Sending money on Mercury Personal

You can send payments from your Mercury account using the Send Money flow in your dashboard — this is where you’ll start most outgoing payments from Mercury, including ACH transfers, domestic wires, international wires, real-time payments, and mailed checks.

The only exception is physical checkbooks, which are ordered and managed separately.

When you send money, you can add or select a recipient, choose an available payment method, enter the amount and timing, then review and submit your payment.

Domestic payment methods

ACH payments

ACH payments are electronic transfers between U.S. bank accounts. They’re commonly used for standard domestic payments, like paying vendors, contractors, employees, or external accounts.

ACH payments are free to send on Mercury. If submitted before the ACH cutoff and eligible for same-day processing, funds typically post the same business day. Otherwise, ACH payments are processed the next business day.

Domestic wires

Domestic wires allow you to send money in USD to a recipient at a U.S. bank. They’re typically used for larger or time-sensitive domestic payments.

Domestic wires are free to send on Mercury. If submitted before the domestic wire cutoff and eligible for same-day processing, funds typically post the same business day. Otherwise, domestic wires are processed the next business day.

Real-time payments

Real-time payments (RTP) allow you to send payments that arrive within seconds.

Real-Time Payments are free to send on Mercury and work 24/7, including weekends and holidays. Availability depends on your Mercury account, the recipient’s bank, and the payment details. If your account is eligible, you’ll see Real-Time Payment as an available option in the Send Money flow.

Real-time payments are only available to Mercury accounts provided through our partner, Column N.A.

Mailed checks

Mailed checks let you send a paper check to a U.S.-based recipient without writing or mailing it yourself. Mercury prints and mails the check on your behalf.

Mailed checks are free to send on Mercury. They’re typically printed within 1 business day, then sent via USPS. Checks can take up to 10 business days to arrive.

International payment methods

International wires in USD

USD international wires let you send U.S. dollars to recipients outside the U.S. This can be useful if your recipient wants to receive USD or has provided USD wire instructions.

USD international wires are free to send on Mercury. They’re typically processed and sent by Mercury within 1–3 business days from when they’re requested. In general, international wires can take up to 5 business days to reach your recipient if all information is correct.

International wires in non-USD (FX)

Non-USD international wires allow you to send money to recipients outside of the United States in 40+ local currencies.

Non-USD international wires include a 1% currency exchange fee on the USD amount to account for the conversion handled as part of the payment flow. You’ll be able to review the exchange rate, applicable fees, and final amount before submitting the payment.

Non-USD international wires are typically processed and sent by Mercury within 1–3 business days. Arrival timing can vary based on the destination country, currency, recipient bank, intermediary banks, and any routine payment review.

Sending a payment

To send a payment:

  • In your Mercury dashboard on web, go to Move Money > Send
    • On mobile, tap the middle ⇄ icon on the of your bottom menu bar, then tap Send
  • You can either start by adding a new recipient/selecting an existing one or uploading a bill to pay directly
  • Choose an available payment method
  • Enter and confirm the amount, funding account, and send date
  • Review the payment details
  • Submit the payment
A note on timing and errors

Processing times can vary based on cutoff times, weekends, holidays, payment review, recipient bank processing, intermediary banks, and whether all payment details are complete and accurate.

For international wires, Mercury may process and send the payment before the recipient receives it. Intermediary or recipient banks may take additional time to deliver the funds.

If you’re encountering errors with a failed/returned payment, we recommend locating the payment on your Transactions page and looking for a failure reason.

For more information, see section 10.7 in the Column N.A. account agreement. To confirm whether your account is eligible to receive RTP payments, please contact personal@mercury.com.

Sending real‑time payments (Personal: Send Money)

Send money instantly — and know it arrived. Real-time payments (RTPs) are electronic transfers that complete in seconds, 24/7/365, giving you more certainty and cash flow clarity, while helping you avoid follow-ups and late fees. Real-time payments are only available to Mercury accounts provided through our partner, Column N.A. This article explains how sending RTPs works on Mercury.

What is a real-time payment (RTP)?

In the U.S., real-time payments (RTPs) move funds over networks operated by The Clearing House (the RTP® network) and the Federal Reserve (the FedNow service). Because RTPs settle instantly, these payments are typically irreversible once submitted.

When might a real-time payment not arrive instantly?

  • The recipient’s bank is experiencing delays or a maintenance window
  • Network delays between participating institutions or payment processors

How to send a real‑time payment

As with any payment, real-time payments should only be sent to people or businesses you know and trust – always double-check recipient account details before sending:

  • Go to Move Money > Send (on web) or tap the ⇄ icon in the bottom navigation bar (on mobile)
  • Create a new recipient or select an existing one
  • Select Real‑Time Payment as the payment method
  • Add or confirm your recipient’s account details (routing and account number)
    • If the receiving account can’t receive RTPs, you’ll be prompted to choose another method
    • Before sending, check with your recipient to make sure their bank can receive real-time payments
  • Enter the payment amount, set the send date or schedule a recurring payment (optional), and add any optional details (like memos or internal notes)
    • You can schedule a payment for a future date, and we will attempt delivery on that date, subject to bank/network availability
    • You can also set up a recurring payment that repeats on a weekly, monthly, or custom schedule
  • Review and confirm the payment

Once your recipient’s bank receives your real-time payment, it may be coded as a real-time payment, “instant payment”, “instant transfer”, or something similar.

How to view outgoing real-time payments

You can check the status of your real‑time payments anytime from your Transactions page. Use filters and select Real-Time Payment Out as the payment method. The statuses include:

  • Sent: The payment was delivered successfully. You’ll see the delivery timestamp in the transaction details.
  • Pending: The payment has been submitted and is still processing. Status will update once it’s delivered or fails.
  • Failed: The payment didn’t go through. If a failure reason is available, you’ll see it in the transaction details.
Troubleshooting
Payment failure reasons

If a real-time payment fails, a failure reason will be stated when available. Common failure reasons include:

  • Recipient’s bank account does not support real‑time payments
  • Recipient’s account is closed
  • Account or routing numbers were entered incorrectly

Here are some best practices to help you avoid real-time payment failures:

  • Double-check your recipient’s account and routing numbers before you confirm a payment
  • Save recipients only after you verify their details
  • Confirm that your recipient’s bank can receive real-time payments before sending one
Payments sent in error

Real‑time payments are designed to be final and irrevocable once submitted. In general, since settlement happens immediately, they cannot be canceled or reversed by the sender.

If an RTP was sent in error:

  • Try to resolve the issue directly with the recipient
  • If that’s not possible, contact Mercury support

While we can’t revoke an RTP once it has been submitted, we can send a return request through the payment network to ask the recipient’s bank to return the funds. Return requests are not guaranteed and depend on the recipient bank’s response.

FAQs

I don’t see the option to send a real-time payment. Why?

If RTP (Real-Time Payments) isn’t appearing as an option when you go to send money, it may be because of one of the following reasons:

  • Your account is on Choice rather than Column. Real-time payments are only supported for accounts provided through our partner, Column N.A.
  • The recipient’s bank or routing number isn’t RTP or FedNow eligible. Even when RTP is supported on your end, the receiving institution has to support the RTP network or FedNow. If the recipient’s routing number isn’t eligible, RTP will be hidden or blocked for that payment.
  • Consider checking with your recipient to make sure their institution is able to receive real-time payments.

Will recipients always receive their funds instantly?

In most cases they will, but instant delivery is not guaranteed. Processing times can vary and some transfers may take longer to complete. Once your recipient’s bank receives your real-time payment, it may be coded as a real-time payment, “instant payment”, “instant transfer”, or something similar.

Can I cancel an RTP after it’s sent?

RTPs are designed to be final once submitted. If you made an error, contact the recipient first to resolve it directly, and then Mercury support. We can request a return request to the recipient’s bank, but returns are not guaranteed.

Are real-time payments only for U.S. accounts?

Yes — real-time payments move funds between U.S. banks/payment providers that participate in the RTP® network and/or the FedNow service.

Does Mercury support receiving real-time payments?

Yes, and can read more about receiving RTP here.

Real-Time Payments (RTP) are available only to Mercury customers whose accounts are provided through Column, N.A., Member FDIC. Third-party fees may apply. Stopping a check payment on Mercury Personal

If you’ve written a check that hasn’t been deposited yet, you can request a stop payment from Mercury to prevent the funds from leaving your account.

Note: If you want to cancel mailed checks created through the Send Money flow, you can do so on your Transactions page.

What is a stop payment?

A stop payment prevents checks from being processed before they’re deposited. They can be applied to any checks/checkbooks assigned to your enabled Mercury accounts, including physical checks ordered from third-party providers.

When to request a stop payment

You might want to request a stop payment if:

  • You sent a check to the wrong recipient
  • A check was lost, stolen, or voided
  • You changed your mind about making the payment
  • You issued a replacement payment and need to cancel the original check

You may also decide after ordering a checkbook that you no longer need it. If this is the case, message us — our team can help you cancel that checkbook if it hasn’t been mailed yet. Otherwise, you will need to request a stop payment on the checkbook number range you ordered by following the instructions in the section below.

Tip: If you still have the check in hand, write “VOID” on it to prevent misuse.

If a check deposit appears for review in your Checkbooks page and you don’t want to honor it for any of the reasons above, you can reject it via check review — no need to submit a stop payment.

How to request a stop payment

Note: Only account admins can request stop payments for physical checks.

Head to your Payments page or Checkbooks page and click the chat icon in the bottom right corner to start a new conversation. You should see a “Stop Check Payment” option, which will lead to you a form to fill out these details:

  • The issuing checking account
  • The check number or check number range (matching the checks you ordered exactly, e.g., “001-025” is not the same as “1-25”)
  • (Optional) any additional notes for context on why you’re stopping the check
  • (Optional) the check amount

Once submitted, we’ll block processing of any checks matching those details for 180 days. You’ll also receive a confirmation email when your stop payment is created.

After submitting a stop payment

Next steps:

  • Check your email for a confirmation of the stop payment
  • If the check does go through within the 180-day stop payment window, notify us immediately by replying to the confirmation email
  • Monitor your account in case of any processing delays

Transfer timelines

Between Mercury accounts:

Between Mercury and a Plaid-linked external account:
  • To Mercury: Transfers from an external Plaid-linked account typically take 3 business days to clear
  • From Mercury: Transfers to a Plaid-linked account typically arrive within 0–1 business days

Understanding check review on Mercury Personal

Check review is an optional fraud prevention feature that allows you to review checks written from your check-enabled checking accounts at the moment they are deposited. It’s turned off by default, so checks you write will be paid as usual unless you choose to turn it on. If you turn it on, you’ll have a ~24-hour window to approve or reject each check before any money leaves your account.

Check review is an account-wide setting and adds a step to every check you write, so it’s entirely up to you whether it’s a good fit. You can turn it on or off at any time.

Learn more about setting up checkbooks in our overview article.

How check review works

If you’ve turned on check review, whenever someone attempts to deposit a check written from one of your check-enabled checking accounts, Mercury flags it and gives you a 24-hour review window.

You’ll be notified of pending checks in a few ways:

  • Email: Includes check number, amount, last four numbers of the associated Mercury checking account, and the number of pending transactions. Multiple checks may be grouped into a single email.
  • Push notifications: You will get in-app push notifications, directing you to the Tasks page.
  • Tasks: Flagged checks appear in your Tasks tab on both desktop and mobile. The task will then link you to the Checkbooks page.

If you don’t act within the review window, the check is automatically paid or rejected based on your default review action settings (see next section).

In rare instances, a check may be processed the same day, which could shorten or eliminate your chance to review it beforehand. You can always dispute a check after it’s been processed by reaching out to our team.

If someone tries to deposit a check from one of your Mercury accounts that is not enabled, it will be returned automatically. Be sure to review all enabled accounts from your Checkbooks > Settings page.

Choosing your default check review action

If you’d like to use check review, you’ll be asked to set it up the first time you order a checkbook. Select Review each check, then choose what happens if you don’t respond within 24 hours:

  • Pay the check: Check deposits will be automatically paid after the review window expires
  • Reject the check: Check deposits will be automatically rejected after the review window expires

To turn check review on or off, or to change your default review action later, click the Settings icon in the top right corner of your Checkbooks page.

FAQs

Who can approve and reject checks during check review?

Only admins are able to review checks and adjust the default check review action.

If someone attempts to deposit a check drawn from a Mercury checking account that isn’t enabled for check issuing, will it be flagged for review?

No. If a check is deposited from a Mercury account that isn’t enabled for check issuing, the deposit will be returned automatically. Be sure to review all enabled accounts from your Checkbooks > Settings page.

Personal: Users

Invite, resend invites, or restore users on Mercury Personal

If you’re an admin, you can send and manage invites from your Users page. There are no limits on the number of users you can add.

Inviting a user

  • Navigate to your main menu in the top left corner of your dashboard and click Users
  • Near the top of the Users page, click Invite a user
  • You’ll be asked to provide their name, email address, and assign them a role.
    • If you’ve enabled a control requiring admin approval for certain actions, the invite request will be sent to your other admins. Once 2 admins approve, the invite will be sent. If you don’t have this control enabled, the invite will be sent immediately.
  • Your invited User will get an email with a link to create their account

Resending an invite

If an invited User can’t find the email to create their account, you can resend the invite from your Users page.

Here’s how:

  • Navigate to the Users page
  • Find the user’s name and click on it to open up their details
  • To the right of their name, click the triple dot icon and select Resend Invite. If you don’t see that option in the menu, it means they already clicked the invite. If they don’t remember their login details, you can have them reset their password instead

Restoring a removed user

If you’ve removed a user and want to add them back to your account, you’ll need to restore their access instead of re-inviting them. Head to your Users page, select the removed user (they’ll be greyed out) and click Restore. This will add them back to the account with their previous set of permissions.

If you have dual admin approvals enabled, another admin will need to approve this action.

Adding a user to a trust account

Trust accounts currently do not support self-serve user invitations or custom roles. Trustees and grantors associated with the trust are added during onboarding. Learn more about Trust accounts at Mercury.

If you need to update users on a trust account, please contact support at personal@mercury.com.

Managing account access

Admins can customize which Mercury accounts are visible to custom users via the Users page. When account access is granted, a custom user can view transactions, send and receive money, and get a card associated with that account. Without access, the account details and balances are hidden and they’re unable to interact with the account.

Inviting a user as custom user

  • Go to Settings > Users.
  • Click Invite. Note: inviting custom users in bulk is not yet supported.
  • Assign the user the custom user role. From there, you can continue to customize their send money permissions and account access.
  • Custom users can only hold a card that is associated with an account they have access to. Likewise, in order to create a card for this user, they must have access to at least one checking account.
  • Once you confirm the user details and role permissions, the invite will be sent immediately.
  • When the user accepts the invite and sets up their Mercury profile, they’ll have access to the set of accounts you specified.

Editing account access for an existing user

  • Go to Settings > Users.
  • Find the user’s name and click on it to open up their details.
  • Click the triple dot icon and select Edit.
  • If the team member is already a custom user, customize their account access as needed and then Save. If they are not a custom user, update their role to custom user and then configure account access as needed.
  • If you remove a user from an account and they have one or more active cards associated with the account, those cards will be canceled.

Trust account access

At this time, Mercury trust accounts do not support self-serve custom roles, limited access users, or account-level permission management. Access for trust accounts is limited to verified trustees and grantors associated with the trust during onboarding.

If you need to update account access for a trust account, please contact support at personal@mercury.com.

Managing roles and permissions in Mercury Personal

When inviting someone to your account, you’ll be asked to assign them a role. This role determines what they can and can’t do in your Mercury account.

Role types at a glance

When you invite a team member, you assign them a role. Each role comes with its own set of permissions. Some roles are fixed; others can be created and edited to match your team’s needs.

Role

Access Level

Customizable

Admin

Has full access to the account, settings, users, and policies

No

Limited access user

Can be issues cards but cannot view sensitive account information

No

Custom roles

Defined by the permissions and account access you configure

Yes — fully configurable

Admin capabilities

Admins have the highest level of access in Mercury. They’re considered super users because they can manage the account’s structure, security, and financial controls end to end. Admins have all of the capabilities below by default, without additional configuration.

Note: Any permission with an asterisk (*) is available to admins only and aren’t configurable via Custom role

Account and security management
  • Update core account settings*
  • Create and manage checking and savings accounts
  • Link external bank accounts
  • Receive and manage security alerts
  • Create API tokens*
  • Approve 2FA reset requests*
  • Request changes to payment limits*
Team and role management
  • Invite and remove users
  • Manage roles and permissions for all users (including other Admins on the account*)
  • Assign and revoke Custom roles
Money movement and approvals
  • Send money
  • Approve payments (when approval rules are enabled)
  • Initiate internal transfers
  • Create auto transfer rules*
  • Manage payment recipients
  • Create request payments
  • Deposit checks
Policies and controls
  • Configure approval policies for payments and account changes*

Limited access user capabilities

The Limited access role is designed for users who need access to cards funds or submit expenses without visibility into sensitive banking information.

Limited access users can:
  • Be issued debit cards
  • View and manage their own cards
  • View their own transactions
  • Submit reimbursements for approval
Limited access users cannot:
  • View account balances or account numbers
  • See account-wide transactions
  • View other users’ activity
  • Move money between accounts
  • Send payments or manage recipients
  • Access transactions, user management, or security settings

Custom roles

Custom roles let you define reusable permission sets that reflect real responsibilities in your account. Any changes you make to a custom role automatically apply to everyone assigned to it.

Custom roles are created by selecting which permissions to grant and choosing which accounts the role can access. You can get started from your Users page by clicking Roles.

Configurable permissions

When building a Custom role, you’ll select which permissions make up the Custom role and determine what actions users in that role can do.

1 - Select which money movement actions the role can perform:
  • Send money (subject to approval policies if enabled)
  • Add, edit, and remove payment recipients
  • Initiate internal transfers
  • Deposit checks
2 - Select which operational and spend actions the role can take:
  • Managing users (anyone except admins)
  • Managing cards (creating, editing, and managing cards)
3 - Specify which accounts the role has access to. At least one account must be selected.
Permissions only apply to the accounts a user has access to. For example, a user may have permission to send money, but if they don’t have access to a specific account, they won’t be able to send funds from that account or view its details.

Changing a user’s role

  • Go to your Users settings
  • Find the user’s name in the list, and click it to open their details
  • In the upper right corner of their details card, click Edit
  • You’ll be able to change their role
    • Note: To edit the permissions for a role, go to Roles via Users page instead. Role permissions can’t be changed from a user’s details
  • Click Save to lock in the change. If you’re trying to make someone an admin and need another admin to approve, it may say “Request Approval”

Trust account permissions

At this time, Mercury trust accounts support access for verified trustees and grantors associated with the trust during onboarding. Self-serve user management, including inviting additional users or assigning custom roles, is not currently available for trust accounts.

If you need to add, remove, or update users on a trust account, please contact support at personal@mercury.com.

Navigating approvals (Personal: Users)

To increase visibility and oversight over outgoing funds (including external transfers and when paying bills), you can use approval rules to:

  • Set amount-based thresholds for payment approvals
  • Assign specific and/or multiple users as approvers
    • Only users in Admin and Custom roles can be added to approval rules
  • Limit how much a user can send in a day
  • Require dual admin approvals for sensitive actions

To get started, head to Settings > Approvals or read on to learn more.

Per-Payment approvals

Payment approvals help ensure the right people review transactions before money leaves your account. You can create multiple rules with custom thresholds and stack them for multi-level review.

What’s new

You can assign non-admins as approvers. Anyone with account access (except users in the Employee role) can be named in an approval rule. This means you can delegate approvals to trusted users without granting them full admin access.

A note on account access

Designated users can only approve payments from accounts they have access to. When a payment is submitted, Mercury checks that at least one approver can access the funding account. If no assigned approvers have access to the funding account, the payment can’t be approved and may be blocked.

Additional Details

  • If the person submitting the payment is also an approver, they’ll be skipped in the approval process but still count toward the required number of approvers.
  • Admins can edit or remove approval rules at any time. Changes apply to all new payments after the update.

If the payment requester is also an assigned approver, they’ll be skipped in the approval process and count as an approver.

Daily maximum

Set a daily limit on the total amount a user can send, ensuring any payments exceeding the amount set requires approval.

This means if a user’s cumulative payments (including any pending payments) exceed the daily maximum, additional payments will need to be reviewed before they are sent.

Both Payment Approvals and Daily Maximum rules can coexist. If a payment already requires review under a per-payment rule, the Daily Maximum will not add another approval. Instead, it acts as a safety net — ensuring users can’t send many smaller payments under the per-payment threshold without oversight (though this should be unusual).

Admins reviewing Payment approvals would also satisfy the “Any Admin” approvers on the Daily Maximum rule. Admins can act as approvers. If the payment requester is also an assigned approver, they’ll be skipped in the approval process and count as an approver.

Dual admin approvals

If you have multiple admins on your account, this setting requires that two admins approve certain requests.

You’ll need two admins on file before you can enable the policy. If you’re currently the only admin, you’ll need to either invite a new user or update permissions for an existing user.

Actions initiated by an admin will require one other admin to approve and all other roles require two admins to approve each request.

Requests that require additional approvals include:

  • Managing users with elevated permissions
    • Inviting or removing an Admin
    • Changing an Admin’s role
    • Inviting a user with send money permissions
    • Granting send money permissions to an existing user
  • Resetting 2-factor-authentication
  • Enabling or editing approval rules

Removing a user on Mercury Personal

You can easily remove a user from your account at any time from your Users page.

Removing a user does not reset their 2FA. If you remove them, you won’t be able to re-add them later with the same email address, so you’ll want to be extra sure. You can also change their role to give them fewer permissions as a more temporary solution.

To remove a user:

  • Open your menu in the top left corner of your dashboard, then select Users
  • Find the user’s name and click it to view their details
  • In the upper right corner of their details, click the Remove button
  • You’ll be asked to confirm your choice. If your account requires multi-admin approval for certain actions, you may need to wait for admin approval before the user is fully removed

Reusing email addresses (Personal: Users)

Mercury no longer requires the use of unique email addresses. If you’ve used placeholder email(s) in the past, you can now use one profile to manage your various accounts.

Editing your email

You can now convert profiles attached to your old placeholder email(s) to your preferred/main email. To do this, you’ll need to invite yourself to the account using your preferred email by following the steps below.

You won’t be able to edit the email from your Settings page — you will receive an error that the “Email is already taken”

  • Navigate to your company menu in the top left corner of your dashboard and click “Settings” and then select Team.
  • Near the top of the Team page, click Invite.
  • Input your first name, last name, and preferred email.
  • Assign yourself a role and click Next.
  • Review the details of the invite, ensuring details are correct and click Invite.
  • Check your inbox for an email from hello@mercury.com. Click the Accept Invitation button in the body of the email
  • Use your existing login credentials for that profile to login. You’ll be welcomed to the team and prompted to Accept Invite.

Once accepted, you’ll be logged into the newly invited account. Any accounts that share that email will appear in your profile icon in the lower left hand corner of your dashboard. From here, you’ll be able to easily switch between accounts without needing to log in and out. You can learn more about account linking and switching here.

If you’re a non-admin, reach out to an admin on file and ask them to invite your preferred email address to the account. Follow the same steps above to accept the invite.

You can head back to your Team page to remove any old placeholder emails that are no longer needed. If you’re a company owner, reach out to help@mercury.com so we can ensure we have your preferred email listed as the primary user.

Important items to note
  • Removing the old email will also remove any permissions, data and most importantly, cards associated with that account. Cancelled cards will need to be recreated and will have new card numbers. Be sure to check any subscriptions tied to the old cards and decide if this action is right for you.
  • This is a manual process, meaning if you have multiple Mercury accounts and placeholder emails, you’ll need to add yourself to each account using the steps above.

Applying for a new account

To apply for a brand new account using an email address we already have on file, log into the existing profile to get started. If you’re not logged in, you’ll run into an “Email already exists” error message.

Upon login, head to your company menu in the top left-hand corner of your dashboard where you’ll see the option to “Open new account”. This profile will share basic information like name, email and 2-factor authentication.

During the onboarding process, you’ll be asked to provide company details but we’ll pre-fill basic information like your name and email.

Once approved, the accounts will be linked and you’ll be able to easily switch between them from your menu.

Running Payroll

Payroll funding deadlines

Before payroll can be processed, you must have enough funds in your account to cover the total amount being debited

This includes:

  • Team member wages
  • Team member taxes
  • Employer taxes
  • Any deductions or benefits
    • These are typically subtracted from your payroll and left behind in your company bank account for the benefits provider to debit

Think of it as the full cost of payroll, not just what team members take home.

When funds are needed

Funds must be available before payroll is submitted and processed.

If funds are not available:

  • Payroll may not process on time
  • Tax payments may be missed or delayed

Risks of late funding

Failing to fund payroll on time can lead to:

  • Payroll delays (team members not paid on time)
  • Late or missed tax payments
  • Potential tax penalties from agencies
  • Additional processing complications

Note: If payroll funding fails, a $150 fee may apply per occurrence and will be added to your invoice.

Best practices

To avoid issues, we recommend:

Keep a buffer
  • Maintain 1–2 months of payroll expenses in your account
  • Not financial advice, but strongly recommended
Know your payroll totals
  • Review your the total amount being debited before each run from your Pay Runs page, not just net pay
Fund early
  • Ensure funds are available at least 1–2 days before payroll submission
Monitor cash flow

Plan ahead for:

  • Bonus runs
  • Commission payouts
  • Seasonal payroll increases

Quick checklist before payroll

Before submitting payroll, confirm the following:

  • Do we have enough funds for the amount being debited?
  • Are there any extra payments this cycle (bonuses, etc.)?
  • Has anything changed that would increase payroll costs?
  • Are there any other large purchases being made around the time payroll processes that could decrease balances before payroll processing?

Payroll readiness checklist

Before each payroll run, it’s important to make sure everyone is included, their pay is accurate, and you have enough funds to cover payroll. This checklist walks you through four things to review before edits close, including how to check your pay run details and confirm your submission deadline.

Your Payroll homepage shows your upcoming pay runs, including the name of the pay schedule, the pay period, and the run’s status. Select the arrow icon on a card to open the full pay run, or open your Pay Runs page to view all.

Before edits close, check the four things below.

Check everyone you’re paying is included

Open the pay run by clicking the arrow icon and confirm everyone you intend to pay appears in the Payees list. The card’s payday row also shows a count, which is a quick way to spot someone missing.

If someone isn’t there, go to the Team section of your Payroll home page and look at their status:

  • Still onboarding — ask them to finish their onboarding before edits close
  • Fully onboarded but not on the run — check that their start date falls within the pay period

To add someone to the run, select More, then Add payees.

Check their pay is right

In the pay run, each person shows their total earnings and their take-home pay. Select anyone to open their payment, where you can expand details about what’s being paid and/or withheld.

If someone’s pay is wrong:

  • For this run only, select Edit pay on their payment
  • Going forward, change it on their profile instead — see Managing someone’s payroll details

Check you have enough to cover it

The pay run shows Mercury debits, which is the total amount coming out of your funding account. The card on your home page shows an estimate of the same figure.

If you need more in the account, move funds in before edits close, or change your funding account from your pay schedule settings — see Managing your payroll settings.

Tip: the total changes from one pay run to the next, as bonuses, new hires, and deductions come and go. It’s worth checking the amount each time rather than assuming last payroll’s figure.

Note: if a payroll debit fails, a fee may apply.

Check your submission deadline

The pay run shows Edits close & runs — the date and time when the run locks, in local time. Your home page card shows the same date.

  • If the run is on autopay, it submits itself at that deadline. You don’t need to do anything, but any changes have to be in before then
  • If you submit manually, you need to submit before the deadline for your team to be paid on your intended payday

If you need help with an upcoming pay run or edits have closed, contact Support and we’ll connect you with the right team.

Viewing, editing and scheduling pay runs

The Pay Runs page is where you can see upcoming and past payroll, make changes before a pay run is submitted, and create one-time payroll outside your regular schedule.

Viewing your pay runs

Select Pay Runs to see your upcoming and past pay runs.

Toggle between Upcoming and Past to find a pay run, or use the available filters to narrow your results.

Editing a scheduled pay run

Select a scheduled pay run to open its details. You’ll see the payday, the total amount Mercury will debit, and a breakdown of what’s included in the run.

Select More to see the actions available for that pay run, including Skip, Edit, Add Pays, and Advanced.

You can also hover over a pay run and select Skip without opening it.

Changes you make inside a pay run apply to that run only. To change someone’s pay going forward, update their pay details from their profile.

Changing the payday
  • Open the scheduled pay run
  • Click the edit icon in the Payday card
  • Choose a new payday
Editing or removing someone’s pay

Select a team member in the pay run to open their pay details. From there, you can:

  • Change their payment method
  • Move their pay to a different pay run
  • Remove them from the pay run

To include someone who isn’t currently in the pay run, select Add in the bottom left corner of the table.

Changing advanced settings

Select More, then Advanced to change how this pay run is calculated.

You can:

  • Change the tax calculation method: Choose Supplemental, Weekly, or Monthly. Supplemental applies a flat withholding rate and is typically used for payments like bonuses, commissions, and severance. Weekly and monthly use the withholding tables for that pay frequency
  • Change deductions: Choose whether benefits deductions and post-tax deductions are included in the pay run

Mercury doesn’t provide tax advice. If you’re unsure which tax calculation method applies, check with your accountant.

Skipping a pay run

Select Skip to skip the scheduled pay run.

Skipping a pay run doesn’t change your regular pay schedule. Your next pay run will still have its normal payday.

Scheduling a pay run

Select Schedule Payroll to schedule the pay run. The run will be submitted at its scheduled-by deadline.

Creating a one-time payroll

Use a one-time payroll when you need to pay someone outside your regular pay schedule, such as for a bonus, missed wages, or a final paycheck.

  • Select Create one-time payroll
  • Set the pay period start and end dates and the payday
  • Choose whether the pay run is automatic or manual
  • Optionally, adjust the advanced settings, including the tax calculation method and whether to withhold benefits or post-tax deductions

Support & Resources

Getting help with Mercury Books

If you have a question or run into an issue while using Mercury Books, start with Command. Command can help answer your question or connect you with our support team when you need additional assistance.

Getting help

  • Open Command from the left-hand menu
  • Describe your question or issue
  • Follow the guidance Command provides

Command can answer many Mercury Books questions directly. If you need more help, you can connect with a support specialist. Our support team can assist with basic questions and, when needed, escalate your request to a team that specializes in the issue you’re experiencing.

Getting a faster answer

When contacting support, include as much relevant detail as possible. Depending on the issue, this could include:

  • The account name and whether it’s a Mercury account, external account, or imported account
  • The date or date range in question
  • What you expected to happen and what you’re seeing instead
  • The exact wording of any error or banner
  • What you’ve already tried
  • The URL of the page where you’re experiencing the issue

Including the page URL can be particularly helpful when troubleshooting. It may contain information about the filters, period, or entity you were viewing when you encountered the issue.

Tip: If a page is behaving unexpectedly, note the URL. Filters, the period you’re viewing, and the entity you have open are all part of it, so the link reproduces exactly what you were looking at.

Things to check first

A few of the most common questions have quick answers:

  • Transactions are missing. Usually your entry start date. See our Why some transactions are missing from Books article
  • An integration isn’t syncing. Usually an unfinished ledger mapping step, or a connection that needs reconnecting. Check the status on the Accounts page within Mercury Books.
  • A balance doesn’t match. See the troubleshooting section of our Reconciling accounts in Mercury Books article
  • A permission error. Books needs the all accounts, accounting, invoice creation, and recipient management permissions. See our Sharing access to your books article

Things we handle for you

Some changes aren’t self-serve. Contact us for:

  • Changing your entry start date
  • Changing your accounting basis
  • Replacing your chart of accounts
  • Correcting an opening balance after it’s been set
  • Adding a batch of GL accounts
  • Getting matched with a bookkeeping firm after setup

What support can and can’t advise on

We help with the product — how to do something, why Books behaved a certain way, and fixing what’s broken. We don’t give accounting or tax advice, so questions about which method to use, how a transaction should be categorized, or whether your books are correct go to a qualified accountant or bookkeeper.

See our What Mercury Books can and can’t help with article.

Joining the Mercury for Accountants partner program

Mercury for Accountants is a free partner program for accounting firms, bookkeepers, and advisors. This article covers how to apply, what your firm gets as a partner, and how to get support once you’re a partner.

How to join Mercury for Accountants

To join Mercury for Accountants, apply through the partner form on Mercury’s website:

  • Go to mercury.com/for/accountants
  • Scroll to the “Become a Mercury Accountant Partner” section
  • Complete the form and submit your application
  • Once your firm is approved, you’ll receive a welcome email from a dedicated onboarding manager
  • Your onboarding manager will guide you through setting up your Mercury account, setting up your Advisor Portal, accepting the program Terms and Conditions, and creating your referrals landing page

There’s no cost to join Mercury for Accountants, and your firm doesn’t need an existing Mercury account to apply.

What your firm gets as a Mercury for Accountants partner

As a Mercury for Accountants partner, your firm gets:

  • A free yearly subscription to Mercury Pro (an annual $4,200 value)
  • Access to the Advisor Portal, where you manage all clients, team members, and referrals from a single login
  • Up to $1,500 in referral bonuses per eligible client you refer
  • Dedicated onboarding and ongoing support from the Partner Success team
  • A library of marketing materials and educational resources for client conversations
  • Access to Mercury perks — discounts and deals on business tools
  • A NASBA-approved certification course worth three CPE credits
  • Custom partnership opportunities for top referrers
Activating your free Mercury Pro subscription

To activate your free Mercury Pro subscription:

  • Apply and get approved as a Mercury for Accountants partner
  • Set up your firm’s Mercury account
  • Contact your dedicated onboarding manager, who will convert your account to a free Mercury Pro account
Getting Mercury for Accountants certified

The Mercury for Accountants certification course is a NASBA-approved course that awards three CPE credits on completion. The course covers the Mercury platform and how to expand into advisory services for your clients.

  • Sign up and complete the course at mercury.learnuponus.com
  • Earn the “Mercury for Accountants Certified” badge on completion

Understanding categories, ledger accounts, and ledger codes across Mercury

Mercury uses the word “category” in more than one place, and if you’re using Books alongside your banking dashboard — or moving to Books from another accounting system — it’s worth knowing which is which. This article explains the three concepts and how they relate.

The three concepts

Mercury categories

Books ledger accounts

ERP GL codes

What they are

Spend categories in your banking dashboard

The accounts in your Books chart of accounts

The accounts in a third-party accounting system like QuickBooks Online, Xero, or NetSuite

What they’re for

Quick visibility into where money goes

Formal double-entry bookkeeping and financial statements in Mercury Books

Formal double-entry bookkeeping and financial statements in third-party accounting systems

Where you set them

On the Transactions page in your banking dashboard

On the Transactions page in Books

In the third-party system, with codes surfaced in Mercury when it’s connected

Who typically uses them

Founders and employees categorizing their own spend

Whoever keeps the books — you, your bookkeeper, or your accountant

Your bookkeeper or accountant

What they feed

Mercury Insights

Financial reports in Books

Financial reports in your third party accounting system

Mercury categories

Categories in your banking dashboard are a lightweight way to see where your money is going. They’re the categories your team applies to card spend, and they power Mercury Insights.

They’re not accounting categories, which are typically referred to as general ledger, or “GL” accounts. They don’t roll up into financial statements, and they don’t map one-to-one to a chart of accounts.

Today, your Mercury categories are not connected to your Books chart of accounts. Changes to Mercury categories do not affect Books and vice versa. They are two distinct systems.

Books ledger accounts

Ledger accounts are the accounts in your Books chart of accounts — your revenue accounts, expense accounts, assets, liabilities, and equity. When you categorize a transaction in Books, you’re choosing a ledger account.

This is what produces your financial statements. Every ledger account has a type that determines where it appears on your reports, and a code that controls how accounts are ordered and grouped.

A ledger account that represents a real financial account — a bank account, credit card, or payment processor — is called a source account. Books creates and manages those for you.

To learn more, see Understanding your chart of accounts.

ERP ledger codes

If you connect Mercury to QuickBooks Online, Xero, or NetSuite, you code transactions to that system’s ledger codes from your banking dashboard, and they sync across.

Those codes belong to that system, not to Books. Books has its own chart of accounts, and the two are separate — changes in one don’t flow to the other.

To learn more, see Using Mercury Books alongside another accounting system.

If you’re using Books, your ledger accounts are what matter for your financials. Categories remain useful for day-to-day visibility in your banking dashboard.

FAQs

If I categorize a transaction in Mercury banking, does its ledger account change?

No. The two remain distinct concepts — a Mercury category isn’t a ledger account and one does not affect the other.

Do I need to keep using Mercury categories if I have Books?

Not for your financial statements — that’s what your ledger accounts do. Categories are still useful for quick visibility in your banking dashboard and for employees coding their own spend.

Can I make my Mercury categories match my chart of accounts?

You can modify your categories to match your Books chart of accounts, but today they still will not be linked.

Categories and ledger accounts serve different purposes and don’t need to line up. Your chart of accounts is usually more detailed and structured than your category list.

I asked Command to categorize transactions and it used the wrong kind of category.

Be specific and name what you want — “categorize these to a ledger account” or the account name itself.

Using Mercury Books alongside another accounting system

Mercury Books is a full accounting system, not an integration to existing software. It is designed to substitute any system you use today. If you currently connect Mercury to QuickBooks Online, Xero, or NetSuite, this article explains what changes when you turn on Books, what stays the same, and how to try Books without disrupting what you have.

One accounting system at a time, for transaction enrichment

Mercury supports the use of one accounting system for transaction enrichment, the applying of GL codes and classes, to Mercury transactions. This means you can connect Mercury Books, or a third party system like Quickbooks, Xero or Netsuite, but not both at once.

The reason is straightforward. Two systems both trying to be the record of your finances means two charts of accounts, two sets of categorizations, and two versions of the truth.

While Mercury only supports one accounting system for transaction enrichment, you can connect your Mercury accounts to multiple accounting systems as a bank feed.

What changes when you turn on Books

When you turn on Books while connected to a third-party accounting system, one specific thing changes — and one specific thing doesn’t.

  • Enriched syncing stops. The GL coding you’d been doing in Mercury for that system no longer flows to it. That work moves into Books.
  • Your bank feed keeps working. Basic transaction data — amount, date, and description — continues syncing to your other system, and you can keep categorizing transactions there.

So you don’t lose your connection. What you lose is Mercury doing the coding work on the other system’s behalf.

Trying Books without committing

This is the path if you want to see how Books handles your books before you move off your current system:

  • Turn on Books. Your bank feed to your other system keeps running
  • Keep categorizing in your other system as you have been, so your existing books stay current
  • Set up Books in parallel — pick an entry start date, bring in your chart of accounts, connect your accounts
  • Work a month in both, then compare

You’ll be doing the coding twice for a period, which is the cost of running a proper comparison. Keep the trial short and focused on one month rather than an open-ended parallel run.

Tip: Use the same month in both systems and compare the Profit & Loss line by line. That tells you more than a general impression of the interface.

Moving fully to Books

Once you’ve decided, close out your final period in your old system and set your entry start date in Books to your cutover date.

See Moving to Books from QuickBooks Online or Xero for the full walkthrough.

Switching back

If you decide a third-party system fits you better, you can go back to it. To cancel your subscription, reach out to our team or manage your subscription via Settings > Books Details.

FAQs

Will connecting Books disconnect QuickBooks entirely?

No. Your bank feed keeps running. What stops is the enriched GL coding sync from Mercury.

Can I run Books and QuickBooks in parallel indefinitely?

You can, but you’d be maintaining two sets of books, and they’ll drift. Treat it as a short comparison rather than a permanent arrangement.

Does Books sync out to QuickBooks or Xero?

No. Books is an accounting system in its own right, not a feed into another one.

Will my QuickBooks history be available in Books?

No. Keep your old system’s records for periods before your cutover date, and export the reports you’ll want later.

Can I have Books connected for one entity and QuickBooks for another?

Yes. Each business has its own accounting setup.

Using the Advisor Portal

The Advisor Portal is where accounting firms and bookkeepers manage clients, team members, and referrals from a single login. This article covers how to set up and access the Portal, how to move between client accounts, and how to manage client and team access.

How to set up and access the Advisor Portal

The Advisor Portal is available to all Mercury for Accountants partners. How you set it up depends on whether your firm already uses Mercury.

If your firm already has a Mercury account
  • Log in to your Mercury account first, so that your existing and new accounts are connected
  • Go to app.mercury.com/advisor-portal/signup
  • Complete the setup process
If your firm is new to Mercury
  • Go to mercury.com/for/accountants
  • Scroll to the “Become a Mercury Accountant Partner” section and complete the form
  • Once your firm is approved, the Mercury team will be in touch to guide you through setting up your Portal and accepting the Terms and Conditions
If a client invited you to manage their Mercury account
  • Find the email with the subject line “You’ve been invited”
  • Click Activate your Account or Review Invite in the email
  • If you’re new to Mercury, enter your details to complete setup, which includes creating a password, creating your profile, and configuring two-factor authentication

Switching between and viewing all accounts

You can use the account switcher to move between the Advisor Portal and individual client accounts, or open All Accounts to view information across every Mercury account you’re a team member of.

  • On Mercury web, click your company name in the top left corner of your dashboard
  • Select a client account to open its dashboard, or click All Accounts to view all accounts at once

From the “All Accounts” dashboard, you can view balances and money movement across accounts and:

  • Set All accounts as your default view
  • Search for a specific account
  • Add or link another Mercury account for a new client
  • Download monthly Mercury statements for all linked accounts
  • Open an individual client’s dashboard

Adding and managing clients on the “Clients” page

The “Clients” page is the homepage of the Advisor Portal, where you manage the clients who use your firm’s services. From the “Clients” page, you can add and view clients, view balances and money movement, download account statements in bulk, and open client dashboards.

Adding a new client

Only Advisor Portal Managers can add new clients. To add one:

  • Log in to Mercury and go to your Advisor Portal
  • On the “Clients” page, click Add a Client
  • Enter the email address of an Admin on your client’s Mercury account — if you’re not sure which email to use, confirm with your client directly
  • The client Admin receives an email prompting them to approve your request
How your client approves your request

Adding a client gives your firm access only after the client approves the request. Here’s what happens on the client’s side:

  • The client Admin receives a notification by email and on their “Team” page, prompting them to review the request
  • By accepting the invite, the Admin invites your Advisor Portal Managers into their organization
  • The Admin assigns your Portal Managers permission levels and account access
  • Once approved, the organization appears on your “Clients” page and you gain access to their dashboard

After a client is approved, you can extend similar access to other members of your team.

Adding and managing team members on the “Team” page

The Users page is where you can add users to your firm, manage their Advisor Portal roles, and assign them to client accounts.

Adding a team member
  • Open your Advisor Portal on web and select Users from the lefthand menu
  • Click Invite
  • Enter their name and email address, and select a role
  • Send the invitation

The team member will receive an email to create their account and join the Advisor Portal.

Advisor Portal roles

The Advisor Portal has two roles:

  • Manager: can view all clients, add or remove staff, assign staff to clients on behalf of clients, and view referral activity and payouts
  • Staff: can only view their assigned clients and other team members
Managing team members

Managers can assign team members to clients, update their roles and permissions, or remove their access.

On the Users page, click into a user to:

  • Edit role: change their Advisor Portal role
  • Remove from client: remove them from a specific client account
  • Assign to clients: assign them to additional client accounts

  • Edit permissions in client: adjust their access within a client account
  • Remove from accounting firm: remove them from the Advisor Portal entirely

When a client invites you to their Mercury account directly

A client can also invite you to their Mercury account without going through the Advisor Portal. In this case, the client chooses your role. A common option for accountants is the configurable Accountant role.

If you’ll be sending money from a client’s account, the client can set up approval policies based on transaction amount and which Admins need to approve. See Navigating approvals for more information.

Who can add clients to the Advisor Portal?

Only Advisor Portal Managers can add new clients. Team members with the Staff role can view their assigned clients but can’t add new ones.

You can download statements in bulk from both the “Clients” page and the All Accounts dashboard, which lets you pull monthly Mercury statements for all of your linked accounts.

What Mercury Books can and can’t help with

Mercury Books is the software you keep your books in. It records, categorizes, reconciles, and reports — and our support team can help you with any of that. What we can’t do is make accounting decisions for you. This article sets out where the line sits, so you know what to bring to us and what to bring to an accountant.

What we can help with

  • Finding your way around. Where a page or setting lives, how to do something in the product
  • Setup. Walking through your entry start date, chart of accounts, connected accounts, and integrations
  • Access. Permissions, roles, getting your bookkeeper or accountant in
  • Connections. Linking accounts, fixing a broken feed, working out why an integration isn’t syncing
  • Missing or unexpected data. Why transactions aren’t appearing, why a balance looks off, where something posted
  • Requests we handle for you. Changing your accounting basis, replacing your chart of accounts, adjusting your entry start date

What we can’t help with

Mercury doesn’t provide accounting or tax advice. These are the questions to take to a qualified accountant or bookkeeper:

  • Which accounting method to use. We’ll explain how cash and accrual behave in Books. Which one is right for your business depends on your circumstances
  • How to categorize a transaction. We’ll show you how to categorize and how to set up rules. Which account a given transaction belongs in is an accounting judgment
  • Whether something is recorded correctly. We can explain what Books did and why. Whether it’s right for your books is a question for your accountant
  • Anything tax-related. Books is not a tax product. Your bookkeeping is an input to your tax filing, and Mercury doesn’t prepare or file returns
  • Whether your books are ready for a filing, an audit, or diligence. That’s a professional judgment about your specific situation

This applies no matter which path you’re on. If you’re doing your books yourself, it’s worth knowing up front: we can help you use the product well, but we can’t stand in for an accountant.

If you’re looking for an accountant or bookkeeper to help you make these decisions, Mercury Books can introduce you to one from our set of trusted accountant partners.

FAQs

I’m doing my own books. Can support tell me how to categorize a transaction?

We can tell you how the categorization works and what Books proposed. Which account it belongs in is your call or your accountant’s.

Can Command give me accounting advice?

No. Command explains how Books works and what your numbers show. It doesn’t give accounting, tax, or legal advice.

I don’t have an accountant. Can Mercury find me one?

Yes. We can introduce you to a partner bookkeeping firm. See Working with a bookkeeper in Mercury Books.

Does Mercury review my books?

No. Your books are yours, and Mercury doesn’t review or certify them.

Working With Transactions

Categorizing and splitting transactions

Categorizing a transaction in Mercury Books means assigning it a ledger account from your chart of accounts — the account it’s recorded against on your reports. Books categorizes most transactions for you, so the work is usually reviewing what it proposed, changing what’s wrong, and splitting the occasional transaction that belongs in more than one account.

Changing a transaction’s ledger account

Go to Transactions in the left-hand menu of Books. The Ledger account column shows which account each transaction is categorized to. To change one, hover over the Ledger account cell and choose a different account.

Most transactions arrive already categorized. See our How auto-categorization works article for how Books decides.

A transaction that’s matched to a bill or invoice is the exception. Its ledger account comes from that bill or invoice, so you can’t change it from the transaction — open the bill or invoice, change the account there, and the transaction follows. See our Matching payments to invoices, bills, and payroll article.

Splitting a transaction across ledger accounts

When one transaction covers more than one thing you want to track separately — a card charge that’s part software and part hardware, say — split it into line items, each with its own ledger account.

  • Go to Transactions and locate the transaction
  • Click on the chevron (>) to open its side panel
  • Click the pencil icon to edit
  • Under the line items section, click + to add another line
  • Set the ledger account, memo, and amount on each line
  • Confirm that the total line item amount matches the transaction amount
  • Save

Books doesn’t work out the remainder for you, so enter each amount yourself and check that the lines total the transaction before you save.

Adding memos, tags, and matches

The side panel is also where the rest of a transaction’s detail lives. From it you can:

  • Add or edit the memo on any line
  • Apply tags to the whole transaction or to individual line items — see our Tagging transactions in Books article
  • Match the transaction to an invoice, bill, or payroll run — see our Matching payments to invoices, bills, and payroll article
  • Open the original transaction in your banking dashboard, for Mercury transactions

Notes and receipts you added to a Mercury transaction in your banking dashboard come across to Books automatically.

FAQs

Why can’t I change the ledger account on some transactions?

Because they’re matched to a bill or invoice, which is where their ledger account comes from. Change it on the bill or invoice and the transaction follows. Unmatching the payment also releases the transaction, and leaves it uncategorized.

Do the lines of a split have to add up to the transaction total?

Yes. A split isn’t finished until the line amounts match the total, so keep adjusting or adding lines until they do.

Can I categorize transactions by asking Command?

Yes. Command can categorize transactions in bulk, grouping them by proposed ledger account and asking you to approve each group.

Are my Mercury spend categories the same as my Books ledger accounts?

No. See our Understanding categories, ledger accounts, and ledger codes across Mercury article.

How auto-categorization works in Books

Mercury Books categorizes transactions for you as they arrive, so most of your bookkeeping starts from a coded set of transactions rather than a blank column. This article explains what goes into that and how to steer it.

The three layers

Books works through three layers to decide which GL account a transaction belongs to.

  1. Your rules. If a transaction matches a rule you’ve created, that rule decides the category. Rules take precedence over everything else, so they’re the way to lock in a decision you don’t want revisited. See our Managing categorization rules article.

  2. Similarity matching. Books looks at how you’ve categorized similar transactions before — same merchant, same description pattern, same account — and applies the same treatment.

  3. AI. For transactions that don’t match a rule or resemble anything you’ve coded before, Books uses a model that reads the transaction’s description and amount alongside your chart of accounts, and proposes the account it fits best.

If none of the three produces a confident answer, the transaction is left uncategorized for you to code.

How your corrections feed back in

Every time you recategorize a transaction in Books, that decision is learned. The next similar transaction is more likely to arrive coded the way you’d code it.

This works in both directions with your banking dashboard. Categorization is shared across Mercury, so the work you do in Books informs how your Mercury transactions are categorized, and vice versa.

Tip: Correcting the first few of a recurring transaction pays off quickly. It’s usually faster than waiting to fix them in bulk later.

Reviewing what was categorized for you

Auto-categorization is a starting point, not a substitute for review — particularly for a backlog of historical transactions, where there’s less signal to work from.

  • Go to Transactions
  • Filter to uncategorized transactions and code them
  • Then scan the categorized ones, starting with your largest amounts and your recurring transactions

Tip: Sort by amount and check the top of the list first. A handful of large transactions in the wrong account will distort your reports more than a long tail of small ones.

Getting better results

  • Create rules for anything predictable — recurring vendors, subscriptions, transfers you make every month
  • Keep your chart of accounts tight. A shorter, clearly named list of accounts is easier to categorize against than a long one with overlapping names
  • Name accounts the way you’d describe them. Descriptive names give the model more to work with than generic ones
  • Correct as you go rather than in one pass at the end of the quarter

How your chart of accounts should be structured is an accounting question rather than a product one — your accountant or bookkeeper is the right person to ask. See our Understanding your chart of accounts article for how to make changes once you’ve decided.

FAQs

Can I turn auto-categorization off?

It runs as transactions arrive. If you’d rather categorize everything yourself, you can change any category Books assigns, and rules give you a way to control the outcome exactly.

Why was a transaction categorized incorrectly?

Usually because there wasn’t much to go on — a vague bank description, an unfamiliar vendor, or an account name that could plausibly apply. Correct it, and create a rule if it’s a transaction you’ll see again.

Does auto-categorization change a transaction after I’ve set it?

No. Once you set a category, it stays. The one exception is transfers between your own accounts, which Books relinks when the other side of the transfer arrives.

Does it work on historical transactions?

Yes, though results are stronger for ongoing activity than for a large backfill of older transactions. Review a backfill before relying on the reports.

Managing categorization rules

A categorization rule tells Mercury Books to categorize a transaction to a specific ledger account whenever it matches conditions you set. Rules take precedence over automatic categorization, so they’re how you make a decision stick for every future transaction that looks the same.

Creating a rule

  • Go to Rules page in Books
  • Click Create rule
  • Set your conditions
  • Choose the ledger account transactions matching the rule should be categorized to
  • Save the rule

Editing and removing rules

Open your rules from the settings icon above the transactions grid. From there you can change a rule’s conditions or the account it assigns, or delete it.

Note: Changing a rule affects transactions going forward. It doesn’t recategorize transactions that were already categorize.

How rules interact with everything else

Rules are the first layer of categorization. When a transaction matches one, the rule decides its category, and neither similarity matching nor the AI model overrides it.

If a transaction could match more than one rule, write your conditions tightly enough that only one applies. The more specific your conditions, the more predictable the outcome.

See our How auto-categorization works article for the full picture.
