Matching payments to invoices and bills

Payment matching connects a transaction in your bank feed to what it actually settles — an invoice you sent or a bill you owe.

The direction of the transaction determines what you’re matching against. Money coming in matches to invoices; money going out matches to bills.

What Books matches for you

Some payments arrive already matched, because Mercury originated the payment or was already tracking what it settles.

  • Bills paid through Mercury Bill Pay sync into Books matched to the bill.
  • Invoice payments received into a Mercury account and tracked in Mercury Invoicing are matched to the invoice. A payment matched in either product shows as matched in both

Everything else you match yourself — payments into or out of a connected external account, invoices and bills you track in Books from another tool, and anything Mercury couldn’t match on its own.

Books narrows it down for you either way. When you open a transaction to match it, Books suggests the invoices or bills the payment is likely to settle, based on the date and the amount, and you confirm.

Matching a payment

  • Under Books, go to Transactions and open the transaction details panel (>)
  • Click the match icon
  • Books lists the invoices or bills the payment is likely to settle, based on date and amount, with the closest one already selected
  • Adjust the selection, or search for what you’re looking for. A single payment can settle more than one invoice or bill
  • As you select, Applied and Remaining show how much of the payment you’ve accounted for. Books confirms when the full amount is applied
  • Resolve any difference between the payment and the amount owed
  • Confirm the match

Once matched, the transaction’s journal entry reflects the invoice or bill’s line items, so the detail carries through to your reports.

Note: Payments are matched one transaction at a time.

When the payment and the amount owed don’t line up

A full payment marks the invoice or bill as paid.

A partial payment leaves the remainder outstanding. Books allocates the payment proportionally across all the line items rather than settling them in order, so a payment covering half an invoice reduces each line by half. You can leave the remainder outstanding, close the remaining balance, or adjust the invoice or bill.

An overpayment leaves an amount the invoice or bill doesn’t account for. Assign the remainder to another ledger account while matching, and the transaction’s category updates to reflect it. You can also adjust the original payment amount.

Changing the category of a matched payment

A matched transaction takes its categories from the invoice or bill line items, so change them on the invoice or bill and the transaction follows. Edits that would invalidate the match — changing a line item amount, for example — are blocked while the payment is matched. Unmatch it first.

To recategorize lines across many invoices or bills at once, ask Command.

Unmatching a payment

  • Under Books, go your Transactions page, locate your payment and open the transaction details panel (>)
  • Click the unmatch icon
  • Confirm in the Unmatch Payment dialog

Unmatching reverses the journal entry, restores the outstanding amount on the invoice or bill, and leaves the transaction uncategorized so you can recategorize or rematch it.

Note: Unmatching removes the payment from every invoice or bill linked to that transaction, not just the one you’re looking at. If a single payment settled several invoices, all of them are affected.

Payments Books can’t see

Matching needs the payment to exist as a transaction in Books.

  • Paid into an external account. Connect the account, or import the transaction with a CSV, then match it
  • Paid in cash, or by a method Books can’t connect to. Create an account in Books for it, add the payment as a transaction, then match
  • Dated before your entry start date. The payment isn’t in your books. Create a journal entry to clear the corresponding accounts receivable or accounts payable. See Setting your entry start date

Troubleshooting

An invoice paid in Mercury Invoicing shows a banner about matching in Books.

Books applies stricter rules than Invoicing, so a payment matched in Invoicing isn’t always settled from a bookkeeping point of view. A few situations need attention on the Books side:

  • The payment was received into an account that isn’t in your books. Import the transaction into Books and match it there
  • The payment is dated before your entry start date, so it isn’t in your books. Create a journal entry to clear the corresponding accounts receivable
  • The payment is less than the total invoiced. Unmatch it, then rematch in Books so the difference is allocated
  • The payment is already applied to other invoices. Unmatch to resolve the conflict, then rematch

An invoice is fully paid in Invoicing but shows as Paid — Needs Action in Books.

The payment transaction is usually already linked to another invoice. Open the transaction, unmatch, then rematch so each invoice is settled by the right amount.

You can’t mark an invoice as paid outside Mercury.

If you’re using Books, match the payment in Books first. That means the payment has to exist as a transaction in Books, so connect or import the account it landed in.

Matching transfers between accounts

When you move money between your own accounts, both sides show up in your books — one transaction leaving the source account and another arriving in the destination. Mercury Books recognizes these as the same money and links them, so a transfer isn’t recorded as income or expense. This article explains how that works and what to do when a transfer doesn’t link.

What counts as a transfer

The Transfer Between Accounts category covers any movement of money between accounts in your books:

  • Moving money between your Mercury accounts
  • Moving money between Mercury and an external bank account
  • Paying off a credit card from a bank account
  • A Stripe or PayPal payout landing in your bank account

These are all balance sheet movements rather than revenue or expenses, which is why keeping them out of your income statement matters.

How linking works

Books matches the two sides of a transfer on amount and date, within a window of a few days. Once matched, each side records against the transfer account, and the transaction’s side panel shows a Linked transfer detail pointing to the other side.

  • Under Books, go to Transactions and click a transfer to open its side panel
  • Find Linked transfer
  • Click it to jump to the other side of the transfer

Opening a linked transfer from the Reconciliation page takes you to the reconciliation for the other account. From Transactions or Journal Entries, the side panel swaps in place.

Payouts from Stripe and PayPal

Payouts link reliably, because the payout event tells Books exactly which bank account the money is going to. Books matches the deposit in that specific account to the payout, so revenue isn’t counted twice.

Tip: A payout deposit can be categorized as revenue for a short time before the payout event reaches Books. Once it arrives, Books recategorizes the deposit as a transfer and links it. If a deposit looks miscategorized, wait a day before changing it by hand.

This applies to payouts that arrive after your payment processor is connected. For payouts that predate the connection, categorize the deposit as a transfer between accounts yourself.

When a transfer doesn’t link

A transfer stays unlinked when the other side never arrives in your books. The usual reasons:

  • The other account isn’t in your books. A transfer to or from an account you haven’t connected has only one side. Connect the account, or import its transactions with a CSV
  • The two legs are further apart than the matching window. Transfers between institutions can take several days to settle
  • The amounts differ. A wire fee or currency conversion deducted along the way means the two sides don’t match on amount

When that happens, categorize the transaction yourself. Open it from Transactions and set the category to the account that reflects where the money actually went — or record the difference with a manual journal entry if a fee was taken out.

FAQs

Can I tell from the transactions grid whether a transfer is linked?

Not from the grid. Open the transaction’s side panel and look for Linked transfer.

Why is a transfer to my Treasury account unlinked?

Treasury activity isn’t part of your books, so the other side of the transfer never arrives. Record it with a manual journal entry.

Should transfers appear on my Profit & Loss?

No. A transfer between your own accounts moves money without earning or spending it, so it belongs on your balance sheet rather than your income statement. If a transfer is showing up as income or an expense, it’s categorized to the wrong account.

Tagging transactions in Books

Tags let you group activity in Mercury Books along a dimension other than your chart of accounts — most commonly by department — so you can see what a particular part of your business is spending and earning without creating separate GL accounts for each one.

What you can tag

  • Transactions
  • Journal entries
  • Individual line items within a transaction or journal entry

Tagging at the line item level is what makes a split transaction useful across departments. A single card charge can be split into two lines and each line tagged to a different department.

Creating and managing tags

Go to the Tags page in the left-hand menu of Books under Settings. Tags are organized under a Department group, and from this page you can:

  • Create a new tag
  • Rename an existing tag
  • Delete a tag you’re no longer using

Applying a tag

From the transactions grid:

  • Go to Transactions
  • Set the tag in the Tags column on the row you want
  • To apply the same tag to many rows, drag the cell’s corner down, or copy and paste it into other cells
  • Click Save in the action bar at the bottom of the screen

From the side panel:

  • Click a transaction, journal entry, or line item to open its side panel
  • Apply the tag there

Reporting by tag

Every report page in Books can be filtered by tag. Go to Reports, open the report you want, and apply a tag filter to see your Profit & Loss, Balance Sheet, or Cash Flow for that department alone.

Combine the tag filter with the period selector to compare a department across months or quarters.

FAQs

Can I create my own tag groups?

Tags are organized under the Department group today. You can create as many tags within it as you need.

Can I see two departments side by side on one report?

Not in a single view. Filter to one tag at a time, or export each and compare them in a spreadsheet.

Are tags the same as classes in QuickBooks?

They serve a similar purpose — a second dimension for grouping activity alongside your chart of accounts.

Does a tag affect how a transaction is categorized?

No. Tags are independent of your GL accounts. A transaction has one category and can carry a tag as well.

Can I require a tag on every transaction?

Not currently. Tags are optional on every transaction and line item.

Using Mercury Books on accrual basis

On accrual basis, you generally record revenue when it’s earned and expenses when they’re incurred, even if payment happens later.

Books supports this by recording invoices as Accounts Receivable and bills as Accounts Payable. Other accruals and adjustments can be recorded using manual journal entries.

This article explains how Books records transactions, payments, and adjustments when you use accrual accounting.

To check your accounting basis, go to Settings > Books Details and find Accounting basis. Learn more in Choosing your accounting method.

Bank, card, and payment processor transactions

Books automatically records income and expenses from these transactions on the transaction date, unless they’re matched to an invoice or bill. Matched payments clear Accounts Receivable or Accounts Payable; the revenue or expense is recorded on the invoice or bill date.

Payroll transactions

Books records payroll expenses on the payroll run date, even if the money leaves your account later. For example, a payroll run on August 30 that’s paid out on September 3 is recorded as an August expense.

Invoices and customer payments

By default, Books records revenue on the invoice date. Each invoice creates an Accounts Receivable record. Matching a customer’s payment to the invoice clears it from Accounts Receivable.

For example, an invoice dated August and paid in September records revenue in August. The September payment clears the amount owed.

Bills and vendor payments

Books records an expense on the bill date. Each bill creates an Accounts Payable record. Matching a payment to the bill clears it from Accounts Payable.

For example, a bill dated August and paid in September records the expense in August. The September payment clears the amount owed.

The Mercury Bill Pay integration isn’t yet available for accrual basis. In the meanwhile, you can record bills directly in Books.

Match each bill payment to its bill to avoid counting the expense twice. An unmatched payment may be categorized as a new expense while the bill remains open.

Other accruals and adjustments

You can use manual journal entries in Books to record accrued expenses, deferred revenue, prepaid expenses, and depreciation or amortization. Try using Command to create these automatically.

Mercury is a fintech company, not an FDIC-insured bank. Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Members FDIC.

Using Mercury Books on cash basis

On cash basis, you generally record income when you receive payment and expenses when you pay them. Sending an invoice or receiving a bill doesn’t, by itself, record income or an expense.

This article explains how Books records transactions, payments, and adjustments when you use cash basis accounting.

To check your accounting basis, go to Settings > Books Details and find Accounting basis. Learn more in Choosing your accounting method.

Bank, card, and payment processor transactions

Books automatically records income and expenses from these transactions on the transaction date.

Payroll transactions

Books records payroll expenses on the payroll run date, even if the money leaves your account later. For example, a payroll run on August 30 that’s paid out on September 3 is recorded as an August expense.

Invoices and customer payments

Books records revenue on the payment date, rather than the invoice date. Creating an invoice doesn’t record revenue or create an Accounts Receivable record.

For example, an invoice sent in August and paid in September appears as September revenue.

Bills and bill payments

Books records expenses on the payment date, rather than the bill date. Unpaid bills don’t create Accounts Payable records.

For example, a bill received in August and paid in September appears as a September expense.

Adjustments

You can use manual journal entries in Books to record adjustments. Try using Command to create these entries and automate much of the process.

Miscellaneous

Bill Pay overview

Mercury Bill Pay is an automated accounts payable solution that helps you manage and pay company bills from your Mercury account. Bills sent to your dedicated inbox are automatically organized by approval status and due date, and can be scheduled for payment via ACH, check, or wire. You can also sync bill data directly to your accounting software.

This article walks through setting up Bill Pay, managing requests, sending payments, and integrating with your accounting software.

Setting up Bill Pay

  • Click Payments from the left-hand menu on web and select Bill Pay
  • Click Get Started or the gear icon to manage settings
  • Copy your dedicated bill pay email address or edit it as needed
    • You can forward bills here, set up auto-forwarding, or ask vendors to send bills directly
  • Set up approval rules to control which bills require review
  • Add approved senders. Emails from unknown senders will still appear in your inbox but will be flagged for review
  • (Optional) Connect your accounting software:
    • Supported platforms include: QuickBooks Online, Xero, NetSuite

You can adjust your bill pay settings anytime from the Bill Pay dashboard by clicking the gear icon.

Reviewing and organizing bills

From the Bill Pay dashboard, you’ll see:

  • Inbox: New bills forwarded or uploaded to your account
  • Needs Approval: Bills waiting for approval by designated admins
  • Scheduled: Payments that have been scheduled but not yet sent
  • Paid: History of completed bill payments

Each bill shows its due date, amount, and approval status. You can filter by status or due date.

Paying a bill

You can add and pay bills in a few ways:

  • Click Upload Bill in the Bill Pay dashboard
  • Go to Move Money > Send, then upload or drag in a bill
  • Dropping an invoice into your bill inbox or forward to your bill pay email
Payment workflow
  • Upload your bill (PDF only) and view a preview of the bill on the right side of your screen.
    • Each bill must be uploaded as a separate PDF
    • You can drag and drop multiple PDFs at once
  • We automatically scan the bill and extract details using Optical Character Recognition (OCR)
    • Tip: Click into any auto-filled field during the payment flow to highlight the source text in the bill preview
  • Select a recipient
    • Mercury will try to match the bill to an existing recipient. If no match is found, you can create a new recipient using details from the uploaded bill
  • Choose a payment method
    • Supported methods include: ACH, check, domestic wire, international wire
    • Verify your recipient’s bank details
  • Set the payment amount, send date, and funding source
    • You can also schedule recurring payments
  • (Optional) Add a GL code if you use an accounting integration
    • If you’re connected to QuickBooks Online, Xero, or NetSuite, you’ll see the option to tag the bill with a GL code. Only bills with a GL code will sync to your accounting software.
    • You can toggle from “Single GL Code” to “Multiple GL Codes”, which allows you to categorize a bill by one or more GL codes and sync the payment to your accounting software.
  • Complete the Details step
    • Confirm the name to display on the payment, add an optional memo, and choose whether to send an email receipt.
    • You’ll also see the invoice number, date, and due date pulled from the bill. You can add an internal note or upload attachments if needed.
  • Review your payment to ensure details are correct and click Send or Schedule to complete the payment
    • Immediate payments will appear in your Transactions list. Scheduled payments appear in both Scheduled Bills and Scheduled Payments.
    • If a payment requires approval, approvers can review it from the Needs Approval section on either the Bill Pay or Payments page. Learn more about approvals here.

Tips & reminders

  • Supported payment types include: ACH, check, or domestic/international wire. Delivery timelines vary by method.
  • Each bill must be its own PDF: If uploading multiple bills, attach each one as a separate file
  • You can upload multiple PDFs at once: Mercury will queue them in your Inbox so you can review and process one at a time

Syncing with accounting software

If you’ve connected your accounting platform:

  • Add a GL code when reviewing or sending a bill
  • When a payment is scheduled, the bill will sync as unpaid
  • Once paid, it will be marked as paid in your accounting system

To sync as a bill (not just an expense), the uploaded bill must include at least one of:

  • Invoice number
  • Invoice date
  • Due date

You can find this section on the Details step when making a payment. If none of these fields are filled out, the payment will sync to your accounting software as an expense when it is paid — it will not sync as a bill.

If you use another accounting software (or none at all), you can still use bill pay to upload, manage and pay bills.

Setting up employee benefits with Mercury Payroll

Mercury’s affiliate, Central Benefits and Insurance Services LLC, can help you set up health, retirement, and insurance benefits for your team, with the deductions handled automatically in payroll.

This article covers what’s available, how setting benefits up works, and when coverage can start.

What’s available

  • Health — medical, dental, and vision
  • Life and disability
  • Workers’ compensation (via Next Insurance)*
  • 401(k) (via Human Interest and Vestwell)**

Benefits are available to your employees. Contractors aren’t eligible.

How setting up benefits works

Setting up benefits starts with a conversation rather than a form. You can start it from the Benefits tab in payroll.

  • Book a call. You’ll talk to a benefits specialist about what you’re looking for and what your team needs
  • Choose your plans. We’ll quote plans based on your team and your coverage preferences, and you’ll pick what to offer. Most companies decide on the call
  • Set your contributions. You decide how much of the premium your company covers, for employees and for their dependents
  • We handle the paperwork. We build your enrollment, submit it to the carrier, and follow up if the carrier needs anything else
  • Your team enrolls online. We’ll let you know if anyone hasn’t completed their elections

You can start setting up benefits alongside payroll, but setup and activation timelines vary by benefit.

When coverage can start

Two things have to happen before coverage begins:

  • Your first payroll has to run successfully. This is a carrier requirement, not a Mercury one
  • Your plan choices and contributions have to be final

For coverage to start on the first of next month, both need to be done by the 15th of this month. If either slips, your start date moves to the following month.

After that, your plans still go through carrier approval, which can take up to two weeks to show up as active coverage.

Note: Additional restrictions may apply based on the state and insurance company.

401(k)

Mercury offers 401(k) plans through Human Interest and Vestwell. New plans are set up with Human Interest; if you already have a Vestwell plan, you can connect that instead.

When you’re ready, we’ll connect you with the provider’s team to set up your plan. Once it’s connected to payroll, everything runs automatically:

  • Your team enrols and chooses their contributions with the provider
  • Contributions come out of each paycheck and appear on your team’s pay statements
  • The provider tracks annual contribution limits

Your team manages their enrolment and contribution amounts with the provider rather than in Mercury, and changes they make there flow through to your next pay run.

Mercury doesn’t hold or move your 401(k) money. The provider debits your account for contributions separately, after payroll. If you change bank accounts, you’ll need to update your account details directly with your 401(k) provider. Mercury can’t make these changes for you.

Workers’ compensation

Workers’ compensation is required by law in almost every state as soon as you have an employee, and we can set up a policy for you if you’d like.

Because premiums are calculated using payroll information, this can help reduce differences between estimated and actual premiums

Your insurer bills you for the premium directly. It isn’t part of your payroll debit.

Workers’ compensation isn’t available for companies that only pay contractors.

How benefits appear in payroll

Benefit deductions come out of each paycheck automatically and show up on your team’s pay statements.

On a pay run, benefit contributions are listed separately from the amount Mercury debits, because the providers collect those themselves before or after payroll runs (typically on a monthly basis). They’re part of your total payroll cost, but they aren’t part of the Mercury debit.

Where to get help

  • Plan, coverage, and claims questions go to your benefits provider or carrier
  • Questions about deductions or how benefits appear in payroll go to Mercury specialized support
